author: mbayard-sorp
body:
Ticket #16412, phase 3b of the ads control plane (docs/store-team/ads-control-plane-plan.md §4, §7). Built on #1708, which merged before this PR opened, so the route nests under the `admin.ads.tsx` layout.

## What changed

- `app/lib/ads/tree-core.ts` (pure, client-safe): `buildTree()` links `ad_platform_entities` rows by `parent_external_id` into campaign > ad set > ad and puts 1d, 7d and 30d figures on every node.
  - Spend, impressions, clicks and leads come from `ad_platform_insights_daily`. A node uses rows at its own level when the window has any. Otherwise it sums its children. The pull is ad level today, so campaigns and ad sets show what their ads spent.
  - CPL is spend over leads and is flagged above `ads_lead_cpl_ceiling_cents`.
  - Orders, net revenue, CPA and net ROAS (7d and 30d) come from `ad_creative_daily_metrics` by the ad's `creative_id`. A parent counts each distinct creative under it once. If several ads share a creative, each ad's ROAS divides that creative's revenue by the combined spend of those ads, and the row says the creative is shared.
  - Budget comes from the entity that owns it: the campaign under CBO, or the ad set under ABO. Children show "Campaign budget" or "Ad set budget".
  - Rows the sync marked `MISSING` are hidden and counted in the footnote. A row whose parent is not in the mirror shows as a root, marked "parent not in mirror".
  - The status filter keeps a matching row along with the ancestors above it, and drops siblings that do not match. Parent figures are not re-summed after filtering.
- `app/lib/ads/tree.server.ts`: `loadTree({ platform?, status?, campaignId? })` reads Neon only and never calls a platform during the request. It reads the mirror, 30 days of insights, attributed orders for the mirrored creatives, the creatives' idea ids, the CPL ceiling, spend-enabled and break-even. The page cannot render without the mirror read, so a failure there throws to the error boundary. If the insights or orders read fails, the page names it and those columns read "unknown" rather than $0. Ads Manager links reuse `adsManagerLink` from `console.server.ts`.
- `app/routes/admin.ads.tree.tsx`: read-only and loader-only. It renders one `<ResponsiveTable>` with a `min-w-[1180px]` table and a sticky first column. Child rows indent inside that cell and the layout never switches to cards. Columns: name with an effective_status chip, budget, spend 1d, spend 7d, impressions 7d, CTR 7d, leads 7d, CPL 7d, orders 7d (30d underneath), CPA 7d (named in the ticket text), net ROAS 7d (30d underneath, green at or above break-even and red below), and links to Ads Manager and the Ad Studio creative. Filters are a GET form for status (all, active, paused, disapproved) and campaign. The bulk checkboxes are disabled and titled "Arrives with the actions ledger (phase 5)". A Sim banner shows while spend is off.
- Expansion state is kept in component state. It is seeded from an `open` search param (`all` or comma-separated keys) and written back with `history.replaceState`, so a reload or a shared link keeps the same rows open, and toggling a row does not re-run the admin and console layout loaders. When a status filter is set, every row starts open.
- `app/routes/admin.ads.tsx`: one line adds "Tree" to the sub-nav.
- Overview tiles are not linked here. `Tile` has no href, so linking them would take more than one line.

## DONE WHEN (from the ticket)

- The tree matches the mirror for the live account. The loader reads `ad_platform_entities` directly and builds the tree from it alone. I checked this against fixture rows, not against the live account.
- The loader is tested. `app/lib/admin-ads-tree-loader.test.ts` covers the guard, the empty mirror, the populated tree with search params, a failed insights read and a failed mirror read. `app/lib/ads/tree-core.test.ts` has 23 cases covering parent linking, orphans, hidden MISSING rows, roll-ups from children, own-row precedence, budget owner, CPL against the ceiling, CPA and ROAS, shared creatives, and the status, campaign and platform filters.
- Renders at 375px and 1024px with no page-level horizontal scroll. I checked this in a local dev server with fixture rows that included a long unbroken ad name. `scrollWidth` equaled `clientWidth` at both widths, and the table scrolled inside its wrapper. For the check I temporarily bypassed `requireAdmin` and swapped in a fixture source, then reverted both before committing. The client bundle did not hydrate in that run because of the local disk issue below, so I checked SSR output for open, closed and filtered states, but not the click-to-toggle path.

## Checks

- `npm run typecheck`: no errors in changed files. The only errors left are TS2307 "cannot find module" for packages missing locally (`@vercel/blob`, `imapflow`, `mailparser`, `web-vitals`, `@playwright/test`).
- `npx vitest run`: 7086 tests passed. The only failure is the `scripts/design-snapshots.test.ts` file, which cannot import `@playwright/test`.
- Both failures come from my environment: `npm install` hit ENOSPC (the disk is full), so the worktree resolved packages from the main checkout's older `node_modules`. CI will show the real result.

No protected paths touched. No migrations.

author: khoks
body:
## Summary
Pre-registers how S-8.3.3's two change signals get their thresholds: the cited-set Jaccard and the answer-embedding distance. The rule comes from the plan's discipline ([m3](docs/plans/m3-saved-searches-alerts.md), as D-068 did for E-7.1). It is committed and merged before any overlap or distance is computed from the app's Q&A history.

- **Sample.** Re-asked identical questions in the same context, kept only where nothing new became visible between the two asks.
- **Rule.** The D threshold is the 95th percentile, rounded up. The J threshold is the 5th percentile, rounded down.
- **Negative control.** D must separate different-question pairs at least 80% of the time.
- **Fallback.** Below 20 pairs, the detector uses the priors J < 0.50 and D > 0.15, and calibration is recorded as pending.
- **Privacy.** Only aggregates are published.

Docs only. A note in `docs/notes/` and a pointer on T-8.3.3.2.

body:
## Goal

Repair a moved registered prompt folder without changing historical bindings, saved dreams, review decisions, drafts, or approved memory.

## Changes

- Add `dream relocate-prompts-preview` and `dream relocate-prompts-confirm`.
- Compare the complete replacement inventory against one validated frozen input. Require confirmation of the exact preview.
- Save one immutable relocation record. Use the replacement only for fresh preparation and queue inspection.
- Preserve frozen replay and existing review authority. The selected snapshot does not prove equivalence with every historical version.
- Reject mismatches, changed targets, corrupt records, and pre-existing relocation records.
- Exclude only the top-level relocation record from dream-authority traversal and its 10,000-entry budget. Keep other limits unchanged.

`README.md` documents the commands and their limits. The base includes the merged review-triage feature. All three task patches remained identical during the rebase.

Verified head: `9ee84eb0f155f85f0d08b7e01bbf21a33e4a3dc3`.

## Verification

- One complete `swift test -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors` run reported 489 tests, three opt-in skips, and four passing process helpers.
- A new relocatable package passed executable, resource, license, metadata, and source-identity checks.
- Four packaged-command runs passed. They cover preview, confirmation, worker preparation, and queue inspection through standalone and app-bundled executables.
- Synthetic checks cover missing sources, record conflicts, corruption, scope isolation, and the 10,000-entry boundary.
- The current package passed the isolated graphical scenario below. Confirmation added only the relocation record to dream state.
- Preservation checks verified unchanged approved memory, refs, checkout, historical binding, frozen inputs and replies, generations, progress, review decisions, and profile.
- Final independent source and graphical review accepted this exact head with no findings.
- Review run `0d371398-ae56-433c-90ed-bb61244b6aec` used `openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol` with `xhigh` thinking.

## Visual evidence

The before state shows unknown queue counts and the missing-prompts error. Saved history remains readable.

![Synthetic queue before prompt-source confirmation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/68e1eb12-56d7-42e3-998f-4a198886ea41)

After confirmation, the reopened app shows queue counts and the same saved history. Batch estimates remain explicitly unknown.

![Synthetic queue after prompt-source confirmation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/295db00f-1090-4576-9bf3-945a91a803a6)

Review Suggestions opens without an error sheet. The existing suggestion and approved memory remain present, with zero staged changes.

![Synthetic review after prompt-source confirmation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ae7e4ed6-3ebb-41bd-b19f-2050d8eea62b)

## Limits and state

- The graphical scenario closed the test app before confirmation and reopened it afterward. It does not establish hot activation.
- Equality covers the selected frozen input's complete template subset, not universal historical equivalence.
- Three opt-in checks remain skipped. Actual macOS 13 runtime behavior remains untested.
- All checks used synthetic data without external dream inference. No installation or real-store activation occurred.
- The synthetic app exited, and its temporary discovery link was removed. No memory Save or dream retry occurred.

author: tjackiet
body:
## 背景

段階 A のバッチ 6（`src/handlers/` のうち `portfolio/` 以外の 11 ファイル）。対象のコメントは合わせて 1,258 行あり、`analyzeMyPortfolioHandler.ts`（548 行）と `detectPatternsViewsHandler.ts`（560 行）で 9 割を占めていた。

## 変更

コメントだけを変更し、コードには触れていない。基準は `.claude/rules/comments.md`。

残したのは、コードからは読み取れず、知らないと誤った変更をしてしまう理由だけ（各 1 行）。

- 機密情報：警告ラベルは銘柄名と件数のみで金額は出さない（HIGH 分類）。PrivateApiError 以外のエラーは `err.message` を伏せる
- LLM に届く `content` の契約：
  - 未計測・率の抑止を黙って行ごと省かない
  - 価格の解決欠損では増減額にも資産推移シリーズにも誘導しない
  - 原価を抑止したときは「反映した値です」と断言しない
  - 実効パラメータ行・検出経路行は view 間で同じ文字列を通し、行が無いことを LLM に推論させない
  - `data.warnings` は structuredContent にしか無いので content に出す
- 意図的な非対称：
  - ゼロ建玉は消さず、省略件数を申告する
  - `avg_buy_price` だけ `price_digits` より桁を残して丸める（pairs を取れないときは丸めず、整数丸めに逃げない）
  - `currentFiltered` だけ 0 のとき省く
  - クランプ発火は抑止せず申告だけする
  - 継続系では山2 / 谷3 などの語を混ぜない
- 単一ソース・他とそろえている値：
  - `resolveTrimCounts` / `formatReasonParts` / `DETAILED_VIEW_PATTERN_LIMIT`
  - 日次点を `boundaries` と同じ瞬間から導く
  - テストが抽出に使う `*_LABEL`
  - `ReductionSchema` / `EffectiveParamsSchema` と対の型
  - `get_margin_status` の警告文言
- 判定順・前提：
  - 数量不変条件より先に入庫日価格の抑止を判定する
  - `breakoutDirection` の `null` は `??` ではなくキーの有無で分ける
  - `pivots.length === 3` を `>= 3` にしない
  - `roleLabels.length` で回す
  - 今日の雲は `ichi_series` の 26 本前を見る
- TODO：`buildVolatilitySummaryText` は本番未使用で、PR 6 をやらないと決めた時点で削除する（`docs/internal/view-vocabulary-unification.md` §5-3 がこのコメントを残すよう求めている）

削除したもの：

- 関数・引数・フィールドの JSDoc のうち、名前と型から分かる説明。`// RSI`、`// === 1. ローソク足データ ===` などの見出し
- 経緯・計測値（「旧実装は〜」「ライブの btc_jpy 1hour で 62 件と宣言しながら 57 件」「12,104 ケースで 0 件」など。各 issue に残っている）、区切り線、太字、🚨
- 「〜の doc 参照」という案内。`analyzeMyPortfolioHandler.ts` の「`calcPnl` の doc 参照」は参照先がバッチ 5 で無くなっていたので、案内部分を消した（バッチ 5 からの申し送り）
- ファイル内の繰り返し（#87 の復元数量を出す理由、positional 引数を末尾に足す理由、sensitive-data の HIGH 分類、`tests/view-content-superset.test.ts` が使うラベル など）。最初の 1 箇所だけに残した

catch の中身がコメントだけの `/* noop */` / `/* ignore */`、行末コメントはそのまま残した。

### コメント行数

| ファイル | 変更前 | 変更後 |
|---|---:|---:|
| `detectPatternsViewsHandler.ts` | 560 | 74 |
| `analyzeMyPortfolioHandler.ts` | 548 | 99 |
| `getVolatilityMetricsHandler.ts` | 50 | 8 |
| `analyzeIndicatorsHandler.ts` | 36 | 4 |
| `analyzeCandlePatternsHandler.ts` | 18 | 0 |
| `detectPatternsHandler.ts` | 18 | 3 |
| `analyzeMarketSignalHandler.ts` | 14 | 1 |
| `getTickersJpyHandler.ts` | 6 | 1 |
| `renderChartSvgHandler.ts` | 5 | 1 |
| `analyzeFibonacciHandler.ts` | 2 | 0 |
| `runBacktestHandler.ts` | 1 | 0 |
| 合計 | 1,258 | 191 |

## 確認

- `main` からの差分に含まれるコード行：0 行（差分の全行がコメント行か空行。Biome の折り返しも起きていない）
- `tsc --removeComments` で出力したコンパイル結果が、変更前と全 439 ファイルでバイト単位で一致
- `npm test`：235 ファイル / 6058 passed・1 skipped（変更前と同数）。ソースの文字列を読むテストは `src/handlers/` を読んでいない
- 中身が空になったブロックは無い（変更前後で 0 件）
- `npm run typecheck` / Oxlint / pre-commit（gitleaks・型生成・型チェック・banned-patterns）通過。`biome check` の warning 5 件は `main` と同じもの（下の別 PR 候補 5）

## 別 PR 候補（段階 B）

行番号はこのブランチのもの。

1. `analyzeMyPortfolioHandler.ts:360` の `analyzeMyPortfolioHandler` は 1 関数で約 1,260 行ある。取得・損益・期間パフォーマンス・summary 組み立て・出力の段に分けられる
2. `detectPatternsViewsHandler.ts` は 1,158 行で、debug view 専用の部品（`:218` `formatCandidateDetails`、`:431` `formatRejectionSummary`、`:513` `formatDebugView` まわり）が半分近くを占める。別モジュールに移せる
3. 「今日の雲」の算出が `analyzeIndicatorsHandler.ts:505` と `analyzeMarketSignalHandler.ts:233` に重複している（`ichi_series` の末尾 26 本前を読む）。`lib/` に寄せられる
4. `detectPatternsViewsHandler.ts:75` `FlagFamilyViewFields`：`PatternEntry` の optional フィールドを写した型で、view からは `unknown` 経由のキャストで読んでいる。`PatternEntry` をそのまま使える。`:119` `buildTypeSummary` の未使用引数 `_tz` も外せる
5. `biome check` の既存 warning：`analyzeMarketSignalHandler.ts:74`, `:84-86` の `noNonNullAssertion` ×4、`detectPatternsHandler.ts:30` の `useOptionalChain`（コードの変更になるのでこの PR では触れていない）
6. `analyzeMyPortfolioHandler.ts:213` `QTY_MISMATCH_CAUSE.unknown`：`qtyMismatchReasonFor` はもう返さず、`Record` の網羅のためだけに残っている。enum から外すかを決める
7. `getVolatilityMetricsHandler.ts:67` `buildVolatilitySummaryText`：上の TODO。PR 6 の要否を決めれば消せる

## 他のバッチへの申し送り

- バッチ 8：`tools/detect_patterns.ts:385` が「#180 の `resolveTrimCounts` docstring」を参照している。docstring は消した（理由は 1 行で残した）。経緯は issue 側にあるので、参照を issue 番号だけにする必要がある
- 段階 A の表に無い：`docs/internal/view-vocabulary-unification.md:666` が `getVolatilityMetricsHandler.ts:72-77`、`:127` が `detectPatternsHandler.ts:44-108` を行番号で参照している。このバッチでどちらもずれるので、シンボル名で書くほうがよい

author: tomergee
body:
> Recreated from agent-substrate/env PR 93, opened by tomergee on 2026-10-15; originally closed without merging on 2026-10-19; original branch `openhands-agent-server-example` into `main`. > Mentions and references below are defused; numbers refer to agent-substrate/env. Builds on #​92 (merged as fccd920); rebased on `main` and retargeted. Adds `integrations/openhands`, a pip package (`ate-env-openhands`), and its examples in `examples/openhands`, that runs OpenHands task runs on ate-env. Its `AteEnvWorkspace` mirrors OpenHands' own `AgentSandboxWorkspace` (`openhands-workspace[agent-sandbox]`, kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox), so code written against that workspace moves over by changing the constructor. Unlike agent-sandbox, which runs the stock agent-server image, the agent-server here is a runtime layer, so any unmodified task image gets it. This is PR C of the plan for agent-sandbox-compatible task runs (Tunix included); the fleet and R2E-Gym adapters follow separately. ```diff -from openhands.workspace import AgentSandboxWorkspace +from ate_env_openhands import AteEnvWorkspace -with AgentSandboxWorkspace(warmpool="openhands-pool", namespace="default") as workspace: +with AteEnvWorkspace(template="oh-agent-server", image=TASK_IMAGE, + api_url="ate-env-api.ate-env:7777", api_key=SESSION_KEY) as workspace: conversation = Conversation(agent=agent, workspace=workspace) ``` ## What - **`AteEnvWorkspace(RemoteWorkspace)`** (`src/ate_env_openhands/workspace.py`). Same lifecycle order as `AgentSandboxWorkspace`: create the environment (`template`, optional digest-pinned `image`), wait for the agent-server's `/health`, initialize the parent, and on any failure after the create delete the environment before raising. `pause()` suspends, `resume()` waits for `/health` (which wakes it), `__exit__` sends the completion callback then `cleanup()`, and `cleanup()` is idempotent. - The host is #​92's path form, `/v1alpha/atespaces//envs//ports/

`. No `kubectl port-forward`, and `RemoteConversation`'s event WebSocket goes through it unchanged. - `env_id=` attaches to an existing environment and leaves it on exit. - A lost create answer is deleted by name. A wrong session key fails the constructor with `PermissionError`; the SDK would otherwise turn the 401 into a failed command result. - `working_dir` (default `/workspace`, like upstream) is created. SDK and agent-server versions are compared and a mismatch is logged. - `api_token` goes to the gRPC API only, because the port proxy would forward it to the sandbox. - All workspaces share one loop thread and one gRPC channel per endpoint. - **`layer/`**: the agent-server runtime layer from the earlier commits (standalone CPython 3.12, agent-server/sdk/tools 1.55.0, hash-locked, glibc >= 2.31), moved unchanged. - **`examples/openhands`** (top level, next to the repository's other examples; the package README links to it): `convo_with_ate_env.py` (OpenHands' agent-sandbox example 17 with the workspace line changed), `codeact_agent.py` (CodeAct with a model or `--scripted`), `run_trajectory.py` + `oh_tool.py` + `trajectories/` (execute a CodeAct trajectory from outside), `demo.sh` (register the base template, drive the agent-server over plain HTTP per image). The scripts use the package. - **`ate-env manifest template --env NAME=VALUE`** (repeatable): how the template carries the agent-server's session key and settings. POSIX names, `PORT` reserved, duplicates rejected, kept by derived templates. - **CI**: an "OpenHands integration" job (its own, because openhands-sdk and the agent-server pull in a large dependency set): the tests, and ruff on the package and the examples. - README rewritten around the package: install, layer, base template, field table next to `AgentSandboxWorkspace`'s, migration, examples, versions, testing, limits. | `AgentSandboxWorkspace` | `AteEnvWorkspace` | |---|---| | `warmpool` | `template` (base template with the agent-server layer) | | image fixed in the SandboxTemplate | `image`, any task image | | `namespace` | `atespace` | | `connection="port_forward"` / `direct` + `host` | `api_url` (+ `proxy_url`); the port proxy, no kubectl | | `server_port`, `working_dir`, `api_key`, `health_check_timeout` | same | | `sandbox_ready_timeout` | `create_timeout` | | `operatingMode` Suspended / Running | `SuspendEnvironment` / wake on request | | `shutdown_after_seconds`, `labels`, `pod_labels`, `pod_annotations` | not mapped: ate-env has no environment TTL or labels | ## Finding: the published agent-server binary does not run on older distributions `ghcr.io/openhands/agent-server:1.55.0-*` ships a PyInstaller binary built on Debian bookworm (glibc 2.36). On Ubuntu 22.04 (glibc 2.35), the base of many coding-task images: ``` ImportError: /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.36' not found (required by /tmp/_MEI…/libstdc++.so.6) ``` Ubuntu 20.04 fails the same way on `GLIBC_2.33`. Starting it through the image's own bookworm loader fails too (PyInstaller re-executes itself: `Floating point exception` on 22.04, an `ld.so` assertion on 20.04). The layer is python-build-standalone CPython 3.12.15 (built for glibc 2.17, relocatable, checksum-pinned per architecture) with `openhands-agent-server`, `openhands-sdk` and `openhands-tools` 1.55.0, installed by uv for `manylinux_2_31` from a hash-locked set. The layer uses the image's C library: it runs on glibc 2.31 and newer, not on musl (Alpine), Ubuntu 18.04 or CentOS 7. About 250 MB compressed. ## Verification - `python -m pytest integrations/openhands/tests`: 18 passed, 1 skipped (the live test), in a fresh venv installed exactly as the CI job does (`pip install -e 'clients/python[dev]' -e 'integrations/openhands[test]'`), with CI's ruff 0.16.10 clean. The tests run the workspace against an in-process fake of ate-env-api (gRPC environment lifecycle) and of its port proxy (path form, wake on request, upgrade relay), in front of a real agent-server 1.55.0 on localhost. They cover: create arguments and host, commands, files, health wait through 503s, cleanup after a health timeout, a lost create answer and a wrong session key, attach, attach to an unknown environment, pause/resume with a file kept, exit ordering when the parent exit raises, idempotent cleanup, the API token never reaching the sandbox, another port's URL, and a `RemoteConversation` whose event WebSocket goes through the proxy. - `go test ./cmd/ate-env` (the `--env` flag), `make verify-gofmt verify-boilerplate`, shellcheck (`demo.sh`, `lock.sh`) and zizmor on `ci.yaml` clean. - The rebuilt layer (hash-locked, 2026-10-16), local Docker on arm64: `/health` and a command with the key (401 without) in `debian:bullseye-slim` (glibc 2.31) and `ubuntu:24.04`. author: matteo-endodeals
body:
**Features section ("Built for how agencies actually work.")**

Before this change the pill bar didn't stick, the highlight never left "Valuation", and all six features were stacked down the page.

- **Why the pills didn't stick:** the section had `overflow: hidden`, which turns off `position: sticky` for everything inside it. It's now `overflow: clip`, which keeps the rounded corners.
- **Wide screens (≥761px wide and ≥621px tall):** the heading, pills and current feature pin together as one frame, centered under the floating header. The gaps between them grow with screen height, so there's no wide blue band at the top or bottom. Scrolling steps through the features one at a time, about 65% of a screen of scrolling each, with a short fade between them. On shorter laptops the clip shrinks to fit.
- **Pills:** the highlight follows the current feature. Clicking a pill jumps straight to that feature without flashing through the ones in between, and updates the URL (`/#financials`). Links like `/#contracts` open the right feature on load.
- **Phones:** no pill bar. The features stack, and each already has its own label (the usual pattern on mobile marketing sites).
- **Short desktop windows (under 621px tall):** stacked features under a sticky full-label pill bar that follows the feature in view. Clicking a pill holds its highlight while the page scrolls smoothly.
- Only the feature on screen plays its video, so each video starts from the beginning when its feature appears.
- New component: `app/feature-tour.tsx`.

**Pricing**

> **Enterprise-grade tools. Agency-friendly pricing.**
> You pay per seat for the people using endo, so signing more athletes never raises your bill. *Get a quote for your team →*

The link is a text link to `/book`, not a button, so the bottom of the page doesn't get stacked CTAs again. No prices are shown.

**Tested locally**
- At 1357×866, 1366×700 and 1920×1080: the frame fits, scrolling shows each of the six features in order, and pill jumps go forwards and backwards without passing through other features.
- At 375px: stacked features, no pill bar, no horizontal scroll.

author: kindraywind
body:
Closes #752

- **Gospel** (370): a small silver cross hovers over each Gospel cell, bobbing 6 ± 3 units and breathing, until its unit goes (alpha 200, at most 100 on `ecl_fild01`); the effect's sound row is gone.
- **Assumptio** (375): a monster or NPC gets one grown copy in its own colour instead of the player's two white ones.
- **Soul Drain** (378, 379): three blue sparks swing out from over the dying target in arcs and fall back to the caster (the ghost of Soul Strike with other numbers and a trail that begins at the caster's feet), the caster flashing blue on ticks 55–65; the target's body deepens from #CDCDFF to #0606FF over 200 ticks.
- **Magic Crasher** (380): the target flickers in a random colour each tick for ticks 30–60 (also from Soul Burn's use); its sound at 400 ms and the shake at 480 ms for 650 ms.
- **Magic Power** (382): the weapon is drawn once more, added on, every other drawn frame (players only); the angel sprite and the old row are gone, and the skill's sound is heard at the listener when used.
- **Indulge** (383): 15 green sparks (three on each of five ticks) loop out and back; the caster glows in violet outline copies on ticks 50–80.
- **Soul Change** (384): a blue core inside an orange tube grows from the caster to the target (found by its id read through a float) in 0.24 s, holds and fades by tick 77; hidden for good once an end is missing.

### 1. Was there a real issue, and is it solved?
Yes, each was missing, a generic part, or wrong. Not played in the client by request (code and unit tests only).

### 2. How was it verified?
`verify.sh`: `VERIFY: PASS`. Unit tests (no data.grf): the cross's height and radius at n = 1/18/54/72/90/270 and its alpha; the monster's one copy and the player's two; Soul Drain's three fanned sparks (colour, scale, F at ticks 23 and 60, the arc −31 at tick 30, a 90° spark arcing to +x, 7 trail copies with the older ones at the caster, drawn ticks 0–59); the target's colours at 0/100/199 and the fade; Magic Crasher's colours in order blue/green/red and its ticks; the flicker toggle; Indulge's 15 sparks, F at 29/59/60 and the last drawn tick 63; Soul Change's alpha steps, growth, the two tubes, the float id lookup and being hidden for good; the table rows.

### 3. How do we know nothing regressed?
Soul Strike's ghost is the same code with its old numbers; its trail now starts filled with the caster's feet and the sideways arc goes to the line's right (+x when flying toward −z), as the new sparks require, which mirrors Soul Strike's fan. Left open by the issue: Magic Crasher's colour after tick 60 fades back from its last colour.

author: mherman1990
body:
## What this does

**Step 7 of `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`: a local MCP server for the Claude desktop app.**
- **Server:** `gleaner-mcp/server.mjs` is one file with no dependencies. It speaks stdio JSON-RPC directly and calls Gleaner's `/api` with the token of the computer it runs on, over Tailscale.
- **Tools:**
  - `list_items`, `get_item`, `open_loops`, `get_notes`, `search_notes` and `list_events` read, and are marked read-only.
  - `create_item` adds an item through `POST /api/items`, including `dry_run`.
  - `update_item` closes, drops, reopens, snoozes and edits an item through `POST /api/items/:code`.
- **Output:** every tool returns `structuredContent`, so a Claude artifact can read the result as data.
- **Errors:** come back as readable `isError` results, for example "token refused", "can't reach Gleaner at …", or "item 14 not found".
- **Packaging:** `gleaner-mcp/manifest.json` is an MCPB 0.3 manifest. It asks for the Gleaner URL and the token at install time, and the token field is marked sensitive. `npm run pack:mcpb` builds `gleaner-<version>.mcpb`, which installs with a double-click.
- **Docs:**
  - `gleaner-mcp/README.md` covers install, a `claude_desktop_config.json` fallback, and troubleshooting.
  - `docs/RUNBOOK_v0.2.md` step 7 covers one token per computer: `claude-home` and `claude-work`, with scopes `read,write,create` and sensitivity `all`.
  - The plan and CLAUDE.md are updated.

**Release 0.2.1.** `POST /api/items` (step 3, #12) is merged but isn't in a released image yet, so `create_item` can't work on the Pi until it is.
- This PR sets the version to 0.2.1 in `package.json`, the lockfile and the store listing.
- It writes release notes for creating items and for the extension.
- It links the extension from the README's API section.

## Tests

- `test/mcp.test.js` starts the server against a test Gleaner and checks:
  - the handshake and the tool list;
  - read, create, update and snooze round trips;
  - argument checking;
  - errors for a bad token and an unreachable host;
  - that the manifest's tool list matches the server's;
  - that the packed bundle has `manifest.json` and `server.mjs` at its root.
- `npm test`: 204 pass.

## Needs Matt

- **Tokens:** add one per computer (runbook step 7). Then install `gleaner-1.0.0.mcpb` in the Claude app on each computer and enter the Gleaner URL and that computer's token.
- **Release:** after merge, tag `v0.2.1` so that adding items works on the Pi.
- **Artifact:** the Gleaner Ledger artifact uses this extension. A first live read, and a first tick-off from the artifact, will show whether it needs changes.

author: tmgaminghd
body:
## What this is

The round of 19 Oct 2026: a second-reader review of `core/`, a real FMECA, a repaired and complete mutation run, and documents whose numbers can no longer go stale. Based on `main` after #75 (merged at 17:01 UTC today, after the fix for its CI failure passed); the four commits of this branch were rebased onto the squash commit, whose tree is exactly the one this work was built and verified on.

## 1. The review of `core/` found eight defects (all fixed, each pinned by a test and a mutant)

`docs/verification/CODE_REVIEW_CORE.md` has the method (NASA-STD-8739.9 §7.7 checklist and defect classification), what was and was not read (about 53 % of the flight code line by line; the guidance not at all), and an honest statement of independence: this is a fresh reader of the *same lineage* as the author, not an independent human.

| # | Severity | Finding |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | major | `config_digest` omitted `sensor_split`: an upset in it changed how every frame was judged and the scrub saw nothing |
| 2 | major | **ACT kept its mode in a plain byte.** Safe (2) and Standby (0) are one bit apart, so one upset could end a Safe with no operator. Now guarded by a complement; a mismatch enters Safe with the new cause `integrity` (5) |
| 3 | minor | ACT's configuration was never validated (`persist_m = 0` excluded every computer on frame 1) |
| 4 | clerical | stale comment on `arm_code_` |
| 5 | minor | the IMU channels ignored `strike_window_frames` |
| 6 | major | `FlightLog::push` indexed the ring with an unchecked `head`: a recorder that could corrupt the memory around it |
| 7 | minor | a ground command that found the queue full was dropped *after* its counter was committed |
| 8 | minor | `Supervisor::config_ok()` was never called |

Each was demonstrated on the original code first. Six observations are left as they are with the reason (e.g. an all-zero key falls back to the public bench key: fail-open, an owner's decision).

## 2. The mutation check was not working, and now is

- The scheduled workflow **had never passed**: three runs, each cut at the 6-hour limit (the unit job never finished; the simulator job's "17 survivors" were 17 *stale patterns* reported as "not killed"); about 18 runner-hours a week on a 2,000-minute plan. It is now sharded, monthly and on demand, with `--shard`, `--rerun-survivors` and `--changed-since`.
- On this branch **every simulator mutant failed to build**: `vehicle6.hpp` now includes `../cfd/viscous.hpp` and the harness copied only `sim/vehicle`. Fixed, and tested (`test_mutation_tables.py`).
- 22 simulator patterns were stale (and one name was defined twice): all re-anchored. `tools/mutation/check_tables.py` now fails CI when a pattern stops matching exactly once.
- **17 of 38 core headers had no mutant at all** (the monitors, the MAC, the sensor consensus, ACT's ground path, the logs). About 80 were added.
- Once the mutants worked again they found **18 real gaps in the tests** (7 in the simulator's, 11 in the tests of recent core code): all closed.

**Full runs on the final tree:** core **469/469** killed, simulator **494/494** killed, fault-campaign oracles **77/77** of the mutants they can reach (the other 392 are classified as C++-only, each with its reason). 9 core and 12 simulator headers still carry no mutant (the guidance, navigation, attitude control; the mission code, propulsion model, CFD tables); that is stated, not hidden.

## 3. FMECA (ECSS-Q-ST-30-02C) and a software FMEA (NASA-GB-8719.13 App. D)

`tools/fmeca/` generates `docs/verification/FMECA.md` from data and **fails CI** if a fault-matrix row or a fault kind is left out, a critical item has neither a test nor a recommendation, or `LIMITATIONS.md`'s single points are not in the analysis. 49 failure modes, 32 critical items, 10 single points, 6 critical items with no compensation, an HSIA table, and a software FMEA with 4 gaps (REC-18, REC-19). New fault-matrix rows F99 to F103. Ratings are one person's judgement (stated).

## 4. Documents

- `tools/docs/metrics.py`: every number a current page quotes is a computed or recorded marker; CI fails when one is stale. It found, on day one, a stale `11,300 scenarios` that my own survey missed. (Status page said 801 tests when there were 877, 34 decisions when there were 58.)
- `STATUS.md` and `README.md` rewritten as short dashboards; the dated measurements (nothing lost) moved to `docs/verification/RESULTS.md`. New `CODE_REVIEW_CORE.md`, `FMECA.md`, risks R19 to R23, `FUTURE_WORK.md` 6d.
- **`P-S1-02`**: a fault-free soak and the IMUs' Allan deviation, with `tools/bench/allan.py` and `soak_report.py` (exact Poisson bound; 300 hours with none demonstrates one false isolation per 100 hours at 95 %), requirement FDIR-047, tested on synthetic records.

## Verified locally on the final tree

896 C++ tests under ASan/UBSan, 650 Python tests (42 skipped: need `vcan0`), flight-code coverage 100.0 % lines / 98.2 % branches (gates 100/98) and simulator 99.1 / 90.1, clang-tidy and cppcheck clean, `check_standard`, the trace gate (tightened 19 to 17), the full fault campaign (12,362 scenarios, no anomaly; the generated tables are byte-identical), the nine mission steps.

## Not verified here (CI will)

The two Zephyr firmware changes (`firmware/act`, `firmware/supervisor`: the cause text and the `config_ok()` check at boot) and the Zephyr builds; I have no SDK on this machine. Nothing here has run on a board.

## Owed

An outside human reader for `core/`; mutants for the guidance and mission code; the detectors' parameters into the scrub (REC-09); the soak and noise run on the rig.

author: jacobotoll
body:
## TL;DR

New: Work Items are durable owner-scoped to-dos or tickets in an active User-owned Project. The API supports creation, paged reads, explicit User actions, versioned edits and to-do deletion, with personal realtime notifications.

## Changes

- Add migration 0049 and a Project/owner-constrained Work Item table with calendar due dates, optimistic versions and immutable creation idempotency, including hidden deletion tombstones. Exact delayed creation replay after deletion returns `410`; payload drift returns `409` with `current: null`.
- Validate public contracts and accept only existing browser/session or personal-collaboration device authority. Personal API Tokens cannot authorize Work Item operations; Team-linked Projects remain unavailable on the Personal path.
- Keep automatic execution and PR transitions behind an internal trusted evidence adapter that is unavailable by default. Persist allowed state transitions atomically with current owner, active Project, version and exact execution/PR binding checks.
- Append owner-only realtime events in the same transaction; reauthorize current records at delivery through both the direct API and Desktop-facing local-edge broker. Preserve the strict remote Personal envelope and its existing operation-family binding; Team streams cannot deliver these records. Deletion requests a resync and re-list instead of delivering stale content.
- Page deterministically by exact PostgreSQL timestamp and ID, with an owner/Project-bound cursor and explicit continuation metadata.

## Related Issues

HQ-401 — Work Items: schema, API, realtime. Depends on merged HQ-201.

### Acceptance

- [x] Define storage, strict public contracts, owner-scoped CRUD and `409` conflicts containing the current record.
- [x] Enforce the section 6.5 state table in the server repository; cover legal and illegal persisted transitions.
- [x] A closed-unmerged PR becomes blocked, never automatically done (N9). Explicit User completion remains permitted.
- [x] Emit personal `work_item_changed` transactionally and reauthorize the current owner/active Project before delivery.
- [x] Preserve dispatch/source-line idempotency foundations; reject payload drift on an existing creation identity.
- [ ] Actual runtime dispatch/provider adapters and their UI remain with HQ-404/HQ-405 and later ticket owners; this PR exposes no public event-forging path and does not claim the compound walkthroughs pass yet.
- [ ] Durable Project activity rows remain with HQ-206; the committed documentation states that dependency boundary.

## Type of Change

- [x] Feature
- [x] Documentation

## Validation

- Full workspace `pnpm build`, production and test typechecks, formatting, lint, environment example and ADR checks pass. The final fixture-only update also passes affected ESLint/Prettier and the full test typecheck.
- Expanded DB run: all 682 test cases passed, with 31 existing conditional skips. The unchanged Team authority suite had one local DROP-database cleanup hook timeout under cluster DDL load; its complete 12-case suite subsequently passes in isolation, including cleanup. No timeout, assertion or coverage was weakened.
- Shared Memory full-file proof: 106/106 passed. EXPLAIN identified stale synthetic fixture statistics causing an authorization lookup to examine nearly 15 million policy combinations; the same eligible-row lookup uses indexes after statistics refresh. The test refreshes those statistics before its original global pending claim and embedding writes, retaining global queue, revocation, zero-decryption and unchanged time-budget assertions. Existing frozen embedding tests now explicitly assert exact Team chunk decrypt counts.
- Full API: 1,286 passed, 25 existing conditional skips, and the same six preexisting local terminal checkout-identity failures reproduced on the baseline. Before: after every merge Jon had to download Solace-macos.zip, unzip it and click through a Gatekeeper warning to play the newest build.

body:
## 目的
Python 3.10 から Azure App Service で GA 提供される **Python 3.14** へ更新し、Requests の既知の脆弱性を最新安定版で修正する。Python 3.15 は 2026-10-20 時点の Azure App Service ではプレビューのため採用しない。

## 変更
- `.python-version` を追加: `3.14`
- `requirements.txt`: `requests==2.31.0` → **`2.34.2`**、`numpy==1.22.0` → **`2.5.4`**（Python 3.14 に対応するビルド済み wheel が提供される版）
- テスト用 workflow の Python を `3.14` に統一
- Azure デプロイ用 workflow の setup-python と appservice-build を `3.14` に統一
- Python 3.14 / NumPy 2.x の実行機能を検出する POST スモークテストを追加
- README に Azure App Service の本番実行ランタイム移行手順を明記

## 確認済み
- [x] Python 3.14 は Azure App Service for Linux で正式提供
- [x] Requests 2.34.2 と NumPy 2.5.4 の PyPI メタデータで Python 3.14 対応を確認
- [x] GitHub 上で変更ファイルを再取得し、設定の一致を静的検査した（8項目成功）
- [x] `master` との差分ファイル一覧を確認
- [x] セキュリティ対象である `requests` の脆弱版指定は変更後ファイルに存在しない

## **マージ前に必要な確認（未完了）**
- [ ] **High: Azure App Service 実行ランタイムの切り替え・確認。** GitHub Actions の `platform-version` を変更しても Azure 本番サイトの `linuxFxVersion` は変更されません。これを `PYTHON|3.14` にするまでは、3.14 向けのビルド成果物と本番実行環境が食い違う可能性があります。Azure 管理アクセスがなく現在値を確認・変更できていません。README に検証・変更コマンドを記載しました。
- [ ] **High: Python 3.14 で依存関係をインストールし、`python -m unittest discover -s tests -v` を実行。** 現在の実行環境は Python 3.13 しかなく、外部ネットワークにアクセスできないため、3.14 の実インストール／スモークテストは未実行です。
- [ ] Azure にデプロイした際のヘルスチェック・主要機能の確認（未実施）
- [ ] 既存の古い依存ライブラリ（`janome==0.3.10` 等）の Python 3.14 互換性は実機で未確認

## 運用
- 現時点は Draft のまま。上記 High 項目を解消するまで 95/100 以上の品質合格判定は行いません。
- CI は壊れているため検証の根拠にしません。GitHub Actions の手動起動・再実行は行っていません。
- GitHub リポジトリの自動マージ設定は `allow_auto_merge=false` のため、自動マージを有効化できません。
- Azure 本番ランタイムを移行できるアクセスがないため、現時点では手動の即時マージも控えています（本番障害回避）。

author: omaribannez
body:
## Summary

Implements SP-03a task D2 of `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-19-sp03a-list-catalog.md`: the shared source catalog and its seed, the fetcher port and HTTP adapter, `xolotl lists seed` and `xolotl lists status` (spec §6.1, §6.2 step 2, §13).

- `src/xolotl/modules/screening/sources.yaml`: the five shared sources (`UN_CONSOLIDATED`, `OFAC_SDN`, `EU_FSF`, `UK_FCDO`, `MX_SAT_69B`) with intervals PT15M, PT30M, PT1H, PT1H, P1D. Each URL is the one the library's fixture README records; `url_checked_on` is that README's retrieval date (2026-10-19).
- `catalog/sources.py`: `SOURCES_FILE`, `SourceSpec`, `SeedReport`, `read_sources` (422 `VALIDATION_FAILED` on a missing or malformed file, an unknown field or a duplicate code), `seed_list_sources` (owner session; upserts the catalog columns by code, writes only changed columns, never the operational ones; a code that leaves the file is disabled, not deleted).
- `catalog/fetcher.py`: `FetchResult`, `ListFetchError` (`code` plus `"<code>: <short reason>"`, never the body), the `ListFetcher` protocol and `HttpListFetcher` (conditional headers, redirects, timeout, size cap on `Content-Length` and while streaming, SHA-256).
- `cli.py`: `lists_app` with `seed [path]` and `status`; `db upgrade` and `serve` seed right after `migrate.upgrade()` (Deviation 9); `db upgrade` prints the seed line, `serve` logs it.
- `tests/modules/screening/catalog/support.py`: `seed_sources(admin_engine)`.

### Decisions
- `SourceSpec` is `frozen=True, extra="forbid"` but not pydantic `strict=True`: strict mode refuses the YAML's strings for the enums and the ISO-8601 durations. Field patterns guard `code` and `jurisdiction`.
- The YAML is a top-level `sources:` list.
- The OFAC URL is the README's export base plus the file name it records (`SDN_ENHANCED.XML`); the SAT URL stays `http://` as the README and the library record it.
- `SeedReport.disabled` counts rows newly disabled by this seed; a row already disabled is not counted. A disabled code that comes back to the file is re-enabled and counted as `updated`.
- `lists status` with no rows prints `no list sources; run xolotl lists seed`. `failing` (consecutive failures > 0) takes precedence over `stale`; it shows the part of `last_error` before the colon. `next` shows the time alone when it is today (UTC), the date and time otherwise.

## Test plan
- `uv run pytest tests/modules/screening/catalog/test_sources.py tests/modules/screening/catalog/test_fetcher.py tests/test_cli.py --no-cov -q`: the catalog file, the seed's idempotency, URL update with the operational columns kept, disabling, the app role refused (`permission denied`), the fetcher against `respx` (200, 304 with conditional headers, redirects, the cap with and without `Content-Length`, error codes, no body in messages), and the CLI commands.
- `make lint`, `make types`, `make vulture`, `make importlint`, `make ci`.

author: explorrrr
body:
## Summary

GitHub Release notes for every tag currently contain the entire cumulative `CHANGELOG.md`, because the release workflow passes the whole file to `gh release create --notes-file`. For example, v2.3.0's body contains 1.0.0 through 2.3.0.

This PR:

- adds `scripts/release-notes.mjs` to extract only the `## [<version>]` section (excluding `[Unreleased]`);
- uses the extracted file for the GitHub Release body and updates an existing Release with `gh release edit`;
- rejects duplicate version headings and stops at trailing link definitions or later H2 sections;
- adds `scripts/check-release-notes.mjs` to cover all eight versions, the CLI and failure paths from `pnpm check`, so extraction is verified before npm publish;
- documents the behavior in `docs/VERSIONING.md`.

The release itself is intentionally out of scope; this takes effect on the next tag.

## Out of scope

- Backfilling the existing v1.0.0–v2.3.0 Release bodies.
- Publishing a Release that already exists as a draft; the workflow keeps the previous draft/prerelease state.

## Self-review (solo maintainer)

- [x] I read the complete `git diff main...HEAD`.
- [x] `pnpm verify` passes.
- [x] N/A — no security behavior or security regression test is involved.
- [x] No secret, runtime dependency or lifecycle script was added.
- [x] README/CHANGELOG are unchanged because this is release tooling; `docs/VERSIONING.md` records the new behavior.
- [x] Rollback: revert this PR; it only changes the source of the Release notes.

## Security checklist

- [x] No secret, token or API key is added to the repository or logs.
- [x] No new runtime dependency, or its license/install scripts were reviewed. (No dependency added.)
- [x] No `preinstall`/`install`/`postinstall`/`prepare` script was added.
- [x] Host endpoint handling, response caps, client bundle and updater code are untouched.
- [x] The extraction script only reads `CHANGELOG.md` and writes stdout; the check script spawns Node with fixed arguments and no shell. Neither performs network access or filesystem writes.
- [x] `scripts/check-release-notes.mjs` runs from `pnpm check` and covers the changed behavior, including missing/empty/duplicate sections, partial versions, trailing link definitions, H2 footers, CRLF, and the CLI.

## Testing

- `pnpm verify` — typecheck, build, 139 tests and `pnpm check` all pass.
- `node scripts/check-release-notes.mjs` — 8 existing versions, CLI output and fixtures pass.
- `actionlint .github/workflows/release.yml` — pass.
- `node scripts/release-notes.mjs 2.3.0` — only the 2.3.0 section.
- All tags v1.0.0–v2.3.0 — exactly one `## [` heading per output.
- Missing, empty and partial version arguments — exit 1.
- Mocked `gh` — `release create`, `release edit` and `--prerelease` paths.

> **Autoria:** PR aberta por **Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5)** em 19/10/2026, em nome do operador.

Refs LCV-421 · Relacionada: LCV-Ideas-Software/astrologo-android#47 (ASTANDR-11)

## Por quê

Na verificação da marca OAuth do projeto `lcv-ideas-and-software`, o item "Requisitos da política de privacidade" foi reprovado em 19/10/2026: "Sua página de política de privacidade não tem conteúdo suficiente… Please update your privacy policy to clearly and sufficiently detail your app's data collection and usage, then retry."

A [answer 13806988](https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/13806988) do Google pede que a política descreva os dados de usuário do Google que o app acessa: uso, armazenamento, transferência, proteção, retenção e exclusão, além de declarar o Uso Limitado. A [answer 13807376](https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/13807376) pede que a página inicial descreva o app e o motivo de pedir dados do usuário.

## O que muda

1. **Política 1.9**, em vigor a partir de 19/10/2026, com a nova subseção **11.1**, "Dados de usuário do Google no aplicativo Oráculo Celestial" (âncora `#google-user-data`). Ela tem um parágrafo para cada item exigido e a declaração de Uso Limitado com link para a política oficial do Google. As demais seções não mudam.
2. O **arquivo** da 1.8 fica sem mudança de texto em `/privacy/1.8/`, com o aviso de versão arquivada, como nas versões anteriores. A lista de versões anteriores ganha a 1.8.
3. O **cartão da página inicial** passa de "Astrólogo Android · v0.2.0 · ainda não há… análise por IA" para "Oráculo Celestial · v0.3.7 · Teste Interno". O texto explica que o login Google existe só para a análise paga e aponta para a 11.1. O cartão não leva link de loja.

## Fatos que sustentam o texto

- Login: o app pede só o login básico do Google (`openid`, `email`, `profile`), via Credential Manager.
- Armazenamento: o Firebase Authentication guarda e-mail, nome e foto da conta de acesso. O backend grava só o SHA-256 do identificador.
- Provedor de IA: as requisições ao provedor não levam identificador, e-mail nem metadado da conta.
- Exclusão: o app tem "Excluir conta de acesso".
- O texto novo não usa "coleta" nem "compartilha". A varredura do texto inteiro não encontrou nenhuma afirmação de que a LCV coleta ou compartilha dados. As ocorrências de "compartilh…" são frases já aprovadas, sobre ações do próprio usuário.

## Verificação

- `npm test` verde e `prettier --check` verde nas duas ilhas.
- O `site/` está idêntico byte a byte nas PRs gêmeas, com o mesmo manifesto.
- Conferi a página renderizada: a subseção 11.1 e o cartão novo.

body:
# Configured header string reads

Baseline: `10701f166ae500214641484e283b2c4c96701ba5`.
Runtime: Go 1.27.2, darwin/arm64, Apple M4 Pro, `-cpu=1`.

This phase removes repeated owned-string allocations when `GetString` reads
exactly a configured session identity. It preserves the public owned-string
contract and actual field lookup. It does not intern arbitrary incoming strings
or change message routing, wire encoding, validation or application ownership.

## Ownership and limits

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Session construction copies immutable SessionID strings] --> B[One immutable field metadata object]
    B --> C[Inbound and replay parse slots]
    B --> D[Control and caller-owned output messages]
    C --> E[Actual field lookup]
    D --> E
    E -->|missing| F[Existing dictionary reject or unknown-tag fallback]
    E -->|exact configured identity bytes| G[Return immutable configured string]
    E -->|different bytes or other tag| H[Create ordinary owned string]
    G --> I[Caller may retain string after callback and session retirement]
    H --> I
```

Only tags 8, 49, 50, 56, 57, 142 and 143 are eligible. Sender/target pairs
recognize both inbound and outbound directions by exact byte equality. Missing
fields remain missing, including empty configured optional identities. Different
CompIDs, per-message SubIDs and standalone messages keep ordinary owned-string
behavior. The metadata contains the immutable dictionary reject map and seven
immutable string values, with no session, message, frame or output-slot pointer.
Each session creates its own object; traffic never adds values or changes it.
This adds one metadata allocation during session setup (and for dictionary-backed
public slots). It reuses the existing immutable strings rather than copying their
bytes, and replaces the old map handle without enlarging `FieldMap`.

Copies, owned inbound materialization, arena attachment/detachment and slot reset
preserve the appropriate metadata reference. Sending a caller-owned message
through another session rebinds that message to the destination session's object;
previously returned strings and copied messages remain independent. No new hot
mutex, pool, mutable intern table or unsafe byte/string alias is introduced.

## Frozen measurements

`session_header_strings_benchmark_test.go` SHA-256:
`e5ce92a676815d27eb339c40ca40f4ba7f32be869ac43e84e3e9f93aaebdd7c8`.
The companion semantic fixtures passed against unchanged production source before
measurement. The benchmark source is unchanged between before and after captures.

```sh
GOTOOLCHAIN=auto rtk proxy go test . -run '^$' -bench '^BenchmarkAllocationBaseline$' -benchmem -benchtime=1s -count=5 -cpu=1
GOTOOLCHAIN=auto rtk proxy go test . -run '^$' -bench '^Benchmark(SessionHeaderString(Read|Heartbeat)|PreparedMissingField|PreparedRejectHeartbeat|SessionRequiredValidation|SessionRequiredReject)$' -benchmem -benchtime=1s -count=5 -cpu=1
```

Setup, dictionary construction, parsing and warm-up are outside the timed loops.
Getter results escape into package-level string sinks. The completed-heartbeat
component performs three real header string reads inside each callback, persists
to the bounded journal, encodes, completes the writer copy, returns its output
slot, validates the independent peer frame and retires the acknowledged journal
entry. It is not a network or whole FIX-server latency benchmark. Existing
missing-field and required-validation benchmark rows are preserved as controls.

## Results

Five samples per row. Times below are medians; allocation counts and bytes are
identical across all five samples for each before/after row.

| Getter/component | Before ns/op | After ns/op | Before B/op / allocs/op | After B/op / allocs/op |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Configured inbound sender | 21.53 | 10.79 | 24 / 1 | 0 / 0 |
| Configured inbound target | 21.31 | 10.40 | 24 / 1 | 0 / 0 |
| Configured outbound sender | 21.41 | 10.60 | 24 / 1 | 0 / 0 |
| Configured outbound target | 21.58 | 10.43 | 24 / 1 | 0 / 0 |
| Different inbound sender | 21.38 | 22.29 | 24 / 1 | 24 / 1 |
| Per-message inbound SubID | 21.27 | 22.14 | 24 / 1 | 24 / 1 |
| Standalone sender | 21.37 | 22.22 | 24 / 1 | 24 / 1 |
| Completed heartbeat with three callback identity reads | 2,006 | 1,971 | 16 / 3 | 0 / 0 |

Matched getter timing roughly halves in this component. The completed heartbeat
removes three allocations; its small timing difference is not a claim about
network or deployed latency. Nonmatching/standalone getter medians increase by
about 0.9 ns and retain the existing owned-copy allocation. Raw results are in
`header-before.txt` and `header-after.txt`.

Configured missing-field errors (including two text reads), completed heartbeat
reject-getter controls, valid/missing-Side validation and completed required-field
rejects remain 0 B/op and 0 allocs/op. The unknown-tag missing-field fallback
remains 72 B/op and 2 allocs/op, with or without repeated Error calls.

The mandatory allocation baseline preserves every allocation row in all samples:
non-overflow decimal parsing, reused parsing with/without dictionaries/groups and
valid NewOrderSingle validation remain 0 B/op and 0 allocs/op. Decimal overflow
remains 168 B/op and 5 allocs/op; legacy construction remains 144 B/op and
5 allocs/op; legacy framed reads remain 160 B/op and 2 allocs/op. See
`allocation-before.txt` and `allocation-after.txt`. No whole-library
zero-allocation claim is made.

## Qualification

Semantic fixtures cover all seven identity tags in both directions, missing and
nonmatching values, mutable input overwrite, owned copies/materialization,
detachment, slot reset and cross-session caller-message reuse. Performance and
race testing are separate. The package suite excludes only the previously
documented unrelated `TestMongoLogTestSuite` teardown failure; Mongo store tests
remain enabled.

Final qualification passed on the frozen production source:

```sh
GOTOOLCHAIN=auto rtk proxy go test ./... -skip '^TestMongoLogTestSuite$' -count=1 -timeout=180s
GOTOOLCHAIN=auto rtk proxy go vet ./...
GOTOOLCHAIN=auto rtk proxy go test -race . ./internal/... -count=1 -timeout=180s
```

Receipts are `correctness-all.txt` and `race-core-internal.txt`; vet exited
successfully without output. The new allocation regression checks all seven
matching identity reads after owned materialization, CopyInto and arena
detachment. Metadata-isolation tests share dictionary errors across distinct
session identities and use separately owned messages for concurrent readers.

author: rogeriojorge
body:
## Problem
With the new default `wall_closure = "bohm"` the HSX blob run crashes ("invalid imex-ssp222 stage", or NaN in `eig`) a little after t = 0.1. Reproduced on the 16-cubed geometry with the default deck (dt = 7.5e-4, amplitude 0.05, rho* = 5e-4): the 800-step run to t = 0.6 fails at step 229 (t = 0.1717) with an unaccepted phi inversion. The 200-step documented run still completes. `zero-flow` is unaffected.

## Cause
The Bohm entrance state took Te and Ti from the wall-endpoint trace. In cut cells that trace is interpolated from hotter neighbours (for example Te_w = 0.44 and 0.26 against an owner Te of 0.08). The wall leg then removed energy at the neighbours' temperature, `gamma n_w Te_w c_s`, from a cell that has no heat supply (parallel conduction is off by default). Wall-bounded cells cooled steadily toward zero (Te about 1 to 0.07 by t = 0.17). At Te about 0.069 the Te jump across the cell makes the curvature face flux jump from 0.05 to about 3e3 in the vorticity row, the next stage's phi solve returns phi = -99, and Ve reaches -400.

## Fix
`bohm_wall_state` limits the entrance Te and Ti to the owner values (`min(trace, owner)`). Two lines, sheath path only.

## Evidence (16-cubed HSX, default deck)
- The old failure step (229, t = 0.1717) is passed; the run now fails later, at step 554 (t = 0.4155). **The default run to t = 0.6 is not yet finite**, see below.
- zero-flow path bitwise unchanged: `scripts/fci_gate.py record` on main vs this branch with `wall_closure = "zero-flow"`, `compare` reports `GATE PASS (bitwise)`.
- `pytest -n 2 -m "not slow" tests/fci_braginskii`: 429 passed, 10 skipped.
- Slow wall-closure and recycling tests pass, including the 1D flux-tube analytic checks.
- New tests: a unit test of the limiter, and a slow HSX test that builds the 16-cubed geometry from the deck [geometry] table (cached) and runs the default deck to t = 0.18, past the old failure.
- Wall ledger imbalances stay at 1e-12 to 1e-13 per step, as before.

## Remaining failure at t = 0.4155 and what removes it
A grid-scale Ve sawtooth (about +3, -4, +3 along b) grows in interior cells with a hot/cold Te pair beside it (Te 2.8 next to about 0). The parallel terms are all off by default: `parallel_diffusion = 0` (which feeds Te/Ti conduction, Ve and Vi viscosity, density and vorticity diffusion together) and `electron_collision_frequency = 0`.

Default deck, 16-cubed, 800 steps to t = 0.6, with this branch's limiter. All other keys default.

| Case | Result | Min Te / max abs Ve at end | Ledger (particle, Ee, Ei, rel. to max wall step) |
|---|---|---|---|
| main (before fix) | fails step 229 (t=0.172) | - | - |
| limiter only | fails step 554 (t=0.416) | - | - |
| limiter + `electron_collision_frequency=0.04` | fails step 598 (t=0.449) | - | - |
| limiter + `parallel_diffusion=0.1` | fails step 649 (t=0.487) | - | - |
| limiter + `parallel_diffusion=0.3` | finite to t=0.6, but Ve and Te max still growing | 0.24 / 4.5 | 1.7e-12, 7e-13, 1.5e-12 |
| limiter + `parallel_diffusion=1.0` | finite to t=0.6 | 0.37 / 1.2 | 1.7e-12, 6e-13, 1.2e-12 |
| `parallel_diffusion=1.0` on Te and Ti conduction only | finite to t=0.6 (density drains to 0.1) | 0.38 / 1.2 | 1.8e-12, 7e-13, 1.1e-12 |
| `parallel_diffusion=1.0` on Ve viscosity only | fails step 573 (t=0.43) | - | - |

So the sawtooth is not cured by Ve dissipation or friction; Te/Ti parallel conduction is what suppresses it, as expected for a sheath-bounded run whose wall cells need heat supplied along b. I did not change any default.

How a physical value compares: Spitzer-Harm chi_par,e is about 3.6e6 m^2/s at Te = 24 eV, n = 1e19 m^-3 (lnLambda = 15), which is about 75 in c_s0 L_ref units (c_s0 about 4.8e4 m/s, L_ref = 1 m, see the Normalization section of the HSX doc). The conduction term is explicit, so dt * chi / dx^2 must stay below about 0.5; with the shortest wall leg dx = 0.069 and dt = 7.5e-4 that caps chi at about 3. The physical value therefore needs an implicit conduction solve, which does not exist yet; `parallel_diffusion = 1.0` is a stable stand-in, not a physical value. `electron_collision_frequency = 0.04` is the Spitzer rate (about 77 cs/L_ref) divided by mi/me, assuming the code's `mi_over_me * Ve_nu * n (Vi - Ve)` friction form; I did not check that normalization independently.

Not done: 32-cubed (no cached geometry; the build takes hours). Zero-flow bitwise check was run before the final test-only commit; the source change is unchanged since.

author: rmartz
body:
Adds an optional `alias-domain` input to `vercel-preview.yml`. When it is set, each successful UAT deploy runs `vercel alias set <preview-url> <alias-domain>`, so a consumer gets one stable hostname for whatever is in UAT now. Allowlists (OAuth redirect URIs, Firebase authorized domains) can then name that host instead of all of `vercel.app`.

- New input `alias-domain` (default `''`). When it is unset, both new steps are skipped and nothing changes.
- A new early step checks that the value is a bare hostname, right after the secrets check. A bad value fails in seconds, before the build. The alias step after the deploy passes the token only through `--token="$VERCEL_TOKEN"`, the same way `vercel pull` and `vercel deploy` do. Both steps read the input through `env:`.
- New workflow output `alias-url`, now listed in the public surface in `AGENTS.md`. The alias URL also appears in the job summary and the sticky comment, which says that this PR now holds the alias.
- The last PR deployed holds the alias. Removing the UAT label leaves the alias pointing at that PR's last preview, matching how the preview itself behaves today (#4). This is documented in `docs/consuming.md` and `docs/gating.md`.
- Per-PR hostname templating is left for a follow-up, as the issue allows.

**Reuse/extend/new:** this extends the existing deploy job and sticky-comment step. It reuses the CLI install, the `.vercel/project.json` scope from `vercel pull`, the `--token` pattern, and the fail-fast style of the secrets check. There is no parallel mechanism.

**Acceptance criteria:**

1. `alias-domain` is documented in the README and `docs/consuming.md`, and there is no behaviour change when it is unset. ✅
2. The alias step uses the deploy's token handling. ✅
3. The PR comment and job summary include the alias URL. ✅
4. Tests cover the input wiring, and they test the hostname pattern itself against accepted and rejected values (`test/vercel-preview-workflow.test.ts`). ✅

Not yet verified against a live Vercel project. The first consumer is rmartz/personal-budget#505.

Closes #8

author: breferrari
body:
## State

Ready for the proof packet. Head b313d57: the feature, the review fixes, a merge of main with #676, and the mutation tests. Known limits are below.

## Summary

An image stored with Git LFS redraws when `git lfs fetch` brings its content, with no edit to the file. Closes #639.

- **The store wakes the pane.** A write under the LFS store's `objects` ticks as a git-dir change that names no file, wherever the store is. `tmp` and the rest of the store wake nothing. A store inside the worktree is already under its recursive watch. One outside it (a linked worktree's common dir, or `lfs.storage` elsewhere) gets its own recursive watch, or, before it exists, a watch on its nearest existing ancestor until it appears.
- **A diff drawn without its object is read again once it lands.** The frame keeps the missing object's path with the diff and its height, and `provenance` treats the diff as moved once that path is a file: one `stat` per missing object, nothing for any other file.
- **Only a repository that uses LFS watches an outside store**: an attributes file git itself reads names `filter=lfs`. That means a tracked `.gitattributes` at any depth, `info/attributes`, the user's file or the system's. A write to `info/attributes` or a non-ignored `.gitattributes` re-checks.
- **The store's watch arms on its own thread** with its own OS watcher, since a macOS watch restarts its event stream. A finished watch on `objects` ticks once, as an object may have landed while it armed.
- **The store's watch fails soft.** If it cannot be armed (a full inotify table, or anything else), the main watch is kept and the footer says once: "LFS images redraw on the next change, not when their objects arrive: <reason>".
- The scene bed gains `lfs/missing.png`, drawn `binary` in `static`, whose object `replay` lands.

Plan: https://github.com/breferrari/vigia/issues/639#issuecomment-6280729362

## Test plan

- Reviews:
  - /simplify on 684784d, fixes in e2050ef.
  - /two-axis-review on e2050ef, fixes in a7f5ce8.
  - /code-review high on a7f5ce8, fixes in 9b4824a.
  - Post-review /code-review on a7f5ce8..c37e83e. Its 10 findings are fixed in b2a7ecb; the largest is an object that lands while the store arms.
- CI with #676's tooling: run 39407534090 (this branch merged with #676) was green on test and budgets for ubuntu, macOS and Windows. `lfs_ancestor_released` took 0.47s on macOS, 0.14s on ubuntu and 0.76s on Windows.
- Release budgets on b313d57: `budgets` 37/37, `vigia-core` budgets 30/30, `first_paint` 8/8. The full suite runs in CI on ready; local full runs were skipped because another session's batteries were using the same machine.
- Mutation, killed on the final code:
  - `mutate.mjs`: arm on watch thread, arrival does not tick, ignored attributes count, user attributes ignored, stale ancestor kept, comment counts, filtered not negated, filtered multiplied, io arm deleted, ancestor spelling none, canonical not pushed, info not matched, any word is lfs, no states, arrived always, arrived never, arrival probe uncounted, arrival guard always, awaited probes dropped, ancestor on any event, watch never spawned.
  - Earlier, on code the later fixes did not touch: store write not relevant, notice repeats, limit reason lost, no ancestor spelling, missing object not recorded.
  - cargo-mutants (CI dry runs 39407534090 and 39410739731) found 10 missed mutants. Each is killed above by a new test, or its code is gone: the seed arithmetic in `scene.rs` is now a constant.
- Deleted rather than killed:
  - The `awaiting` dedupe in `worktree.rs`.
  - The span walk's arrival check in `frame.rs`. An arriving object fills only an image side, whose span is `binary` before and after, so that check could never change a height. `diff` reads the picture again.

Debt: filed 1, #674 (fail the flake-rate workflow when its filter matches no test), found while measuring this PR.

## Known limits

- **Mutants not killed.** All four are in the shell's watch thread or `run`. They were cut by the PR's time-box:
  - `lib.rs` spawn_watch `if !told` inverted (first notice ends watch): unrun.
  - `|| !told` changed to `&& !told` (notice decides ticks): unrun. It differs only once the shell is gone, when the thread keeps waiting instead of exiting.
  - `|| !told` changed to `|| told` (told ignored): unrun.
  - `run` returning `Ok(())` (run does nothing): unrun. That function predates this PR and is in the diff only because a line in it moved.
- **A pre-existing stress flake.** `a_burst_of_writes_becomes_one_tick` failed once in three concurrent full-suite runs. An A/B against main under the same load gave 0 of 30 failures on main and 0 of 30 on this branch, so it predates this PR.
- **Store edge cases.** A store deleted and recreated while the pane is open is not re-armed. An object copied into `objects` without a rename can tick before it is complete; git-lfs always renames.
- **A watch that cannot be armed.** On Linux, a full inotify table, or anything else that stops the store's watch arming, falls back to the next ordinary event, with a one-time footer notice.

## Release note

Release-note: An image stored with Git LFS redraws when `git lfs fetch` brings its content, with no edit to the file.

author: futrime
body:
## FINAL-FIX-AGENT-A (3): fixes from the code review of #34

Fixes from two code-review passes over the agent core. Only files FINAL-FIX-AGENT-A owns are changed:
`packages/agent/src/**` (not portal/nether/end), `scenarios/overworld/final-chain.js`, the agent README and the agent
tests.

### Meals
- **Counted holds.** Auto-eat is held off through counted holds (`Safety#suppressMeals`). Fights, pillar steps,
  placements and the pause after failing meals each take one, and auto-eat comes back only when the last hold is
  released. Before, a fight that ended while a placement was still going switched auto-eat back on.
- **Failed meals are reported.** Auto-eat's `strictErrors` throws instead of emitting `'eatFail'`, so the pause after
  3 failed meals never fired. `guardAutoEat` now emits `'eatFail'` for a meal that began and failed.
  - It arrives after that meal's `'eatFinish'`, so `hunt` takes back a meal it had counted as collected meat.
  - The pause only counts automatic meals.
  - The pause ends when the agent stops (its timer is unref'd).
- **No meals mid-fight setup.** A fight takes its hold before it equips its weapon.
- **`eatNow` skips** while a safety behaviour has the controls.
- **Auto-eat's flag.** The guard resets auto-eat's "eating" flag only when the failure left it set.

### Mining and ores
- **The ore watcher counts only the ores the bot digs.** It checks `bot.targetDigBlock`, or a dig aborted within
  the last 2 s. It is the first `blockUpdate` listener, because the pathfinder's listener completes the dig and clears
  the target. Before, any ore that changed within 7 blocks of a recent dig counted, including one blown up by a
  creeper. A throwing event handler can no longer break the world's update dispatch.
- **Lost drops.** "Three digs without a drop, leave the spot" applies only to blocks that always drop the item
  (yield ≥ 1) and never to filler.
- **Interruptions.** The interruption count starts over after every successful dig.

### Creepers
- A creeper within 5 blocks is fought even when it was given up on before (it had been 3 blocks). The exception ends
  after it was given up on twice; that count starts over once 3 minutes pass since the last give-up.
- When fleeing a creeper gains less than 3 blocks (cornered by a ledge, lava or a wall), the bot fights it for the
  next 15 s instead of fleeing again.

### Climbs and suffocation (found by the validation runs)
- **Climbs step aside under gravel.** When gravel or sand sits over the cell above the head, the climb moves to a
  neighbouring column (dry above, ground under it) and goes up there. Digging straight up under gravel dropped it on
  the bot ("suffocated in a wall" twice).
- **No fight while suffocating.** Air going down out of the water while being hurt means the server has a block in
  the bot's head that the client does not show yet. Then no fight starts, and a running fight stops for it (and for
  a full block in the head cell); the climb gets out.

### Fishing, inventory and chain
- **Cobwebs.** The web is out of the planner's natural sources again. Fishing cuts the webs in sight itself, with a
  sword: it makes a wooden one if none is carried, because shears would keep the web whole.
- **Late declutter** keeps 8 raw iron and 32 cobbled deepslate.
- **Gear phase.** It makes sure of an iron ingot for N1M3's flint and steel, unless a flint and steel is already
  carried.

### Validation (BDS 1.26.51.1, seed 1234, easy)
| code | gates | final chain |
|---|---|---|
| a7b8254 (first review round) | M3 5/5 (106, 89, 99, 107, 89 s), M5 5/5 (366, 270, 262, 297, 393 s) | f1 PASS 35.1 min; f2 ✗ M3 (details below) |
| eb634f2 (second review round) | — | f3 PASS 41.8, f4 ✗ M5 (details below), f5 PASS 38.0 |
| 2709ffd (climbs wait for falling gravel to land) | M4 run 1: 4 deaths, first one suffocating in M4's gravel column | (stopped: reverted) |
| 1c93e82 (climbs step over to the next column under gravel) | M4 5/5 (247, 181, 178, 184, 193 s), no deaths | f8 PASS 41.7, f9 PASS 47.8, f10 PASS 36.8 — no deaths |
| **9536847 (final, after the review of the climb change)** | **M4 5/5 (180, 192, 187, 219, 187 s), no deaths** | **f11 PASS 36.2, f12 PASS 43.8, f13 PASS 39.4 — no deaths** |

Failures before the climb change:
- **f2:** the shaft down opened into a cave with zombies and a skeleton, and the bot died there. On the way back it
  climbed under gravel and suffocated.
- **f4:** the bot climbed under gravel and suffocated in M4. Unarmored at night, a creeper then killed it, and M5 timed
  out.

Neither failure came from the review fixes themselves. Climbing straight up into gravel was always a hazard; the
earlier code had survived M4's gravel column only through timing ("Server refused to place dirt … still gravel").
From M4's snapshot, every climb starts under that column. With the side step, the bot steps over to the next column
twice and reaches the surface in ~80 s.

author: jed-4
body:
> **Stacked on #274** — it shares `TakeoffPlanViewer.tsx`, so this targets that branch rather than `main`. Merge #274 first and this retargets cleanly.

## Zoom

There was **no wheel zoom at all** — only the toolbar's ±25% buttons. And the plan is sized by multiplying its width by the zoom, so the content grew from its top-left corner: whatever you were looking at slid away, and on a big sheet it slid off the screen.

- **Cmd (or Ctrl) + wheel zooms, at the cursor**, holding that point still.
- It has to be a **native, non-passive listener**. React registers `onWheel` passively, so `preventDefault` there is ignored and the browser zooms the whole page instead of the plan.
- **A trackpad pinch arrives as a wheel event with `ctrlKey` set**, so pinch-to-zoom works through the same path without extra code.
- **A plain wheel still scrolls.** Scrolling a long plan is the other thing people do constantly; taking it over would be worse than the problem being solved.
- The buttons go through the same anchored path, centred on the viewport.
- **Fit now actually fits** the page to the window, rather than jumping to 100% — on a large sheet 100% is not a useful place to land.

## Pan

Panning required selecting the Pan tool, so moving around the plan meant putting the pen down, switching tool, and switching back to carry on. **Cmd-drag and the middle button now pan whatever tool is in hand**, and the Pan tool still works as before.

## The panel

The second line crammed the measurement type, the height, the usage count and a full list of page numbers into a column about 287px wide. It wrapped, and every extra line squeezed the name above it — which is why names showed as `Bath 1 F...`.

Measured on the same three items, in the running page, with main's file swapped in and back out to compare like for like:

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| name column | **65px** | **97px** |
| second line | `AREA · pp 1, 2, 3` — two lines | `3 pages` — one line |
| row height | 53 / 67 / 67 | 52 / 52 / 52 |

- **The type word is gone.** The unit beside the quantity already says m², lm or each — printing `AREA` as well was saying it twice. It is on the colour swatch's tooltip now.
- **Pages are counted, not listed.** The list grew without limit; it is in the tooltip, and the expander one click away names each page with what it measured there.
- The line **can no longer wrap**, so rows are a uniform height and the name keeps its width.

## Verified

Dev had no take-off plans and a plan needs a real PDF, so I seeded one against a PDF already sitting in local object storage. With the viewer actually open:

- Cmd+wheel: 100% → 272% → 400% (clamped), with `scrollLeft/scrollTop` adjusted each time to hold the anchor point
- Three notches out: 147% → 54% → 25% (floor)
- Fit: reset to a computed fit with scroll back to 0,0
- Panel figures above measured from the live DOM

Seeded plan, pages and measurements deleted afterwards; dev is back to zero.

`tsc` **1252**, unchanged. `check:schema` ok. `takeoff-mark-index` test (from #274) still passing. **No migration.**

## Summary
Three small changes, one commit each.

**1. Offline eval defaults to `gpt-5-mini`.** `qa/run_eval.py` defaulted `OPENAI_EVAL_MODEL` to `gpt-4.1-mini`, which OpenAI retires on 2027-01-14. The script already sends GPT-5 reasoning and verbosity settings. `OPENAI_EVAL_MODEL` is added to `.env.example`, and `qa/README.md` is updated. Nothing else in the repo referenced 4.1-mini.

**2. Plain ESLint 9 instead of `next lint`.** `next lint` is deprecated in Next 15.5 and removed in 16, and ESLint 8 is end-of-life.

author: pedrofrxncx
body: Follows #8084, which gave `config.ReadDiskConfig` a third return value (`err`) so the daemon's boot path (`main.go`) can log a malformed `.decocms/daemon.json` instead of silently discarding it. `Orchestrator.fillApplicationDefaults` (called on every sandbox setup run, before install) calls the same function but discards all three return values (`diskCfg, _, _`), so the exact same malformed-JSON case that boot now logs stays completely silent on this path. Why a maintainer wants it: without this, a broken `daemon.json` on a repo silently falls back to autodetected application defaults on every setup run with zero signal in the logs, making it hard to tell "we picked a default" from "the user's config loaded but had unexpected values" — exactly the debugging gap #8084 closed for boot but missed here. Change: `fillApplicationDefaults` now checks the returned `err` and logs it with `slog.Error("ignoring malformed .decocms/daemon.json", "error", err)`, matching the exact log message and pattern `main.go` already uses. No behavior change otherwise — `diskCfg` is still `nil` on a parse error, so the function falls through to the same autodetected defaults as before. Reviewer command: `cd packages/sandbox/daemon-go && go test ./internal/setup/...` Local checks run: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/setup/...`, `go test ./internal/setup/...` (all pass), `gofmt -l` clean on the touched file. Full CI validates the rest. --- ## Summary by cubic Logs malformed `.decocms/daemon.json` files during sandbox setup so they no longer silently fall back to autodetected defaults. Uses the same `slog.Error` message and pattern the daemon boot path already uses; no other behavior changes. Written for commit ab3b4c164b17ff417d734f91cc5bf8dc1f22869a. Summary will update on new commits.
