author: meepleai-app
body:
Closes #4547

## Il difetto

`PdfUploadQuotaService.ReleaseQuotaAsync` controllava la prenotazione con `KeyExistsAsync` e poi chiamava `DecrementUploadCountAsync`. Questo ricalcolava le chiavi giornaliera e settimanale dall'ora **del rilascio**. Una prenotazione di domenica alle 23:50 UTC, fallita lunedì alle 00:10, decrementava `daily:<lunedì>` e `weekly:<settimana nuova>`. Il contatore del periodo nuovo restava sottostimato di 1, e l'utente aveva un upload in più del limite. Lo stesso succedeva a ogni mezzanotte per la chiave giornaliera.

Leggendo il codice è emerso un secondo difetto, che ho corretto qui perché costa una riga. Il controllo (`EXISTS`) e la cancellazione (`DEL`) erano comandi separati, con i decrementi in mezzo. Due rilasci concorrenti della stessa prenotazione la vedevano tutti e due e decrementavano due volte. Non è teorico: il test d'integrazione su Redis vero, prima della correzione, ha dato contatore 0 invece di 1 (vedi Prove). Il rilascio parte da più punti di `UploadPdfCommandHandler.Processing.cs`, fra cui il ramo «documento già `Failed`» di `ValidateAndPrepareProcessingAsync`.

## Cosa cambia

Tutto in `PdfUploadQuotaService`:

- **Rilascio**: legge e cancella la prenotazione con `StringGetDeleteAsync` (`GETDEL`), poi decrementa le chiavi calcolate da `ReservedAt`. Se `ReservedAt` non si legge, ripiega sull'ora attuale, cioè il comportamento di prima, e lo scrive nel log come warning.
- **Prenotazione**: incrementa i contatori dello stesso istante che scrive in `ReservedAt`. Prima `ReserveQuotaAsync` leggeva l'orologio per il JSON, e `IncrementUploadCountAsync` lo rileggeva dopo la scrittura su Redis. Una mezzanotte caduta fra le due letture separava le chiavi incrementate da quelle che il rilascio ora decrementa.
- Le chiavi (`DailyCounterKey`, `WeeklyCounterKey`, `ReservationKey`) si calcolano in un punto solo, usato da incremento, decremento e lettura.
- `IPdfUploadQuotaService.ReleaseQuotaAsync`: la documentazione dice quale periodo si decrementa e che un doppio rilascio decrementa una volta.

Le chiavi Redis e il formato del JSON non cambiano.

## Decisioni

- **Strada (a): le chiavi da `ReservedAt`, non (b), cioè salvarle nella prenotazione.** `ReservedAt` è nel JSON da prima di questa PR, quindi (a) funziona anche per le prenotazioni scritte prima del deploy, senza un formato nuovo. Con (b) le prenotazioni di prima del deploy non avrebbero le chiavi, e servirebbe comunque (a) come ripiego: (b) è (a) più un campo in più. (b) protegge da un cambio futuro della formula delle chiavi (come #4545), ma solo per le prenotazioni a cavallo di quel deploy (al massimo 30 minuti). E un cambio di formula sposta comunque tutti i contatori del periodo, quindi quel rilascio sarebbe il problema minore.
- **`GETDEL` invece di un unico script Lua con prenotazione e contatori.** `GETDEL` rende atomico ciò che conta: chi consuma la prenotazione. Uno solo dei rilasci concorrenti trova il valore. Uno script unico renderebbe atomici anche i decrementi, ma toccherebbe tre chiavi in un comando (non portabile su Redis Cluster) e cambierebbe gli script che già ci sono. Rischio che resta: se Redis cade fra `GETDEL` e i decrementi, la prenotazione è consumata e il contatore no. L'utente perde un upload fino al cambio di periodo, il lato prudente per una quota. È la stessa classe di guasto parziale che il codice già tollera (i decrementi stanno in un `catch` che registra e prosegue).
- **`GETDEL` richiede Redis ≥ 6.2.** Staging usa `redis:7.4.1-alpine3.20` (`infra/docker-compose.yml`), CI e Testcontainers `redis:7-alpine`. Non ci sono altri Redis nel repo.
- **`ConfirmQuotaAsync` non è toccato.** Ha lo stesso schema `EXISTS` + `DEL`, ma non tocca i contatori: un doppio confirm cancella due volte, senza effetti.
- **Il ripiego sull'ora attuale resta.** Una prenotazione illeggibile si rilascia comunque, come prima, invece di restare lì fino alla scadenza. Ha un test con cinque valori malformati.

## Cosa succede alle prenotazioni in corso al deploy

Sono in Redis con il JSON del codice di prima, che ha già `ReservedAt` in UTC nello stesso formato. Il nuovo rilascio le legge e decrementa il loro periodo. Non serve nessuna migrazione e non c'è una finestra di comportamento diverso. Il test `ReleaseQuota_ReservationWrittenBeforeTheDeploy_DecrementsItsPeriod` usa quel JSON scritto a mano. `ReserveQuota_WritesTheReservationJsonTheReleaseReads` blocca il formato scritto oggi: se qualcuno lo cambia, il test gli ricorda che per 30 minuti dopo il deploy il lettore vedrà ancora il formato vecchio.

## Prove

Da `apps/api/tests/Api.Tests`.

**Rossi prima della correzione** (stessa build dei test, codice di `main-dev`):

- `dotnet test --no-build --filter "FullyQualifiedName~PdfUploadQuotaServiceTests"` → `Non superati: 5. Superati: 75. Totale: 80`.
  - `ReleaseQuota_AfterSundayMidnight_…`: decrementava `2026-10-19` / `2026-W43` invece di `2026-10-18` / `2026-W42`.
  - `ReleaseQuota_AfterAnyMidnight_…`: `2026-10-15` invece di `2026-10-14`, settimana uguale.
  - `ReleaseQuota_ReservationWrittenBeforeTheDeploy_…`: come il primo.
  - `ReserveThenRelease_MidnightFallsInsideTheReservation_…`: l'incremento andava su lunedì con `ReservedAt` di domenica.
  - `ReleaseQuota_SecondReleaseWhileTheFirstIsDecrementing_DecrementsOnce`: 4 decrementi invece di 2.
- `dotnet test --no-build --filter "FullyQualifiedName~PdfUploadQuotaEnforcementIntegrationTests"` (Redis e Postgres della fixture Testcontainers) → `Non superati: 2. Superati: 11. Totale: 13`.
  - `ReleaseQuota_AfterSundayMidnight_RestoresOnlyTheReservationPeriod`: `daily:2026-10-18` restava a 1.
  - `ReleaseQuota_SameReservationReleasedConcurrently_DecrementsOnce`: otto rilasci in parallelo hanno portato il contatore a 0 invece di 1.

Il ripiego (`ReleaseQuota_ReservedAtUnreadable_FallsBackToTheCurrentPeriod`, 5 casi) e `ReleaseQuota_NoReservation_DecrementsNothing` erano verdi anche prima: documentano il comportamento che resta, non il difetto.

**Verdi dopo**:

- `--filter "FullyQualifiedName~PdfUploadQuotaServiceTests"` → `Superati: 81. Totale: 81`.
- `--filter "FullyQualifiedName~PdfUploadQuotaEnforcementIntegrationTests|FullyQualifiedName~UploadPdfIntegrationTests.QuotaReservation"` → `Superati: 16. Totale: 16`. Comprende i tre test di prenotazione, conferma e rilascio di `UploadPdfIntegrationTests`.
- `--filter "(FullyQualifiedName~Quota|FullyQualifiedName~UploadPdf|FullyQualifiedName~UploadPrivatePdf)&Category=Unit"` → `Superati: 301. Totale: 301`.

**Perturbazioni** (rotta la riga che conta, ricompilato, test rossi, poi ripristinato e ricompilato):

| perturbazione | rossi |
|---|---|
| il rilascio usa l'ora attuale invece di `ReservedAt` | i 4 test di periodo (domenica, giorno qualunque, JSON di prima del deploy, mezzanotte dentro la prenotazione) |
| la prenotazione rilegge l'orologio per l'incremento | `ReserveThenRelease_MidnightFallsInsideTheReservation_…` |
| `GET` + decrementi + `DEL` invece di `GETDEL` | `ReleaseQuota_SecondReleaseWhileTheFirstIsDecrementing_DecrementsOnce` (4 decrementi invece di 2) |

`dotnet format whitespace --verify-no-changes` sui quattro file: pulito.

## Cosa non ho verificato

- Nessuna prova su staging né sul servizio vivo: il comportamento a mezzanotte è coperto solo con l'orologio finto, in unit e su Redis vero via Testcontainers.
- Il test d'integrazione concorrente non è un rosso deterministico sul codice vecchio: la gara dipende dai tempi (qui è uscita rossa al primo colpo). Il rosso deterministico è quello unit, che ferma il primo rilascio dentro il decremento.
- Non ho lanciato l'intera suite di backend, solo i filtri sopra.

author: repcoders
body: ## Why Twelve answers into a coding chat, the script you want again is in answer 3, inside a round that is folded or on a history page that is not loaded. Getting it back means scrolling, opening disclosures and finding the right block by eye. The recording already holds every answer's full Markdown, and Copy answer already reads it back whole, but nothing lists the pieces you came for. This targets 2.1.44. ## What changed The right dock gets an **Artifacts** tab (Ctrl+Shift+5, also in the launcher and the `+` menu). It lists the open chat's code blocks, tables and display formulas in the order they were written, with All / Code / Tables / Formulas filters and a count on each. A filter for a kind the chat has none of is disabled. Each entry shows the block's language (or Table, Formula), its line count and its first eight lines, at most 2,000 characters. Copy puts the whole block on the clipboard as written: the code, the table's Markdown, the formula's LaTeX. The answer link under it ("Answer 2 · The export is 4 GB now. Can it stream?") opens the chat at that answer with the same scroll and wash as a Find in chat result, loading the history page around it when needed. Before it scrolls, an expanded panel is restored, the panel closes on a window too narrow for both, and the chat's settings sheet gives way to the timeline. Esc closes the panel like the other dock tools. Main reads the list from the whole recording, so a folded round or an answer far above the loaded page counts too. The new `sessions:artifacts { id }` route calls `artifactsInSession` in `session/markdown-export.ts`. It takes the final answers in spoken order (`transcriptEntries`), with the full text of answers the log cut (the same `fullText` Copy answer uses), and parses each with `shared/answer-artifacts.ts` on marked's lexer. Code inside lists and quotes counts. A display formula is `\[ … \]` or `$$ … $$` opening a line, as `math.ts` draws it. Formulas inside code, inline `\( … \)` and escaped brackets such as `a\[0\]` are left out. The reply holds at most 500 artifacts and 2,000,000 characters, and says `limited` beyond that ("Showing the first 500"). The panel reads again when the chat's `lastAssistantFinalAt` or `lastTurnEndAt` moves, not when history pages load, and an unchanged list is not redrawn, so the reader's place in it stays put. A failed read keeps what was listed, or says it could not read the chat, and is tried again when the panel next opens. AGENTS.md describes the route and the panel next to the other dock tools. Eleven new strings are in all 12 catalogs. The change is 405 added lines outside tests and translations. ## Edge cases - A chat with no code, tables or formulas says so; a filter for a kind it has none of is disabled ("says when a chat has none, and when the list holds only part of them"). - A very large chat: the reply holds at most 500 artifacts and 2,000,000 characters and says "Showing the first 500" beyond that ("bounds a chat's artifacts and says when it lists only part of them"). - A failed or throwing read keeps what was listed, or says it could not read the chat, and is tried again when the panel next opens ("says a read failed instead of calling the chat empty", "treats a read that throws as a failed read, and tries it again when the panel reopens"). - Formulas inside code, inline brackets such as `a\[0\]`, fences written inside quotes, lists or indented code, and a fence line that names a language are read the way marked reads them ("leaves out formulas inside code, inline brackets and empty blocks" and the other `answer-artifacts` tests). - An answer in a folded round or far above the loaded history is listed from the whole recording, and its link loads the page around it. An expanded panel is restored, a panel that covers a narrow window closes, and the settings sheet gives way to the timeline first ("makes room for the chat an Artifacts link opens", "shows the chat itself when an artifact's answer is opened from its settings"). - A preview of one very long line stops at 2,000 characters, and Copy still gives all of it ("cuts a long line in the preview and still copies all of it"). ## Platforms The shortcut is Ctrl+Shift+5 on Windows 11 and on macOS, like the panels' Ctrl+Shift+1 to 4. The handler ignores Cmd and Alt, so macOS's Cmd+Shift+5 (screenshot) is not involved, and it reads the physical key (`Digit5`), so it works on layouts where Shift+5 types another character. I know of no default system shortcut on either OS that takes Ctrl+Shift+5. I did not try it on a Mac; the fork's macOS CI and UI checks pass. ## Test - `test/answer-artifacts.test.ts`: "lists an answer's code blocks, tables and display formulas in the order written", "leaves out formulas inside code, inline brackets and empty blocks", "keeps a fence open past a line that names a language, as marked does", "keeps written order inside lists, where a formula can come before a code block", "leaves out formulas inside code fenced in a quote or a list item", "keeps a fence open past quoted or listed fence lines written inside it", "leaves out formulas inside indented code, at the top and in a list" and "reads formulas after indented code that shows a fence line". - `test/session-markdown-export.test.ts`: "lists the code, tables and formulas of every answer with its question and place", "bounds a chat's artifacts and says when it lists only part of them" and "numbers the answers of one turn as one answer, as Copy answer joins them". - `test/artifacts-drawer.test.ts`: "lists a chat's code, tables and formulas by kind, copies one whole and opens its answer", "reads again only when the chat or its answers change, and not while hidden", "says when a chat has none, and when the list holds only part of them", "tries a failed read again when the panel reopens, not on every repaint", "says a read failed instead of calling the chat empty", "cuts a long line in the preview and still copies all of it" and "treats a read that throws as a failed read, and tries it again when the panel reopens". - `test/renderer-timeline.test.ts`: "shows the chat itself when an artifact's answer is opened from its settings". - `test/renderer-workspace-docks.test.ts`: "opens Artifacts from its own entry and Ctrl+Shift+5, and says why it is off without a chat" and "makes room for the chat an Artifacts link opens: restores an expanded panel, closes one that covers the chat". author: bikeborb
body:
Part 17 of 35 of the re-landing of #370, #376, #380 and #401 as one-subject pull requests, after the revert in #403. Based on #419; until that one is merged this PR shows its changes too. This PR on its own: https://github.com/bikeborb/emulator/compare/pr/16-vma-stop-token...pr/17-driver-guest-memory

### feat(core): allocate guest memory from the GPU driver on Android

Vulkan::ExportGuestMemory (vulkan_common/vulkan_guest_memory.cpp, new)
creates a throwaway instance and device on the first physical device and
allocates the guest's memory from the driver as exportable dma_buf
memory: total_size / chunk_size chunks (GuestMemoryChunkSize is 1 GiB),
each a buffer plus one allocation from the first memory type the buffer
allows that is device local, host visible, host coherent and host
cached, exported with vkGetMemoryFdKHR. Only on an integrated GPU with
VK_KHR_external_memory_fd and VK_EXT_external_memory_dma_buf; every
failure closes the descriptors and leaves guest memory as it was.

Common::HostMemory takes the descriptors (at most MaxBackingChunks) and
maps every chunk over a PROT_NONE reservation; a mapping that crosses a
chunk boundary is made in pieces (FirstChunkRange, with compile-time
checks and Linux test cases in tests/common/host_memory.cpp). With no
descriptors the memfd path runs unchanged. System::Impl calls the export
from InitializeKernel at every game start until it works, because the
Android frontend loads the driver after System::Initialize has created
guest memory.

This only provides guest memory the GPU can address; importing it into
the renderer's device is the next step. Logged once per attempt as
"Guest memory from the GPU driver: on (N chunks of M MiB)" or
"off (reason)". On the AYN Thor: on, 4 chunks of 1024 MiB, frame rates
unchanged in five games.

> Recreated from agent-substrate/env PR 99, opened by tomergee on 2026-10-16; originally open; original branch `fix/python-streaming-auth-97` into `main`.
> Mentions and references below are defused; numbers refer to agent-substrate/env.

## Summary

`grpc.aio.Channel.__init__` dispatches each interceptor with `if` / `elif` across `UnaryUnaryClientInterceptor`, `UnaryStreamClientInterceptor`, `StreamUnaryClientInterceptor`, and `StreamStreamClientInterceptor`. As a result, a single multi-inheritance `_AuthInterceptor` instance was only registered for `UnaryUnary` RPCs and never invoked for `UnaryStream` (`StreamProcessOutput`, `ReadFile`), `StreamUnary` (`WriteFile`, `WriteProcessInput`), or `StreamStream` RPCs.

## Changes

- Register four separate single-arity interceptor instances (`_auth_interceptors(token)`) on the `grpc.aio` channel so all four gRPC call shapes carry `authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- Attach `("authorization", f"Bearer {self._client._auth_token}")` in `Env._metadata()` so caller-supplied channels also carry the bearer header on environment/process/filesystem calls, and deduplicate in `_BaseAuthInterceptor._inject`.
- Add regression tests in `clients/python/tests/test_client.py` verifying that `_auth_interceptors` injects the bearer across all four `grpc.aio` call shapes and that `Client(..., auth_token=...)` sends `Authorization: Bearer` exactly once across unary and streaming environment RPCs.

Fixes #​97

author: albertofonsecaq
body:
Closes #37. **Closes #8.**

## Why guards, not documentation

#8 is already done in the code: 36 columns across 18 models declare their time zone, nothing calls `utcnow()` or `date.today()`, no conversion shim survives. None of it was *checked* by anything — which is how it got broken in the first place. I added two aware-schema columns with naive mappings **while writing the decision that forbids it** (#10, #12), and the shims in the sources API read like deliberate choices for months before #8 identified them as workarounds.

## Four guards

1. Every mapped model's timestamp columns must declare their zone.
2. Their `default=` and `onupdate=` must produce an aware value — the half a type check misses, since a column can *accept* aware values while its own default shifts an instant on every insert.
3. `utcnow()` and `date.today()` must appear nowhere in `app/` or `scripts/`.
4. Nothing may strip a time zone outside the connector boundary — where the allowed set is now **empty**.

## Each one verified by breaking the convention on purpose

| Break | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Retyped a column to a bare `mapped_column` | fails, naming `users.created_at` |
| Put `datetime.utcnow()` back in a service | fails, naming file and line |
| Re-added a `.replace(tzinfo=None)` shim | fails, naming it |
| Naive `onupdate` on an aware column | fails, naming `plan_items.updated_at.onupdate` |

Each went green again on restore.

**That verification is the deliverable, not a nicety.** Three tests written across #34–#36 could not have failed as first written — the hazard test under `TZ=UTC`, a proxy assertion against a parameter that no longer existed, and a zone loop that never changed zones — and all three were caught by review rather than by running. A guard that cannot fail reads as coverage and is worse than none. Two of these tests also guard *themselves*: one asserts it found at least 36 columns, another that the file scan found more than 40 files, so a registry or glob that silently collected nothing cannot pass.

## `to_naive_utc` is deleted

#4 added it for Telethon and YouTube; neither insists on naive, so it spent all three batches with **no caller**. ADR 1 keeps the exception as the right *shape* — a platform that demands a naive value converts at the connector boundary and nowhere else — and a comment where the helper was says so, with git history holding the implementation.

Its unit tests went with it. #4's actual guarantee lives in the `fetch_range` bound tests, which stay: a connector accepts a bound whichever way it arrives, and comparisons inside it never mix the two.

## The ADR

Gains an **Enforcement** section, so the next reader learns the convention is checked and how, rather than trusting a document — and records that three guards across the batches had to be fixed after review, since that is the reason this section exists.

## Verification

Offline 146 passed / 24 skipped; with a database **170 passed**, and 170 under `TZ=UTC`.

## What #8 ends up having been

| Ticket | |
| --- | --- |
| #32 | a database-backed fixture, and the UTC session assumption pinned |
| #33 | the ADR, and one source of `now` |
| #34 | 16 ingestion columns, the API boundary, connectors reversed to aware |
| #35 | 12 knowledge/validation columns, the changelog ordering, UTC dates in validation |
| #36 | 8 tenancy/billing columns, token expiry, the Stripe period write that could never have worked |
| #37 | the guards that stop all of it drifting back |

Four of those batches needed a follow-up PR after review. Every migration was verified up and down against a real database, and your row counts are unchanged throughout: 2 users, 2 workspaces, 2 members, 8,582 evidence, 1,274 ideas, 11,630 usage events.

author: f3nn3x
body:
This PR adds Library delete, a right-click menu on Library cards, and turns off the webview's own right-click menu in the desktop app. It is the first of three PRs for the app settings redesign; the handoff is now in `docs/redesign/app-settings/`.

**Right-click menu on Library cards.** A right-click selects the card and opens the app's context menu. The menu lists the item's primary and secondary actions (Set as background, Open in editor, Duplicate, Export…), then Rename and Remove from library.
- Rename focuses and selects the name field in the detail pane.
- The menu key opens the menu from the card.
- Delete or Backspace on a focused card asks to remove it. Keys pressed inside a child element of the card are ignored.
- Config stand-ins (saved panels and styles kept in the config) offer only their actions.

**Remove asks first, and deletes the file too.** A confirm dialog says that copies already placed stay where they are.
- After the item is deleted, its files (a gauge's frames too) go from the asset store, unless something still uses them. The server's `?unused=1` scan covers the saved config, the library and the canvases. The studio's live config is also checked, read just before the files are deleted.
- If a file fails to delete, the item stays removed and the toast says how many files were kept.
- This fixes the known limit noted in the previous PR.

**No native webview menu.** The desktop app no longer shows the webview's own menu (Back, Reload, Inspect). Text fields keep it, for cut, copy and paste. This covers the studio (`src/lib/native-menu.ts`, installed only inside Tauri) and the static local pages (`common.js`).

**Review:** one round found two serious bugs, both fixed:
- The suppression never ran in production builds, because it was wrapped in `import.meta.hot?.`.
- Rename didn't focus a pane that was already mounted.

The same round also fixed partial failure reporting, the timing of the live config read, the card's key guard, the dialog keeping its title while it closes, and the text field list in common.js. Not changed: after a removal, focus falls back to the page rather than moving to the next card.

author: jjackson
body:
Fixes #3254

## Premise (verified live, anonymous, 2026-10-19)

```
$ for i in 1000001 1000004 1000003; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "$i %{http_code} %{redirect_url}\n" https://labs.connect.dimagi.com/solicitations/$i/; done
1000001 200
1000004 404
1000003 404
$ curl ... /solicitations/9999999/   -> 404   (no such record)
$ curl ... /solicitations/1000002/   -> 302 https://labs.connect.dimagi.com/solicitations/past/ulab-scoping-2026/
$ curl ... /solicitations/           -> 200; the index contains 1000001, not 1000004
```

`get_solicitation(1000004)` returns the record with `"is_public":false,"status":"active"`, and the fixture
for 1000001 has `"is_public": true`. So an unlisted call returns the same 404 as a missing record, and a listed
call can be read without a login. Step 6's "expect 302 → /labs/login/, 404 is a BLOCKER" rule therefore
blocks every private publish, and "requires a labs login by design" is now false.

## Fix

- `skills/solicitation-create/SKILL.md` § Step 6: a table of the observed answers. For a **listed** call,
  expect 200 (or a 302 to `/past/`) and BLOCKER on a 404. For a **private** call, skip the anonymous probe;
  Step 7a's `get_solicitation` round-trip is the check. The `is_public` row and Step 7a's "why round-trip"
  paragraph are reworded to match.
- `CLAUDE.md`: the "Public is a misnomer" sentence is replaced with what the live route actually does,
  with the observation cited. Whether someone without a labs account can respond was not observed, so it
  is stated as unknown rather than promised.
- `agents/solicitation-management.md`, `playbook/integrations/connect-labs.md`: the same correction.
- New rail `test/skills/solicitation-route-probe.test.ts` (registered in `lib/rail-registry.ts`). It failed

Plan and floor plan for one fabricated UNO R4 WiFi shield, usable on all five air handlers, to replace the MBR node's hand-wired proto-shield, DIN-rail buck converter and 792 relay.

- `docs/air-handler-shield-pcb-plan.md`: scope, the Unico SCB thermostat signals and which to read, the terminal edge, circuit by block, pin map, layout, parts and concerns.

The design in brief: an 86.36 × 53.34 mm board, with terminals on a tab past the R4's edge (MKDS 3.81 mm for R · C · Y2 · W2 and MPT 2.54 mm for the sensors). The two air sensors take plain twisted pair on 2-way terminals. The 24 VAC is half-wave rectified into a Traco TMR 3-4811WI feeding the 5V header pin. LTV-814S AC optocouplers read Y2 and W2. The Unico EAC contact is a blower-running input on A2, and A3 is reserved for a flow meter. A DS2482-100 drives the 1-wire bus, with a jumper rollback to D2. Every part is SMD except the converter, the terminals and the headers.

No board is generated yet. The open items are in §8: meter W2 and the EAC terminals at the SCB, read the transformer nameplate, confirm the ICSP and jack positions against an R4. Digi-Key pages returned 403 to automated loads, so stock is unconfirmed.

author: nandan-varma
body:
"Keep R2 round trips low; cache aggressively" is a hard constraint (Vercel function limits; R2 is the only object store) that had nothing enforcing it. This makes it mechanical: the guard reads the **perf tree's own tallies** and asserts them.

## What it asserts

- **A repeated history read makes zero R2 calls** and reports cache hits — the result cache's promise, frozen.
- **A repeated file read stays inside one round trip**, with a cold read bounded by a generous ceiling (20) so a per-call explosion fails here instead of in production.

## Mutation testing (what makes it a guard rather than a screenshot)

- Object cache set to hold nothing: **both tests fail** — 2 R2 calls instead of 0, and 12 instead of ≤ 1.
- Ops result cache disabled: **nothing changes**, because the metric that matters is R2 round trips and the object cache absorbs those reads. That is deliberate — the guard asserts round trips, not which memo answered, so it does not lock in today's cache layering.

## It immediately found a real gap

A repeated `getFile` for the same ref and path still does one R2 range GET: the parsed tree is cached, the blob content is not. Filed as **#79** with the perf trees, which is why the file-read bound is `≤ 1` today; that issue tightens it to `0`.

## Verification

`pnpm --filter @pushstack/web test src/server/__tests__/r2-budget.test.ts` — 2 passed; both mutations above were reproduced locally and reverted. Counts are per test file (vitest isolates files in workers), so they are deterministic.

author: makenowjust
body:
A program naming Marshal got both per-class dispatchers, `sp_marshal_obj_dump` and `sp_marshal_obj_load`, with an arm per class each. A program that only loads (`INDEX = Marshal.load(data)` in a library it requires) carried the dump half for nothing.

## Change

Each half is now a stub when every reference to Marshal is the receiver of the other half's calls: `load` / `restore` for the dump, `dump` for the load (`src/codegen.c`). A reference of any other kind (a send, the module handed on) keeps both. The answers do not change.

## Size

A program of 200 classes with two accessors each, one object of each, and a `Marshal.load` of plain data, at `-O 0` (one Mac):

| | executable |
|---|---|
| before | 1,189,520 bytes |
| after | 1,139,272 bytes |

## Tests

`test/marshal_load_only_dispatch.rb` covers a program that only loads: an Array and a Hash of plain data, an object of the program's class with its ivars, and the class used normally beside it. It matches CRuby 4.0 (`--enable-frozen-string-literal`), as master does too: it guards the answers of a program whose dump half is now left out.

On 84c965208, 29 other tests mention Marshal. Of these, 25 generate byte-identical C before and after (same input paths). The other 4 (`ivar_presence_init_order`, `marshal_dump_exception`, `object_new_singleton`, `string_binary_tag_sources`) use only one half, and the other half is now a stub. All 30 pass under the harness with `--int-overflow=raise` and with `--int-overflow=promote`. The change is in `src/codegen.c` only.

body:
Supersedes #9 (M5). Still stacked on #8 (M4): merge #8 first, then this one, and close #9.

## What changed
Without the hourly IT PIN the desktop app is view-only. Users can look at My computer and Full details. Everything else needs the PIN.

- **Server enforces it**
  - `POST /register`: PIN is checked after the enrollment key. Wrong PINs are rate-limited per client IP.
  - `PUT /user`: PIN required.
  - `POST /scans`: PIN required for `scan_type: manual`. `on_demand`, `scheduled` and `startup` need none.
  - Wrong or old PIN gives `403 wrong_pin`. 5 wrong tries per minute give `429`.
  - Every attempt is recorded with its method (Signup, Update my details, Report now, Settings). The device page shows the method.
- **Contracts and migration**
  - `it_pin` is added to `register.request` and `user.request` (required) and to `scans.request` (optional).
  - Migration `0004` makes `device_id` nullable, adds `client_ip`, and adds three attempt methods.
- **Agent and desktop**
  - A correct PIN unlocks the app for 10 minutes, or until the window is hidden. The PIN is kept in memory only.
  - Report now (window and tray), signup, Update my details and Settings all need the PIN.
  - Dashboard `scan_now` and `send_logs` need none.
  - One 5-tries / 60 s lockout covers every PIN prompt.
  - Offline, these actions say "Can't reach the server. Try again when this computer is online." Only Settings keeps the enrollment-key fallback.
  - The window has a PIN dialog, an "Unlocked for IT · Lock" indicator, and PIN fields on signup and Update my details.
  - The dashboard confirm-details prompt also needs the PIN.
- **CLI**: `pcreader register --pin`, and `scan --upload --pin` for manual scans.
- Docs, CLAUDE.md, plan v2 and the INBOX summary are updated.

## Verification
- `bun run lint` and `bun run test` pass (contracts 37, server 111, Go all packages).
- `TestEndToEnd` passes against a real server and Postgres.
- `GOOS=windows go vet` of `agent/desktop` passes. The frontend only had a syntax check.

## Needs a check on a real PC
- The close button now uses `OnBeforeClose` plus `WindowHide` instead of `HideWindowOnClose`. Please confirm on Windows that it still only hides the window and that the app comes back locked. On macOS this also stops Cmd+Q from quitting.
- I could not run `wails build` here. CI builds the desktop apps.

author: zafnok
body:
## Summary

- `RewindScreen` and `GuidesScreen` are now screens of their own, pushed over the battle. The rewind screen pops with its `RewindEffect` (`Close` or `Rewind(point)`), and the battle applies it in `uncovered`. Closing the rewind screen on a lost battle still brings Game Over back exactly as it was left (1158's behavior). `RewindFrom` is gone: a decided battle can only have the screen open if it came from Game Over.
- Removed from the battle: the `rewind` and `guides` fields, `rewind_step` and `guides_step`, their branches in `play_key`, `help`, `scene` and `view`, `bare()`, and `BattleView`'s `rewind` and `guides` fields. `play_key` now returns which screen to open, and `open` pushes it after the lessons tick.
- The rewind list now uses the engine's `ListCursor`. Each sound plays where its key is handled, instead of being guessed from the focus before and after.
- The tips' flag is renamed `covered`. It is set in `covered` and cleared in `uncovered`, for any screen over the battle.
- Both pop-ups are opaque, not overlays: each paints the whole screen. The rewind screen paints its own map preview through the battle's camera and look (`MapFrame`). Guides pops without a value, since closing it changes nothing in the battle.
- Tests: unit tests drive the battle on a real stack (`testing::Stacked`, which derefs to the battle but has no `DerefMut`), and integration tests find the screens with `h.screen::<RewindScreen>()`. Snapshots and assertions are unchanged, apart from the plumbing listed in the ticket's notes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The grep for `rewind: Option`, `guides: Option` and `set_under_scene(false)` in `battle/mod.rs` finds nothing.
- [x] The rewind and Guides tests and snapshots pass. No snapshot changed. The tests' assertions are the same; only how they reach the screens changed.
- [ ] `cargo xtask code-lines` shows `trpg-ui` fell. **Not met:** 311 lines added, 244 removed (+67 net). The battle lost the ~130 lines the sweep counted, but each pop-up now carries what every screen needs: a `Screen` impl, a whole-screen view and a painter (ADR-0054). The rewind screen also carries the battle's camera so it can paint its own map.
- [x] All local gates in the `run-gates` skill pass.

Two tiny player-visible differences, as with any pushed screen:
- Keys pressed in the same frame after the key that opens the pop-up are dropped. This only matters for two presses inside one frame, or for several crank notches in the frame that opens the rewind screen.
- The battle waits underneath, as it does under Options.

Follow-up tickets: none.

Engine friction: estimate 150, measured 311 (2.1×). Accepted, with a row in `docs/engine/friction.md`.

Nick input: none. On the Pages build, please open the rewind screen (r) and the Guides list (map menu) in a battle and check they work as before.

author: iscasasola
body:
Owner, 2026-10-20: asked "Do you want a 'Move to another category' option for suppliers?" → "okay". Dunkin' Donuts was typed in under Everything else; it is really a Food Truck.

## Rule 0: what exists · what was missing · the delta
- **Exists:** `ServicesCoveredPicker` (one searchable list of the Suppliers page's rows, #6706), its locked own row; `HostServiceDetails` (workspace) and `NewManualVendorModal` edit mode (card sheet) both mount it; `updateHostServiceDetails` (session + RLS + off-platform-only) is the card's edit auth; `restoreTileToPlan` puts a row on the event; `bucketForVendor` buckets money by `category`; `event_vendors.category_key` (taxonomy-keyed TEXT, FK → `service_categories`, added 2026-08-15 "for a tile the enum can't store", never read).
- **Missing:** nothing wrote `event_vendors.category` after an add. And **`category` alone can't express the move**: it is an enum, and 48 of the 80 Suppliers-page rows have no label of their own. Food Truck stores `misc`, which draws as Everything else, so rewriting `category` would put Dunkin' straight back where it started.
- **Delta:** a move writes `category` (the enum label the rest of the app keys on) plus `category_key` (the row) when the enum can't name it. `homeTileForRow` reads it back. It only refines the category, never contradicts it, and never names a row the page doesn't draw. **Measured 2026-10-20: zero live production rows had a `category_key`, so no existing card moves.** No migration.

## What it does
- Beside the locked row in "What services does this cover" (workspace and card sheet): **Move <name> to another category**. It opens the same searchable one list, single pick. The confirm is in place: "Dunkin' Donuts moves from Everything else to Food Truck. Its price and payments move with it." · Move · Cancel. After that, a toast with **Undo**.
- `moveSupplierToCategory` (workspace/actions.ts): one action with the same auth as `updateHostServiceDetails` (session, RLS, `marketplace_vendor_id IS NULL`). It reads the update back, so a zero-row update is never reported as a move. What it writes comes from the pure `planSupplierMove`, which the guard also runs. Also-covers drops the new home and does not gain the old one. Price, payments and notes are on the same row, so they move with it. A row the event doesn't have yet is added through `restoreTileToPlan`.
- **Budget** follows `category`. A row with no enum label (Food Truck) has no Budget line of its own, so its money stays where `misc` buckets. That is the same place a supplier added under Food Truck lands today. The guard asserts this for every row.
- **Claim link:** `vendor_invites.service_category` is kept in step for `pending` and for `claimed` invites. The write uses the service role, after the session write has shown the caller may write the row.
- Placement now reads `homeTileForRow` in: the Suppliers page builder, also-covers, the workspace's locked row and header label, the card sheet, and Find's "Booked".

## Claimed suppliers: which rule I found
Supplier access **keys on `event_vendors.category` alone**: `get_vendor_seat_plan` (floor list, meal counts) and `get_vendor_event_brief`; since #6709, `answer_claim_access_request` too. Per the brief, that means the move is allowed and the access consequence is stated, with no "Ask the shop" line. In practice:
- **A supplier linked to a shop** (`marketplace_vendor_id` set) never sees this block. Shipped rule: the block is off-platform-only, and the card shows the shop's own package. The action refuses such a row too.
- **A supplier waiting for Approve** (#6709, link-on-Approve: no `marketplace_vendor_id` yet) can move. Approve then gives what the new category gets, so the confirm line adds: "When you approve them, they see what a booked food truck sees." Moving into the coordinator trade gives: "…they get the same access as you." The fact comes from `hasClaimAsk` (`event_access_requests`, kind `claim`, pending).

## Guards + sabotage
- `lib/a-moved-supplier-is-drawn-once-under-its-new-row.test.ts` (8 tests, executed against `buildShortlistFolders` and `bucketForVendor`). For every row the page draws: the card is drawn once as its own card under the new row and not under the old one, the price travels with it, the money sits in the bucket a supplier added there would use, also-covers excludes its own home and the old home, and other ticks stay as no-money copies. Undo restores the drawing and the money. A contradicting or undrawn key is never the home. Source checks on the action: one update, read back, shop row refused, claim link synced. The confirm line wording is checked too.
  - Sabotage: category_key never written → 4 failed · page ignores category_key → 2 failed · update not read back → 1 failed · old home kept in covers → 1 failed · claimed invites not synced → 1 failed. Each restored → green.
- `tests/db/a-supplier-moves-only-for-its-own-couple.db.test.ts` (5 tests, the action's statements under RLS on the replayed schema): the couple's move returns one row and the FK accepts `food_truck`; another couple's identical move matches nothing; a shop-linked row is not moved; an unknown key is refused by the FK; pending and claimed links are synced on the service role, and a stranger can't touch them.
  - Sabotage: run as service role with the shop filter dropped → 2 failed; restored → 5/5.

## Other
- **Round 2:** `guards` went red on `lint:no-card`, not on the ceiling: the confirm's hand-drawn Cancel was a bordered rounded box. Move / Cancel are now the house `ActionButton` (brand main + neutral), the same pair the sheet's footer uses. The shots were retaken.
- **Server-action ceiling:** the count was exactly at 1225. I removed `mapAddPlusOne` (`guests/map-actions.ts`), which has had no caller since the 2026-10-07 List/Map rewrite. Count is still 1225.
- Merged `origin/main` (#6709, #6711). Kept both sides of `fetchEventVendors` (booked-if-paid read + `category_key`). No generated baseline needed regenerating: `ugat:screens:check`, `lint:dup-rule` and `lint:port-controls` are clean.
- **Not walked:** the toast/Undo after a real Move. The lab has no database, so the action can't run there. Undo is covered by the guard (plan) and the db test (statements).
- **Follow-up, not fixed here (owner call):** adding your own supplier from the Food Truck row still files them under Everything else. `AddYourOwnWalk` collapses rows that share a stored category ("the first one names it"), and the add writes no `category_key`. That is probably how Dunkin' got there.

## Shots (`~/Documents/Claude/Projects/shots-2026-10-19/6712/`, 375 + 1280, light)
`*-1-block-with-move` · `*-2-picker-search-food` · `*-3-confirm-line` · `*-3b-confirm-claim-waiting` · `*-4-suppliers-before` · `*-5-suppliers-after-food-truck` (Dunkin' is its own card under Food Truck, "added by you", not "included with").

Labs: `/dev/add-your-own-lab?s=record&who=dunkin[&claim=1]` · `/dev/suppliers-lab?dunkin=moved&open=food_truck`.

## Phone check (maria-and-jose, never cale-ice)
1. Suppliers, open a supplier you added yourself, then "What services does this cover".
2. Press "Move … to another category", type "food", pick Food Truck.
3. You should see the one-line confirm. Press Move: the card is now under Food Truck as its own card, and Undo in the toast puts it back.

body:
## Why

v0.2 promises an MCP install command for every terminal and editor agent (#17, #18). `knode connect` only knew Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Claude Desktop.

## What changed

- New `knode connect` targets, each editing the agent's documented MCP settings on macOS and Linux:
  - `cursor`: `mcpServers` in `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (`type: stdio`)
  - `windsurf`: `mcpServers` in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/devin/mcp_config.json` (current docs, after Windsurf became Devin Desktop) and in `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json` when that folder exists
  - `cline`: `cline_mcp_settings.json` in `globalStorage/saoudrizwan.claude-dev/settings` of every VS Code, VS Code Insiders, VSCodium, Cursor and Windsurf where Cline is installed, plus Cline CLI (`~/.cline/data/settings`, `CLINE_DIR`, `CLINE_MCP_SETTINGS_PATH`)
  - `roo-code`: `mcp_settings.json` in `globalStorage/rooveterinaryinc.roo-cline/settings` of the same editors
  - `copilot-cli`: `mcpServers` in `$COPILOT_HOME/mcp-config.json` or `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` (`type: local`, `tools: ["*"]`)
  - `opencode`: `mcp` in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/opencode.json` (or `opencode.jsonc`), `type: local` with the command as an array
  - `amp`: `amp.mcpServers` in `~/.config/amp/settings.json` (or `settings.jsonc`)
  - `vscode`: `servers` in the user `mcp.json` of VS Code and VS Code Insiders (`type: stdio`), for GitHub Copilot agent mode
  - `zed`: `context_servers` in `~/.config/zed/settings.json` (macOS) or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/zed/settings.json` (Linux)
  - `aider`: no MCP client (Aider-AI/aider#2525, #3314 still open), so it prints guidance (`knode markdown folder` + `aider --read`, or `/run knode search`), edits nothing and issues no key
- Same guarantees as the existing targets: only the `knode` entry changes, `<file>.knode-backup` first, permissions kept, idempotent, `--print` dry run, key issued with the existing flow.
- JSON editing now goes through a concrete syntax tree (`jsonc-parser =0.34.0`, `cst` feature): the rest of the file keeps its layout. For agents that read JSONC (VS Code, Zed, OpenCode, Amp) comments and trailing commas are kept; for plain-JSON agents a file with comments is refused with a message saying so. Anything looser (single quotes, bare keys) is refused for all.
- Every settings file is read and checked before the agent gets a key, so a broken file or a missing Cline/Roo Code leaves nothing half done.
- `knode connect --list`: every target, whether it is detected on this machine (program on PATH or its settings folder exists), the file it would change and whether Knode is already there. Starts nothing.
- `connect.rs` is now `connect/{mod,json,places}.rs`. Fixes a stray run of spaces in the "There is no space yet" message.

## Verification of each location

| Target | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|
| cursor | verified | cursor.com/docs/context/mcp |
| windsurf | verified (Devin path); `~/.codeium/windsurf` unverified for current releases, kept as a fallback | docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/mcp |
| cline | verified | cline/cline `apps/vscode/src/core/storage/disk.ts`, `sdk/packages/shared/src/storage/paths.ts`, docs.cline.bot |
| roo-code | verified | RooCodeInc/Roo-Code `src/shared/globalFileNames.ts`, `src/services/mcp/McpHub.ts`, `src/package.json` (publisher) |
| copilot-cli | verified | docs.github.com, "Adding MCP servers for GitHub Copilot CLI" |
| opencode | verified path and format; XDG_CONFIG_HOME handling unverified (not in docs) | opencode.ai/docs/config, /docs/mcp-servers |
| amp | verified | ampcode.com/docs/customize/mcp, /docs/cli/settings |
| vscode | verified format; profile folder paths from the VS Code settings docs | code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/reference/mcp-configuration |
| zed | verified | zed-industries/zed `crates/paths/src/paths.rs`, `crates/settings_content/src/project.rs`, zed.dev/docs/ai/mcp |
| aider | verified: no MCP client | Aider-AI/aider issues #2525, #3314 |

Unverified spots are also marked in comments in `connect/places.rs`.

## Decisions

- Windsurf: both the current (Devin) and the earlier (`~/.codeium/windsurf`) files are edited when their folders exist; with neither, the current documented one is created.
- Cline and Roo Code are only set up in editors where the extension's storage folder exists; with none, `knode connect` fails before issuing a key.
- VS Code: the user `mcp.json` (as asked), not the newer "Copilot Global" `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`, which `copilot-cli` already covers.
- Cursor is treated as plain JSON (comments are not documented), so a commented `mcp.json` is refused rather than risked.
- Amp: `~/.config/amp` as documented, without guessing XDG_CONFIG_HOME support.

## Docs

- [ ] Nothing users see changed
- knodemd/docs#16

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build`, `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check`
- [x] `tests/connect.rs`: every target in a sandboxed HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME (never the real configs): `--print` changes nothing, backup holds the old file, second run changes nothing, permissions kept (Cursor), comments kept (VS Code, Zed, OpenCode), invalid or commented plain-JSON files refused and untouched, multiple editors for Cline (plus Cline CLI) and VS Code, Windsurf current and earlier locations, Cline and Roo Code missing refused without a key, Aider gets guidance and no key, `--list` shows all 14 targets and detection without starting anything
- [x] Unit tests for the JSON/JSONC editor (comments, trailing commas, dotted keys, refusals)

author: minjaekimartist
body:
## Why
Only the `volatile_load`/`volatile_store` builtins produced volatile LLVM accesses. A `volatile` variable, struct field, or `volatile T*` pointee compiled to ordinary loads/stores, so -O2 could delete them — including `std/mem.sc`'s `mem_zero_secure` wipe (secrets left in memory) and MMIO register writes in `std/hal`, `std/debug/jtag.sc`, `std/interrupt/vector_table.sc`.

## What changed
- **Parser/types:** the qualifier is kept on pointee types (`PointerType`/`ReferenceType::pointeeVolatile`), array elements (`ArrayType::elementVolatile`), struct fields (`FieldDecl::isVolatile`), locals, globals, parameters and typedefs. Placement follows C: `volatile int *p` → pointee, `int *volatile p` → the variable. `volatile &T` is a reference to volatile T.
- **Codegen:** `CodeGen::isVolatileLValue` drives `load volatile`/`store volatile` for plain, compound and bitfield assignment, `++`/`--`, subscripts, member access and dereference.
- **Sema:** `&x` of a volatile lvalue is `&volatile T`; volatile arrays decay to `volatile T*`. Implicit conversions that drop volatile (`volatile T*` → `T*`, volatile array → `T*`, `volatile T**` → `T**`, `&volatile T` → `&T`/`T*`) are now errors; explicit casts still work. Type names print the qualifier so diagnostics read correctly.
- **Tests:** new `compiler/tests/` IR regression suite — each `.sc` is compiled at -O2 and matched against `// CHECK:` lines by a small FileCheck-subset script (`filecheck.py`; LLVM's FileCheck isn't in the release toolchains), with `// EXPECT-ERROR:` for negative tests. Wired into `.github/scripts/smoke-test.sh`.

## Verification
- `compiler/tests/run.sh`: 5/5 pass (store loop, volatile field, pointer to volatile, `&x`/decay/params/typedefs, rejected conversions); the first three fail on the old compiler.
- All std `.sc` files and `compiler/examples` compile at -O0 and -O2 as before; files without `volatile` emit no new volatile ops.
- `tests/stdlib` `safeguard test`: 9/9. Bare-metal sweep and Unicorn runs: all 14 targets pass.
- At -O2, `std_mem_zero_secure` keeps all its `store volatile` byte/word wipes.

## Notes for reviewers
- The stricter conversion rule is a source-level change: code that passed a `volatile T*` where `T*` is expected now needs a cast. Nothing in std or the examples hit it.
- The Cortex-M VTOR write in `vector_table.sc` is volatile now, but that `#if` branch only compiles once ARM arch macros are predefined — handled separately on `claude/funny-jones-0e4b8c`.
- A generic instantiated with both `volatile T*` and `T*` may share one instance (mono cache keys ignore volatility); nothing in std does this.

author: le-who
body:
💡 **What:** Throttled the global activity event listeners (`mousemove`, `keydown`, `touchstart`, `click`) in `components/Player.tsx` to fire at most once every 200ms. I also set `{ passive: true }` on these listeners.
🎯 **Why:** Rapid continuous events like `mousemove` and `touchstart` fire continuously (e.g., ~60 times a second). Unthrottled, they trigger unnecessary timeout clearing and setting, which blocks the main thread and could delay important UI updates. Non-passive touch listeners can also block native scrolling performance.
📊 **Impact:** Reduces rapid continuous DOM event calls from ~60Hz down to ~5Hz, completely eliminating pointless timeout re-evaluations while retaining perfect UI responsiveness.
🔬 **Measurement:** Open the Chrome DevTools Performance tab, record a profile while wildly wiggling the mouse and tapping the screen over the player component. You will observe significantly fewer long tasks and `setTimeout`/`clearTimeout` calls being invoked by `handleUserActivity`.

Spec: transition-plan-alignment-design

Phase 1 of transition plan alignment (Part B, capex credibility):
- a capex extraction preset (`sch_transition_capex`)
- a curated, cited, owner-signed benchmarks file with its validator and CLI
- a pure ACT D01.a capex score, plus the R&D tests and the redlines
- `GET /api/companies/{ref}/transition` and a sector run list
- a new **Transition** section on the company page

Runs only on demand, through the existing `POST /api/extraction/start`.

**risk:high**: `arp/db/observations.py::decide` changes how facts are recorded for every preset (see "Behaviour change" below). No schema migration, workflow, hook or auth change.

## Owner items

1. **Sign benchmarks v1.** `backend/arp/transition_alignment/data/benchmarks.json` is signed as v1 with `approved_by "<owner, pending approval in this PR>"` (ruling R3). On approval, put your name in `history` in place of that text, or re-sign to v2 with `arp transition-alignment benchmarks sign --approved-by <name>`.
2. **Check AC-47:** `test_ac47_existing_presets_unchanged` pins the existing presets' snapshot.
3. **Wording calls:**
   - `act_levers["hdt.public_charging"]` reads "Depot charging".
   - Capex `see_also` holds the spec table's second sources (ACT Electricity, Generic, Auto). It is neither validated nor served; it can be folded into `method` if you prefer.

## Behaviour change (all presets)

- **What changed:** a **rule-based** not-applicable is now observation-only, like a miss. These are rows that `planning/applicability.py` marks `not_applicable_by_rule` because the company is outside the field's sector rules. They no longer create a fact or replace one (AC-48).
- **Why:** before this, an out-of-scope company got empty "not applicable" facts, and such a row could even replace an accepted value if the company's ISIC changed.
- **What did not change:** a not-applicable stated in a document and approved in review still becomes a fact, as before. Tests: `test_not_applicable_is_observation_only` and `test_document_not_applicable_is_a_value`.
- **How it is carried:** the observation's `method` is `not_applicable_by_rule`, so the fact trail shows that method for these rows. The importer replay applies the same rule.
- **Side effect:** `arp db verify` on a database imported before this change reports each old rule-based N/A fact as a difference. Those facts are not deleted.

## Acceptance coverage (phase 1)

| AC | Test |
|---|---|
| AC-66, AC-2 | `test_ac66_bundled_validates`, `test_ac2_benchmarks_api` |
| AC-3–8, AC-64 | `test_ac3_capex_no_source` … `test_ac64_unknown_lever`, plus `test_ac3_cli` (CLI lines) |
| AC-67, AC-57 | `test_ac67_sign`, `test_ac67_cli`, `test_ac57_startup_refused` |
| AC-9 | `test_ac9`, `test_ac9_api` |
| AC-10–14, AC-70 | `test_ac10` … `test_ac14`, `test_ac70` |
| AC-15, AC-65 | `test_ac15`, `test_ac65`, `test_ac15_ac65_api` |
| AC-16, AC-17, AC-61 | `test_ac16`, `test_ac17`, `test_ac61` |
| AC-19, AC-20 | `test_ac19_ac20`, `test_ac19_api` |
| AC-21 | `test_ac21_no_model_call` |
| AC-22, AC-58 | `test_ac22_ac58_out_of_scope` |
| AC-23 | `test_ac23_run_to_fact` |
| AC-51, AC-44 | e2e `test_transition_section.py`; evaluator in the running app |
| AC-52 | `primaryCitation` unit test; **owed to the evaluator** (click 12% → P2 p.45; needs P2 stored as a file) |
| AC-45, AC-47 (must not change) | `test_ac45_green_fact_unchanged`, `test_ac47_existing_presets_unchanged` |
| AC-48 (must not change) | `test_ac48_out_of_scope_company_extracts_nothing`, `test_ac48_api` (capex preset; the plan-actions preset arrives in phase 2) |

Holdout rows above run here as unit/API tests; the hidden versions run via the Holdout acceptance job. AC-46 starts in phase 2. Holdout note: the root `arp` CLI needs `ARP_POSTGRES_DSN` (existing behaviour), so an AC-66 holdout run must set it or call the sub-app.

## Test changes

- **Existing tests modified:**
  - `backend/tests/test_mutation_check.py`: one added assert that `ARP_TRANSITION_ALIGNMENT_DATA_DIR` is set (R14).
  - `backend/tests/test_fact_rules.py`: two tests added; none removed or weakened.
  - `frontend/tests/company.test.ts`: imports widened; `primaryCitation` and `fmtNumber` tests added.
- **New test files:**
  - `test_presets_transition_capex.py`
  - `test_transition_alignment_benchmarks.py`
  - `test_transition_alignment_capex.py`
  - `db/test_transition_alignment_api.py`
  - `e2e/test_transition_section.py`
  - fixtures under `tests/fixtures/transition_alignment/` (F-TA, BM, snapshot S) and `transition_alignment_helpers.py`.

## Rulings made during the build

| Ruling | Why |
|---|---|
| Plan R1–R14 (in the plan file) | — |
| The rule book has 29 action ids, not the plan's 30; `act_levers` maps all 29 | Matches the rule book and research 13.4(a) |
| R4 basis preference (`""` first) applied once, in the endpoint's fact mapper | Keeps `capex.py` pure |
| A redline is "not breached" only for a real `False`; otherwise "no disclosure"; the latest real Yes/No wins | Spec: a missing redline is never "not breached" |
| Rule-based not-applicable is observation-only (above) | AC-48 |
| Benchmark values must be finite and above 0 | A 0, NaN or Inf crashed scoring |
| Shares are rounded half up in the UI (`fmtNumber`, same as `fmt_number`) | Global rounding rule |

## Known limits (not blocking)

- An edited amount (canonical value cleared, `EUR million`) next to an unedited one (`EUR`) blocks the share computed from amounts. It shows as "not scored", never wrong.
- The percentage fields also carry the currency-unit sentence in their instructions; the phase 3 golden set checks this.
- The R&D "used" figure is computed, so it has no trail button.
- `RULE_NOT_APPLICABLE` repeats a literal used in `applicability.py`, `routing.py` and `schemas/review.py`.
- With an overridden benchmarks dir, the preset scope (bundled, R2) can differ from the endpoint scope.

## Checks

- `ruff` is clean.
- Backend full suite: the only failures are from the environment (no Neo4j DSN, no Playwright headless shell, no `hdbscan`/`botocore`). All `tests/db` pass when run alone.
- Frontend: lint shows 0 errors, `tsc -b` is clean, `npm test` passes 207/207.
- The e2e Transition section test passes, and the impeccable audit found nothing.
- `openwiki/` needs an update (new module, endpoints and page section); the weekly `/context-refresh` regenerates it.

author: thekillermax
body:
## Why this change is needed

DoubleTapReactionHook captured the adapter that installed a getView hook.
Because a method hook is shared by other instances of the same adapter class,
a second conversation could bind its row to a message from the first adapter.
Reinstalling the same method also accumulated callbacks, allowing an older
callback to overwrite the new row's reaction target.

Recycled rows retained their previous message when the next item was null,
unsupported, failed to load, or was rebound while the preference was disabled.

## What changes

- Reserve each resolved getView Method once and release the reservation if hook
  registration fails so a later adapter can retry.
- Read the ListAdapter from the getView callback receiver and bind the message
  actually rendered by that instance.
- Clear the previous message and pending tap state before every row binding,
  including disabled and failed bindings. Only a typed FMessage gets a new
  reaction target.
- Preserve the original touch listener's event delivery and returned handled
  value. Host selectors and the reaction-sender contract are unchanged.

## Validation

qa/test_double_tap_adapter_binding.py compiles the complete production
DoubleTapReactionHook.java. It installs setAdapter/getView callbacks, delivers
synthetic touch events through the production wrapper, and records the exact
message object passed to a synthetic reaction sender.

- Candidate: 11/11 scenarios pass.
- Immutable V38: complete production compilation and all 11 scenarios finish,
  with seven failures, including the wrong adapter/message target.
- Four compiling mutations are detected: remove deduplication (one failure),
  retain recycled identity (four), retain a failed registration reservation
  (one), and restore the captured installer adapter (two).
- Positive cases retain ordinary first-adapter reactions, the original touch
  handler, retry after registration failure and gesture reset across recycling.

See qa/DOUBLE_TAP_ADAPTER_ACCEPTANCE.md for commands and device acceptance.

## Limits

The Android, Xposed, DexKit and sender endpoints are explicit JVM doubles. The
fixture supplies synthetic message/sender types at the reflection boundary and
does not prove discovery in a real host build. No external message or reaction
was sent. Real conversations, native injection, view rendering and delivery
remain device acceptance work. No measured scrolling/latency improvement is
claimed.

## Combined V39 integration evidence

The combined integration commit is `66559468acc0b2f44a1c319ee98f9ed0be27157a` (tree `ad9a9ea304211ff2199624c25e4d6bd5eee25fe2`). Its [final GitHub Actions run](https://github.com/TheKillerMax/WaEnhancerX/actions/runs/39361583696) completed all 15 jobs successfully. The 14 framework groups contain 933 observed JUnit executions, including repetitions across SDKs. All 17 artifact archives were downloaded and checked against GitHub SHA-256 digests and ZIP integrity.

This shared result includes the other V39 proposals and retained V38 changes. The focused results and limits above define this PR's individual evidence; the combined CI result does not establish a full signed APK, real WhatsApp/LSPosed operation or device performance.

body: ## Summary Upgrade the legacy Gorgias package to a **Frigg v2** API module at `packages/v1-ready/gorgias` (`@friggframework/api-module-gorgias@1.0.0`). Shaped like `packages/v1-ready/fathom/`. The old `packages/needs-updating/gorgias/` folder is removed in this PR (Mongoose `manager.js` / models dropped). **Scope rule:** this PR touches only `packages/needs-updating/gorgias/` → `packages/v1-ready/gorgias/`. No root `package-lock.json`, root `package.json`, or other-package edits. ### What the API is / sources [Gorgias](https://gorgias.com) helpdesk **REST API** + **OAuth 2.0** for public apps. Official per-operation OpenAPI fragments are published on the developer site (servers: `https://{domain}.gorgias.com`). `gorgias.openapi.yaml` is Left Hook’s curated subset matching `api.js` 1:1. - Docs: https://developers.gorgias.com/reference/introduction - OAuth: https://developers.gorgias.com/docs/oauth2-authentication-for-creating-apps-with-gorgias - Scopes: https://developers.gorgias.com/docs/oauth2-scopes - HTTP integrations / widgets: https://developers.gorgias.com/docs/create-integrations-and-widgets-programmatically ### Auth | Detail | Value | |---|---| | Method | OAuth 2.0 authorization code | | Authorize / token | `https://{subdomain}.gorgias.com/oauth/authorize` / `/oauth/token` | | Token auth | HTTP Basic (`client_id:client_secret`) | | Access token | 24 hours | | Refresh token | Non-expiring when `offline` is requested | | Identity | `GET /api/account` → `domain` (persisted as `subdomain`) | | Auth form | Collects helpdesk **subdomain** before redirect | Default scope (overridable via `GORGIAS_SCOPE`): `openid email profile offline account:read tickets:read tickets:write customers:read customers:write integrations:read integrations:write` ### Endpoints covered | Client method | HTTP | |---|---| | `getAccount` | `GET /api/account` | | `listTickets` / `getTicket` / `createTicket` / `updateTicket` / `deleteTicket` | `/api/tickets` | | `listCustomers` / `getCustomer` / `createCustomer` / `updateCustomer` / `deleteCustomer` | `/api/customers` | | `listIntegrations` / `getIntegration` / `createIntegration` / `updateIntegration` / `deleteIntegration` | `/api/integrations` (HTTP integrations = webhook-style outbound) | | `listWidgets` / `getWidget` / `createWidget` / `updateWidget` / `deleteWidget` | `/api/widgets` | ### Skipped - Users, teams, tags, macros, rules, views, custom fields, satisfaction surveys, jobs, statistics, apps uninstall, file upload (`/api/upload`) — not required for the core integration cut; available in the official reference if needed later. - Dedicated `/webhooks` resource — **does not exist**; use HTTP integrations (`type: http`) with `http.triggers`. - HubSpot-style Tier-3 `extensions/webhooks/` receiver — Gorgias outbound HTTP integrations call *your* URL; no public signature-verification docs found for inbound callbacks (open question). - Private-app HTTP Basic (email + API key) — module targets OAuth2 public apps. ### Capability manifest `gorgias.capabilities.json` — `capability-manifest/v0.1`, version **1.0.0** (matches package). Objects: `account`, `ticket`, `customer`, `integration`, `widget` with field tags. Every capability `method` exists on `Api`. Webhook subscription management maps to `createIntegration` / `listIntegrations` / `deleteIntegration`. ### Fenestra `gorgias.fenestra.yaml` drafted — Gorgias is listed in `specs/fenestra/PLATFORMS.md` (Customer Support, JSON + Iframe). Covers ticket/customer sidebar extension points and documented template components (`wrapper`, `card`, `list`, `text`, `boolean`, `date`). Validated with `fenestra.js validate` from branch `claude/fenestra-spec-draft-Q367t`: **Valid** (1 warning: no SDKs — expected; widgets are declarative JSON, not an npm host SDK). ### Proof ```text $ cd packages/v1-ready/gorgias && npm test PASS tests/api.test.js PASS tests/definition.test.js PASS tests/spec-sync.test.js Test Suites: 3 passed, 3 total Tests: 28 passed, 28 total ``` Terminal capture artifacts: - `/opt/cursor/artifacts/gorgias-npm-test.txt` - `/opt/cursor/artifacts/gorgias-test-summary.txt` - `/opt/cursor/artifacts/gorgias-frigg-validate.txt` - `/opt/cursor/artifacts/gorgias-fenestra-validate.txt` **frigg validate** (ADR-051 / `feat/frigg-validate`): CLI validates Frigg *app* Definitions, not a standalone api-module. Offline Ajv check against `api-module-definition.schema.json` from frigg@next: - Without `getAuthorizationRequirements` / `modelName` in the serialized object: **PASS** - With them (as in this module / fathom / frontify / skill): **FAIL** (`additionalProperties`) — schema lag; kept the methods per skill + prompt **frigg auth test .**: **pending credentials** (no sandbox client id/secret in this environment). Do not fake. ### Open questions 1. **Root `package-lock.json`:** installing this workspace package locally wants a root lockfile refresh (`@friggframework/core@^2.0.0-next.107`, jest, js-yaml, `@aws-sdk/client-scheduler`). Left out of this PR per module-only scope — maintainers should regenerate/commit the lockfile before publish/CI that relies on the root lock. 2. Should `api-module-definition.schema.json` allow `getAuthorizationRequirements` / `setAuthParams` / `modelName` (sibling modules already use them)? 3. author: yavrsky
body:
## Why

`last_trade_prices_for_tokens` prices every token on a `/markets` or `/events` page. It also runs for the board and for single positions. For every requested token it read and sorted every mirrored print on the tape, which is kept for 30 days. On production (2026-10-19) the tape holds 3.64M rows after 7 days and grows by about 490k a day; `trades` is 1.8 GB. `EXPLAIN` showed two parallel full scans of `trades` and a sort of 1–3M rows, even for a page of 50 markets. With `work_mem` at 4 MB that sort spills to disk. `/markets?limit=500` took 0.75–0.84 s, and the cost grows with the tape, not with the page.

## What changed

- **Query.** `last_trade_prices_for_tokens` now unnests the requested tokens and, for each one, takes the newest print from each side with `ORDER BY MATCH_TIME DESC LIMIT 1`, then the newer of the two:
  - YES on `ASSET_ID`;
  - NO on `MAKER_ASSET_ID` at `1,000,000 - PRICE`, skipping rows written before the NO token existed.

  Same answers as before.
- **Indexes.** Two partial indexes, `(ASSET_ID, MATCH_TIME DESC)` and `(MAKER_ASSET_ID, MATCH_TIME DESC)`, `WHERE STATUS = 'MIRRORED'`. Indexes alone don't help the old query (checked: it still reads every print); the rewrite needs them.
- **Startup.** Startup drops and rebuilds either index if a cancelled `CONCURRENTLY` build left it INVALID. Without a valid index the new query is far slower than the old one.

## Testing

- The full suite passes on top of current main (with #36): 1877 passed, 0 failed.
- New tests, each failing before its change:
  - the two index definitions;
  - a 12,000-print tape where `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` shows the scans of `trades` reading at most 2 rows per token, counting rows they filter out, with the right YES and NO prices;
  - an index marked INVALID is rebuilt at startup.
- **Local benchmark** (3.6M prints over 13,000 markets, one market with 15% of the tape, `work_mem` 4 MB, warm):

  | Tokens | Old | New |
  |---|---|---|
  | 100 | 0.7–0.9 s | 0.65 ms |
  | 2,000 | 1.7–6.7 s (sort spills ~160 MB) | 10–20 ms |

  Old and new returned identical rows (2,000 of 2,000).
- **Production planner check.** Production `pg_stats` gives `n_distinct` 6,478 for both token columns, far from the point (about 20) where the planner would prefer walking the time index instead.

## Cost

- Each new index is about 390 MB at today's 3.6M rows and about 1.6 GB at 30 days; production has 48 GB free.
- `idx_trades_mirrored_maker_asset_id` is now superseded by the new maker index and can be dropped in a follow-up.

## Deploy

The indexes must exist before the new code starts. Otherwise the startup migration builds them inside its transaction, which blocks writes to `trades` and delays startup.

1. Back up as usual (`deploy/backup.sh`). Check `df -h`: each build needs about its index size again in temporary space.
2. Build both indexes while the current API keeps running. Do it from tmux or nohup: a dropped session cancels the build and leaves an INVALID index.
   ```bash
   docker exec -i agentpit-db psql -U agentpit -d agentpit -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 <<'SQL'
   SET maintenance_work_mem = '256MB';
   CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_trades_mirrored_asset_time
     ON trades(ASSET_ID, MATCH_TIME DESC) WHERE STATUS = 'MIRRORED';
   CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_trades_mirrored_maker_asset_time
     ON trades(MAKER_ASSET_ID, MATCH_TIME DESC) WHERE STATUS = 'MIRRORED';
   SQL
   ```
   Each took 20–23 s locally at 3.6M rows. Two `CONCURRENTLY` statements in one `psql -c` string fail ("cannot run inside a transaction block"), so feed them through stdin as above.
3. Check that both indexes are valid. This must print nothing:
   ```bash
   docker exec agentpit-db psql -U agentpit -d agentpit -Atc "SELECT indexrelid::regclass FROM pg_index WHERE indrelid = 'trades'::regclass AND NOT indisvalid"
   ```
   If it prints a name, run `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY <name>;` and repeat step 2.
4. Deploy `api` as usual (build, then `up -d`). The startup `IF NOT EXISTS` lines find the indexes and skip the build.
5. Verify:
   - `EXPLAIN` of the new query for a few tokens shows `Index Scan using idx_trades_mirrored_asset_time` and `..._maker_asset_time` under `Limit`;
   - `/markets?limit=500` in the Caddy log is well under the 0.75–0.84 s it takes today.
6. Rollback: the previous image runs unchanged with the indexes in place.

author: ghazmotiebipro
body:
## Problem
The platform had no volume or liquidity reading. There was no same-time RVOL, no volume profile, no prior-day breakout volume check and no sweep detection. The published chart bars carry no volume, and the stock chart report is near its 700 KB cap.

## Implementation
**New `options_radar/volume_liquidity.py`** (pure, research-only) runs on the **same completed** Yahoo 15M/1D bars that the stock charts use. All definitions are disclosed in the output.

| Signal | Definition |
|---|---|
| RVOL | Same-time cumulative 15M volume ÷ median of ≥3 prior sessions with the same completed-bar count. Never compared with full-day volume. HIGH ≥1.5, LOW <0.7. Withheld when history is insufficient. |
| Volume profile | POC/VAH/VAL per session and as a 5-day composite. An **estimate**: each bar's volume is spread uniformly over its range (24 bins, 70% value area). Method and bin size are published. |
| VWAP | Session OHLCV approximation, plus where the price sits relative to it. |
| Opening range | First two 15M bars (09:30–10:00): ABOVE, INSIDE or BELOW. |
| Gap | Session open vs the prior close. |
| Breakout | A close beyond the prior-day high/low is `*_VOLUME_CONFIRMED` when the crossing bar's volume is ≥1.5× the median 15M bar volume of prior sessions. It is `FAILED_*` when the price closed back inside. |
| Sweep proxy | One completed bar pierced the prior-day level and closed back inside. Labelled a price-action proxy. |

**Arabic reading (`read_ar`):** it never claims accumulation, distribution or order flow as fact. Every reading ends by stating that no order-book or trade data exists.

**Publishing:**
- `build_stock_watch_charts.py` takes a new `--liquidity-output` option.
- The stock-watch-charts workflow writes `runtime/public/data/liquidity_map.json`; it is the **single writer** of that file.
- The chart report is unchanged, so the size cap isn't affected.
- `order_book_available`, `trade_prints_available` and `quote_spread_available` are all `false`.

## Tests actually run
- New `tests/test_volume_liquidity.py`:
  - POC lands where volume concentrates, and the value area is ordered
  - RVOL uses same time-of-day, gives exactly 3.0 against 3 prior sessions, and is withheld with too little history
  - breakout confirmed vs unconfirmed vs failed
  - a one-bar sweep is distinguished from a failed breakout
  - insufficient bars fail closed
  - the reading never claims order flow
- Integration test: `collect(liquidity_out=…)` fills a row for each symbol it publishes, withholds RVOL on one session of history, and the report schema carries the inference flags.
- `pytest -q`: 1124 passed, 1 skipped. All `tests/*.cjs` pass. Critical Ruff gate passes.

## Runtime status
CODED + TESTED. To verify after merge: the push-triggered stock-watch-charts run publishes `liquidity_map.json` on bot-state.

## Remaining risks
Yahoo 15M volume is unofficial and may be delayed. The profile is an OHLCV estimate, not traded-at-price volume. Display in the terminal comes in a follow-up PR.

author: khalidadan
body:
Fixes a 0.12.0 regression from #83: resizing the window made the reader go blank, and it stayed blank.

**Why:** a new layout spec (a resize, a new text size) cleared the layout engine's queue as well as its cache. The page asks for chapters only when *where you are* changes, not when the window does, so nothing asked for the chapter on screen again.

**Fix** (`reader/layout-engine.ts`):
- The engine remembers every section asked for, most needed first. A new spec lays them all out again in that order without being asked.
- Until a chapter arrives for the new spec, its last layout stands in for it (`get` falls back to it, `isFresh` tells them apart). The text reflows a moment behind the window's edge and never disappears.
- The snapshot saves only a chapter laid out for the current spec.
- The engine takes an optional layout function, so its queue can be tested without a worker. `test/layout-engine.test.ts` covers the order, laying out again after a new spec, the stand-in, and a drag of many sizes.

**Checked in the built app** (`e2e-resize`: a window drag of 20 sizes 30 ms apart, every animation frame watched for visible text)

| | Before | After, 1× | After, 6× CPU |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pages: frames with no text | all, and blank for good | 0 of 206 | 0 of 93 |
| Scroll: frames with no text | all, and blank for good | 0 of 205 | 0 of 68 |
| Text reflowed to the final size (no line wider than its column) | — | yes, within 1 ms of rest | yes, within 15 ms |
| Back to the original size | blank | text | text |

body:
flatpak\047s OCI token flow keeps its system cache under /var/tmp, hardcoded (it ignores $TMPDIR). Image builds never boot, so systemd-tmpfiles never creates it, and installs from the OCI tuna-os remote fail:

> error: Failed to get tokens for ref: opendir(/var/tmp): No such file or directory

Ostree remotes (Flathub, file:// installer) never take that path, which is why every earlier flatpak in the step installs fine and only tuna-os refs fail. The fix is one line in install-flatpaks.sh alongside the existing machine-id / D-Bus / TMPDIR container-build shims, plus a skill note in docs/skills/local-testing.md.

author: lll-peanut
body:
# Why

流式 LLM 采集路径存在重复预算扫描、活跃连接误驱逐和 SSE 重复解析，消耗 CPU pacing 预算并影响采集完整性。本次减少这些重复工作，同时保留字节预算和 CPU pacing。

## What changed

- 增量维护 HTTP/1、HTTP/2 retained-bytes，减少逐事件全量扫描。
- 同步更新连接活跃顺序，保护最近活跃连接及 keepalive 请求；默认连接容量提高至 128。
- 资源处置只发送带原因的元数据级 incomplete 记录，并抑制已处置流的尾部重建。
- 使用借用 SSE frame、快速边界扫描及已解析 JSON，减少复制、分配和序列化往返。
- 增加 FFI 压测支持、行为回归测试，并同步中英文文档。

## Related issue

Closes #8214

## User / Agent impact

容量紧张时优先保护在途请求，减少采集不完整和重复 incomplete 事件。默认 CPU 预算保持 25%，支持已验证的 32/64 并发流式负载。

## Risk and compatibility

- Public CLI, API, configuration, or documented behavior changed
- Privileged or security-sensitive behavior changed
- Cross-component contract changed
- Migration or rollback guidance is needed

默认连接容量调整为 128，显式配置仍然生效。FFI ABI 和 eBPF 探针保持兼容。DashScope 未知输出模式保留精确前缀判断，保证累计与增量模式切换兼容。

1 MiB 请求、容量 128 的场景仍有待排查的 RSS 增长；内存收益不作为所有负载下的保证。

## Validation

自动检查：

- Rust workspace 单元测试、集成测试、doctests 通过。
- Python：499 passed，22 subtests passed。
- Rust formatting、workspace Clippy、架构边界、SQLite 入口检查通过。
- 无 server feature 构建、enforcer 构建及产物校验通过。
- 打包检查、中英文文档检查和网站构建通过。
- 增量行覆盖率 89%，通过 diff-cover --fail-under=85 门禁，包含 Rust、Python 和 C FFI 宿主。

Linux 实机 FFI 压测使用冻结候选库 after-r3.so。以下仅列候选库结果；流式负载均运行 300 秒，每路 100 output tokens/s、每响应 1000 tokens。

| 场景 | 并发 / 连接容量 | 平均 CPU | P95 CPU | Peak CPU | 平均 / 峰值 RSS | 完整且 token 正确 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Compact，4 KiB 请求 | 32 / 128 | 9.39% | 10.97% | 10.98% | 152.42 / 152.61 MiB | 960/960 |
| R1 churn，1 MiB 请求 | 32 / 32 | 11.83% | 28.94% | 32.91% | 221.70 / 225.45 MiB | 960/960 |
| R1 churn，1 MiB 请求 | 32 / 128 | 11.85% | 24.93% | 32.92% | 234.78 / 244.63 MiB | 960/960 |
| 保留 raw SSE，1 MiB 请求 | 8 / 256 | 7.19% | 12.97% | 17.96% | 184.65 / 190.22 MiB | 240/240 |
| 25% pacing，4 KiB 请求 | 32 / 256 | 9.65% | 10.98% | 11.98% | 153.87 / 154.40 MiB | 960/960 |
| 25% pacing，4 KiB 请求 | 64 / 256 | 16.59% | 17.97% | 18.97% | 155.43 / 156.31 MiB | 1920/1920 |

上述场景均为 VALID，ring buffer、channel 和 FFI 丢事件均为 0。

- R1 容量 32：54 个 churn 请求均返回仅元数据的容量拒绝记录，正式请求全部完整，LRU 驱逐为 0。
- R1 容量 128：54 个 churn 请求全部正常完成，没有容量拒绝或 LRU 驱逐。
- 真实 HTTPS fallback：覆盖非 LLM、无法解析的 LLM 请求，以及 typed/v2 回调；开启时均收到 4/4 个正确回调，关闭时均为 0。

实机压测结果对应上述冻结库；整合最新 main 后的代码通过了 Rust workspace 测试。

## Documentation and rollback

更新中英文配置、CLI、数据存储说明、payload memory 设计文档及 benchmark 使用说明。

回滚可撤销本次采集路径改动；CPU pacing 继续作为独立保护机制。无需数据库迁移。

author: jitokim
body:
Closes #402.

A graph where one node has two or more `handoff: session` children is now refused at load (`run`, `lint`, `run --dry-run`, `resume`, and auto's planned-graph validation). The children would resume and write the same session. Run one after another, the later child inherits its sibling's conversation and, with #398's cost correction, its spend. Run in parallel, both branches land in one session file. The error names the parent and the children and gives the fixes: `handoff: artifact` on all but one child, or chain them. A run started before this change with such a graph cannot be resumed. `resume` says so and tells the user to start a new run. There's no snapshot exemption, as the maintainer decided.

Docs that state the session-handoff rules now carry the new rule: DESIGN.md, CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and plugin/agents/oh-my-graph.md. The changelog fragment is filed under "Changed". No shipped, example or testdata graph has two session children of one parent (checked before the change).

## Before / after
