author: ngoziobidigwe212
body:
Closes #1311
Closes #1312
Closes #1313
Closes #1314

## Summary

Four production-hardening fixes, one commit per issue:

1. **Graceful shutdown** — SIGTERM/SIGINT drain in-flight Prisma work and close Prisma + Redis cleanly instead of severing them.
2. **Granular API-key scopes** — mutating routes enforce the permission the key was actually granted and return an RFC 9457 403 naming the missing scope.
3. **Central CSRF enforcement** — cookie-session mutations are rejected at the proxy edge without a valid double-submit token, and `api-client` attaches tokens automatically.
4. **Spending-limit windows** — daily limits reset by ledger day (including multi-day inactivity), and batches are pre-checked atomically.

## Commits

- `efc608b` — `fix(lifecycle): drain Prisma and Redis before exit on SIGTERM`
- `fdf5bfe` — `feat(api): enforce granular scopes on mutating API-key routes`
- `05a7da9` — `fix(csrf): enforce double-submit tokens at the proxy edge`
- `1ca8bef` — `fix(contracts): reset daily spend limits by ledger day`

## Changes

### 1. Graceful shutdown (`src/lib/lifecycle.ts`)

- Registers SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers once on Node startup via `src/instrumentation.ts`; skipped outside production so `next dev` hot reload is unaffected.
- Stops new background work (`isShuttingDown()` / `assertAcceptingOperations()`), waits for in-flight operations up to `SHUTDOWN_GRACE_PERIOD_MS` (default 5000 ms), then runs cleanup tasks.
- `src/lib/prisma.ts` tracks each query in-flight and registers `$disconnect()`; `src/lib/redis.ts` registers a real `QUIT`.
- Structured `Graceful shutdown started` / `complete` logs, idempotent shutdown across concurrent signals, per-task timeouts.
- Documented in `docs/architecture.md`; env var added to `.env.example`.

### 2. Granular API scopes

- Added `payments:write`, `batches:create`, `escrow:write`, `escrow:release`, and `webhooks:write` alongside the legacy scopes.
- `requireScope(request, scope, auth)` in `src/lib/api-route.ts` returns an `application/problem+json` 403 with `code: INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`, `missingScope`, and `requiredScopes`. Browser sessions (owner auth) are exempt; only API keys are scope-limited.
- Enforced on `POST /api/batches`, `POST /api/escrows`, and `POST`/`PATCH`/`DELETE /api/webhooks`.
- Updated API-key UI labels and `docs/openapi.yaml`.

### 3. CSRF

- Added edge-safe `src/lib/csrf-token.ts`; `src/proxy.ts` now rejects session-cookie mutations without a matching CSRF cookie/header before the handler runs. API-key and cron-secret callers bypass.
- `src/lib/api-client.ts` mints the token from `GET /api/csrf`, attaches `x-csrf-token`, and retries once on a stale token.
- CSRF cookie is now `SameSite=Lax`, `HttpOnly`, `Secure` in production.

### 4. Spending limits

- `spending_limit.rs` derives the day/month window from `timestamp / 86_400` and resets accumulators when the recorded window precedes the current ledger window.
- `create_batch` totals valid entries first, checks the whole sum against remaining daily/monthly capacity, and reverts before writing any payment.
- Emits `SpendingLimitExceeded { user, requested, available, daily_limit, timestamp }` and returns `PaymentError::SpendingLimitExceeded`.
- Added `contracts/ophirpay/tests/spending_limit_test.rs` covering day-boundary resets, multi-day gaps, atomic batch rejection, and read-only checks.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` ✅ (includes error-catalog parity check)
- ESLint on all changed TypeScript files ✅
- Targeted Vitest suites: 238 passed ✅
- `cargo test` in `contracts/ophirpay`: all suites pass, including 6 new spending-limit tests and the updated 317-variant error uniqueness check ✅
- Full `npm test` in this environment: 3579 passed, 29 failed. The failures are in environment-dependent suites that also fail on unmodified `main` here (`prisma-pool-metrics`, `endpoint-metrics` snapshot, `lib-coverage-6`, `api-routes/fee-rbac-policy-contracts`, `api-routes/analytics-audit-metrics-stats`); causes include the local `DATABASE_URL` being set and Prisma 6.19 exposing native `$metrics` output instead of the expected fallback snapshot.

## Notes

- The repository has no `src/middleware.ts`; Next.js 16 uses `src/proxy.ts` as the middleware entrypoint, so CSRF enforcement lives there.
- The repository's architecture doc is `docs/architecture.md` (lowercase), not `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`; the lifecycle section was added there.
- There is no `/api/escrow` or `/api/escrow/release` route in this tree; `escrow:write` is enforced on `POST /api/escrows`, and `escrow:release` is registered for the release flow when that route is added.

body:
A pipeline compiled from code carries no layout, so every node arrives at one position and the editor drew them stacked. Laying them out to see them counted as an edit: after saving a Git-managed pipeline through `gitSave`, the editor returned to the pipeline as it is and still said "Unsaved changes".

- `arrangeStacked` (document.ts): lays out nodes when there are several and all share one position; otherwise returns them unchanged.
- `useDocument`: applies it on load and on every reset, which stay clean. `change(fn, history, view)`: a view-only change leaves a clean document clean (a dirty one stays dirty).
- `EditorPage`: with `gitSave`, dragging and auto-layout are view-only and stay out of the undo history. Without `gitSave` nothing changes: positions are saved as before.

Tests: `useDocument.test.ts` (new, renderHook) and `arrangeStacked` cases in `document.test.ts`; each fails with its part of the fix removed.

author: hsbt
body:
On macOS with a static libruby, the default of `./configure`, every mkmf link check takes about 2 seconds. clang compiles and links `conftest.c` in one invocation, and since `CFLAGS` carries `-g` it then runs `dsymutil`, which reads the DWARF of every object pulled in from `libruby-static.a`. The link itself is not slow.

This passes `-g0` to link checks on darwin only. On an M1 Max a single `have_func` check goes from 2.2 s to 0.17 s, `gem install bigdecimal` from 12.0 s to 3.4 s, and reconfiguring all 120 extensions from 45 s to 17 s. The generated `Makefile` and `extconf.h` are byte-identical for every extension.

#16660 targets the same slowdown by splitting compile and link, which avoids `dsymutil` too (0.19 s per check here). This keeps the single invocation and leaves `try_link0` as is.

## What this adds

A time-series view of the reviews: does a product that drew poor reviews early get better later, and do its negative reviews fade?

- `src/timeseries.py`: compares each product's first and last third of reviews, draws product timelines and a recovery curve, and has a CLI (`--list`, `--asin`, `--top`)
- `notebooks/07_time_series`: platform trend, product timelines, the recovery test, stars vs text sentiment, and sensitivity to the definitions
- `tests/test_timeseries.py`: runs on synthetic reviews, no download needed
- `README.md`: documents the new notebook, CLI and tests

## Method note

Products picked for a bad start improve somewhat by chance (regression to the mean). The notebook therefore repeats the whole analysis on copies where each product's ratings are shuffled across its own timeline, and only improvement beyond that counts.

body:
Closes #528 (ARCH-02a). Docs only: zero production bytes (`git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD -- server/src agent/src shared pwa ui ccd deploy` prints nothing).

## What changed

**`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-10-architecture-ddd-clean-solid.md`**
- (a) **Timer rule** under L3: "A deadline timer inside one adapter call is L3; schedulers and pollers are L4." Where the handle lives decides which: a local of one call, or a handle that is never kept (`setTimeout(...).unref()`, `new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, ms))`), is a deadline; an object field or module scope is a scheduler or poller. A timer is `setTimeout`/`setInterval`; `setImmediate` is a yield and decides no ring. A function a scheduler calls on each tick is not a poller, and a poll whose stop handle goes back to its caller is that caller's to schedule (so `io.ts`'s tail poll is a deadline and `io.ts` stays L3). L4 owns "schedulers and pollers" instead of "timers".
- **The timer rule is a ring fact, not just prose:** the server L3 predicate catches a file that holds a deadline timer and the L4 predicate a scheduler or poller; the PWA predicates do the same. So no file gets one ring from the predicates and another from the sentence. This moves `inject/send.ts`, `livestate.ts` and `shutdownseal.ts` from L1 to L3, and `pwa/src/lib/ws.ts` (reconnect timer on `this.timer`) from L3 to L4.
- (b) **`.mjs` carve-out** under L0 lists every `node:*` module it allows: `node:crypto`, `node:fs`, `node:url` (what `shared/mark.mjs` and `shared/modelenv.mjs` import on `main`).
- (c) **Contexts 7 Update control plane** (`update/`), **8 Auth & box token** (`auth/`, `token/`), **9 Docs** (`docs/`), each with its language and its allowed dependencies. The dependency lists were grepped from every import in each directory on `main`, so nothing they import today is missing (C7: `coord/store.ts`'s types and `NODE_ID_RE`, `coord/token.ts`'s `checkMailToken`/`MAIL_TOKEN_HEADER` at its routes, `fastify` in L4; C8: K's `refuse.ts`, `coord/store.ts`'s `NODE_ID_RE`, `fastify`, `node:*` as the ring rules allow). A **K** row covers the kernels and platform files; `remote/client.ts` is named as K's agent link, an L4 platform file, not an adapter.
- (d) **"Deciding a file's ring and context"**: server and PWA ring predicates; the header declaration rule (outward only), its grammar widened to `— Lx`, `ring Lx`, `is Lx` and `Lx <ring noun>` so `update/converge.ts`, `token/link.ts` and `accounts/audit.ts` are read as they state; a sentence that a ring pin (e.g. the docs ring) may be stricter than these rules inside its own directory but never looser; and one path table between `ring-context-map` markers. `stopDone.ts`/`stopDoneSweep.ts` are in **C4** (the consolidation spec's §1, §2.2 and §3 put stop-done next to hibernation), and `fleetstate.ts` is in **C1** (the consolidation spec's C1 port).
- (e) **Status tables**, one row per increment and per enforcement item, each naming its test file or ARCH ticket. The stale "still open" lines were re-verified on `main` by symbol: all five `CoordStore` delivery writers carry `state NOT IN ${TERMINAL_DELIVERY_SQL}`; `bumpReplayCount` answers `counted | terminal` and `FleetWatcher.sweepMail` consumes it (`bumped.state === 'counted'`); `markDelivered` still returns `void` (ARCH-15, #532).

**`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-19-ccrc-consolidation-wave-design.md`**: §2.1 quotes the adopted wording; C7 to C9 point at the 08-10 contexts.

**`CLAUDE.md`**: the "Rings / bounded contexts" bullet carries the spec's timer, `.mjs` and PWA sentences word for word. The hunk (lines 250-263) is line-disjoint from #842 and #867 (both lines 7-13); #434 is not touched.

**`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-19-consolidation-w0-pins.md`**: Task C0h (Files, Steps, doc checks, mutation table, Verify), **D-6000** defined once, **D-6001** (departure: lands standalone instead of riding the superseded #434). 6002 issued and unused.

D-6000 records two rules beyond the ticket's wording: `node:path`/`node:url`/`node:util`/`node:crypto` stay allowed in L1; and a file acting only through handed deps may declare its ring in its header, outward only. **Fourteen** files rely on the latter (thirteen by header: `hibernateSweep.ts`, `stopDoneSweep.ts`, `coord/mirror.ts`, `coord/heldFor.ts`, `turnmark.ts`, `turnverdict.ts`, `fleetidentity.ts`, `update/catalogue.ts`, `update/inventory.ts`, `update/converge.ts`, `token/link.ts`, `accounts/audit.ts`, `docs/cache.ts`; plus `docs/ccdsource.ts` by `DOCS_RING_ROLES`). One inward declaration is refused: `accounts/ops.ts` (port L2 next to two L3 arms → L3).

A throwaway checker (`map-check.mjs`, not committed; ARCH-04 stage 4 is the committed assertion) parses the spec's table and applies the written ring rules, timers included, to every non-test file under `server/src` and `pwa/src`.

**Rings are exclusive by construction** (each predicate is an ordered "any other file" clause), so "0 files with two rings" is not evidence and is not claimed as such. What the checker measures for rings is coverage, plus a **header audit**: every header that names a ring token without an accepted declaration is listed and was read by hand. On this branch each such token is a reference to another file's ring or to a part of the file (e.g. "(`coord/stall.ts`, L1)", "the L4 half"), except two files whose comments call them adapters but state no ring in an accepted form, `coord/store.ts` and `fleet.ts`; D-6000 names them as deciding L1 by rule (follow-up below). author: erincena
body:
The loading screen showed the bundled LOADING picture under the stock progress_bar sweep. Once the main menu has been shown, it now shows the real ring, read from the player's `ui.map`, under the same sweep: the original loader, drawn with the real ring.

## What it does

- **Scene from the player's files at runtime.** When a map change leaves the main menu (`halo_loading_begin`, before the old map is disposed of), `port/linux/game/loading_scene.c` reads the ui map's ring as the game draws it: the most detailed geometry from its vertex and index buffers, the textures the texture cache holds, and the sky's light. It goes to the presenter in one block (`loading_scene.h`, `XGPU_STREAM_LOADING_SCENE`), which validates every count and offset before use.
- **No Microsoft art shipped.** Nothing is read from disk. Nothing of the map's is kept in the repository or the releases. Without a scene (the first load, before the menu) the bundled picture is drawn as before, bit for bit.
- **One renderer for every backend.** The presenter draws the ring on the processor into the picture's 640x480 image (`loading_ring.h`). Vulkan (Linux, Android, Steam Frame, win64), Metal and the in-process OpenGL backend all show it without pipelines of their own.
- **The look, matched to the picture:**
  - **Still.** The ring does not move. The sweep and its trail are all that moves.
  - **Framing.** The stock ring is framed as the picture shows it, from the camera found by matching the picture's ring silhouette to the drawn one. Another ui map's ring falls back to the menu's camera.
  - **Background.** The ring is shown against black, without the menu's sky.
  - **Depth.** The far side is softened by a depth blur; the near edge stays sharp.
  - **Colour.** A narrow band of hues about the picture's blue, cyan to violet, by the ring's own colour. It has the picture's grain and a few cyan, lavender and near-white specks in the detail, matched to measured hue and saturation statistics of the original loader.
  - **What the sweep lights.** The trail is fed the ring etched the way the picture is. The band acts as a light behind the ring, so the rim and detail flare as it passes.
  - **Idle.** Between sweeps the ring stays dimly in view (about 9%).
  - **Unchanged.** The sweep's own maths is the stock one. The feedback blur is now summed row first; it gives the same sums, and the picture's frames are bit-identical to master's.

## VR

- **A world-locked window.** The scene is a stereo pair on a window in the world, 8 m in front of where the head faced as the load began. It is level, 4:3, and as wide as the picture's camera saw. Each eye gets its own quad layer (`vr_host_layers.hud_stereo`), so the compositor holds it still on every frame whatever the loader's own rate.
- **The reveal.** It starts flat: both eyes see the same picture. Over the first sweep the eyes move apart to the tracked eye positions (`host_vr_loading_eyes`), each with an off-axis view through the window. The ring is found far behind the glass at eight times the game's scale, while the sweep's light and "LOADING..." stay on the window plane. The window's edges fade into the dark, and the far side of the ring is softened slightly.
- **Into the level.** The level's first pictures fade up out of the dark over 0.6 s (`vr_loading_fade_draw`, the eyes' tint). The HUD stays lit.
- **Without a scene** the old flat panel is used.

## Sound

Unchanged, as the original does it. Menu sounds fade out over 0.3 s at the map change. The loading screen's own choir drone still plays, swelling with the progress.

The load's progress is also passed to the presenter (`XGPU_STREAM_LOADING_PROGRESS`), so the picture fades out as a load completes, as the original's draws did.

## Cost

Measured on an M2 at 60 Hz, all on the presenter thread:
- **Before** (bundled picture): 3.8 ms a frame.
- **After, flat screen:** 4.2 ms a frame. The ring is redrawn every other step (30 Hz).
- **After, VR:** about 6 ms per 60 Hz step. Between steps the headset's frames reuse the pictures already drawn.
- **Load time is not affected.** Reading the scene at the map change takes about a millisecond and reads nothing from disk.

## Diagnostics

- `HALO_LOADING_SCENE_DUMP=<file>` writes the scene block as the presenter receives it.
- `HALO_LOADING_CAPTURE_DIR` now works on Metal too.
- `HALO_LOADING_CAPTURE_EVERY=<frames>` captures every that many frames.

These are documented in `port/assets/loading/README.md`.

## Testing

- **On this Mac:** `ninja macos` builds, and the game was run here on Metal from the main menu into a30 (co-op) and Blood Gulch, with the loading frames captured.
- **New tests:** `tools/test_loading_ring.py` covers scene validation, drawing, DXT decoding, the colour band, giving the picture back when the scene is cleared, VR starting flat and finding its depth, and the fade on completion.
- **Updated tests:** `test_preparation.py` and `test_progress_ownership.py` for the new calls. `test_loading_art.py` passes unchanged.
- **CI is green on every platform,** including the Steam Frame and Linux VR builds.
- **VR has not been run on a headset.** No OpenXR runtime was available here.

body: ## What this changes After viewing a planet on the Interstellar Map, HTML text everywhere in MekHQ lost its default styling, so Markdown in the biography editor preview (and elsewhere) rendered as plain text: no bold, italics, heading sizes or list bullets. This restores normal rendering. `HTMLEditorKit.setStyleSheet` replaces the default style sheet shared by every `HTMLEditorKit` in the application, not just one kit. `PlanetViewPanel` installed an empty dossier style sheet that way, wiping Swing's default HTML styles for every pane created afterwards. `ImmersiveDialogCore` used the same call: it kept the defaults but leaked its transparent-background and paragraph-margin overrides globally and chained a new sheet onto the shared one on every call. Both now add their rules to the pane's own document style sheet, which inherits the Swing defaults. Side effect: planet dossier text now inherits the standard HTML styles, so Markdown bold and headings in planet descriptions render too. The dossier's own colours and paragraph spacing still apply. Fixes #10542 ## Testing - Loaded a campaign, viewed a planet on the Interstellar Map, then edited a personnel biography: the Markdown preview and the saved biography render headings, bold, italics and lists correctly. On `main`, the same steps reproduce the plain-text preview. - Added `ImmersiveDialogSizingTest.configuredHtmlDoesNotChangeSharedDefaultStyleSheet`; it fails without the fix and passes with it. - `./gradlew :MekHQ:spotlessCheck :MekHQ:checkstyleMain :MekHQ:checkstyleTest`: passed. - `./gradlew :MekHQ:test`: passed. ## Screenshot After fix, markdown renders again correctly: ## What is not proven yet No automated test covers `PlanetViewPanel.createHtmlTextPane`, which is private; that change was only checked manually in game. --- - [x] This PR is focused on one issue or RFE. author: chrislee0223
body:
## Goal
Evaluate whether VeInvite can safely increase rewards to legitimate users without weakening immutable reservations, Sybil clearance, cohort budget caps, or late-reward protection.

## Current production evidence (read-only, 2026-10-20)
- 44 gross PAID referrals in reward cohorts 114–120; 27 post-payout invalidated, **17 currently recognized**.
- Only four cohorts are >=21 days after end; they contain 9 currently valid payouts and 20 still-ACTIVATING referrals (right-censored).
- Forecast history currently learns recent individual reward batches as `[1,1,1,1,1,1,1,1]`, not cohorts; do not use that as a clean ground truth for real payout adjustment.
- Cohort 120: 5 gross paid, 5 BLOCKED pre-payout, 4 ACTIVATING; `1329.665272` B3TR allocated to cohort, `650.384120` B3TR lifetime committed.

## Changes
- Add **pure, read-only** historical-cohort validity/calibration audit and conservative counterfactual quote comparer; fail closed when insufficient mature cohorts, legitimate payments, or unresolved backlog is high.
- Add regression test with anonymized aggregate production evidence, strict exclusion of post-payout invalidations, exact wei arithmetic, physical/cohort capacity limits, future entrant sensitivity, and no integration with any production reservation/payout routes.
- **No** production DB changes, no migrations/cron, no reward formula change, no payout/reservation change, no UI changes or new admin pages.

## Explicit rollout gate
Do not merge or enable new payout formulas based on these seven preliminary cohorts. Only consider a carefully scoped future policy change after sufficient independent cohorts, delayed-completion liabilities, Sybil appeals and adversarial worst-case replays have been validated.

This draft is research/QA only.

author: ashesfall
body:
Every agent job in the fleet failed for a full working day while the test suite stayed green. A large change was merged and deployed against the outage and nothing improved, because the change addressed the reporting path and never touched the line that was firing. Nothing in the pipeline ran an agent job, so nothing could tell.

Two layers are added. One runs a real job on the real fleet after each deploy. The other establishes that the tests watching agent behaviour are green for a reason.

End-to-end tests with the oracle outside the process 
-----------------------------------------------------

AgentJobEndToEndTest runs a coding agent job the whole way through and asks only what is observable from outside: did the work reach the remote? Every assertion reads a bare git repository standing in for origin, never the job's own accessors — a job can be made to return any string, but it cannot make a commit appear in a remote without doing the work.

One thing is substituted: the model. tools/ci/agent-e2e/fake-agent.sh emits a real stream-json transcript and makes real edits. Everything above that process boundary is production code — the runner's command line, its NDJSON parsing, the MCP init-event handling, phase dispatch, staging guardrails, commit and push. Existing unit tests stub the runner itself, which is why the runner's handling of an init event reporting a server as not connected was invisible to them.

Two of the eight scenarios cover the path where the harness itself destroys the session's output: an agent that makes its own git commit trips the tampering detector, and the revert discards what that commit held. Unlike every other drop there is nothing left afterwards — no working tree holding the changes, no commit, nothing for a later session to recover. The only artefact is the report, so the test pins the status to FAILED specifically rather than to "not SUCCESS": the difference between FAILED and DEGRADED is the difference between "this job lost your work" and "this job finished with a caveat", and a fleet dashboard is read at that granularity.

A fault catalogue, because green is not evidence
------------------------------------------------

The test named for the outage passed while the outage was live. The job it constructed never configured an ar-manager URL or token, and the policy under test is only reachable when both are set. It was green and covered nothing, and the whole pipeline agreed with it.

tools/ci/agent-e2e/faults/ holds defects as patches, each naming the test that must fail when it is applied. run-fault-catalogue.sh applies each to a scratch worktree and requires the declared outcome. Seven faults are included: the outage policy, the base-branch test-method lock, the dropped-work reporting, the commit-message-with-nothing-published rule, the harness's two missing-message fallbacks, the tampering revert's report, and the restart that recovers from it. Two of them point at the same test, one per assertion, so neither half of it can quietly stop being checked; two more point at the paired tampering scenarios, because each of those scenarios alone permits the defect the other catches.

Three properties of the runner are load-bearing:

- The verdict comes from the surefire XML, never Maven's exit code. Maven exits 0 for a test that does not exist and for a run that was skipped; an earlier version of this script reported a fault "undetected" when nothing had run. "Did not run" is now a third outcome, distinct from pass and fail.
- It tests the working tree rather than HEAD, since building from HEAD excluded the very test a new fault is written to validate.
- It is two-sided. One entry is a control whose patch changes no behaviour and whose test must still pass. Without it, a runner printing "detected" unconditionally would satisfy every entry forever while verifying nothing — the same failure the catalogue exists to detect, one level up. The runner refuses to report success on a full run when no control is present.

A post-deploy canary
--------------------

The outage was environmental: ar-manager did not connect from the agent host. No in-repo test sees that. post-deploy-canary.sh submits a genuine job through the controller's submit endpoint, lets the deployed fleet run it, and checks the git remote for a nonce it generated.

The controller's job status is the thing that lied, so it is never the evidence. A job reporting success while publishing nothing is raised as its own distinct error, because that combination means something worse than an honest failure. A submission the controller skips or rejects is also fatal here: no job ran, the deploy is unverified, and reporting "nothing went wrong" as "the thing worked" is the substitution being guarded against.

The canary branch is deliberately not named ci/*, since that prefix grants permissions ordinary branches do not have. The branch is never reset, so its log becomes the record of every deploy proven to produce a working agent.

The verifier is separable and proven in both directions against a scratch repository: it must accept a nonce that landed and reject one that did not. That selftest runs on every pull request rather than only at deploy time, because a change that breaks the verifier must not reach master and be discovered afterwards.

Deployment parity
-----------------

An agent host runs its own installed copy and merging does not update it, so every other layer can be green while the fleet runs last week's code.

install.sh now writes BUILD_PROVENANCE into the staging directory — swapped into place by the same mv as the JARs it describes, since a file written afterwards could survive a failed swap and name a build that is not installed. verify-deployed-build.sh reads it back and rejects a missing file, a commit that is not the one deployed, an install built from a dirty tree, and an install that ran --no-build and may serve JARs older than the commit it names.

The commit to compare against is passed from deploy-macos-agent as a job output rather than re-read from master later, because master advancing between the two jobs would otherwise be indistinguishable from a stale deploy, and a check that cries wolf gets turned off.

It does not prove the JARs were compiled from that commit; only a reproducible build would, and this is not one. What it catches is an install from a stale or dirty checkout. The residue is written down in the plan rather than left for a reader to discover.

The seam, and the catalogue's own contents
------------------------------------------

Two things that were previously guaranteed by prose are now guaranteed by a check, because both describe the cheapest ways to fake this system rather than use it.

seam.txt enumerates every substitution the end-to-end tests make, with a justification saying what production behaviour stops being covered. check-seam.sh fails on any it finds that is not declared. The cheapest way to turn a red end-to-end test green is to stub one more thing, and in a diff that looks like a test being fixed; requiring the manifest edit puts it next to the test it excuses. The scan also fails on setDryRun(true) — one line that lets the job run, log what it "would" commit, satisfy every assertion about its own state and push nothing — and on the disappearance of the bare repository, without which the suite can only assert the job's account of itself. It is a token scan, not a parser: it makes the obvious routes loud, and cannot prove no stub is present. That limit is written down rather than left to be discovered.

faults/MANIFEST names every fault that must exist, and the runner refuses to run at all when the directory contents and the manifest disagree. Deleting a fault would otherwise be a silent pass: fewer entries, all green, nothing saying something used to be checked.

Wiring
------

- analysis.yaml gains agent-e2e-faults, in the All Checks merge gate. AgentJobEndToEndTest itself already runs under test-flowt

author: vinchi777
body:
## Description

The desktop asked for thinking on every turn (`thinking: true` in `ChatService`), and the effort picker was disabled for Ollama models. So a thinking-capable local model such as `qwen3:8b` reasoned before every reply and every tool call, with no way to stop it. On a laptop GPU that adds tens of seconds per turn. In a local measurement one tool round took 8.6 s with thinking and 0.6 s without.

The server already turns thinking off when asked to (#5057): for an Ollama model that can think, a request without `thinking` gets `think: false`. The desktop just never left the flag out.

For an Ollama model the server reports as able to think (`can_think`), the effort picker is now a **Thinking On / Off** switch. Off leaves `thinking` out of the turn's request.

## Customer note

When you chat with a local model that can think, the effort control next to the model picker now switches thinking on or off, so you can get fast answers when you don't need the reasoning.

## Changes

- `ModelCatalog.selectUsableModels` reads `can_think` from `/api/models` and sets a new `ChatModelOption.thinkingToggle` for Ollama models that can think.
- `ReasoningEffortPicker` shows a "Thinking: On / Off" switch for a `thinkingToggle` model, instead of the disabled "Effort: n/a".
  - Off is stored as the existing `minimal` effort setting (`THINKING_OFF_SETTING`), so there is no new persisted value and no migration. Any other stored setting reads as On.
  - Hosted models keep the effort scale exactly as before.
- `requestsThinking` (in `reasoningEffort.ts`) decides the turn's `thinking` flag. It is false only for a `thinkingToggle` model set to Off. A catalog that hasn't loaded keeps today's behaviour, which is to ask for thinking.
- Tests cover:
  - the catalog mapping (Ollama with and without `can_think`, a hosted model reporting `can_think`)
  - `requestsThinking`
  - the turn request (Off omits `thinking`, On sends it, a hosted model is unaffected)
  - the picker's faces, including a tighter check for the disabled face (the `Mui-disabled` class rather than the word "disabled", which Joy's inline CSS always contains)

## Guide for Testers

Prerequisite: a self-host stack with a host Ollama (`OLLAMA_BASE_URL` set) that has pulled `qwen3:8b`, a server that includes #5057, and a desktop build from this branch signed in to that stack.

1. Start a new chat in the desktop app.
2. In the model picker, select `qwen3:8b`.
3. Expected: the control next to the model picker reads `Thinking: On` and is enabled. It no longer reads `Effort: n/a`.
4. Send: `Reply with exactly: pong`.
5. Expected: the reply shows a reasoning block before `pong`.
6. Open the control and choose `Off`. Expected: it now reads `Thinking: Off`.
7. Send: `Reply with exactly: pong`.
8. Expected: `pong` with no reasoning block, noticeably faster than step 5.

### Regression Checks

- Select an OpenAI reasoning model (e.g. GPT-5). The control reads `Effort: Default` and lists Default / Minimal / Low / Medium / High as before.
- Select a Claude model without effort support. The control reads `Effort: n/a`, is disabled, and shows its tooltip as before.
- Select an Ollama model that cannot think, if one is installed. The control reads `Effort: n/a`.

### What NOT to test

- Server behaviour for hosted providers: this change is desktop-only and doesn't alter what a hosted model is sent.

## Additional Information

- **Per conversation:** the effort setting is stored per conversation, and new chats start at `default` (thinking On). Off is chosen per chat.
- **Switching models:** a chat set to Off that switches to a hosted reasoning model carries `minimal` effort there, which is the closest meaning.
- **Verified:**
  - desktop `typecheck` and eslint are clean
  - the touched test files pass (55 tests)
  - the full desktop suite passes (266 files, 3728 tests)
- **Not yet checked live in a desktop build:** this branch hasn't been run against a local `qwen3:8b`. The server half (no `thinking` flag leads to `think: false`) was verified live with #5057.

## Checklist

- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings

author: devswha
body:
<!-- See CONTRIBUTING.md for checks, translations, contract tests and the changelog (a file in changelog.d/, never CHANGELOG.md). -->

## Change

Until now the chat's command menu was built from scans plus hand-copied builtin lists, and commands were hidden in eight places. A command Chat can't drive was either missing or sent as typed text. This PR (group B of the agent command capabilities plan, todos 4 to 18 and 20) gives every catalog row a description of how it runs and fixes the measured scanner drift for each agent.

### What changes for users

- Every command row carries its forms (`bare`, with arguments, ...) and each form's interaction: terminal-bound, dialog, inline, none or unknown. A name with no recorded form is still offered, as `unknown`.
- Commands that only run in the terminal are listed apart, last, under Terminal commands with a Terminal badge. Picking one, or typing it and pressing Send, keeps the draft and offers Open Terminal (shows the terminal, sends nothing) or Run in Terminal. They're never sent from the chat as typed text. Observe-only connections still have no message box.
- Commands the agent's own menu hides are marked agent-hidden and stay out of the menu. Typed by hand, they're still sent.
- For an OpenCode pane whose skills are `@` attachments, the `@` menu lists them under Skills before files; picking one inserts the skill id.
- Each row carries provenance (`scan`, `static`, `native`) and a `verified` flag. A static table is verified only when the pane's agent version matches the table's pin by major.minor. Claude, Codex and OpenCode carry a store-read version; the other agents stay unverified until a version source exists.
- One resolver decides a pane's agent and version. An OmO pane that herdr labels Claude is now treated as OmO by the composer, and a multi-line message to an unlabelled OmO pane goes as one bracketed paste.
- A skill reached through a symlinked root is listed once, identified by its real file.

Per agent:

- **Claude** (pin 2.1.301, from live official docs): the seven hidden names come back with their forms, terminal screens such as `/config` go to the Terminal group, Claude's own hidden set (`agents`, `heapdump`, `setup-bedrock`, ...) is agent-hidden. A skill or command named like a builtin (`/compact`) is listed once, as the skill Claude runs.

- **OpenCode** (pin 1.19.3): v1 and v2 are read as each version does, with the v1 shape for a missing or 1.x version and v2 for 2.x.

author: subrising
body:
## Problem

The 0.2.26 release hang check (FU-413) armed a Node inspector on the **signed release build**. The scratch daemon log showed `Debugger listening on ws://127.0.0.1:9229` after SIGUSR1.

A packaged supervisor starts its worker through the entry point runner (`resolveWorkerSpawnSpec`), not through `fork()`. That path did not pass `workerExecArgv`, so the release worker did not get `--disable-sigusr1` (FU-79). Any process of the same user could then run code inside the daemon.

Evidence on the signed 0.2.26 build:
- MacBook: the worker reported `process.execArgv: []` through the opened inspector.
- Mac mini: the worker tried to open the inspector ("Starting inspector on 127.0.0.1:9229 failed: address already in use"). Another process held port 9229.

## Change

- New `packages/server/scripts/packaged-worker-spawn.ts`: `packagedWorkerSpawnArgs()` puts `packagedInspectorFlags()` before the runner script.
- `supervisor-entrypoint.ts` uses it for the packaged spawn path.

## Tests

- New `packaged-worker-spawn.test.ts`: argument order, and a real child process that reports `--disable-sigusr1` in its `execArgv`. It fails before the change (module missing).
- `inspector-flavour.test.ts`: the entry point must build the runner arguments with `packagedWorkerSpawnArgs(`. Fails before the change, passes after.
- Full project suite once on the Mac mini (after `build:server` and `build:app-deps`, clean environment). The remaining failures are the same on base `d8578d421` (git tests in a partial clone, one lifecycle test, one plugin test). This change adds no failure.

author: lyingbug
body:
Automation runs introduced in #4492 can lose their execution identity when delegating, leave recoverable child work after cancellation, overlap across scheduler instances, and exceed their execution budget after approval resumes. Blocked runs can also prevent unrelated queued work and later approvals from being processed.

## Changes

- Persist the automation identity and run mode in delegated snapshots, including inherited children, and prevent ordinary collaboration recovery from reviving scheduler-owned parent turns.
- Stop delegated work and discard parent wait checkpoints on cancellation or unsuccessful termination. Fence stale finalizers and make cancellation win approval-resume races.
- Serialize admission through an automation-row write lock so separate scheduler instances cannot start different runs of the same automation concurrently.
- Exclude automations with running or approval-waiting work before applying the queue batch limit.
- Reconcile every approval batch using keyset pagination, including when earlier rows leave the waiting set during the scan.
- Persist cumulative execution duration across approval suspensions and service restarts, excluding queue and approval waiting time. Add PostgreSQL and SQLite upgrade/rollback migrations.

## Validation

- Added regression coverage for all six issues, stale finalization, approval/cancellation races, and SQLite upgrades preserving existing runs. The six original defect scenarios fail against the pre-fix implementation.
- Passed `env -u LOG_FORMAT go test ./internal/database ./internal/agent/... ./internal/application/service ./internal/handler ./internal/container`.
- Passed `env -u LOG_FORMAT go test -race ./internal/application/service -run 'TestAutomation|TestCollaboration' -count=1`.
- Passed `git diff --check`.

The local `LOG_FORMAT=json` setting is interpreted as a literal log template and breaks two existing log assertions on both the baseline and patched code; it was unset only for validation processes. PostgreSQL migrations have not been exercised against a live database.

author: griffincancode
body:
The 3.0 upgrade made Billy’s saved compact JSON workload roughly 17 times slower and untyped NDJSON 3–6 times slower. Shared native helpers recover eligible JSON encoding, exact decoding and whole-blob NDJSON parsing while retaining public functions, call signatures and 3.0 JSON values/output. Compiler-less builds retain the portable implementation.

Native default spacing now counts separators during the existing type proof and adds spaces only outside quoted strings. The encoder and decoder share a bounded quote scanner. Exact-output default source encoding is 4.05 times faster than 3.0; all 13 selected 3.0 comparisons pass.

The 105-pair comparison with 2.1.1 shows equivalent-output compact encoding 0.9–1.1% faster, small-request JSON 19–25% faster and NDJSON 11–13% faster. Source decoding remains 0.30–0.55% slower, so the strict legacy performance gate still fails. Default encoding also remains slower than 2.1.1, whose compact bytes differ from 3.0’s required formatting. The 3.1.0 release discloses these costs; it makes no universal speedup claim.

Native wheels target CPython 3.12–3.14. Instrumented calls use ordinary Python behavior, and module reinitialization retains live configuration checks. The measurement report records the observed machine-stack boundary limitation.

Validation for the implementation: native serde suites passed on Python 3.12 (2,706 tests), 3.13 (2,707) and 3.14 (2,744); the full Python 3.14 suite passed 6,085 tests. Five benchmark assurance tests, Ruff, formatting, mypy and suite inventory passed. All 56 remote checks passed for runtime commit 0653735. The release candidate must also pass its current checks and the release workflow’s wheel tests before publication.

See `bench/billy-serde-optimization-results.md` and both raw JSON reports for all samples, output/native acceptance checks, source/artifact hashes and reproduction commands.

## Why

ADR-0002 fixes the dependency direction in the ecosystem: the core and the SDK reach the Toolbox through its published HTTP contract, and the Toolbox's only ecosystem dependency is docstruct. Part of A11yDevs/acessilia#188 (the docstruct and SDK guards are in the core repository).

Modules are read as `utf-8-sig`. The first run failed with `SyntaxError` on `providers/nougat.py`, which starts with a BOM: Python accepts the BOM on import, but `ast.parse` does not when the file is read as plain `utf-8`.

author: angriestbird
body:
## Bottom line

Keep parent-mod and base-game file paths visible after deleting a workspace override. A watched delete now drops only the workspace's own file-index contribution, and filepath errors in open documents refresh without a reindex.

The file index records which keys the workspace owns and which of those a parent mod or the base game also provides. A delete releases the workspace claim and keeps the key when a lower layer still provides it. Parent precedence and `replace_path` behave as before. In case-sensitive runs the workspace's spelling of a path now wins over the base game's.

Review changes:
- The index tracks only overridden keys instead of a fallback spelling for every parent and base-game path. That map held about 57,700 extra entries for a HOI4 install, copied on every index clone, and the LSP never read the spellings because its index ignores case.
- The builder reuses `visible_parent_files` with no same-path shadowing by the workspace, so the parent-layer walk refactor and `LayerShadow::is_replaced` are gone. The unused `build_file_index` wrapper and `FileIndex::remove` are deleted.
- The layered-delete driver tests are one table, each case checked against a full rebuild. Three LSP tests that repeated builder cases are removed. LSP tests that cover LSP-only behavior stay: case-only renames, the requeue, snapshot sharing, and the CW113 publish.

Earlier fixes kept: resource deletes are released before creates claim, resource deletes are requeued when an over-cap batch loses the scan flag, a resource-only delete batch does not drop the semantic token cache, and deletes of paths the workspace never owned do not clone the index.

Out of scope: folder deletes, and deletes whose parent directory is also gone, still release nothing.

Format, strict clippy and the workspace tests (2,661) pass. `guard.py md --compare origin/main` and `guard.py vanilla --compare origin/main` match (12,801 and 5 diagnostics). No baselines re-blessed.

Closes #1067

author: angriestbird
body:
## Bottom line

Store retained comment text in one shared per-parse buffer, with each comment holding a byte range instead of its own `String`. Inline-script expansions share that buffer rather than copying comment text.

The `.cwb` cache stores the pooled text once and moves to format v6. Old v5 entries fail the version header and re-parse. Cached comment ranges that are out of order, past the pool, leave pool text uncovered, split a UTF-8 character, or are empty are rejected, so consumers never load a comment with no text. The v6 golden fixture is included, and the tracked v5 fixture now checks the incompatible-version rejection. Comment directives and semantic-token positions behave as before. The contributor guide's `.cwb` version note now describes v6.

Rust formatting, strict workspace clippy and the full workspace tests passed, including the allocation gate, the retained-text and shared-pool tests, both cache-layout tests and the cache-corruption tests. The MD and vanilla guards matched clean revision `dc2657c7` on the current inputs (12,801 and 5 diagnostics); no baselines were re-blessed.

Timing measurements were noisy and inconclusive. This change claims only the removal of per-comment text allocations, not a parser or end-to-end speedup.

Closes #575

## Summary

Recovery branch for the Dusk dynamic-color UI overhaul, including deep-inspection crash fixes.

### Crash fixes (deep inspection)
- **Navigation crash**: `navController.navigate()` was being passed a *testTag* (`nav_tab_telegram_destination`) instead of the actual NavHost *route* (`telegram_destination`), producing `IllegalArgumentException: Navigation destination that matches route ... cannot be found in the navigation graph`.

body:
Adds `install.sh`, which installs or updates Reclaim from GitHub releases without macOS's "unsafe app" warning.

```bash
gh api -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw" repos/whatron/reclaim/contents/install.sh | bash
```

## What it does

- Downloads the latest release, or a tag you name (`./install.sh v0.1.0`), with the GitHub CLI. That works with this private repo and doesn't trigger the warning: macOS only flags files downloaded through a browser.
- Quits Reclaim if it's running, replaces the copy in Applications (using `sudo` only if Applications isn't writable), clears any browser quarantine flag, says which version you went from and to, and opens it.
- Stops with a clear message on an Intel Mac (release builds are Apple-silicon only), if `gh` isn't installed, or if you're not signed in.

The README gets an "Install with one command" section above the manual download. The one-liner works once this is merged, because it reads the script from `main`.

## Description
Upgrades `@yospace/admanagement-sdk` from `3.8.3` to `3.11.3` (Zendesk #32989). Kept to the minimum needed for the new SDK; no refactors, so downstream forks can merge it easily.

Changes required by the SDK:
- Deep type imports (`types/Public/TrackingError`, `types/Core/XmlNode`) no longer resolve after the package layout moved to `dist/` → now imported from the package root
- `Advert.getCompanionAdsByType()` was renamed to `getCompanionCreative()`
- The SDK now ships native ES classes, so `YospaceAdListenerAdapter` **implements** `AnalyticEventObserver` instead of extending it (extending threw `Class constructors cannot be invoked without 'new'` in our ES5 build)

- `YospaceAdBreak.id` is generated if the Yospace SDK provides none (as requested in the #191 review)
- `DateRangeEmitter` now passes a `TimedMetadata` instance (via `createFromMetadata`) to `onTimedMetadata` instead of a plain object (Live session mode)

Supersedes #191 (3.10.0 upgrade by @saravanans-github) and addresses its review feedback, including keeping `onTimedMetadata` for the deprecated Live mode.

Notes:
- The Live session mode is deprecated in the SDK as of 3.10 (still works; integrators should prefer DVR Live)

The coexec strategy places instructions in the open cycles of WMMA and MFMA co-execution windows, and the generic post-RA scheduler then reorders that schedule. Use the nop post-RA scheduler for functions that use the coexec strategy, unless amdgpu-post-sched-strategy is set.

author: abhijit-mudigonda
body:
## Problem

`SafeCompositum(K, L)` is used by `StrongAdd`/`StrongMultiply` (and hence by `ThetaSeries` when building dihedral forms). Magma's `Compositum` requires **at least one** of the two fields to be normal; when neither is, it throws:

```
Runtime error in 'Compositum': At least one of the fields must be normal
for the composite to be well defined. Use CompositeFields in the other case
```

`SafeCompositum` previously only guarded against a *different* Magma bug (the "Invalid embedding" one) by rebuilding a side, so all of its `Compositum` attempts still threw on non-normal inputs.

This surfaced as `dihedral_error` in the weight-(1,3) non-CM search — e.g. Q(√5), the split prime of norm 241, order-2 nebentypus — where `NewDihedralBasis`/`DihedralBasis` → `ThetaSeries` → `StrongAdd` → `SafeCompositum` hit two non-normal fields.

## Fix

Add a final fallback that uses `CompositeFields` (exactly what the error message recommends) and takes the maximal-degree compositum, which contains both fields so the downstream `StrongCoerce` in `StrongAdd`/`StrongMultiply` places elements correctly.

body:
Builds the manage half of the workspace members page on top of NEWFRONT-537's roster, from `parity/specs/workspace-settings.md` §10–§14. Written new against the spec; the old app was read for behavior only.

**What it does**
- **WSET-009** — bulk invite dialog: one Member-defaulted row, add/remove rows, per-row role picker limited to the actor's own role, inline "Email is required"/"Email is invalid" that block the send, success closes with an "Invitations sent" notice and the pending rows appear, a failed send keeps the dialog and its input. Add is admin-only.
- **WSET-010** — admin-only pending group: collapsible with a count, emails matched by the roster search, role edits never above the actor's role, copy-link, withdraw behind a naming confirmation, failures toast and keep the row.
- **WSET-012** — member role control on other people's active rows only; options at or below the actor's role; PATCH persists, a refusal toasts and leaves the row on its previous role.
- **WSET-013** — removal behind `Remove {name}?`; self-leave behind `Leave workspace?`, then navigation to the just-left workspace home, which renders the not-authorized gate (`Not Authorized!`, matching the oracle's pinned assertion).
- **WSET-015** — no billing/upsell affordance renders in the members header in this checkout (absence pinned through the driver).

**Structure** — pure rules (`roles.ts`, `inviteForm.ts`, `invitations.ts`, `memberRules.ts`), mutation hooks (`mutations.ts`), presentational pieces (`InviteDialog`, `PendingInvitations`, `InvitationRoleControl`, `MemberRoleControl`, `MemberActions`, `RemoveTargetDialog`), wired into `MembersPage`/`MemberRow`. The shell gained one optional `onLeaveWorkspace` seam so a page can hand navigation back to the route.

**Coverage** — every changed line and branch of the members feature, registry, outlet, auth screen and route is covered by unit tests (100% statements/branches/functions/lines on those files). The driver methods this slice implements are unit-tested too, including their error and timeout paths.

**Notes for review**
- Inventory rows WSET-009/010/012/013/015 now read `oracle green, built`.
- Spec §13 gained a decision note: the leave landing is the not-authorized gate, which is what the oracle pins.
- No parity stack was run (per the build-slice rule); the area gate proves the rows on apps/web_new.

author: femboy2112
body:
## What / why (#79, R1 P0)

`Context::run_once` **never returned** after the terminal hung up (SIGHUP) if the
process survived the signal — it busy-spun at ~66% CPU forever. Root cause (traced
to crossterm 0.29's mio backend): once the fd reports `POLLHUP`, crossterm's
internal read loop sees endless `Ok(0)`/`EIO` and **never honours its poll
timeout**, so the spin is inside crossterm, not in any LibGibson loop. LibGibson
had zero hangup detection on the poll path.

## Fix (`src/input.rs`, single choke point `poll_event`)

On a Unix controlling terminal, `poll_event` no longer hands a possibly-hung fd to
crossterm with a blocking timeout. It:
- waits on stdin itself in short (25ms) slices via `libc::poll`, checking
  `POLLHUP`/`POLLERR`/`POLLNVAL` each slice;
- asks crossterm to decode only with a **zero** timeout once stdin is readable;
- surfaces a hangup within one slice as `Err(ErrorKind::BrokenPipe)` — which
  `run_once` / `ui::App` / the C FFI already propagate, so **no ABI change, no new
  type**;
- paces (does not busy-loop) a readable-but-undecodable fd — the upstream crossterm
  "stranded input" stall (#15) — preserving stock behaviour without burning CPU.

Non-Unix and non-tty stdin keep the original crossterm path unchanged.

## Red-first test (`tests/pty_hangup.rs` + `examples/hangup_probe.rs`)

A new additive `Capture::hang_up()` drops the kernel's last reference to the PTY
master (`dup2 /dev/null` over the master fd), delivering a **real** SIGHUP to the
child's controlling session. The probe child ignores SIGHUP and loops `run_once`;
the test asserts it **exits 3 (BrokenPipe) within 1500ms** instead of spinning
(`None`). A **control** (no `ignore-sighup`) proves the harness delivers a genuine
hangup and that this death is distinct from the BrokenPipe path.

## Verification boundary — read this before merge

- **Reasoned, compiles via CI.** The control-flow is designed against crossterm
  0.29's mio source; CI validates compile + clippy + fmt + rustdoc + non-PTY tests.
- **Runtime behaviour UNVERIFIED locally** (host-RAM safety — no local PTY run). The
  decisive validation is the PTY suite. If CI's main `test` job runs `pty_hangup`
  (as it does `terminal_ownership`), that's real validation — otherwise run
  `cargo test --test pty_hangup -- --test-threads=1` before merge.
- **This changes the core tty poll path for *every* interactive poll.** It must be
  checked against the existing event-pressure matrix (`tests/event_pressure_pty.rs`,
  `tests/pty_resize_torture.rs`) to confirm it does not perturb the pinned #15 stall
  signatures. Those live in the (CI-skipped) PTY job; **run them before merge.**

Draft; references #79 (not `Fixes`). No merge without owner consent.

author: john-doebot
body:
## What and why

A failed document showed its raw exception string (`ConnectError: [Errno 61] Connection refused`, `RuntimeError: Tika rejected file (422): org.apache.poi…`) in red, whatever the cause. On the dogfood corpus, 92% of failed documents were transient service blips that looked exactly like genuinely unreadable files (#555 data comment).

**Backend**

- New `src/harbor_clerk/document_failure.py`: `explain_failure(error)` is a small pure function with an ordered rule table. It sorts the stored error text into one of three families, each with a fixed plain-language `message` and suggested `action`:
  - `temporary`: connection refused or reset, transport errors, timeouts (including the stage alarm `Stage X timed out`), 5xx, 429, retry-later, `EmbedderUnavailableError`, Apple Intelligence unavailable. It also covers the terminal embed failure as it reads since #862 (`Embedder unavailable: gave up after N attempts … Last error: …`).
  - `unreadable`: Tika 422; encrypted or password-protected files (POI `EncryptedDocumentException`, PDFium `Incorrect password`); broken image or PDF data (`UnidentifiedImageError`, `broken data stream`, truncated images, `PdfiumError`); decode errors; 415 unsupported type; `WatchedFileMissing`, `NoReadableSource` and the legacy `No source for doc` string; `FileNotFoundError` and `PermissionError`.
  - `other`: deliberate stops (`Cancelled by user`, `Queue cleared…`), `DocumentTooLargeError`, missing Tika configuration, an embedder 4xx rejection, Apple Intelligence document errors, and the fallback.

  The rules are ordered: specific causes come before the generic connection and timeout patterns, because their messages often quote one (a 422 whose rmeta refetch timed out, a watched-file read failing with an errno, the embed give-up quoting its last `ConnectError`). The function works on the stored text, so rows written before this change are explained too.
- `ErrorInfo {family, message, action}` is added to:
  - `DocumentSummary` (`GET /api/docs`);
  - `DocumentDetail` (`GET /api/docs/{id}`);
  - each `JobInfo` whose status is `error`.
- `DocumentSummary` now also carries the raw `error`, but only while `pipeline_status == error`, so a stale error on a ready document is not shown.
- **Redaction is unchanged.** The new list `error` field is named `error`, so `redact_paths_for_principal` path-redacts it for API keys, exactly as on the detail route. `message` and `action` are fixed strings that never quote the raw error, so they carry no path for any principal. A test asserts that no message or action contains `/`, `Errno` or `Error:`.
- MCP and CLI output are unchanged.

**Frontend**

- New `components/DocumentErrorNotice.tsx`, with styles and the pill mapping in `utils/documentFailure.ts`:
  - shows a title, the message and the action, all uncropped;
  - puts the raw error in a collapsed "Technical details" `<details>` (`whitespace-pre-wrap`, never truncated) with a Copy button;
  - renders temporary failures amber, unreadable files red, and other failures neutral.
- `DocumentsPage.tsx` gets small, localised edits so they don't collide with the parallel "Reprocess all failed" work:
  - a failed row's status pill follows its family (amber `temporary error` / red `can't read file` / red `failed`);
  - a one-line explanation sits under the filename;
  - the full notice appears in the expanded row.
- `DocumentDetailPage.tsx`:
  - the red `Error in <stage>: <raw>` banner and the separate red `Error: <raw>` line are replaced by one notice;
  - a live `error` job event now refetches the document so its explanation arrives.

## Sibling sweep

Grepped for every place a stored pipeline error reaches a reader (`doc.error`, `job.error`, `pipeline_error`, `DocumentSummary(`, `DocumentDetail(`, `JobInfo(`):

- `api/routes/documents.py`: list, detail and jobs. All updated.
- `mcp_server.py` `kb_get_document` (`pipeline_error`) and `kb_ingest_status`: left unchanged as the brief asked. They keep `_error_text` redaction.
- `api/routes/jobs.py`: the human-only jobs and queue snapshot. It returns `IngestionJob.error` raw, and the queue tray shows only "Error in <stage>", with no raw text. Left unchanged.
- `watched_source.failed_for_a_missing_source`: a second, narrower classifier that decides watcher requeue. Not merged, because it keys recovery behaviour and should stay exact. A test asserts that every error it treats as a missing source is `unreadable` here, so the two cannot drift apart.
- Frontend: no other page renders `doc.error`. The queue tray's `CompletedRow` shows only the stage.

## Tests

- `tests/test_document_failure.py`: table-driven, with 40 real stored-error shapes. They include every row of the #555 data comment, the post-#862 embed give-up, `describe_error(WatchedFileMissing(...))` and `describe_error(NoReadableSource(...))`, the deliberate stops (kept in step with `DELIBERATELY_STOPPED_ERRORS`), the no-raw-text-in-explanation check, and the agreement with `failed_for_a_missing_source`.
- `tests/test_rest_api_key_tier.py`:
  - a failed document's list and detail carry `error_info` (unreadable) for the human and for a read key;
  - the key's raw `error` is path-redacted on the list, and the folder path is absent from both responses;
  - a ready document with a stale error carries no `error` or `error_info` in the list.
- Frontend:
  - `DocumentErrorNotice.test.tsx`: message first with the raw error collapsed; the raw error uncropped and copied; temporary amber vs unreadable red, and the pill states; the unclassified fallback; the compact line;
  - `DocumentDetailPage.test.tsx`: a failed document shows the explanation once, with no old `Error: …` line.

Results:

- Full Python suite: `4342 passed, 12 skipped, 109 warnings in 635.42s`.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check`: clean.
- `gen_docs`: already up to date.
- Frontend: `lint` has 0 errors (the warnings were already there); `format:check` and `type-check` pass; vitest `34 files, 275 tests passed`.

**Mutation checks** (each run done on its own after the commit, then restored):

1. List route: `failed_error = doc.error` without the `pipeline_status == error` guard. `test_a_ready_document_carries_no_error_in_the_list` fails.
2. `api/scope.py`: `"error"` removed from `ABSOLUTE_PATH_TEXT_FIELDS`. `test_failed_document_explains_its_error_and_keys_still_get_no_path` fails, because the key's list `error` leaks the path.
3. `document_failure.py`: the `WatchedFileMissing` / legacy `No source for doc` rule disabled. `test_family[WatchedFileMissing…]`, `test_family[RuntimeError: No source for doc…]` and the `failed_for_a_missing_source` agreement test fail.

## Review round 1

- The 429 rule now matches only in an HTTP context (`HTTP 429`, `'429 `, `Too Many Requests`). Bare-number counterexamples (`index 429`, `KeyError: 429`, `index 503`, `expected 500 rows`) are tested as `other`. The 5xx rules already required HTTP context.
- `DELIBERATE_STOP_ERRORS` holds every stop text, job- and document-level, including `Cancelled by admin (queue clear)`. An AST sweep of the literal `.error =` / `error=` writes in `worker/`, `watcher/`, `api/routes/system.py` and `api/routes/documents.py` must equal that set.
- The detail's `error_info` follows the list's rule: it is set only while `pipeline_status == error`. The raw `error` on the detail is unchanged.
- The detail banner no longer shows "Ingestion complete" over a document in error whose listed jobs are all done. The new document-driven branch needs this fix to be reachable.
- The compact fallback reads "Open the document for the technical details."
- New tests:
  - DocumentsPage failed rows: family pill, one-line notice, full notice in the expanded row;
  - the SSE `error` refetch;
  - the document-driven banner branch.

Mutation checks for this round (each run on its own, then restored):

- bare `\b429\b`: 2 classifier tests fail;
- `Cancelled by admin (queue clear)` dropped: the stop-text sweep fails;
- detail `error_info`

author: sardark942
body:
## Shop SP2b — Escrow Transfer on Onboarding

Closes the escrow loop from SP2a: when a vendor finishes Stripe Connect onboarding, their accumulated **held** escrow balance is paid out to their connected account, and the dashboard surfaces that balance as an onboarding nudge.

Builds on SP2a checkout (PR #180, squash `3dfd143`). Spec + plan: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-shop-sp2b-escrow-transfer-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-18-shop-sp2b-escrow-transfer.md`.

### What it does
- **One idempotent money path** — `transferHeldEarnings(db, vendorProfileId)`: one Stripe `Transfer` per `vendor_ledger` row with **`source_transaction`** = the original charge, a stable **`idempotencyKey = escrow-transfer:${ledger_id}`**, and a **compare-and-swap** stamp (`WHERE id=$id AND status='held'`). Failures leave the row `held` and are retried; the transfer-succeeds-then-DB-write-fails corner is covered by the stable key.
- **Two triggers** — the `account.updated` webhook transfers immediately when a vendor becomes `payouts_enabled`; a **daily** cron (`/api/cron/shop-escrow-transfer`, `30 3 * * *`) is the self-healing safety net. Both call the same idempotent function.
- **`source_charge_id`** is stamped on each escrow ledger row at capture time (migration 00089), with an on-demand PI-retrieve fallback.
- **Vendor earnings card** on `/dashboard/profile/payments` — 4 states (held / transferring / paid out / none). A page-load status refresh means a just-onboarded vendor never sees a stale "set up payouts". The held balance is the onboarding lever.
- **Notification** — `shop_funds_transferred` (best-effort, never throws into the money path), linking to the payments page.

### Charge-mode recap (unchanged from SP2a)
Escrow orders are **platform charges**, so transfers draw from the platform balance against the specific charge (`source_transaction`), avoiding "insufficient available balance" on pending funds. The vendor becomes merchant of record for *new* sales once onboarded (direct charges).

### How it was built
Subagent-driven: 10 TDD tasks, each implemented + independently reviewed + fix-looped (the money core took one fix round to pin the no-double-pay guarantee with tests), then a whole-branch review on the most capable model (**no Critical, no merge-blocking Important**) + one fix wave. Local: typecheck clean, **1175 unit/RTL tests pass**.

### ⚠️ Before merge / deploy
- [ ] **Apply migration `00089`** (`vendor_ledger.source_charge_id` + `shop_funds_transferred` notification type) to dev, then prod. Additive (nullable column + widened CHECK), safe to run live.
- [ ] (Optional validation) Run the **deferred e2e** `tests/e2e/shop-escrow-transfer.spec.ts` with `E2E_STRIPE_TRANSFER=1` + `E2E_CONNECT_TEST_ACCOUNT_ID` + a `sk_test_` key. It is skip-guarded, so CI is unaffected.
- Earnings card stays behind the shop's existing gating (local bridal-wear vendors; inert with no ledger rows).

### Deferred / parked (follow-ups, not blocking)
- **Webhook latency at scale:** `account.updated` does N inline `transfers.create` for a vendor's held rows. Self-heals (idempotent + daily cron) but a high-held-count vendor could exceed Stripe's ack window — cap per-invocation in a hardening pass. Latent at zero-volume pre-launch.
- **24h idempotency-key edge:** a stamp-failed row retried >24h later *without* `source_transaction` could double-pay — unreachable in prod (`source_transaction` is always set; cron retries well within 24h). A `transfers.list`-by-metadata precheck would close it.
- Reserve/clawback, international lane, multi-currency remain Phase 2.

author: yu2971512385-ui
body:
Closes #14845

## What a user sees

Add a DateTime column, open its options, and pick **Pacific/Chuuk** — it is in the picker, which is built from `@vvo/tzdb`. Then filter on that column. The filter is evaluated in **UTC**, ten hours from the zone that was chosen, so rows fall on the wrong side of the boundary.

```js
getNodejsTimezone('Pacific/Chuuk')   // 'Etc/UTC'   <- should be 'Pacific/Truk'
```

## Why

`timezoneUtils.ts` built the reverse half of the alias map by assigning back into the same object:

```ts
for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(_timezoneAliases)) {
  _timezoneAliases[value] = key;
}
```

Several legacy aliases can share one canonical zone, and each assignment overwrote the last, so the canonical zone kept only one of them. Fifteen canonical zones have more than one alias here; eighteen aliases ended up with no reverse entry at all.

Harmless until the surviving alias is one Node does not carry — true for three zones:

| canonical zone | aliases | kept | Node carries | returned |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Pacific/Chuuk` | `Pacific/Truk`, `Pacific/Yap` | `Pacific/Yap` | `Pacific/Truk` | `Etc/UTC` |
| `America/Indiana/Indianapolis` | `America/Fort_Wayne`, `America/Indianapolis`, `US/East-Indiana` | `US/East-Indiana` | `America/Indianapolis` | `Etc/UTC` |
| `America/Argentina/Cordoba` | `America/Cordoba`, `America/Rosario` | `America/Rosario` | `America/Cordoba` | `Etc/UTC` |

`getNodejsTimezone` feeds `filter/validate-row-filters.ts`, `filterHelpers_withparser.ts` and `db/field-handler/handlers/date-time/date-time.general.handler.ts`, so this lands in filter evaluation, not only in display.

## What changed

**`packages/nocodb-sdk/src/lib/timezoneUtils.ts`** — the reverse entry is now the alias Node actually accepts, and `getNodejsTimezone` takes one more hop when the canonical name is not one either (`Pacific/Yap` → `Pacific/Chuuk` → `Pacific/Truk`). That also resolves `America/Fort_Wayne`, `US/East-Indiana`, `America/Rosario` and `America/Argentina/ComodRivadavia`, which used to give up.

**`packages/nc-gui/lib/timezone-aliases.ts`** — `isSameTimezone` looked the alias up in one direction only, so with the canonical zone recording a single alias it answered differently depending on argument order:

```js
isSameTimezone('America/Montreal', 'America/Toronto')  // false
isSameTimezone('America/Toronto', 'America/Montreal')  // true
```

24 pairs behaved that way; checking both directions brings it to zero. This matters at `DateTimeOptions.vue:21` and `datetimeUtils.ts:89`, where a stored or browser-reported name is matched against the picker list.

## Deliberately not changed

`Asia/Chungking` and `Asia/Chongqing` are each other's alias in this table and neither reaches `Asia/Shanghai`, so both still resolve to UTC. That is a gap in the alias data rather than this bug, and it seemed better to leave it to you than to guess.

`nodejsTimezones` is also one zone short of Node 26 / ICU 78 — `America/Coyhaique`, added in tzdata 2025a. The only difference in either direction out of 418, so the snapshot is otherwise current. Left out to keep this to one cause.

## Testing

Added to `timezoneUtils.spec.ts`: the three zones by name, plus two properties — a zone must resolve whenever any name in its alias group is one Node carries, and nothing may resolve to a name Node rejects.

```
$ npx jest src/lib/timezoneUtils.spec.ts
  ✓ will get Asia/Kolkata                                    (the existing case, unchanged)
  ✓ resolves Pacific/Chuuk to an alias node accepts
  ✓ resolves America/Indiana/Indianapolis to an alias node accepts
  ✓ resolves America/Argentina/Cordoba to an alias node accepts
  ✓ never answers with a zone node does not accept
  ✓ gives up only when no name for the zone is one node carries
  ✓ will evaluate some test cases
Tests: 7 passed
```

With the change to `timezoneUtils.ts` reverted, four of those seven fail. Offsets confirmed with `Intl.DateTimeFormat(..., { timeZoneName: 'longOffset' })`: `Pacific/Truk` is GMT+10:00, `Etc/UTC` is GMT+00:00.

body:
FLR-T-12.47. The `unit` job ran every package's Vitest at once (`pnpm test` through turbo) on one two-core runner, so every new heavy suite pushed the others into their timeouts (PR #85: render2d `renovation.test.ts`, 30.3 s on a 30 s timeout, though render2d had not changed).

## What changed
- **`unit-groups` matrix** in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, one runner per group, each running `pnpm turbo run test --filter=…` (turbo builds each group's dependencies):

  | group | packages |
  |---|---|
  | cli | @floorspec/cli |
  | worker | @d3-floorspec/worker (installs ffmpeg, as before) |
  | mesh | @floorspec/mesh |
  | web | @d3-floorspec/web |
  | render2d | @floorspec/render2d |
  | solvers | layout-solver, dsl, migrate |
  | rest | engine, ops, rules-engine, mcp, mcp-stdio, package, analysis, both assistants, server, agent-eval, plus the `pnpm build` the old job ran |

- **Aggregator `unit`** (the required check keeps its name; `images` still needs `unit`): fails when a workspace package (the globs in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`) with a `test` script is in no group or in two, and when any group failed. I tested both the pass and the fail case locally.
- **`.github/vitest-timeouts.mjs`**: a reporter passed beside the default one. For each package it prints the three slowest tests against their own timeouts, and adds a `::warning` for any test that took more than half of its timeout. It never fails a run.
- **Cheap wins**
  - `packages/cli/test/cli.test.ts`: the ~1,450 per-case tests start one process each, and they used to run one after another. They now run concurrently (`it.concurrent.for` + async `execFile`), with the same assertions. Local time went from 149 s to 34 s.
  - `packages/render2d/test/renovation.test.ts`: the combined-plan test that rendered nine plans is now one combined test plus one determinism test per filter. Nothing tested was dropped.

## Measurements (CI, 2-core GitHub runners)
**Before** (one job, last five main/PR runs): the job took **549–705 s**. Per package, with all of them running at once: cli 518 s, worker 360–371 s, mesh 264–293 s, web 160–168 s, layout-solver 123–134 s. Slowest tests: mesh "watertight…" 65 s of 120 s (54%), render2d renovation combined 28 s of 30 s (94%), worker laundry light-levels 27.7 s of 30 s (92%).

**After**: unit wall clock (first group start to the end of `unit`) is **274–305 s**. The worker group (~265–292 s) is the long pole. The highest share of any test's timeout so far is 44% (worker `tour.test.ts`, added on main by #89).

author: bdbarnett
body:
This makes a dense General MIDI file keep its tempo on an ESP32-P4, and lets every instrument say how many notes it can sound at once. Fixes #167.

**Voice writes sent together.** Every write to an engine voice (a note, a release, a level, a stop) waits for the block the audio pump is pulling. On the P4, playing Dvořák's Ninth IV on FluidR3 through a 64-voice pool, that block was being pulled almost all the time, so each write waited about 3 ms. Three writes a note added up to roughly 9 ms an event, and the piece played at half speed: 549 s took 1072 s. Inside `with pool.deferred():` the writes queue and leave together at the end, with the pump parked once for all of them (`audiopump.park()`). The pool answers `playing` as the queue will leave it, so the slot bookkeeping, the arena's pinning and `sounding()` all see a queued note as sounding. Outside the block nothing changes. midiEngine wraps each service tick in it, and the piece now takes 550.3 s.

**The reserve stops its oldest releases instead of holding them at level 0.** A stopped voice fades out over 5 ms on the engine's tail and frees its slot, so the reserve no longer leaves silent voices costing render time. A stolen voice also isn't stopped before its new note, because `play()` hands the old one to the tail anyway.

**The arena outside the collected heap.** Where audiosampler has `SampleBuffer` (PyDevices/audiodsp#282), the arena's buffers come from it. The bank keeps a replaced arena until the voices playing from it stop, because a view of a SampleBuffer doesn't keep it alive. With an older audiodsp the arena is bytearrays, as before.

**The voice count, from Python.** A pool's `voice_count` can change while it plays, up to `max_voice_count` (the engine's ceiling, `audiosampler.MAX_VOICES`). Lowering it stops the voices above the new count with the 5 ms fade. `create("soundfont", ..., voices=n)` gives an instrument's own pool n voices.

**`voices` on every instrument (#167).** It is 1 for a monophonic instrument, the voice limit otherwise, and `None` for a drum machine. The CR-78 says 4, the voices its steal rule actually sounds. `tools/validate_api.py` checks that it's a positive int or `None`, and `docs/audio-component-api.md` describes it.

**Renamed:** a SoundFont instrument's shared pool is now `voice_pool`, both the `create()` keyword (was `voices=`) and the property (was `.voices`), so that `voices` can be the count. The CHANGELOG says so. If you passed `voices=pool`, pass `voice_pool=pool`.

Checked: the scoped contract tests and the soundfont, sf2 and piano-polyphony tests, `validate_api` (55 instruments, 45 effects) with the pinned audiodsp, the effects smoke test, flake8, and the soundfont tests against audiodsp#282's CPython build too (new tests for deferral, the reserve, the voice count and the own-pool count). On the DEV-KIT, running this branch's soundfont over audiodsp#282's firmware, the whole piece took 550.4 s against 549 s with 64 voices, chorus and reverb, and the pump produced 99.9% of the blocks it needed. With midiEngine's board profile (48 voices, no chorus) it took 550.3 s with 100%.

Not run: the instruments parity gate (`run_instruments_parity.py`). The instruments only gained a keyword on their `Instrument(...)` call; no sound path changed.

author: orchard254
body:
## Problem

The Phase 0 schema stores both `anchors.entity_id` and `anchors.repo_id`, but had no database trigger requiring the entity and anchor to belong to the same repository. Later observation isolation checks validate the anchor's declared `repo_id`, not the repository of its referenced entity. A mismatched anchor can therefore pass the observation-level check, breaking the canonical repository-isolation invariant.

## Changes

- Add a database-level `trg_anchors_repo_isolation` insert trigger that rejects an anchor whose entity belongs to a different repository.
- Add the trigger to the canonical schema guardrail tests.

author: joshuaspence
body:
## Summary

This ports joshuaspence/electronics-kit#57 to Dino Park.

The game could already be installed. But Chrome shows its own install banner only now and then, and its ⋮ → **Install app** menu item is easy to miss. So the game now offers to install itself.

### What changes

- **Install offer.** When the browser allows installing (`beforeinstallprompt`), the **parent area** shows "Put Dino Park on this device, to play it like any other app." with an **Install** button, which opens the browser's own install dialog. Unlike electronics-kit's level list, it's behind the grown-up gate, because gameplay has no text and a child should never meet a browser dialog.
- **Already installed.** The manifest now lists the game as its own `related_applications` entry, so `navigator.getInstalledRelatedApps()` can tell Chrome on Android that the game is on the device. Then, or after `appinstalled`, the parent area says "Dino Park is installed on this device. Look for "Dino Park" in your apps."
- **When nothing shows.** Nothing shows inside the installed app itself, which runs full screen (`display-mode: fullscreen`; `standalone` is checked too). Nothing shows in browsers that don't support any of this, such as Safari and Firefox.
- **Manifest.** `id`, `start_url` and `scope` are now all set to `/dino-park/`. These are the values they already defaulted to, so existing installs aren't affected. Setting them keeps the app's identity stable if the start URL ever changes, and keeps it apart from other apps on `joshuaspence.github.io`.
- **Docs.** `docs/design.md` §11 records the install offer.

## Screenshots

These are from this branch's own build at 1180×820. The browser's install offer can't be triggered for real in a test, so the screenshots fake it the same way the e2e test does. Before this change, the parent area showed neither line.
