author: crazycoder
body:
Fixes #628.

The radio's housekeeping decrements every pending `nextCheckIn` once a minute.
It also decrements a value with bit 15 set, which means seconds.

The AP sends `5 | 0x8000` ("come back in 5 s") in `checkQueue()` when a tag
has more than one queued item. If the tag picks up the first item 5 minutes
later, it gets `0x8000`. The ZBS243 firmware sleeps `0 * 1000` ms, and
`sleepForMsec(0)` means "forever" (the timer caps it at about 12 days). One
minute later the value is `0x7FFF`, which the tag reads as 32767 minutes
(22.7 days). The watchdog does not run during sleep. The tag stays silent until
someone removes the battery and shorts the contacts.

The change counts down minutes only. The AP side already treats a seconds value
this way when it computes the expected check-in.

The same line is in the ESP-IDF C6 firmware and in the Arduino C6 and H2
ports. I changed all three.

### How it showed up

Yellow AP 2.91 with C6 `0x001F`, three M2 ZBS243 tags on `0x0029`. A Home
Assistant automation sent two images about 2 minutes apart every hour. For
years, every few weeks one tag stopped checking in and needed a battery pull. In one case
I logged it: a 2.9" tag fetched the first of two queued images about 4.5
minutes after the second one arrived, the transfer completed, and the tag did
not check in again for 67 hours, until I reset it.

Newer AP builds replace a queued image with a newer one (`1ba895af`). This
makes a two-image queue rare, but an image plus a command or a preload still
gives a queue of two.

### Test

ESP32-S3 Yellow AP on current master, C6 built with this change (ESP-IDF
5.5.4). I set `maxsleep` to 10, so the queued items wait longer than 5 minutes
in the radio. Right after a check-in, I queued a resend and an `ledflash`
command for one tag. The tag took the image 9 minutes later and came back 6
seconds later for the command. On the old C6 firmware this case gives
`nextCheckIn` `0x8000` or `0x7FFx`.

I did not bump the C6 version number. I left that for the release.

body:
Project Room exposed competing attention destinations and lost the selected result when people left and returned. This makes chat the primary surface, groups catch-up and decisions in Updates, and keeps an exact result beside desktop feedback. Returning restores the inspected version and unsent feedback; a newer result does not replace the version being reviewed. Narrow screens keep contextual reading and return to the composer for replies.

The branch removes Activity, the misleading Saved filter and seven unused human UI modules, consolidates external-AI return actions, simplifies entry, and extracts result comparison/feedback controllers. Existing persisted records and agent APIs remain available. Live Updates preserve focus and unchanged rows; permission decisions use current authority. The public marketing footer stays on the signed-out page and no longer overlaps active-room controls at large text sizes.

Result recovery stores only scoped, expiring identifiers and re-fetches content through the authorized endpoint. It preserves exact-version, withdrawal, stale-response and private-draft protections. Web, responsive mobile and the Mac shell share the implementation. No room schema or server write/storage/sync/replay behavior changes; bench:room does not apply.

Validation for the latest runtime source:
- 71 result/comparison browser cases, including seven new recovery/boundary cases, pass.
- Broader action/invitation/session/layout/draft/first-use run: 88 pass and one navigation-sequence failure; the corrected cookie-isolation case passes separately with its data-isolation assertions intact.
- Five additional hosted navigation repair cases pass; the large-text overlap reproduces before the footer fix and passes afterward.

The implementation plan and original failures/repair evidence are recorded in docs/COLLABORATION-COMPONENTS-PLAN-20261019.md. The local concept experiments are exploratory engineering evidence, not human usability or live-agent superiority claims.

The deletions remove redundant UI modules and their current delivery entries instead of retaining hidden maintenance and payload cost. author: monocap-tech
body:
MG23 builds directly on verified MG22 (#271). It retains MG12's full-original-frequency physical source Loewner inequality `S_o <= M² H23 + τ I` instead of replacing `H23` with `tr(H23)I` and dividing by a small Gershgorin floor. The original pole rank-one coupling remains in the matrix envelope `Sstar <= (1+η)(M² H+τI)+4(1+η⁻¹)σ bb*` before any optional scalar bound.

### MG23 verified — October 19, 2026

Focused [GitHub Actions 39374084861](https://github.com/monocap-tech/weil-lab/actions/runs/39374084861) **PASSED** all calculation-bearing and independent Fraction-only algebra/scope checks at commit `ad8e7f09cee20fd3d45c3348b5f0096e886101a2`.

- Full original pole-corrected physical 23D one-step squared-residual gap: **1.384097214793479×10⁻¹²** (MG22: 5.722919722192653×10⁻¹⁶), approximately 2.42×10³ improvement.
- Genuine original 22D pole-null one-step squared-residual gap: **1.2659747790054887×10⁻⁹** (MG22: 1.012671231756979×10⁻¹²), approximately 1.25×10³ improvement.
- Both choose the now-improved dyadic cutoff `2^16` rather than MG22's `2^12`.
- Recomputed original full 25D physical interval Gram, dual-boundary 23D transform, and nonzero pole overlap. All five entire-frequency original strong tails paid.
- Valid upper envelopes **still** imply squared-residual contractions extremely close to 1, and the source frame is **not invariant** under the residual operator.

body:
## M6.0 P2c — test-only prepare/commit/acknowledge/restart fault model

**Baseline:** merged PR #104 `main@689b5172e2b90df357c2239187e49bb25b22da7f`. Continues the bounded P2/P2b purely structural issuer/replay experiments, without implementing a producer or custodian.

### Exactly three new files
- `scripts/bdiag_p2c_fault_state_lab.py`: pure import-only, in-memory state machine. PREPARE validates synthetic P2/P2b receipts and returns an intent; COMMIT performs a **Python-value CAS predicate** and returns an immutable hypothetical updated checkpoint/commit record; ACK creates a nonauthorizing response object only after matching *supplied* commit; RESTART classifies supplied old/new/unknown/contradictory states with never-authorizing NO_GO flags. No actual durable store, file reads, signature, service, transaction or filesystem effects.
- `tests/test_m60bdiag_p2c_fault_recovery_model.py`: crash cutpoints before/after prepare/commit/ack, lost ACK, ack without commit, conflicting ACK, stale CAS, divergent forks of the same old checkpoint, missing intent/store, malformed records, replay, old checkpoint+checksum rollback and safe fixed failure messages. **Fundamental witness**: full rollback of caller-supplied slot/anchor after a hypothetical commit permits the original receipt to be prepared again. A matching commit-looking slot can be forged by the caller; no independent trust follows.
- `docs/architecture/M6_0_BDIAG_P2C_CRASH_RECOVERY_STATE_MODEL.md`: explicit 8-way in-memory recovery semantics, F-C01–F-C12 negative matrix, exit criteria and post-merge ordinary-user focused runbook.

### Security contract
- Every LabRecovery decision is **`NO_GO_P2C_FAULT_STATE_MODEL_ONLY`**; `safe_to_retry_without_external_reconciliation`, `commit_durable_proven`, `acknowledgement_delivered_proven`, `issuer_authenticated`, `independent_anchor_proven`, `durable_replay_prevention_proven`, `source_origin_proven`, `cross_store_epoch_proven`, `custody_proven`, all operational export/reader/Seal/migration flags are required literal FALSE. Even 'COMMIT_VISIBLE' means *visible in caller-supplied Python data*, not proven durable.
- There is no cryptographic signer/key/trust anchor, real anti-replay/custody store, fsync, SQL/SQLite connection, guest stop/restart, SIGKILL, network, source project, path walk, privileged command or public CLI. **In-memory immutable objects do not prove interprocess atomicity or power-loss recovery**.
- Accepted ADR-039, ADR-040 Path A and R0b active WAL fail-closed C stay in force; P0–P4 real proofs remain UNVERIFIED, M0/v3, W1, R1, protected custodian and Collector/CLI remain NO_GO. `projectctl/` runtime, DB schemas, CI and Worker/Task authority untouched.

**Draft for human review; do not auto-merge.** Exact-head GitHub CI required. After review and merge, only ordinary-user pure pytest `tests/test_m60bdiag_p2c_fault_recovery_model.py` and `git diff --check 689b5172e2b90df357c2239187e49bb25b22da7f..origin/main`. No real guest/root exercises.

body:
`Database(create=True)` previously backed up and deleted an existing file before rebuilding it. Creation now builds a complete SQLite/APSW database privately and publishes only to an absent destination, including collisions during preparation. The Database, registry, Core and terminal paths share this contract.

Intentional replacement is a separate offline operation with a required, create-only recovery backup. Preparation and backup failures preserve the original; a published backup survives failed final replacement. Backups preserve file permissions, busy writers cause bounded refusal, and closed WAL databases are covered. Callers must stop all users before replacement; identity checks are not a process lease.

PostgreSQL creation accepts an absent or empty namespace, serializes competing initializers, rejects populated schemas and rolls back partial DDL. Pre-created empty setup namespaces remain supported. File-style PostgreSQL replacement remains unsupported.

The creation/recovery contract, architecture/database task lists, API comments and handoff are updated. The new helper is included in formatting, lint and strict typing gates.

_Requested by **Tianyang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Cy4cMgRtNoXwvAAD9bSPFG?thread=cmsg_01Cy4cMgRtNoXwvAAD9bSPFGSm56wHvMqDy7Wmyqrgq4vC)_

Before: `swing_pivots` could confirm a pivot on the bar it was measured from, so the latest bar could become a pivot (and the same bar could be confirmed as a high and a low, or twice). Those phantom pivots became candidates and moved S/R zones. A zone's `sources` also listed every candidate in its density region, so a 52-week high or low outside the zone's band could exempt a weak zone from `LEVEL_MIN_SCORE`. The backtest note said "within 20 bars", but the outcome window runs from the touch, so it can end up to 39 bars after the build.

After: a pivot is confirmed only by a later bar, and the opposite extreme is searched from the bar after the pivot. A zone's sources come from the candidates inside its band. The backtest and methodology text describe the windows as computed. Nothing else changes: the backtest outcome logic is unchanged, so the old-code rows in the table below still hold.

How: `levels.py` (`swing_pivots`, `density_zones`), `levels_backtest.py` (docstring), `methodology.md`, and tests for the pivot repros and the zone-source case. 400 tests pass on the branch, which is main plus this change.

Backtest, rerun on the fixed code (same six daily series as before, 1995–2018; step 5, 20-bar windows as described above):

| | hold rate | placebo | edge | median width |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| old, swing | 43.4% | 43.8% | −0.5 pts | 0.38 ATR |
| new, swing (fixed) | 53.3% | 54.9% | −1.7 pts | 0.75 ATR |
| old, position | 47.3% | 47.5% | −0.1 pts | 0.55 ATR |
| new, position (fixed) | 53.0% | 53.9% | −1.0 pts | 0.84 ATR |
| new, swing on synthetic data with planted levels | 65.5% | 63.6% | +1.9 pts | 0.75 ATR |

The planted-level oracle check (+22.7 pts) is unchanged. It measures the test itself, not the algorithm. The conclusion from before still holds: these zones are not more predictive than shifted zones.

Known, not fixed: the placebo index wraps modulo the number of as-of bars, so a series with exactly 17 or 41 as-of bars (a very short history) gets a placebo that equals the real zone. The six runs above have hundreds of as-of bars, so they are unaffected.

author: ousret
body:
2.25.903 (2026-10-21)
=====================

- The ``python-socks`` dependency will be removed in a future release. We are
  evaluating alternatives. Version 3 is incompatible with our SOCKS integration
  and must not be installed. The dependency remains capped at <=2.8.1 (#437)
- Fixed HTTP/2 GOAWAY errors reporting ``None`` instead of the error code.
  Errors now include the code and its name when known, in both sync and async. (#436)
- Improved HTTP/3 connection close errors to include the error code and its name
  when known, while preserving the peer's explanation, in both sync and async.
- Fixed QUIC TLS alerts other than ``bad_certificate`` being reported as
  ``ProtocolError`` instead of ``SSLError``, in both sync and async. HTTP/3
  application errors with overlapping codes remain ``ProtocolError``.
- Fixed protocol restrictions for a web extension leaking into other connection
  pools through shared settings, in both sync and async. (#433)
- Fixed redirect header handling comparing against the proxy's origin instead
  of the request's origin. Cross-origin redirects now rebuild the ``Host`` header
  and apply the configured sensitive-header policy, including deferred responses,
  in both sync and async. Backported from https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/5126.
- Fixed ``Retry.parse_retry_after()`` raising ``ValueError`` or ``OverflowError``
  for dates outside the supported range. It now raises ``InvalidHeader``, in both
  sync and async. Backported from https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/5310.
- Fixed incomplete pool shutdown leaving connections open after their last
  response was consumed or closed. Responses and promises returned before
  shutdown remain readable and retrievable, in both sync and async. (#432)
- Fixed closing an HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 response interrupting other responses on
  the shared connection. Unfinished streams are cancelled and their queued
  data is discarded, allowing connection reuse, in both sync and async.
- Fixed cancellation of the async idle connection watcher leaving a connection
  checked out and preventing its cleanup during pool shutdown.
- Fixed the synchronous idle connection watcher retaining its checkout and lock
  after an early exit when generator cleanup is delayed, notably on PyPy.
- Fixed garbage collection of unread synchronous responses blocking the collecting
  thread while waiting for a connection checkout, notably on PyPy.
- Fixed concurrent synchronous connection cleanup raising ``AttributeError``
  when another thread closed the same connection.
- Fixed oversized QUIC probes aborting synchronous HTTP/3 sends or causing
  subsequent async UDP reads to fail, including on Windows. Rejected oversized
  datagrams are now consistently discarded so valid traffic can continue.
- Fixed unrestricted response reads losing buffered decompressed data after a
  partial read. Zero-byte reads also leave the transport and decoder untouched,
  in both sync and async.
- Improved gzip decompression performance by avoiding unnecessary copies when
  only one output chunk is produced, in both sync and async.
  Backported from https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/5304.
- Fixed DNS over QUIC sockets remaining open after protocol termination, in both
  sync and async, and when synchronous setup fails during the handshake or
  because no default CA certificates are available.
- Fixed DNS over QUIC certificate failures being reported as socket timeouts
  while waiting for the QUIC closing timer, in both sync and async.
- Fixed async Happy Eyeballs DNS timeouts being reported as ``ProtocolError``
  instead of ``NameResolutionError``.
- Fixed zero-byte receives waiting for input on native async WASI sockets,
  including TLS connections.
- Fixed address queries on closed native WASI sockets raising ``AttributeError``
  instead of ``OSError``, in both sync and async.
- Fixed requests with custom header mappings lacking a ``copy()`` method raising
  ``AttributeError`` before connection setup, in both sync and async.

body:
## Why
The `lint` job ran an unpinned `pip install ruff`. Ruff 0.16 widened its default rule set, so since **2026-07-24** every CI run has failed `lint` with 10 new findings (LOG015, PIE790, UP017, PYI034, S110, ASYNC251, I001). Every other job `needs: lint`, so go-unit, python-unit, contract, frontend, integration, e2e, compose-stack and the nightly load test have all been skipped. After 60 days with no repo activity GitHub then set the workflow to `disabled_inactivity`.

## Change
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: `pip install ruff==0.15.22`, the newest release the current code passes.
- `simulators/pyproject.toml`: dev extra `ruff>=0.3` changed to `ruff==0.15.22` so `make lint` matches CI.

## Verification
- `ruff check simulators` (as CI runs it) and `cd simulators && ruff check .` (as `make lint` runs it) both pass on 0.15.22. On 0.17.1, today's latest, the same tree reports the 10 errors.
- `ci.yml` parses, and `pip install --dry-run -e "simulators[dev]"` resolves.

## Not in this PR
- **Moving to ruff 0.17.** Some of the new findings are real. One example is a blocking `time.sleep` inside an async test (`test_e2e_ingestion.py:87`). That belongs in its own PR.
- **The nightly `load-test` job.** It has failed independently since 2026-06-11. `ingestion_load.js` is closed-loop (500 VUs, no sleep), so it drives about 6,200 RPS, and p99 comes in at 163 ms against the 500 RPS / p99 < 50 ms gate. It will still fail once lint passes again.

## 概要

[pstack](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack) の `correct` を手元向けに直し、`prevent-recurrence` スキルとして追加します。繰り返している誤りを種類ごとに洗い出し、その種類を型・lint/CI・テストなど強制できる最も高い段で防ぎます。新しいチェックについては、過去の実際の誤りで赤くなることを確かめるところまでを手順にします。

#255〜#257 で、レビュアーが指摘に `encodable` タグを付けるようにしました。このスキルは、溜まったタグをはじめとする記録を、実際のチェックに変える側です。

## 変更内容

- `home/dot_claude/skills/prevent-recurrence/SKILL.md`（新規）: 明示的に呼んだときだけ動く（`disable-model-invocation: true`）
  - 材料: git の履歴、PR のレビューコメント、PR 本文の「Encodable findings」節、メモリの feedback 記録、回避策を説明する注意書き
  - 種類として扱うのは 2 回以上起きたものだけ。1 回きりのものは理由を付けて報告に残す
  - 強制の段は、既存の `encodable` の尺度（`architecture > type > lint > test > hook > rule`）をそのまま使う。選んだ段より上を使えない理由を 1 行ずつ書く
  - 新しいチェックは、誤りが起きたコミットで赤、現在のツリーで緑になる出力を付ける
- `workflow.md`: ユーザーに直されたときに、同じパターンがすでにメモリにあれば `/prevent-recurrence` を提案する、と既存の 1 行に足した。明示呼び出し専用のスキルは、呼ばれるまで読み込まれないため

pstack から取り込まなかったもの: ルールと強制手段の対応表（手で同期する一覧になるため）と、行ごとの期限付き例外。

## 検証

このリポジトリで、同じ課題（「繰り返している誤りを見つけて、再発を防いで」）を、スキルなしとスキルありの 2 回、別エージェント（sonnet、使い捨ての worktree）に実行させました。

| | スキルなし（Red） | スキルあり（Green） |
|---|---|---|
| 作ったもの | ルールファイル 3 つと CLAUDE.md の書き換え | テスト 1 本と CI チェック 1 本 |
| 効くかの証拠 | 書式チェックだけ | 誤りが起きたコミット（`8754c10`、`53ff735`）で赤、HEAD で緑 |
| 1 回きりの誤り | 種類として数えた | 理由を付けて除外した |
| メモリで承認が要るとされた変更 | 許可なく適用した | 適用せずに一覧にした |

赤と緑の結果は、エージェントの報告だけでなく、私の手でも再現しました。Green が作った 2 つのチェックは、別の PR で出します。

`just fmt-check` は exit 0 です。

author: zhangjiadi225
body:
### What this PR does

Before this PR, Mobile had no voice input or output, and audio files could not be attached. After this PR:

- **Dictation**: a composer control dictates into the draft with live text. The default system engine (iOS Speech, Android `SpeechRecognizer`) needs no setup and spends no tokens. An AI transcription model is an optional engine. On Android, the system engine currently requires Google's recognition service; devices without it disable that choice in settings.
- **Read aloud**: assistant replies can be read aloud from the more menu. The default is system text-to-speech; an AI speech model and voice are optional.
- **Audio attachments**: audio files attached in chat are transcribed by the configured transcription model before sending. `read_file` reads audio the same way. Transcripts are cached per file revision and model.
- **Settings → Voice**: an engine per capability, the system or AI voice, and the transcription and speech models.

The composer control, the menu entry and the settings layout are interim; the UI design follows separately. All new copy is translated into the 13 supported locales.

Fixes #1379
Related product request: #1356.

### Screenshots or videos

Pending: the native modules need a new development client, and device acceptance has not run.

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

- `Backend.voice` is the only caller surface; callers never choose an engine. `VoiceRuntime` is the single place that resolves the user's choice, or the first engine the device supports when none is set. It also owns the one active dictation or speech: dictation stops reading, reading replaces reading, and backgrounding or host disposal aborts it.
- Each native library lives in exactly one adapter: `systemDictation` (expo-speech-recognition), `systemSpeech` (expo-speech), `aiDictation` and `aiSpeech` (expo-audio). Adding an engine means one adapter and one registration in `createVoice`.
- Audio attachments go through an optional `transcribeAudio` reader port on the shared attachment reader. The file service does not depend on voice or AI, and chat attachments and file tools share one path. Without a transcription model, sending fails with a `transcription-unconfigured` attachment issue.
- AI requests reuse `AiService` account resolution with the OpenAI audio adapter, one attempt each. Upstream audio APIs report no usage or price, so no usage records are created.
- Engine choices and the system voice are device-local preferences.
- Restores the "Invocation Usage And Context Occupancy" section of `provider-integration.md` that an earlier commit removed by mistake.

### Breaking changes

Existing development clients must be rebuilt: this adds `expo-speech-recognition` and `expo-speech`, recording and speech-recognition permissions, and Android package visibility for Google's recognizers.

### Special notes for your reviewer

Vendor recognizers, such as Xiaomi's `com.xiaomi.mibrain.speech`, implement the same `RecognitionService` but are not enabled until verified on devices. An on-device model engine (sherpa-onnx) is a candidate follow-up for devices without Google services.

Validation passed:
- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm i18n:check` (13 locales), `pnpm docs:check-links`.
- Focused Jest: 292 suites and 3,484 tests across voice, file, AI/agent, bootstrap, shared, chat, settings, composer, and architecture boundaries. These cover engine choice, the single-activity rule, backgrounding and disposal, Markdown to prose, request splitting, utterance joining, Android recognizer detection, audio classification and limits, attachment transcription, caching and failures, transcript paging, dictation draft restoration, and the composed native configuration.

Not run: native builds, device acceptance, and real provider calls. Native fakes establish contracts, not device behavior.

### Checklist

- [x] Branch: targets `main`
- [x] PR: describes behavior, constraints and validation
- [ ] Preview: screenshots/video pending UI design and device acceptance
- [x] Code: reuses the provider, attachment reader, permission and composer boundaries
- [x] Upgrade: documents the required development-client rebuild
- [x] Documentation: `docs/references/voice.md` and shared building blocks updated
- [x] Self-review: reviewed the final diff

### Release note

```release-note
Add voice input and read-aloud with built-in system engines or optional AI models, and transcription of attached audio files.
```

author: lukaszrozmej
body:
Follow-up to the review on #142. The overlap ordering it raised is already fixed on `main` by #143, and #147 has since moved the big-endian limb helpers into shared code with the `>= 32` span asserts this PR first added.

- The README's RISC-V zkVM section documents how a guest whose zkVM has Zbb's `rev8` and native misaligned word access switches big-endian conversion to a word load plus `rev8`: a substitution file with the `<linker>` root, passed to ILC through `IlcArg --substitution:`. ILC ignores a file without the root silently and warns IL2009 when the method is not found.
- `HasByteReverse`'s summary names both conditions the flag stands for, and its remarks say the substitution matches `get_HasByteReverse` by name, so a rename or a constant stops it from applying with IL2009.
- A zkVM-only test checks that `get_HasByteReverse` stays a static `bool` getter, so a rename fails CI.
- CI gains a Debug zkVM row, so the limb helpers' asserts run; the other Debug rows take the hardware-accelerated paths.
- The offset test's comment says it checks the scalar paths' offset handling: test hosts never fault on misaligned access.

No behaviour change. The README's substitution was checked with a NativeAOT compile against the zkVM build: with the root it shrinks `ToBigEndian` from 401 to 107 bytes and the big-endian ctor from 551 to 204; without it the output is unchanged. All tests pass in both builds, including the new Debug zkVM row.

author: ianborders
body:
Before: the app's Update rolled two agents back without running a single eval. One builds its judge inline in `evals.config.ts` (`model: createAnthropic({ baseURL: … }).evaluationModel(…)`), which `kyb upgrade` could not resolve, so it decided the gate "can only run on its host" while already on the host. The other has a subagent scaffolded with `exeModel({ model: … "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5", createOpenAI })`; exe 0.17 refuses a Claude id without `createAnthropic` at load, so the eval suite stopped before its first case.

After: the judge lookup reads an inline provider as well as a named one, and `kyb upgrade` passes `createAnthropic` to every `exeModel` call that has only `createOpenAI` (adding the import, and installing `@ai-sdk/anthropic` if the agent lacks it). Both agents can then run their own eval gate.

How: `exeJudgeUrl` tries the inline `create…({ … })` body before the named-binding form. The new `exe-claude-route.ts` repair runs with the other repairs, in both the install and the nothing-to-install paths. Passing `createAnthropic` is harmless for a non-Claude id, since exeModel only uses it for `anthropic/…`. Tests cover both (create suite 150/150).

author: copilot
body:
This PR adds a pure photo-processing path that generates redacted JPEG bytes from image bytes + `HideRegion` list, aligned to MVP section 6 requirements. It normalizes orientation into pixels before redaction and emits output without EXIF metadata or embedded original thumbnails.

- **Core processing (`PhotoProcessor` implementation)**
  - Added `ImagePhotoProcessor` in `lib/core/photo/image_photo_processor.dart`.
  - `normalize(Uint8List)` now:
    - decodes input bytes,
    - bakes EXIF orientation into pixels,
    - re-encodes to JPEG with EXIF cleared,
    - returns `SourcePhoto` with normalized dimensions.
  - `redact(SourcePhoto, List<HideRegion>)` now:
    - decodes normalized source bytes,
    - burns each region as opaque black pixels,
    - re-encodes to JPEG with EXIF cleared,
    - returns `RedactedJpeg` preserving source pixel size.

- **Dependency update**
  - Added `image: ^4.5.4` to support decode/orientation/redaction/encode flow.

- **Unit coverage for issue acceptance criteria**
  - Added `test/core/photo/image_photo_processor_test.dart` to validate:
    - orientation normalization changes dimensions as expected,
    - redaction output keeps original normalized size,
    - target pixels are blackened at expected coordinates,
    - output JPEG has no EXIF (and therefore no carried thumbnail payload).

```dart
final normalized = await processor.normalize(inputBytes);
final redacted = await processor.redact(normalized, regions);
// redacted.bytes: JPEG without EXIF, same pixel size as normalized
```

author: pojuiatwork3881154
body:
Refs #36.

## What

Adds the PLDM Type 2 PDR read path as codecs only: GetPDRRepositoryInfo
(0x50), GetPDR (0x51), and the multipart transfer state machine the latter
needs. No dispatch arm calls any of it, so `pldm-interface` behavior is
unchanged and `GetPLDMTypes` still reports Type 0 and Type 5 alone.

Two commits:

- `protocol/platform.rs` carries the 20 Type 2 command codes, the enum8
  enumerations, both timestamp wire types, and the per-command completion
  codes. `util/crc.rs` wraps CRC_8_SMBUS, the polynomial DSP0248 names for
  the transferCRC.
- `message/platform/` carries the two codecs and `pdr_transfer.rs`, the
  state a multipart GetPDR walks.

## Why the GetPDR codec is hand written

`recordData` is variable length and `transferCRC` is conditional. DSP0248
Table 69 places that CRC on the End part alone, and computes it over the
whole PDR rather than over the part carrying it. Encoding therefore refuses
a flag and CRC combination that disagrees, rather than shifting every
following byte in the requester's decoder.

Clause 26.2.7 shapes the transfer state. The requester repeats the
recordHandle it opened the transfer with, which is 0x0000_0000 for a walk
of the whole repository. The state keeps that handle beside the one the
repository resolved it to, and checks each against its own source. A part
is also capped by what the caller's response buffer can carry, since
Table 69 lets a responder return fewer bytes than requestCount asks for.

## The repository stays outside this crate

The transfer state holds no record data. The caller resolves the requested
recordHandle in whatever repository it owns and passes the record in, so
this crate keeps no storage of its own. The trait that carries the
repository across that boundary lands with the dispatch, in the next PR
for #36.

## One question

The `pldm-interface/src/config.rs` hunk is a single line: it declares PLDM
Base 1.2.0 in place of 1.1.0, the version the OpenPRoT PLDM middleware
specification names. It adds no Base command and is the only change outside
`pldm-common`. I can drop it from this PR if you would rather see it on its
own.

## Tests

Unit tests cover every codec here: the GetPDR and GetPDRRepositoryInfo wire
formats, the transfer state's own rules from clause 26.2.7, and
CRC_8_SMBUS against the catalog check value of 0xF4 for "123456789".

## Dependency

`crc` 3.4.0 with `default-features = false`, pinned to the version the
OpenPRoT firmware tree already locks so both resolve to one copy. It and
`crc-catalog` 2.5.0 declare `MIT OR Apache-2.0`, which the repository's
`deny.toml` allows.

## AI disclosure

Written with AI assistance. Every wire format traces to a DSP0248 clause or
table, and the tests were run.

author: remenby31
body:
Suit la revue de #43 côté cœur. Le cœur passe le struct en **version 2** (build de 07:30).
- **v1** (0075 avant la revue) : diagnostics facultatifs (88 ou 256 octets), 4 paires top-miss puis `spare`.
- **v2** : 256 octets obligatoires, 3 paires top-miss puis `installMaxSliceMs` (le plus long temps d'installs dans une tranche), `installsFast` (installs de moins de 0,5 ms, donc des hits du cache natif V8) et `installMs` (temps hôte de compilation des modules de région). Ces trois champs sont cumulés et jamais remis à zéro ; `p4.diagnostics` porte la valeur de la dernière fenêtre.
- Toute autre version est refusée. Un cœur v1 n'est jamais décodé avec les noms de la v2 (un PC lu comme des ms).
- La remise à zéro (n ≥ 0) est appliquée par le CPU à la tranche suivante, sans effet pour race-perf, qui lit en fin de fenêtre.
- `docs/jit-flags.md` : le coût mémoire par défaut est celui de mem7, +57 Mo en médiane (+51 à +126 Mo, pic +50 à +94 Mo), et non +36 Mo.

Tests : un test v1, un test v2, un refus de version inconnue, et v2 sans diagnostics refusée. Harnais : 117/117. Seuls le harnais et la doc sont touchés.

author: ahsanali-taxsimba
body: Stacked on the invoice extraction engine. This adds the accountant review workspace so extracted invoices can be compared with the original document, corrected, approved into a draft, and posted to the ledger. ## Pages - `/invoices/extraction` — queue of documents by review status and confidence - `/invoices/extraction/[documentId]` — side-by-side original document + extracted form - `/invoices/[id]` — approved invoice/bill detail with attachments, audit, journal preview, and post ## Review workspace - **DocumentViewer** — PDF.js canvas for PDFs, image viewer for JPG/PNG, zoom / rotate / page navigation - **ExtractedInvoiceForm** — supplier, invoice number, dates, line items, VAT/ITSA - Low-confidence fields highlighted yellow; missing fields highlighted red - Line items add/remove with auto-calculated subtotal, VAT, and total - **Differences detected** banner when the accountant edits extracted fields - **Ready to post** banner after approval ## Actions - Approve & Create Invoice (draft sales invoice or purchase bill) - Save as Draft - Reject Extraction - Re-run Extraction - Attach additional receipts/contracts - Post to Ledger + View Journal Preview on the detail page ## API - `GET /invoices/extractions?clientId=` - `POST /invoices/extraction/:documentId/save-draft` - `POST /invoices/extraction/:documentId/reject` - `POST /invoices/extraction/:documentId/reprocess` - `GET /invoices/extraction/:documentId/audit` - `GET /documents?invoiceId=` / `?billId=` - `GET|POST /bookkeeping/invoices/:id` and `/post` + `/journal-preview` (same for bills) Do not merge independently of the stacked MTD/document/extraction parents.

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>google-antigravity/antigravity-cli (antigravity-cli)</summary>

### [`v1.4.3`](https://redirect.github.com/google-antigravity/antigravity-cli/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#143)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/google-antigravity/antigravity-cli/compare/1.4.2...1.4.3)

- Added `/` search to the `/diff` file list and file view: matches are highlighted as you type, the search prompt shows how many matches the diff and each file contain, `Enter` jumps to the first match, and `n`/`N` step through matches one at a time across every file, with `match A/B` in the file view header. `n`/`N` in the artifact viewer now also step through matches one at a time, including several on the same line, instead of jumping from line to line.
- Improved `agy plugin validate` to also check a plugin's hooks, sidecars, and component lists: it reports an error when `hooks.json`, a `sidecar.json`, or a `skills.json`, `rules.json`, `agents.json`, or `sidecars.json` file can't be parsed, and warns about unknown hook events, hook matchers that aren't valid regular expressions and so never match, a `hooks/hooks.json` file (which isn't read), list entries with no path or with a path missing from the plugin, `commands/` folders and `workflows/` Markdown files (which plugins don't load), and a Claude Code-style top-level `"hooks"` key, which loads as a single hook named `hooks`.
- Improved timer labels in `/tasks` and the active task list to show durations in days, hours, minutes, and seconds, such as `1d 2h timer` or `5m timer`, instead of raw seconds such as `93784s timer`.
- Fixed Gemini 4 Argon not shown in `/model` and `--model` when you connect with a `GEMINI_API_KEY`.
- Fixed the CLI offering options that need the terminal sandbox on systems where it can't run, such as Linux systems that block unprivileged user namespaces and Windows before Windows 11 24H2.
- Fixed subagents and custom agents in Auto mode asking you to approve every command that would leave the terminal sandbox; like the main agent's, their commands are now first reviewed by a separate agent, so safe commands run without asking and risky ones still prompt you.
- Fixed the agent losing track of its most recently started subagents after a conversation was compacted, because the summary included each subagent's full initial prompt and was cut off before their conversation IDs; the summary now keeps only each subagent's type, role, and result, which also leaves more room in the context window.
- Fixed a `PostToolUse` hook that fails to run, for example because its command is missing, exits with an error, times out, or prints invalid JSON, marking the tool call it follows as failed even though the tool succeeded; the failure is now logged and the tool keeps its result.
- Fixed the agent failing to create empty files such as `__init__.py` or `.gitkeep`, and failing to write or edit regular project files with `... is not a valid artifact path` when the model sent blank artifact details.
- Fixed updating or reinstalling a marketplace plugin on Windows leaving it half-deleted when another `agy` session, the Antigravity desktop app, or the Remote Control background service had it open; the installed plugin now stays intact until the new copy is in place, and the previous version is restored if the replacement fails.
- Fixed `agy plugin install` and `agy plugin import` writing color codes into piped or redirected output, ignoring `NO_COLOR`, and showing raw codes in older Windows consoles; like `agy plugin validate`, they now use color only in a terminal and follow `NO_COLOR`, `CLICOLOR`, and `CLICOLOR_FORCE`.
- Fixed Remote Control on iPhone and iPad asking you to accept the `Security Notice & Data Use` terms and showing the `Enable Notifications` prompt again every time you reopened it; it now remembers your answers, along with your theme, layout, and dismissed tips.
- Fixed the prompt cursor appearing in the wrong place after resizing the terminal (sometimes on the `↑ N more lines` indicator or below the input box), when a slash command's completion hint didn't fit on the last line of the prompt (the hint is now shortened or left out), when the prompt was taller than the terminal, after pressing `Up` or `Down` onto a line with CJK characters or emoji, and after entering Vim visual mode, which also rewrapped the text.
- Fixed the cursor drifting on lines with emoji such as 👩‍💻, 👍🏽, or ⚠️ inside tmux 3.6 and later, and after returning from your external editor (`Ctrl+G`) or a `Ctrl+Z` suspend in terminals that support grapheme-cluster widths.
- Fixed the cursor drifting and lines wrapping too early under Japanese, Chinese, or Korean locales such as `LANG=ja_JP.UTF-8` when text contains characters like `→`, `…`, `─`, or `•`, which parts of the CLI counted as two columns wide while the rest drew them as one.
- Fixed `Left`, `Right`, `Backspace`, and `Delete` in the prompt and other text boxes moving over or deleting only part of an emoji such as 👩‍💻 or 👍🏽, a flag, or a letter with a combining accent, and fixed text boxes cutting off a wide character, such as a CJK character or emoji, at the end of a wrapped line instead of moving it to the next line.
- Fixed lines containing combining marks or other zero-width characters wrapping too early or leaving blank rows in `/diff` and the inline diff preview, and being cut off with `…` too soon in `/artifact` previews.

author: rileyr
body:
## Summary

GH #1592 step S4. A `std::observe::Otlp { endpoint, service, interval, timeout_ms, max_batch }` param of main sends the runtime's lifecycle and topology events to an OpenTelemetry collector as OTLP/HTTP JSON log records: `locus.birth` and `locus.dissolve` (with locus, instance and parent), `locus.restart`, `locus.failure`, and a `hale.start` record carrying the build identity. The resource carries `service.name`, the model hash, the entity-id digest and `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`. An empty `endpoint` reads the standard `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*` variables. Shared memory stays the local default.

The declaration is a typed param of main recognized by type, like `Scrape` and `Probes`; there is no new syntax.

## Architecture

- Part: the observe backends (`std::observe`, `observe_expand`, the runtime's `lotus_obs.c` event ring).
- A program that observes nothing is unchanged. The event ring and its probes are compiled under `LOTUS_OBSERVE` only for a program that defines `lotus_observe_events` (emitted only when an `Otlp` is held); every other program emits no event call and links the runtime object it linked before.
- One scheduler. The exporter is a locus placed by `placement` that drains a bounded ring (4096 events, never waited on; a full ring drops and counts) and sends through `std::http::Client` on the runtime's own I/O, with a total deadline and no retry. There is no second runtime and no tokio. Dropped batches are counted (`hale_otlp_dropped_total` on a held `Scrape`).
- The backend's own send work is not an event.

## Tests

- `observe_events` (in the `http` area binary): a program with an `Otlp` param against a collector stub bound on port 0 receives the lifecycle records; a collector that never answers costs batches, not the program; a program without an `Otlp` has no event call and no ring in its IR.
- `observe_backend` extended: an `Otlp` param is recognized as `Scrape` is.
- Goldens, stdlib table and topology baseline regenerated.
- Spec (runtime, semantics, stdlib, styleguide) and `docs/src/everyday/logging.md` updated.

body:
Klien melaporkan impor Chapter Roster dan Due Date "masih belum bisa" di versi trial.

## Penyebab
bnisystem.id mendaratkan pengguna di mode **Data Contoh** (nilai awal dari `.env.production` untuk semua host). Importer mode itu hanya membaca CSV, jadi berkas `.xls` BNI Connect ditolak. Backend di bnisystem.id sendiri sudah versi terbaru dan siap.

## Perbaikan
- `VITE_API_HOSTS=bnisystem.id,www.bnisystem.id`: di host itu mode awalnya **Backend API**. Pratinjau Vercel tetap Data Contoh. Pilihan yang pernah disimpan pengguna tetap menang.
- Halaman Impor menampilkan peringatan di mode Data Contoh dengan tombol **Beralih ke Backend API**.
- Importer menolak laporan BNI Connect yang baris "Chapter:"-nya tidak cocok dengan chapter tujuan. Sebelumnya laporan Supreme yang diunggah ke chapter lain menempelkan seluruh namanya ke sana.
- Halaman Chapter: tombol **Tambah Chapter** (admin), supaya chapter seperti Supreme bisa dibuat sebelum impor.

## Bukti
Berkas asli klien 20 Oktober (chapter Supreme) lewat alur wizard di Postgres lokal: Roster → 54 member baru; Dues → 54 diperbarui dengan tanggal jatuh tempo; nol ditolak; hasil akhir 54 member bertanggal jatuh tempo dan bertelepon. Berkas 10 Oktober (chapter Rise) juga lulus. Suite backend penuh hijau; `npm run typecheck && npm run build` hijau. author: roryeckel
body:
## What this changes

Supports pi 1.x and projects Agent Plugin MCP servers into pi's native MCP client.

The scheduled harness-watch run found pi 1.3.0 outside the only profile range, `>=0.84 <1` (#107). Its drift capture-compare showed new payload fields (#112). This PR:

- adds a separate `>=1 <2` profile with 1.3.0 as the reference build and new evidence;
- projects stdio and streamable-HTTP MCP servers into pi 1.x for package and project delivery;
- fixes path bugs in the shared MCP launcher and OpenCode project delivery that the review passes found.

Closes #107, closes #112.

### pi 1.x support

- **Profiles.** A new `>=1 <2` profile (`PI_RANGE`) sits beside `>=0.84 <1` (`PI_LEGACY_RANGE`), with the reference build at 1.3.0 and fixtures in `fixtures/pi/1.3`. The `>=0.84 <1` profile and `fixtures/pi/0.84` stay as that line's evidence. The scheduled-playback record now rolls on the 1.x profile.
- **Captured on 1.3.0, model-free.** All captures used the loopback model:
  - lifecycle, shells, the exit-7 error, RPC compaction and cancelled compaction (`.capture/pi/probe-sessions.mjs`);
  - the feature probes on Windows and Linux;
  - the completion edges;
  - `HOOKNOSTIC_PLAYBACK=pi`.

  Against 0.84.4, all mapped payloads differ only by added fields.
- **Behavior change from pi 1.2.** A `sendMessage({triggerTurn: true})` continuation now fires `before_agent_start` with `messageType: "custom"` and no prompt. The decoder rejects it explicitly, so `prompt.before` does not fire for that run, as on 0.84. The captured fixture `before-agent-start-custom` pins this. Before this change the event was dropped only by accident, through the shim's fail-open path.

### Native MCP (pi 1.x)

Evidence is in `.capture/pi-mcp/README.md`.

- A generated extension calls `pi.registerMcpServer`: `hooknostic-mcp.js` in packages, `.pi/extensions/hooknostic-mcp.js` for project delivery.
  - **stdio** runs through the shared launcher. pi never sees package text, so its `~/`, `$NAME`, `${NAME}` and `!command` expansion cannot reach it.
  - **Streamable HTTP** keeps the URL verbatim and escapes header values with pi's `$$` and `$!`.
  - **SSE** is omitted, because `registerMcpServer` throws for it.
- pi's default codemode exposure is kept. Codemode's nested MCP calls still reach `tool.before` and `tool.after`.
- Project delivery claims `.pi/mcp.json` `mcpServers.<name>` absent, compared by pi's namespace fold. This uses a new optional `fold` on core's absent check, because pi treats names that differ only in `-` and `_` as one server. pi rejects some server names (invalid characters, or a duplicate under the fold); these become project omissions under `components.onUnsupported` instead of failing the build. The rationales note that the user-level `~/.pi/agent/mcp.json` can also shadow a server and that no sync can check it.
- **ADR-0032.** pi's MCP tool names are lossy: they are sanitized, and hashed when too long or colliding. So `mcp__*` classifies as `kind: "mcp"`, and the split is never parsed from the name. `tool_result.details` states the server and tool. That identity reaches the view through `ReportedToolFacts.mcp`, so `classifyTool` rebuilds the same view (ADR-0023). `Adapter.mcpIdentity` declares the source (`statement` on `tool.after`/`tool.error`, for `>=1 <2`). The contract suite, `hooknostic dispatch`, `inspect` and the support page all honour it.

### Path fixes found in review

The new `portableRelative` helper in core computes the offsets generated modules resolve. It works between real paths, is absolute across Windows drives and UNC shares, and leaves POSIX backslashes alone. It is used by pi's MCP extension, OpenCode project delivery and the shared launcher.

This fixes an OpenCode project bug that predates the branch: when the project was reached through a junction or symlink, stdio servers got a working directory that does not exist. A test reproduces it.

`hooknostic-mcp.js` is also added to `.pi/extensions/.gitattributes`.

## Scope

- [ ] Docs / typo / clarification
- [x] Bug fix with a reproduction
- [x] A claim about a harness (capability level, shape table, honoured channel)
- [x] The portable vocabulary (effect, capability id, HNxxx diagnostic, event, tool kind)
- [ ] A new harness adapter

Issue: #107, #112

## Proof of resolution

- [x] Each new test was watched failing against its defect, by applying a mutant and then restoring. Covered:
  - the custom-run rejection;
  - the `mcp__` classification;
  - header escaping (two playback lanes, two unit tests);
  - stated-identity handling (classifier, decoder, dispatch, contract);
  - the version-range gate;
  - the absent claim;
  - omissions;
  - realpath offsets;
  - `__proto__`;
  - `.gitattributes`;
  - the out-of-range hint;
  - UNC and POSIX path handling.

  The OpenCode junction test failed against `master`'s code (expected `…\work\project\tools`, received `…\work\hooknostic-opencode-real-…\work\project\tools`).

<details><summary>Example: the escaping mutant against playback</summary>

```
× runs repository-local integration without installing a plugin
× registers projected package MCP servers and reaches them through codemode (local-path)
Tests  2 failed | 58 skipped (60)
```

</details>

## Proof of no regression

Each command was run separately and its exit code captured, on Windows with pi 1.3.0.

- [x] `pnpm lint`: 0
- [x] `pnpm build`: 0
- [x] `pnpm test`: 0 (2132 passed, 95 skipped)
- [x] `HOOKNOSTIC_PLAYBACK=pi HOOKNOSTIC_PLAYBACK_VERSION=1.3.0 pnpm exec vitest run packages/cli/test/harness-playback.test.ts`: 0 (42 passed). This includes the four MCP lanes: the package by local path and by npm coordinate, repository-local integration, and the fixture MCP tool.
- [ ] OpenCode playback was not run locally. Only `opencode` 2.0.32 is installed here, the v1 lane needs `opencode-ai` 1.x, and the v2 suite has no repository-local MCP lane. CI's lanes cover them.

## Evidence

- [x] Fixtures are added under `fixtures/pi/1.3/`, with provenance in that directory's README. MCP tool payloads come from `.capture/pi-mcp`.
- [x] `validatedOn` records are added for 1.3.0, covering captured, live-probe, schema-derived and playback evidence.
- [x] The recorded provenance matches what was done. Scripted loopback arguments are called constructed inputs, and the payloads are pi's own.

## Generated output

- [x] Committed example artifacts were rebuilt from the repository root, and a second rebuild is byte-stable.
- [x] `docs/harness-support.md` was regenerated.
- [x] Nothing generated was hand-edited. `examples/local-project/.pi/**` is now in `.prettierignore`, because formatting a sync-generated file breaks the examples build.

## Anything else

- **Review.** The change went through five Codex review passes until there were no findings. The first four found real bugs, all fixed here. The last pass checked about 25,600 Windows path round trips for `portableRelative`.
- **Residual, documented in ADR-0032.** The shim sees only the target range, not the running pi version. So on a `>=0.84 <1` target the decoder still reads `details`. There an `mcp__` tool can only belong to another extension, and a split appears only if that extension's `details` names `server` and `tool` as strings.
- **Docs.** README and tutorial snippets, `installing-artifacts.md`, `configuration.md` and the example configs now target `>=1 <2` and drop the `pi:mcp-stdio-omitted` accepts, which no longer apply on 1.x.

`npm test` builds the page, then runs **31 tests** with Node's built-in test runner. The browser tests use Playwright with Chromium. Playwright is the only dependency, and only the tests need it; the site itself is unchanged.

| `tests/logic.test.mjs` | The maths, using the page's own functions: `compute()` against an **independent Sainte-Laguë implementation** over 40 random polls; the 5% threshold (4.9% → 0 seats, 5.0% → seats, under 5% plus an electorate → seats); overhang grows the House and the majority line; Te Pāti Māori's one-name list leaves seats vacant; `seatProbs()` adds to 1 and responds to party vote; `eff()` and the Opportunity squeeze conserve votes; the simulation is repeatable; the 600-run quick pass equals the start of the full run; calling one seat leaves every other seat's results unchanged; every simulated Parliament adds up and is labelled correctly; simulations-off equals the poll as published |
| `tests/ui.test.mjs` | As a visitor: latest poll is the default, every poll and the average run, calling and uncalling a seat, the map (both layers), reset, analytics events, no page errors |

## Checking the tests catch real bugs

I broke the code three ways on purpose. Each break failed exactly the test that should catch it, and everything passes again with the original code:

| Deliberate bug | Test that failed |
|---|---|
| D'Hondt instead of Sainte-Laguë | `seat allocation matches an independent Sainte-Laguë calculation` |
| 5% threshold removed | `a party under 5% with no electorate gets no seats…` |
| Extra random draw for called seats | `calling one seat doesn't change any other seat's results` |

Two August polls were out of order: "Roy Morgan, Jul–Aug" (midpoint 10 Aug) was listed above "RNZ–Reid, 14–21 Aug" (midpoint 18 Aug). It was harmless, because only the first poll is the default, but it's now fixed and checked.

- **`pages.yml`** now calls it first: `deploy` has `needs: test`, so a failing test stops the deploy.

- `CLAUDE.md` gains a "Tests" section, and `README.md` gains a short one.

author: kramhash
body:
## Summary

Closes #30. With `samples > 1`, a loop's frame one loop later wasn't byte-identical (frame 960 vs 0 of LIMINAL VEIN: PSNR ~83 dB).

```diff
 createPasses({
-  accumulation: { samples: 32, shutter: 0.5, fps: 60 },
+  accumulation: { samples: 32, shutter: 0.5, fps: 60, loop: 16 },
 })
```

```diff
 drawPreview / drawCapture(state)
+  state.time = wrapTime(state.time, loop)       # double: 16 → exactly 0
   drawSample
-    u_time = state.time + offset                # float32 near 16 drops offset bits
+    u_time = wrapped + offset                    # added in double, then uploaded
     bindUniforms.get(wrapped + offset)
   finishFrame
     u_frameTime = wrapped
```

**Why not the issue's `u_shutterTime` proposal:** implemented it first, but on ANGLE/Metal `mod(u_frameTime, LOOP) + u_shutterTime` still differed between frames 0 and 960. A GPU probe showed `mod(16.0, 16.0) == 0.0`, yet `fract((mod(u_frameTime, L) + u_shutterTime) / L) == fract(u_shutterTime / L)` failed for one of two samples at frame 960 only, so the compiler reorders the sum. Wrapping on the CPU side doesn't depend on that.

- `ResolvedAccumulation` gains `loop` (`null` by default; `setAccumulation({ loop: null })` clears it). Additive.
- README / docs / CHANGELOG (fx-passes `Unreleased` → Added). LIMINAL VEIN sets `loop: 16`.

## Evidence

- fx-passes e2e (new): 8 samples, 180° shutter, a shader with `sin(u_time * 4111.0)`: with `loop: 16`, frame at 16 s equals frame at 0 s; without, it differs. Also checks `u_frameTime` = 1.5 at 17.5 s and that bound uniforms see the wrapped time. **Fails without the `createPasses.ts` change.**
- Unit: `wrapTime` (16 → 0, 960/60 → 0, negative times), `loop` validation and merge.
- LIMINAL VEIN, `frapx-render` at the default 1920×1080 / 32 spp: `frame_00960.png` is **byte-identical** to `frame_00000.png` (rhythm bindings on). Real time in Chrome: 60 fps, `accumulation.loop` 16.
- `pnpm build`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:e2e` (all suites): pass.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** none without `loop`. With it, shaders see time wrapped into the loop, so effects meant to keep growing past the loop length (a timeline longer than the loop) would wrap — which is what the option is for.

Part of #3.

Names `func_80016D2C` as **`Duel_DrawDecimalDigits`**. It is shared source in every region: `0x80016D2C` in North America, `0x80016C18` in Japan, `0x80016C44` in SLES-03947 and `0x80016C48` in the other European images.

### Evidence
- **Body** (`duel_card_and_status_draw.c`):
  - encodes `source` into `count` decimal digits with `Text_EncodeDecimalDigits`;
  - sorts one `GsSPRITE` per digit, last byte first, with `u = digit * 8`, stepping `x` by 8;

- **Only caller:** `Duel_DrawLifePointsAndDeckCounts`, in the same unit. It calls this function four times: each side's `displayed_life_points` with four digits, and each side's remaining deck count (`DECK_SIZE - deck_draw_cursor`) with two digits.

The name follows `CardList_DrawDecimalDigits`. Unlike that function, this one has no below-10 test and draws every encoded byte.

- **Inventories and symbols:** `functions.csv` and `symbols.txt` for all seven executables.
- **Source:** the definition and its four calls, the declaration in `duel_card_and_status_draw.h`, and two comments in `display_object.h`.

Workers Logs のエラーが 1 日 274 件ありました（10/19〜20）。ほぼすべてが同じ形です。

```
StaticAssetsIncrementalCache: Failed to set to read-only cache key=/route-cache/APP_PAGE/2825bf9e…/$/xmlrpc.php type=cache
```

- パスは `/.env-example`・`/.env.aws`・`/wp-login.php`・`/xmlrpc.php`・`/blog` など、ボットの探索です
- キーの `2825bf9e…` は `sha256("/[locale]/page")` です（Next 16.4 の `route-cache-key.js` は、ルートのモジュール名のハッシュをキーに使います）
- `/[locale]` に `dynamicParams` が無いため、1 階層のパスはどれも `/[locale]` に当たっていました

- Next 16.4 はその 404 を保存しようとしますが、保存先の静的アセットキャッシュは読み取り専用なので、毎回エラーになっていました
- 子ルート（articles・compare・tag・tech・category）は、すでに `dynamicParams = false` です

## 変えたこと

- `src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx`: `export const dynamicParams = false`。言語は `generateStaticParams` の ja / en だけで、それ以外は描画せずに 404 ページを返します
- `src/app/[locale]/layout.test.ts`: `dynamicParams` と言語の一覧を固定しました

## 確認（本番と同じ実行環境：`opennextjs-cloudflare build` → `preview`）

同じパスを、修正前と修正後のビルドに送りました。エラーの件数は、preview が記録したログ（Local Explorer の observability）で数えています。

| | ボットのパス（5 件）の応答 | 読み取り専用キャッシュのエラー |

| 修正後 | 404・約 4ms（描画しない） | **0 件** |

author: laurentftech
body:
## Summary

This follows pi's approach: pi ships its `CHANGELOG.md` in the package, remembers the last version it showed (`lastChangelogVersion`), and after an update displays the newer sections.

- **`CHANGELOG.md`**, hand-written: sections from 0.41.0 to 0.44.0, with a link to GitHub Releases for anything older.
  - Both builds inline it through an esbuild `define`, the same way as the version: `cli/scripts/build.mjs` (npm) and `server/scripts/build-sea.mjs` (executables).
  - Nothing has to be found on disk, so it works offline.
- **Server** (`server/src/changelog.ts`):
  - It writes the running version to `<agentDir>/outpost-version.json`.
  - After an update it sends `outpostChanges { from, to, entries, releaseNotes }`, in the snapshot and through `outpost_changes`.
  - The news stays for as long as the new version runs.
  - Silent for a first install, a downgrade or `dev`.
  - An installation older than the marker is detected through the update check's cache and is told about the running release only. That is what makes the very first 0.43 → 0.44 update show something.
  - The version is recorded *before* the update check runs, so a first run cannot be mistaken for an earlier one.
- **`changelogNotice: false`** turns the banner off. The version is still recorded, so turning it back on does not announce an old update.
- **UI**:
  - `ChangesNotice` shows a one-line banner, "pi-outpost was updated to X (from Y)". **What's changed** expands the rendered sections and a link to the GitHub release.
  - It is dismissed per version in each browser, and hidden in the embedded widget.
  - `UpdateNotice` gains a **What's new** link to the new version's release.
- **Release**:
  - `scripts/changelog-section.mjs` extracts a version's section.
  - `release.yml` refuses the tag when the section is missing, empty or duplicated, before anything is published.
  - The section becomes the GitHub Release body, followed by the generated list of PRs (`--notes-file` together with `--generate-notes`).
  - `test:scripts` fails when the packages' version has no section, so a bump cannot be merged without one.

OpenSpec change: `openspec/changes/embedded-changelog` (`validate --strict` passes; `check:scenarios`: 9/9 covered).

## Verification

- Server: `changelog.test.ts`, `update.test.ts`, `config.test.ts`, `release-workflow.test.mjs`.
  - `versionsBundled.test.mjs` builds the **real bundle** with an inlined changelog and reads `outpost_changes` off the socket.
  - With `changelogNotice: false`, the same test sees the marker update and no message.
- UI: `ChangesNotice`, `UpdateNotice`, `App` (standalone vs widget), `useAgent`. `test:scripts` 18/18. Lint clean.
  - Writing the tests exposed a real bug in the script: a duplicated section went unnoticed because the scan stopped at the next section. Fixed.
- Running app (`scripts/probes/changelog-server.mts`: bundled server at 0.44.0, marker at 0.43.0, update check off), checked in the standalone app:
  - the banner and the rendered section, with links opening in a new tab;
  - seven rapid toggles;
  - dismiss then reload: the banner stays gone;
  - a fresh dark-mode browser still sees it;
  - no page errors.

## Documentation impact

- `CHANGELOG.md` (new).
- `docs/development.md` § Releasing: new step 3, "Write the changelog"; the following steps are renumbered and `CHANGELOG.md` is added to the release commit.
- `README.md`: "Staying up to date" (release notes link, What's changed, the `changelogNotice` key in the table and the index).
- `pi-outpost.config.example.json`: `changelogNotice`.

body:
## Summary
Step 4c of the canonical-detail stack: a read service that builds an `activity_detail.v1` document for one activity from its canonical session records and their stored detail sets. Not wired to HTTP yet (that is 4d).

- `backend/activities/detail_contract.py` (new): session, metrics (measured / derived / gap-fill / alternatives), downsampled streams with per-channel `source` and `aligned`, laps, zones, analysis and `detail_data.providers` (label, kinds, newest fetched_at, refreshable).
- `backend/performance/canonical_detail.py` (new): `CanonicalDetailReader` reads the session records through a `SessionRecordReader` protocol, chooses the analysis record (first Intervals record in measured order, otherwise the first record) and runs the existing analyses on the `analysis_input` adapter from #1304.
- `backend/db/canonical_store.py` / `backend/sync/canonical_table_reader.py`: `session_activity_rows` / `session_activities`. The SQL mirrors `detail_sets_for_session`.
- `backend/activities/detail_merge.py`: public `clock_offset(candidate, primary)`, shared by the contract and `analysis_input`. It replaces the private copy in `analysis_input`.

## Review notes
- **Lap clock alignment:** laps from another recording are moved onto the primary stream clock using the recording start offset. When either start is unknown, the laps keep their own clock. A new `on_stream_clock` flag says which case applies.
- **Per-analysis source labels:** each analysis credits only the providers of the channels it reads (for example, `power_profile` reads only watts and moving).
- **TrailRun legacy parity:** Intervals `TrailRun` maps to RUN + OUTDOOR and round-trips to `"TrailRun"`. The legacy aerobic sensor map has no `TrailRun` entry, so aerobic analysis for trail runs returns insufficient data, same as before. This PR does not change that. Plain Intervals `"Run"` maps to RUN + UNKNOWN; the golden test covers that mapping.
- Layering: `backend/activities` imports neither performance nor sync; `backend/performance` does not import sync.

## Validation (rebased tree ad52e804 on develop e3f5942e)
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests`: 6781 tests OK (19 skipped)
- `python -m compileall -q server.py backend tests`: OK
- `node --test tests/*.cjs`: 222 pass, 1 fail. The failure (viewport contract, "all contracts run on desktop…") was already failing on develop.
- `python -m mypy .`: 280 errors, same as the develop baseline
- `ruff check`: clean; `ruff format --check`: clean on the changed files

author: faisaldhd
body:
## What

Wave B, the highest-risk 2.4.0 tool: **Lock** (Beta). One real file or folder is transformed in place into one self-contained `.dwenc`/`.dwdir`; nothing of the original stays behind.

- Envelope: random 256-bit data key per file, wrapped three times (file password, Rescuer password, one-time Rescuer key), PBKDF2-SHA256 600k. Authenticated fixed header with AAD + header HMAC; chunked AES-256-GCM frames with a trailing length + SHA-256 footer.
- Safety order: sibling temp, flush+fsync, full streaming test-decrypt and size/SHA-256 compare, atomic move, then remove the plaintext. Any failure deletes the temp and leaves the original untouched. Header rewrites use the same verified atomic replace.
- Folders stream a tar-like archive with an encrypted metadata block and the previous `desktop.ini` bytes, restored byte-for-byte. Symlinks/junctions are skipped; the folder badge uses `desktop.ini` + HKCU per-user file types with a generated multi-size pink `.ico`.
- Auto-lock: opens a private session, watches the program / Explorer tabs / file handles, re-encrypts into the **same** container after a configurable grace (default 8 s, 3-60), 15-min idle fallback, crash recovery from `%LOCALAPPDATA%\DropWheel\sessions` (plaintext never deleted on failure).
- Recovery ladder: any of the three secrets opens; the key resets the Rescuer password; changing a file password needs the file or Rescuer password (the key alone is refused). Rescuer key shown once with Copy / Save .txt / Print and a required confirmation.
- UI: 480x460 floating window in the shared chrome, exact Arabic warning text (`tool.protect.warn.*`), eye toggles with live pair status, primary button gated on match + length, Enter = primary / Esc = cancel, RTL-aware, all strings via `Loc` in en+ar.

## Review responses (2026-10-20)

1. **String diff**: `en.json`/`ar.json` are rebuilt from `main` (4a4a39f) with the original ordering and formatting untouched. Compared with main, each file shows **153 added lines and one comma** added to the previously last key. No existing key, value, place or whitespace changed; verified by parsing both sides and comparing every original key/value.
2. **No stored Rescuer secrets**: the DPAPI vault is deleted. `LockRuntime` keeps the Rescuer password and recovery key **in memory only** for the current process; `protection.json` stores only non-secret booleans plus the public "Rescuer configured" marker. A legacy `%LOCALAPPDATA%\DropWheel\protection\rescuer.dat` is deleted on first use. Protecting new files asks for the Rescuer password and the recovery key once per session (the key is needed to create the third slot). Why not public-key ECIES in this PR: .NET 10 exposes no X25519 and no deterministic EC/RSA key generation from a password, so an ephemeral-static scheme would require a hand-rolled curve implementation (worse than the reviewer's fallback) or storing password-wrapped private keys. The fallback is implemented instead: **no password and no recovery key is written to disk**; the test `No_secret_is_written_under_the_app_data_folder` scans every file under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\DropWheel`.
3. **Recycle Bin**: `RecycleContainerAfterUnlock` now defaults to **false**. No code path sends the original or the container to the Recycle Bin unless the user enabled it; protecting always deletes the plaintext after the verified replace. Test: `Recycle_bin_is_off_by_default_and_protection_never_recycles`.
4. Addendum 10/12 safety rules are covered by the tests below; the secret scan test is added.

## Function proof (generated media, real end-to-end)

| Tool | Assertion | Test |
|---|---|---|
| Lock | 0 B file: exactly one `.dwenc`, unlock restores original bytes, SHA-256 equal, no `.tmp` | `Service_roundtrip_creates_and_removes_exactly_one_file` (0) |
| Lock | 1 B file, same assertions | same theory (1) |
| Lock | chunk−1 / chunk / chunk+1, same assertions | same theory (3 cases) |
| Lock | multi-chunk (2·chunk+17), same assertions | same theory |
| Lock | small folder roundtrip incl. nested file and byte-exact `desktop.ini` | `Folder_roundtrip_restores_content_and_desktop_ini_byte_for_byte` |
| Lock | corrupt ciphertext: clear error, no restored file, no staging/temp, container kept | `Corrupt_input_leaves_no_output_files` |
| Lock | read-only folder/file: roundtrip succeeds, no partial output | `Read_only_folder_still_roundtrips_without_partial_output` |
| Lock | cancel mid-run: source intact, no `.dwenc`, no `.tmp` | `Cancel_mid_run_leaves_the_source_and_no_output` |
| Lock | no secret appears under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\DropWheel` | `No_secret_is_written_under_the_app_data_folder` |
| Lock | Recycle Bin off by default; only explicit opt-in passes `recycle=true` | `Recycle_bin_is_off_by_default_and_protection_never_recycles` |
| Lock | header rewrite atomic under an injected failure at every file operation; old secret still opens | `Header_rewrite_is_atomic_under_a_failure_at_every_file_operation` |
| Lock | crash-recovery journal re-encrypts edited plaintext into the same container | `Crash_recovery_reencrypts_the_edited_plaintext_into_the_same_container` |
| Lock | tampered tag/ciphertext/header/MAC refused; truncation refused | `Tampered_*` / `Truncated_file_is_refused` |
| Lock | auto-lock waits for program/Explorer/held file/grace and honors the idle fallback | `Auto_lock_waits_for_the_program_the_explorer_and_the_grace` |
| Lock | real system icons + padlock composition, cache, purple tokens, HKCU-only registry, Explorer refresh | `Padlock_is_the_only_shipped_badge_and_uses_the_purple_tokens`, `Composition_keeps_the_real_shell_icon_and_adds_purple_pixels_bottom_left`, `Icon_cache_reuses_the_extension_cleans_items_and_builds_association_icons`, `Host_is_notified_after_lock_and_unlock_so_explorer_refreshes`, `Associations_are_per_user_and_removable` |

## Files

- New: `src/FileAction.Core/Lock/*`, `src/FileAction.App/Shell/Protection/*`, `src/FileAction.App/UI/Tools/Lock/LockTool.cs`, tests `LockContainerTests.cs` + `LockSafetyTests.cs`.
- Shared, additive: `Theme.ProtectBadge`, `IToolWindowSpec.ApplyLabelKey`, `IToolActionLabel`, `IToolActionGate` + `ToolWindow` wiring.

## Verification

- `dotnet build` Core, App, Tests: succeeded, 0 errors.
- Final CI: [run 39345840462](https://github.com/Faisaldhd/dropwheel/actions/runs/39345840462) - **986 passed, 0 failed** (build, guard, self-contained UI self-test, Test).
- `dotnet test` was not run locally (standing rule: never run an exe built here); CI is the runner.
- `origin/main` merged at `d65d7b6` (the reviewer branch had conflicts in the shared tool window; resolved by adopting main's `PrimaryLabelKey` and keeping the Lock gate/label hooks). Final head: `5be3b2b`. PR is MERGEABLE.
- No version/CHANGES/installer/WheelController/Catalog/workflows/UpdateKey/SelfTest/Diagnose edits. PR only; no merge, tag or force-push.

## Shared asks for the supervisor

1. Wheel registration: add `new UI.Tools.Lock.LockOperation()` to `WheelController.BuildOperations()`.
2. App wiring: `LockCli.TryHandle(args)` in the argument handler (`--lock-open`), `LockCli.RunStartupRecovery()` once at startup, Settings hook to `LockSettingsWindow.ShowSingle()`, `LockSelfTest.Run(outDir, log)` in SelfTest steps.
3. Installer `.iss`: remove the HKCU `.dwenc`/`.dwdir` associations on uninstall.
4. Theme token `Theme.ProtectBadge` is in place; Settings > Protection still needs the shared panel hook.

| Only the purple padlock is shipped; no drawn yellow folder/document art anywhere | **PASS** | `Assets/Lock/padlock.ico` (6 frames) + `padlock-256.png`; old `locked-*` files and old previews removed |

author: gonandrap
body:
## Summary

Fixes issue #1106. `invariants.user_rework_refused` decided the attention sentence for an escalated validation round from the round row's `uncounted_cause` alone. That column says WHO BOUGHT the round (a user rejection), not WHICH CONDITION ended it — the condition is written only into the `validation_escalated` event payload and read back by `ops.escalation_cause`. So every escalation of a user-rework round got `USER_REWORK_REFUSED_BLOCKER`, including `ops.ESCALATION_REPEAT_SUBMISSION` (family `not_reviewed`, no seat ran). On wo-f2a57dd2, `needs_review` for 94.8h, the blocker said the panel judged and refused the rework while the same order's `review:` block said "round 3 was not reviewed", and offered `validation.max_rounds`, a no-op because an uncounted round spends no counted budget.

`user_rework_refused` now reads the cause's `ops.ESCALATION_FAMILY` and gives up exactly one family: `not_reviewed`, served by a new `user_rework_unreviewed` / `USER_REWORK_UNREVIEWED_BLOCKER`. `handover` (judged and refused), `unjudged` and `unrecorded` keep the refusal sentence.

## Implementation notes

- BINARY SPLIT: `not_reviewed` is the only family that moves. `handover` (judged and refused), `unjudged` and `unrecorded` all keep `USER_REWORK_REFUSED_BLOCKER` and its `max_rounds` advice, exactly as before. The first revision gated strictly on `handover` and dropped the other two to `VALIDATION_STUCK_BLOCKER`; the user refused that assumption — it invents a third user-visible attention sentence issue #1106 never prescribed.
- `ops.ESCALATION_FAMILY.get(cause, "")` and not `[cause]`, deliberately against that dict's own "a cause with no family is a `KeyError`" note: these predicates run on the reconciler's invariant path, where an unmappable payload string would break the tick. The `KeyError` discipline stays where it was bought — in `ops`.
- The new sentence is worded for all three `not_reviewed` causes ("gave the panel nothing new to judge"), not for `repeat_submission` alone, because the family and not the cause picks the wording (kn-bec32368).
- No clock and no SHA in the new constant, and no `validation.max_rounds`: `ack_attention` stores the reason verbatim and INV-ATTENTION-REASON re-derives and compares it, so a reason that ticked could never be acknowledged. `test_the_unreviewed_blocker_can_be_acknowledged` pins that round trip.
- Read `_escalated_user_rework_family` first (`src/jarvis/invariants.py:1850`): the two public predicates are one line each on top of it.
- No new spec document — issue #1106 states the defect, the mechanism and the wording rule, and the code cites it plus `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-14-an-escalated-round-says-why-and-what-to-run-next.md`.

## Questions asked to Neo

None.

## Alarms raised

None. `jarvis alarms --wo wo-3f35a3fa` — "no cost alarm has ever been raised against wo-3f35a3fa".

## Learnings

- `kn-27615769` — an escalated round's wording cannot be derived from the round row, `uncounted_cause` is not the escalation cause, and the family mapping is the binary split: do NOT make the gate stricter.
- `kn-cc4dc8ff` RETRACTED. Its first draft told future workers a family gate must be STRICT — the assumption the user refused. Round-2 review caught it; a worker reading it would have reverted this fix and cited it as authority.

## Test evidence

| Kind | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit / integration | `uv run pytest tests/test_rejudge_moved_head.py tests/test_invariants.py tests/test_stale_escalations.py tests/test_attention_premature.py tests/test_adhoc_attention.py -k "test_"` | 268 passed, 1 skipped, exit 0 (after the rework). Includes the pre-existing `test_a_rejected_user_rework_round_with_no_budget_left_goes_to_the_user`, still green, and the 5 new tests. Full suite on CI. |
| UI | not run — n/a, no rendered surface changed; the new constant reaches the dashboard only through the same `true_blockers` string every other blocker uses | see checks |
| Eval | not run locally — `pytest evals -q` on CI | see checks |
| A/B | n/a — no prompt, contract or worker heuristic changed; this is a derivation read by the reconciler | n/a |

## Screenshots

None — no rendered surface changed.

body:
Refs #28 (steps 3 to 5 of the harness-neutral sequence). Does not close the issue.

## What changed

The maintainer ended the trial: delete the typed routing layer and the external launcher, and use v1.4.7 (`fb4d5e2d`) if they are needed again.

- **Deleted** `engineering-mode/scripts/routing/` (catalog, parser, stale-pin migration) and `scripts/runner/` (`pstack-runner`). 5,854 lines. `package.json` test and typecheck scripts drop both.
- **`provider-dispatch.md`** is now the contract, read as text by the parent. It defines the sheet (one `role: entry[, entry...]` line per role), the Route format `[provider:]model@effort`, the native lanes, and the dropout policy.
  - Any provider token is valid. This removes the closed `claude/codex/cursor/grok` list that rejected `opencode:` Routes with `unknown-provider`.
  - Effort is the value the host lists, and is required only when the host lists an effort option for that model. Models with no effort option (for example `opencode-go/kimi-k2.7-code`) can now carry a Route.
  - A line the parent cannot read drops out that role only. There is no whole-sheet fallback.
  - Grammar versions and the grammar 1 and 2 migration are gone. A `Descriptor grammar:` header is prose, so existing sheets still read.
  - Claude Code native lanes map the model to an `Agent` alias (`sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`). Anything else is a dropout.
- **`t3-tools.md`**: the host sheet needs a provider on every Route, a bad line drops that role, and the effort rule matches. The example host sheet uses an `opencode:` lane.
- **`codex-tools.md` and `cursor-tools.md`**: any provider other than the parent's is a dropout. No provider list.
- **`setup-engineering-toolkit`** is rewritten around the host's own model list. No catalog, `bun` smoke, `printRoleMap`, or CLI probe. First run proposes only the families the session serves natively and leaves the rest on `inherit-parent`. An unknown harness prints the sheet. This drops the old cross-provider quad seed.
- **Routed skills and playbooks**: removed "typed Route", launcher, and receipt wording. A lane counts when its child returned a result on the assigned model.
- **Static invariants** (`tests/skill-collision-repro.sh`): dropped the canonical-quad check, kept "panel skills default to `inherit-parent`", added a role-list check, and added a ban on the removed vocabulary.
- **Docs**: `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `docs/reference.md`, `UPSTREAM.md`, `NOTICE.md`. **Version 1.5.0** in all six places.

Divergences to review:
- Merged #59 says a missing host sheet means `inherit-parent`. #28's 2026-10-18 decision said the per-app sheet applies then. This PR keeps #59's rule.
- Plain Claude Code can no longer reach Codex, Cursor, or Grok. Those Routes are a named dropout unless the session is a delegate host.

## Verification

- [x] Bun tests (127 pass), strict typecheck, static invariants, and plugin validation pass.
- [x] Live test, per AGENTS.md (maintainer waived further live tests on 2026-10-20; Codex, Cursor, and the new head `e507f21d` were not run live, and the evidence below is for `fcdd9377`): the exact candidate is installed in each harness this change affects, and the changed behavior passes from the real user surface.

Live evidence (installed version, harness, surface, action, observed result). Candidate: commit `fcdd9377`, plugin `et` 1.5.0, installed from a `git archive` of that commit as a local marketplace with a project-scope install. The user-scope `et` was disabled for the test project only.

1. **Setup on a delegate host.** Harness: Claude Code parent in T3 Code. Surface: a thread launched through the T3 MCP, with the operator answering in the T3 UI. Action: `/setup-engineering-toolkit` with Claude and OpenCode Go models. Observed: it listed the host's model ids per family, probed each selected Route with one read-only child, wrote `~/.agents/engineering-toolkit-models.md` with all 15 roles once and read it back, then ran a mixed smoke panel with a cross-judge (PASS). The operator swapped models and raised an effort during the run, and the sheet reflects that.
2. **`interrogate` on a delegate host.** Harness: Claude Code parent (`claude-sonnet-5-5`) in T3 Code. Surface: a T3 thread (MCP-launched). Action: `et:interrogate` on a one-file uncommitted diff, with the sheet from case 1. Observed: all four `interrogate reviewers` Routes resolved once and ran on their assigned targets: `claudeAgent/claude-sonnet-5-5` (medium), `opencode/opencode-go/gpt-6-luna` (xhigh), `opencode/opencode-go/glm-5.3-flash` (high), `opencode/opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash` (high). Each child self-reported its model. The ledger read `4 of 4 lanes ran, 2 providers`. All four found the same planted off-by-one.
3. **Plain Claude Code, per-app sheet.** Harness: Claude Code 2.1.306, `claude -p` with `--strict-mcp-config`, so no `delegate_task`. Surface: headless CLI. Action: `et:interrogate` with a project sheet `interrogate reviewers: claude:claude-sonnet-5-5@medium, opencode:opencode-go/glm-5.3-flash@high`. Observed: lane A ran natively through `et:pstack-lane` on `claude-sonnet-5-5` at medium. Lane B was a named dropout, `not a delegate host`, with no substitution. The ledger read `1 of 2 lanes ran, 1 provider`.

Caveats:
- The live cases ran on `fcdd9377`.
