author: snapotter-hq
body:
`GET /api/v1/download/:jobId/:filename` probes `outputs/<jobId>/<filename>` and `uploads/<jobId>/<filename>` with `getObjectSize`, which sends `HeadObjectCommand` in S3 mode (`packages/enterprise/src/storage-s3.ts:346`). Because HTTP `HEAD` responses have no body, `@aws-sdk/client-s3` deserializes both a missing key (`NoSuchKey`) and a missing bucket (`NoSuchBucket`) as `NotFound` with `$metadata.httpStatusCode = 404`. When an S3 bucket was deleted or `S3_BUCKET` was set to a nonexistent name, both probes matched `isMissingObjectError` and the route returned `404 { "error": "File not found" }` with a warning log instead of a `503` storage fault.

`checkConnection()` in `packages/enterprise/src/storage-s3.ts` (`HeadBucketCommand`) now relabels a 404 rejection's `name` from `"NotFound"` to `"NoSuchBucket"`; `HeadBucket` takes no object key, so an HTTP 404 there always means the bucket itself is missing. `apps/api/src/lib/object-storage.ts` exports `verifyS3Bucket()`, which is a no-op on the local backend and runs `s3.checkConnection()` through `normalizeS3ReadFault` in S3 mode. `GET /api/v1/download/:jobId/:filename` in `apps/api/src/routes/files.ts` calls `await verifyS3Bucket()` only after both `outputs/` and `uploads/` size probes miss, so healthy downloads from either prefix make no extra S3 requests while a vanished bucket surfaces as a `503` operational `SafeError` (`code: "storage-unavailable"`).

Two out-of-scope `getObjectSize` gaps found during review are filed as #2923 (`copyObjectToFile` and `worker.ts` `loadToolInputs`/`isQueuedInputGone` misclassifying a vanished S3 bucket on `ocr` and `ocr-pdf` `HeadObject` probes) and #2924 (`objectExists` and `resolveOriginalSize` swallowing non-missing storage faults in bare `catch` blocks).

## Verification

- Teeth check: reverted `packages/enterprise/src/storage-s3.ts`, `apps/api/src/lib/object-storage.ts`, and `apps/api/src/routes/files.ts` and confirmed the 8 new unit assertions in `tests/unit/api/s3-error-classification.test.ts`, `tests/unit/api/object-storage-s3-mutation.test.ts`, and `tests/unit/api/files-route.test.ts` failed, then restored the fix and confirmed all 144 unit tests passed.
- Blast radius: checked all references to `checkConnection`, `verifyS3Bucket`, and `fileRoutes` across `packages/enterprise/src/storage-s3.ts`, `apps/api/src/lib/object-storage.ts`, `apps/api/src/lib/file-storage.ts`, `apps/api/src/routes/files.ts`, and `apps/api/src/index.ts`.
- Targeted fleet pair on `ubuntu_gpu` against base `ec228838220957d9447dab83593add0962c23218` (`tests/unit/api/s3-error-classification.test.ts`, `tests/unit/api/object-storage-s3-mutation.test.ts`, `tests/unit/api/object-storage.test.ts`, `tests/unit/api/object-storage-fault.test.ts`, `tests/unit/api/files-route.test.ts`, `tests/unit/api/file-storage.test.ts`, `tests/unit/api/file-preview-s3.test.ts`, `tests/integration/platform/result-download-fault.test.ts`, `tests/integration/platform/s3-result-download-fault.test.ts`, `tests/integration/platform/s3-download-fault.test.ts`, `tests/integration/platform/s3-storage.test.ts`, `tests/integration/platform/download-range.test.ts`, `tests/integration/platform/download-socket.test.ts`): baseline `test=0`, change `test=0` (401 passed, 0 new failures).
- Local `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm check:license-boundary`, and `npx biome check` on all modified files passed with 0 errors.

## Overview

The comment checker read lines inside Go raw strings and /* */ comments
as code. In tests, a shell script's "esac" or a fixture's "func Total"
gave the owner's approvals names that belong to no code. The checker now
skips those lines, so it names the same comments as Go's own parser.

## Changes

- Skip lines that start inside a Go raw string or /* */ comment when
  naming comments.
- Add a test with a shell script and Go source in raw strings.

## Testing

This proves the checker now names comments the way Go itself reads the
file. A one-off Go program using go/parser and go/scanner named every
comment in the repository's 165 Go files; the fixed checker gave the
same 724 names, lines and sizes, and the old one differed by the 12
wrong names. The new test fails on the old checker. Run:
```bash
cd ai && uv run pytest -m "not local_ai"
```
Expect every test to pass. Result: all pass, as do ruff, mypy and the
pde-comment-review Go tests.

Approvals already recorded under the wrong names now fail the fixed
checker as "approved comment is gone". After installing, the owner cuts
them once with a script that backs up every approval file first.

body:
Fixes #466

## Summary

Test-only change. Adds a vitest case to `plugin/src/core/auth/tokens.test.ts`, "does not report a failed sign-in until the previous session's refresh token is removed from disk". It sets up a signed-in `TokenManager` whose sign-in write rejects (`disk full`) and whose removal write (`persist(undefined)`) is held. A fake disk changes only when that write is released. The test checks that:

- while the removal is held, `signIn()` has not settled and the old refresh token is still on disk;
- once the removal is released, `signIn()` rejects with `disk full` and the disk holds no refresh token.

No production code changed. `TokenManager.signIn()` already awaits the removal (#460), so the item was not fixed before this PR. It was only missing a test that would fail without that `await`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Held removal: `signIn()` does not settle until the removal is released, then rejects with the write's error and leaves no refresh token on disk. Covered by the new test above.

### Mutations (each one made by hand in `plugin/src/core/auth/tokens.ts`, then restored)

- Replaced `await this.save(generation, undefined);` in `signIn()`'s catch with `void this.save(generation, undefined).catch(() => undefined);`, the fire-and-forget form from the review. Only the new test fails; the other 20 pass, which reproduces the gap the review found.
- Removed the removal entirely. The new test fails, and so does "removes the previous session's refresh token from disk when storing a sign-in on a signed-in manager fails, so a restart is signed out too".

## Verification

- `npx vitest run src/core/auth/tokens.test.ts`: 21 passed. The new test also passed 50 repeats (`--repeats 50`). It uses no timers or clock: it waits with the file's existing `settle()` helper, and each write's promise controls when it lands.
- `make fmt lint test`: passed.
- No integration, sim or e2e run: nothing they cover changed.

## SPEC principles

This strengthens principle 3 (everything is tested). It covers the sign-in failure path added for principle 1, where the stale session must not come back after a restart.

author: nkasg
body:
Prepares the app to run on Cloudflare Python Workers with Postgres (Neon) through Hyperdrive.

## What changed
- **worker.py**: Workers entry point; runs the FastAPI app through the Workers ASGI adapter and binds the database from the `HYPERDRIVE` binding on the first request.
- **wrangler.jsonc**: Worker config. The frontend is served by Workers Static Assets (free, no Python CPU). Hyperdrive ID still needs filling in.
- **pyproject.toml**: Workers dependencies, with `pg8000` instead of psycopg2 (native C, not available on Workers).
- **app/database.py**: engine is created lazily, so Workers can bind it at request time. Local behaviour is unchanged.
- **app/main.py**: startup migrations/seeding are skipped on Workers (the ASGI lifespan runs on every request there) and moved into `init_db.py`, run once from your machine.
- **requirements/local.txt**: moved from `requirements.txt`, because pywrangler refuses to run while a requirements*.txt exists at the root.

## Before deploying
1. `DATABASE_URL=... python init_db.py` then `python create_admin.py` against Neon.
2. Create a Hyperdrive config in the dashboard and put its ID in `wrangler.jsonc`.
3. `uv run pywrangler secret put SECRET_KEY`
4. `uv run pywrangler deploy`

- Workers Free plan allows 10 ms CPU per request; bcrypt at login will likely exceed it. Workers Paid fixes this with no code changes.

body:
## Tracking issue

Closes #272.

## Summary

Accepted class regeneration returns to the course progress screen immediately. The learner can navigate away and resume the published class after the server finishes.

## Problem

A native regeneration completed successfully on the server after nearly 11 minutes. The app stopped polling after about two minutes and kept the learner behind a foreground loading flow. It also discarded the admitted operation identity and cleared local answers even after a rejected request.

## Approach

Reuse the existing course progress panel and foreground course refresh. Follow the admitted operation through GET requests, require canonical completion and the replacement class attempt, and keep failures, cancellation and unresolved outcomes distinct. Unknown admission outcomes use status checks without another POST. Confirmed failures allow an explicit retry with fresh operation and class-attempt checks. Profile changes and cancellation cannot overwrite newer work.

Six HTTP-fixture request barriers use bounded XCTest waits and release their held responses during cleanup, including when a request arrives late. This prevents a missing test request from waiting indefinitely.

## Scope and remaining work

Native implementation is merged. The author deferred TestFlight publication until the other agents' features are ready. No release archive or upload was produced for this PR. Backend generation, providers, models, request budgets, quality checks and learner history retain their existing behavior. Cancellation retains the existing course-scoped server contract, with an operation identity check before the request.

## Verification

- Full local native suite: 233 tests passed on iPhone 17 and 233 on iPad Pro 13-inch (M5), iOS 26.5. No failures or skips.
- Focused HTTP-boundary suite: 37 passed, including 14 regeneration cases. Covers accepted background work, relaunch, stale completion, explicit retry payload and attempt, lost acknowledgement, transient observation errors, cancellation, rejected admission and profile changes.
- After bounding the fixture waits, both affected classes passed all 25 tests on each device, 50 runs total. Existing behavioral coverage is retained.
- The foreground admission regression failed against the original binary with three assertions and passes with this change.
- Earlier development runs exposed test fixture compile/decoding errors and a retry-button race. All are fixed and covered by the final passing runs. One initial simulator launch and one failed-run finalization were interrupted; completed runs use direct booted simulators.
- Two independent source and behavioral-test reviews found no remaining blocker.
- All applicable GitHub workflows passed at PR head `3e7617dd` and merged main `333cdb98`, including the iPhone and iPad native test job.

- [ ] `npm run ci` passes. Not run locally because this change is native only; applicable GitHub checks must pass before merge.
- [x] Tests were added or updated for changed behavior.
- [x] Documentation was updated where needed. No setup or API documentation change is required.

## Screenshots or recordings

The transition reuses the existing course progress panel. No layout or asset redesign is included. HTTP-boundary regressions verify the previous blocking state and the resulting background progress state; screenshots were not captured.

## Self-hosting and release impact

Include this fix in the next combined iOS release. TestFlight publication is deferred at the author's request. Existing servers support every field used by this update. No server image, database migration, environment variable or provider configuration change is required.

- [x] No environment variables were added.
- [x] No database changes were made.
- [x] iOS versioning and TestFlight delivery are covered above. No desktop, TUI or download change.

## Checklist

- [x] I searched for related issues and PRs.
- [x] No secrets, local environment files, private user data or generated credentials are included.

## Review assistance

- [ ] Maintainers may use AI agents to finish the work and prepare follow-up changes within the scope below. I will review the result.
- [ ] I will make the follow-up changes myself. Please leave review comments only.
- [ ] Please ask me before preparing follow-up changes.

The author has not chosen a standing review-assistance preference. This session explicitly authorizes finishing, merging and publishing this fix. Preserve learner data, configured providers and models, generation budgets and server verification behavior.

Round 15 of deferred game-function matching: 13 deferred functions matched, 3 deferred candidates improved.

### Matched (US `CURRENT (0)`, whitespace and progress gates passed)

### What made them match
- **Per-function float literals.** Many candidates loaded `extern f32 D_8009xxxx/D_800Axxxx` symbols that are really the function's own literal pool. Every value was read from the checksum-validated US ROM. Each unit's generated `.rodata` was checked with objdump against the ROM words. `0x406D70A3` is one unit below the nearest float to 3.71 (`3.71f` compiles to `...A4`), so it is spelled `3.7099998f`.
- **-g3 frame words.** Under `-O2 -g3` every named local *and* every call-containing argument (`f(g())`, RNG calls passed inline) reserves a stack word; `register` does not change this, and sibling block-scoped locals do not share space. Several frame mismatches were fixed by adding or removing exactly one such word.

### Shared dependency: yes (rodata mappings)
The literals give 9 units a new `.rodata` section. Each has a reviewed INFO mapping in `config/game/us-rodata.ld` with a size `ASSERT` and payload size, an owner entry in `config/data/us.json`, and an evidence doc. The mappings follow the existing precedent (`game_177b50_float_constants.md`). The verifier compares only each payload with ROM.

| game_40490 | 0x80096688 | 8 | `docs/evidence/data-layout/game_40490_float_constants.md` |

author: zajca
body:
Closes #136

## Change
- Synthetic sessions run with `SHELL=/bin/sh` (the Pohunek daemon passes only an allowlisted environment, so `ZDOTDIR` is dropped and cannot be used); they no longer source the owner's `~/.zshrc` (D2).
- Linux: the isolated daemon runs in a transient `systemd-run --user --scope` unit; `stop` stops the unit, reaching non-dumpable detached helpers. Fallback for every platform: process-group kill via pid file and termination of the `op daemon` named in `$iso/run/op-daemon.pid` (D1).
- Header comment documents the stop mechanism (D3).

## Evidence (Linux)
- Before: an isolated run left an `op daemon` on `/tmp/ph-ui-agent.*/run/op-daemon.sock`.
- After start/stop: `ss -xl | grep 'ph-ui-agent.*op-daemon'` empty, no `/tmp/ph-ui-agent.*`, no scope unit left. With `/bin/sh` no `op daemon` is spawned at all; a manually spawned one outside the scope is removed by the pid-file fallback.
- Gates: fmt, clippy, test passed.

## Unverified on macOS
No systemd path, `ps -o command=` and pid-file fallback not run on a Mac; `setsid` is needed there (pre-existing).

## Self-review
Independent review: pid-reuse risk on the pid-file kill (accepted, stop runs right after the daemon dies and the command line is checked), unit glob tightened, header wrapped.

## Findings
Multiple MUCs are already supported by the per-account `rooms` object array. `resolveRooms` retains every normal room; `NewXMPPBridge` builds its room allowlist from all of them, used by inbound dispatch, outbound groupchat classification, and history reads. No runtime change is necessary.

## Changes
- Document a complete two-MUC configuration, per-room overrides, and the write-only error room.
- Explain the shared join/allowlist, single-room object-array format, and migration from retired spellings (no compatibility regression introduced).
- Add configuration-to-bridge regressions for one and multiple MUCs: inbound source-room routing, groupchat destination classification, send/read authorization, owner access, unlisted-room rejection, and error-sink isolation.

## Validation
All commands run in the isolated scratch clone via `nix develop`:
- `go test ./...`
- `go vet ./...`
- `go build -o /tmp/pi-msg-beltino-134 ./cmd/pi-msg`
- `go test -race ./internal/pimsg -run "TestConfiguredMUCAllowlist|TestRoomConfig|TestResolveAccountRoomMode" -count=1`

💡 What: Replaced looped `SELECT` queries for comments and reactions in `get_memories` with chunked, batched `IN` queries and O(1) hash map lookups.
🎯 Why: `get_memories` executed 2 queries for every single memory object returned, causing an N+1 scaling bottleneck that would drastically increase latency and database strain as more memories are added.
📊 Impact: Reduces database queries per request from 2N+1 to O(N/900) (essentially ~3 queries total for <900 items). Expected ~80-95% latency reduction on large feeds.
🔬 Measurement: Check the database access logs to verify that exactly 3 queries are executed total when fetching a large list of memories, instead of multiple repeated calls.

author: karllivesey
body:
Split from PR #19 (N1), which found this once sends got earlier. N1 will rebase on this PR.

## Bug (already on main)

A leader step can emit `[SnapshotRequired, Persist]`: `After::LeaderAppend` re-emits `SnapshotRequired` for a follower in snapshot catch-up, then `maybe_commit_into` pushes `Persist(commit)` last. The owner leases the `SnapshotRequired`. When the image loads, `complete_effect_inner` **appended** the continuation (one Send from the pure `snapshot_send` / `repair_snapshot_send`), leaving `[Persist, Send]`. `submit_persists` refuses a Persist that has effects queued behind it (`ProviderContract`), so the replica fenced the owner and the node went into recovery.

This fails closed: the Send was never emitted and the Persist never submitted, so there is no false durable reply and no corrupted state. It is an availability loss during snapshot catch-up under write load, and it repeats on the next leader while the follower still needs the image.

## Rule

A continuation (the effects a completion callback returns for a released lease) **takes the released effect's position** in its visit's queue, in its own order. A visit holds at most one lease (`Active::leased: Option`), and that lease is always the queue front (`take_owned_effect`). So the position is the front, and the continuation is prepended. This matches what a synchronous completion would produce. It is one code path with no per-kind special case, and the rule is documented on `EffectOwner`.

`install_continuation` (the worker's Written/Durable continuation of a Persist that was already submitted) is not a lease expansion and is unchanged. The Persist left the queue when it was submitted, and only early Sends emitted after it can be queued there, so FIFO behind them is correct.

## Audit (every `Effect` kind)

The new rule only behaves differently from append when the continuation is non-empty **and** effects are queued behind the released one.

| Kind | Producer shape | Continuation | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Send`, `ReadReady` | any | empty (release, read capture, cancel) | none |
| `Committed` | index 0, with following effects (`completion.rs:50`) | empty in production (`release`, `complete_applied_capture`) | none |
| `Persist` | last | never through a callback; through `deliver_worker` | none |
| `PersistVolatile` | volatile cores only, which the owner does not run | — | none |
| `VerifyLearnerReadiness`, `CheckpointRequired`, `StageSnapshot` | the step's only effect (`readiness.rs:215`, `raft.rs:1082`, `receive.rs:538`) | new transition | none (nothing behind) |
| `SnapshotInstalled`, `CheckpointCompacted` | pushed last by `after_durable` | new transition | none (nothing behind) |
| `SnapshotRequired` | inside multi-effect broadcasts, with a final Persist | exactly one Send | **the fix** |

With the public `complete_effect` / `complete_effect_with` and an arbitrary callback, the same rule applies. If such a continuation itself holds a Persist and has effects behind it, `submit_persists` fails closed, as append already did whenever a Persist was queued behind. No internal producer creates that shape. I found no kind for which the general rule is unsafe.

## Tests

New owner unit tests in `src/runtime/effects/continuation_tests.rs`. They are deterministic, do no I/O and build the queue white-box on the existing in-crate fixture, now generalised to N groups:

- `loaded_snapshot_send_takes_its_place_ahead_of_the_steps_persist`: start from `[SnapshotRequired, Persist]` and complete the lease with one Send. The queue becomes `[Send, Persist]`, the Persist is leased last, and `submit_persists` accepts it.
- `continuations_released_out_of_lease_order_keep_their_positions`: two visits, `[SR, Send, Persist]` and `[SR, Persist]`, both leased. The later lease completes first, with a two-Send continuation. Each continuation keeps the released position and its own order, and both Persists are accepted in one batch.
- **Mutation:** restoring main's `extend` fails both tests (`[Persist, Send(11)]` and `[Persist, Send(21), Send(22)]`).

## Checks (Linux, cores 10–15)

- `cargo +stable fmt --all -- --check`: clean. Strict Clippy (default, `--all-features`, `--no-default-features`, `--no-default-features --features native`): clean. Matched fmt and Clippy: clean. The pre-push hook passed.
- Default features: lib 551, counter_service 144, effect_owner 210, native_member_startup 27, runtime 57, snapshot 27, snapshot_worker 14. All features: lib 553, counter_service 203, effect_owner 210, native_member_startup 50, runtime 57, snapshot 27, snapshot_worker 14. All passed.
- `quic_promoted_leader_witness_installs_compacted_final_snapshot` (all features): 10/10. On main it does not reproduce the bug, because that needs N1's early sends, so this run only shows there is no regression.

No CPU measurement: per-write releases (`Send`, `Committed`) have empty continuations, so the per-write path is unchanged.

author: tolar07
body:
Autonomy item 2 (builds on #147).

**What it does**
- `engine/leg_postmortem.py` resolves every leg of every graded slip: 50%+ accas, accas, alts, combined codes and megas. Main slips' legs are joined to that day's singles; alt slips carry their own legs.
- Each leg is classed by market family, price band, league, certainty, news level and Gemini verdict.
- Each distinct leg is counted once. Per class it records loss rate against stated chance, a z score, and how many losing slips the class helped kill.
- A **slip killer** is a class with 50+ legs and z ≥ 2. The result goes to `memory/leg_postmortem.json`, rebuilt by `monitor/experiment_run.py` before every board.
- The feedback is a strategy, not a hard rule:
  - **AK** (accas) and **TK** (50%+ accas) keep only slips with no killer-class leg.
  - Both are registered in the experiment engine and count from 2026-10-20, so they must earn promotion.
  - Each day's killers come only from slips graded before that day, so there is no look-ahead.
  - The Gemini dimension is report-only, because no verdict exists when the board is built.
- The supervisor gets one line each for the experiments and the post-mortem. The weekly review gets a post-mortem section and the live rule per slot.

**First numbers (2026-10-20):** 127 of 187 graded slips lost across 629 distinct legs. No killer class yet. The worst class is Serie B legs: 8 of 22 lost (36% against 22% stated, z +1.7).

**Tests:** `tests/leg_postmortem_test.py` (new). Supervisor/weekly, experiment engine, standing orders and agent refs all pass locally. ruff and mypy are clean on the new files.

author: zerocodefast
body:
## What was wrong

`scratch_checkout` built the directory name from the fixture root's `st_ctime_ns`. Creating any child of that root moves it, and a case creates several — `private-evidence`, `guard-home` and more.

A case asks for the stage directory at four moments, each separated by one of those `mkdir` calls:

| call site | purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `harness_case.py:147` / `runner.py:97` | seed `x.ts`, `a.ts`, `b.ts` into it |
| `harness_case.py:182` / `runner.py:140` | render `{{stage}}` into the agent's prompt |
| `case_helpers.py:116` | redact the path out of the published evidence |
| `fixtures.py:164` | remove it after the case |

All four returned different paths.

## What it caused

`omp-native-shell-writes-clone-beside-session-folder` failed on macOS with `native_command_review_required`. The prompt named a directory nothing had seeded, so the agent ran `cat <stage>/x.ts` against a path that did not exist, and Guard reviewed the unresolvable absolute read. The Guard decision was correct for the command it saw; the command was wrong.

Cleanup looked for a third name, so the seeded directory was never removed. Fourteen had accumulated in `/tmp` on this host.

## The change

Bind the name to the fixture root's path, device and inode. Those do not move while the case runs, so every call agrees.

## Test

`test_stage_keeps_one_name_while_the_fixture_root_gains_children` creates a child of the fixture root between the calls, which is what the real case does. It fails on `main` and passes here.

## 変更内容

closes https://github.com/originator-profile/originator-profile/issues/579

External Resource Integrity の「対象要素」の表 (originator-profile/docs.originator-profile.org#645、originator-profile/docs.originator-profile.org#648 で改訂) に検証を合わせます。

| 要素 | 取得する URL | 今まで |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `img` / `video` / `audio` | `currentSrc`。空なら `src` | 同じ |
| `picture` | 子の `img` 要素の URL | `src` がないため例外で検証失敗 |
| `source` (親が `video` / `audio`) | 自身の `src`。親要素で選択されたかどうかによらない | 同じ |
| `track` | `src` | 同じ |
| 表にない要素 (`iframe`、`script`、`embed`、`div`、`picture` 内の `source` など) | 取得せず、検証対象から除く | `src` があれば取得し、なければ例外で検証失敗 |

- 除外した結果、要素が 0 件になった場合は検証失敗とします
- `picture` 内の `source` で選択された候補は、`img` 要素の `currentSrc` に含まれます。`picture` 要素か `img` 要素を指す CA で検証できます

### 設計上の判断

- 除外は要素選択 (`selectExternalResources`) で行います。要素が 0 件なら失敗とする既存の判定をそのまま使えます。lens / inspector のハイライトも、検証対象の要素だけになります
- 要素ごとの URL は `resolveExternalResourceUrl` で決めます。要素の判定は `localName` で行います (cas-monitor は JSDOM の要素を扱うため、`instanceof` が使えません)
- `currentSrc` が空のときは、`img` / `video` / `audio` で `src` を使います。JSDOM (cas-monitor) は `currentSrc` を常に空文字で返すため、代替をなくすと cas-monitor で検証が通らなくなります
- request destination は実装していません。`fetch()` からは指定できず、docs でも参考情報としています
- 既存の `selectByCssOrIntegrity` は公開 API なので、挙動を変えずに残しています

### 破壊的変更

表にない要素だけにマッチする `ExternalResourceTargetIntegrity` は、検証失敗になります。#645 より前の docs では「その他の要素: `src` 属性」として取得対象でしたが、originator-profile/docs.originator-profile.org#548 で対象を HTML の埋め込みコンテンツの一部に絞ると決まりました。

`picture` 内の `source` だけを指す CA は、今までも `src` がないため検証失敗でした。

## 確認手順

- `pnpm --filter @originator-profile/sign test`、`pnpm --filter @originator-profile/verify test`: 表の各行と除外されるケース (`picture` 内の `source` を含む)、選択されていない `video` 内の `source` の検証
- `pnpm --filter @originator-profile/verify e2e`: `picture` 内の `source` で選択された候補を、`img` 要素の `currentSrc` で検証できること。`img` の `src` にはわざと別の画像を入れてあり、`src` で代替すると失敗します
- `pnpm --filter=@originator-profile/inspector run e2e`、`pnpm --filter=@originator-profile/lens run e2e`: ハイライト対象の変更による影響がないこと

author: steipete
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Database-engine admission decodes facts its own typed publishers just constructed, repeating object-shape checks and catalog projections after the physical database boundary already validated them. The private adapter table also allocates members no production consumer uses.

## User Impact

Supported database opening, search, migrations and error messages are unchanged. The physical database, capability, schema, catalog and anchor checks remain at their existing boundaries. Custom SDK key decoders and persisted clean-close proof decoders remain required and unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a core-only fact-key type for trusted publications while keeping the public `SqliteDatabaseAdmissionKey<T>` contract, including its required decoder, unchanged. Existing admission readers and publishers accept both; only the three non-persisted private engine keys stop decoding their typed values. The existing custom-decoder memo and all generation, rollback, revocation, authority and write-settlement behavior stay in place.

Remove unused members from the private adapter table and type the remaining operations with the existing public interface. The public `DatabaseEngineAdapter` interface, actual open/bootstrap/migration bodies, error redaction, standalone search and transaction owners stay unchanged. Delete only assertions on the removed static capability labels; retain actual search and refusal coverage.

This is the database-engine first-area slice of a widely imported admission owner. Other state/delivery consumers are not migrated here. No SQL, schema, durability, retention, permission, config, protocol, dependency or SDK export changes. The standalone session memory backend is untouched.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- `database.engine`: malformed same-process injection under this private key no longer gets a second decoder. The typed internal publication was introduced with the engine adapters in #169933, not as protection for a cited human incident; physical anchor admission still rejects bad external data.
- `database.engine.schema`: already-admitted PostgreSQL capabilities and catalog facts are no longer projected and checked again. #170266 introduced the shared-state engine admission owner; its actual database checks remain. Unsupported in-place mutation was already outside the owner contract clarified in #174919. Malformed private injections may now fail at their consumer rather than returning a cache miss.
- `database.postgres.search`: the engine trusts the signature array it constructed rather than checking every element again. #173625 introduced this internal publication along with active PostgreSQL search; all declared extension, privilege and input checks remain. Unsupported malformed internal injection may now throw instead of causing readmission.

The removed adapter fields and error classifier have no production caller, so their removal adds no runtime fallback tradeoff. The public adapter contract remains available for external implementations and future owners.

## Evidence

Net production: **100 lines removed** across seven production files; tests: **23 lines added** across two existing files. This is an area-split cleanup, not a LARGE result.

- Admission/physical-facts proof: 46 passing cases, including typed publication/replacement/worker cloning and existing custom decoders. Six existing live-PostgreSQL cases were conditionally skipped; no live PostgreSQL claim.
- After adding the adapter-table cleanup: 24 distinct passing adapter/search/open/lint-suppression cases (272.93s wrapper, mostly worker preparation), plus the PR wrapper inventory/import-closure case (40.82s; 18 unrelated cases filtered by the explicit selector). Counts overlap the earlier admission run and are not added into an inflated total.
- Eleven-root targeted types, nine-file typed lint/format and whitespace pass. Runtime and type-inclusive import cycles: zero. The unchanged public SQLite worker SDK consumer is included in the targeted type graph; the broad generated SDK API gate is left to exact-head hosted CI.
- Independent isolated whole-change review through P2 completed scoped-clean (correctness 0.94), with final source verification complete. Author simplification retained only the first-area publication change and unused adapter members.
- All local proof ran serially, nice 10, one Vitest worker, isolated HOME/state/config/XDG. No new suppressions, retries, raised timeouts or skips. No live Gateway, upgrade or performance claim. Hosted CI on the exact pushed head supplies broad proof.

## Exact-head CI attribution

Head `8cf273fe430557ed2f77eba5062bdd71b4eb7a94`, run 39400447601 attempt 1: every selected runtime and PostgreSQL conformance job passed. All 211 check runs were enumerated. `check-prod-types` (118555142632) failed with 809 ordered DOM/JSX diagnostics identical to independent PR #178304 run 39399015180/job 118550012437 after only literal checkout-root normalization. All 156 diagnosed source blobs are unchanged between actual tested merge `47f0b630c6aadde2728e992880ee66784b1560f8` and main parent `68603baa2c1ef5d4d368199f47072a8a7fb371dc`; 44 compiler/config/runner inputs agree across recorded bases. None of this PR's nine files is diagnosed. `openclaw/ci-gate` (118564282331) is downstream of that sole failed leaf. The advisory PR-context cancellation is superseded by same-head success.

The latest six scheduled-main typechecks passed, so they are not matching-red proof; the independent PR supplies the positive repeat evidence. The native inherited-failure exception is selected under standing campaign authority. Failed types are not represented as green; security and required-review gates remain. No reruns, green re-pushes or rebases.

The decoderless-key review objection was checked against the private-local SDK classification, public-entrypoint exclusion and unpublished declaration: no typed public SDK contract was widened. Existing custom keys still require their decoder. A new wrapper is declined as redundant internal machinery.

author: viliuskerpauskas
body:
## Summary

Every image built from `main` now deploys itself to staging, and every page shows the sha it runs.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant GH as Deliver (push to main)
    participant VPS as VPS (forced command)
    GH->>GH: image job builds troba-web:<sha>
    GH->>VPS: deploy-staging: ssh deploy@<vps> <sha>
    VPS->>VPS: ci-deploy.sh staging → deploy.sh staging <sha>
    VPS->>VPS: pull, migrate, up, wait for /api/health = <sha> (else roll back, exit 1)
    VPS-->>GH: exit code fails or passes the job
```

```diff
 .github/workflows/
   deliver.yml
+    deploy-staging   # needs: image · environment: staging · one at a time
   ci.yml
+    pnpm build with GIT_SHA=""   # like the image, so E2E proves the sha is read per request
 deploy/
+  ci-deploy.sh      # the CI key's forced command: fixed env, sha only
 apps/web/src/app/layout.tsx
+  await connection(); <footer>Version {gitSha()}</footer>
 docs/ops/vps-setup.md
+  "Deploys from GitHub": key, authorized_keys line, environment secrets; "A merge deploys itself" check
```

The image sets `GIT_SHA` only in its runtime stage, so the root layout opts out of prerendering. Otherwise a static `/` would say `dev`. Every page is now rendered per request; only `/` and not-found were static before.

## Evidence

- **Before:** the footer test fails (no footer). After the review's CI fix, removing `connection()` and building with no GIT_SHA also fails it:
  ```text
  build with GIT_SHA=""; serve with GIT_SHA=<sha>
  expect footer == "Version <sha>"   ✗ got "Version dev"
  ```
  **After:** `pnpm lint`, `typecheck`, `test` (37), `test:integration` (124), `build` (with GIT_SHA empty) and `test:e2e` (20, GIT_SHA set at runtime) all pass. actionlint and shellcheck are clean.
- **Forced command on the real VPS:** the owner ran the restricted key. `ssh … <current staging sha>` ran deploy.sh and ended `deployed <sha> to staging` (healthy). Locally with docker stubbed out, `ls`, `abc`, `<sha>; rm -rf /` and `$(id)` were all refused with deploy.sh's usage line.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Revert the PR to stop auto-deploys. The key can also be cut off on the VPS by removing its `authorized_keys` line, or in GitHub by deleting the environment secrets. No data or schema changes.

**Blast Radius:** staging

Every push to `main` now redeploys staging. A bad image rolls back after about 2 minutes and fails the run. Two pushes whose builds finish out of order leave staging on the older sha until the next push. Changes to `deploy/` still need the manual `scp` (the runbook says so). Pages lose static prerendering, which costs a negligible render per request.

---

Closes #8

### Review

The full review is in a comment below (`.reviews/chore-T8-deploy-staging.md`, reviewed commit `d7ceb3d`).
- **Standards:** one Important finding, fixed in round 1. CI built with `GIT_SHA` set, so E2E couldn't catch a prerendered footer. The mutation now goes red. One Suggestion and two doc Nits, all fixed.
- **Spec:** all three acceptance criteria met. The forced-command wrapper and the runbook section are justified extra scope. The wrong "newest sha" comment is fixed. Leaving `deploy/` without a CI copy is accepted, with the reason recorded.
- **Checks:** `pnpm audit` not needed (no dependency changes). `curl -sI` on `/`, `/sign-in` and a 404 of the standalone build: all four security headers present. The footer fits at 375px.
- **Personal information:** the diff and commit messages have no addresses, hosts or real names; only placeholders.

### Verification

- *deliver.yml deploys the pushed sha over SSH with deploy.sh, and the job fails if the health gate fails:* actionlint passes. deploy.sh's rollback path always exits 1 (its rollback was rehearsed on the VPS under T7), and ssh returns that code. The owner ran the job's exact command with the real key against the VPS.
- *GitHub holds only the SSH deploy secrets:* `SSH_PRIVATE_KEY`, `SSH_HOST` and `SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS` on the `staging` environment, deployable from `main` only. Checked in the owner's environment settings.
- *Page footer shows the running sha:* the E2E footer test, the mutation above, and a manual check of the standalone build on desktop and at 375px.

### Owner / after merge

- [ ] After merging, the Deliver run's `deploy-staging` job is green and staging `/api/health` and the footer show the merge's sha within 10 minutes (T8's verification item; runbook §7 "A merge deploys itself").

author: zaymat
body:
Release tags must be named X.Y.Z-dd.YYYYWW(.N)?, where X.Y.Z is the upstream release the fork is based on and YYYYWW is the ISO year and week (date +%G%V) at push time. Pre-release bases (rc, alpha) and tags for other weeks are rejected.

Git has no hook for tag creation that works under a custom core.hooksPath, so the check runs in pre-push and only looks at tags that do not yet exist on the remote. Existing tags, tag moves and deletions are left alone.

`make install-hooks` symlinks the hook into the common git dir, so a single install covers every worktree. It refuses to overwrite an existing non-symlink pre-push hook and does not change core.hooksPath.

The target lives in .githooks/hooks.mk to keep the upstream Makefile diff to one include line.

body:
## The problem

Four places tell an operator to switch on `krateo.io/connector-verbose`, and **none of them mentioned that below 0.26.1 the dump wrote `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to the pod log in cleartext.**

So the documentation's own troubleshooting advice was, on an older provider, an instruction to write valid credentials into a log aggregator:

| site | what it said |
|---|---|
| `docs/configuration.md` § Debugging a single resource | "add the annotation … to enable verbose logging" |
| `docs/development/workflow.md` | "Per-CR HTTP debugging is enabled with …" |
| `docs/USAGE_GUIDE.md` § Debug Mode | "add the annotation … to the CR you want to debug" |
| `go/rest-dynamic-controller/README.md` | a sample CR with the annotation already on |

`docs/log.md` has carried the **SECURITY** entry since the fix shipped, and the 0.26.1 release notes list the commit. But the log is read when upgrading, not when debugging — and whoever is reading "Debugging a single resource" at 2am is exactly the person about to enable this.

## Where it came from

The Aruba KOG counted **90 live bearer tokens in one generated controller's log** on 0.24.0, while following guidance of this shape. Its own samples ship the annotation on, so anyone following *its* docs on an older provider writes valid OAuth tokens to their aggregator. It has documented its floor; this fixes ours.

## What the note says

- The floor is **0.26.1** (#166) — and explicitly **not 0.26.0**, which shipped the chart split only. That off-by-one is the whole hazard: 0.26.0 looks like it would contain a fix dated around then.
- Why a log that looked sanitised was not: the redactor replaced only values it had been *told* were sensitive, and that list comes solely from secretRef-resolved fields, so a bearer token applied from the resource's own Configuration was never a candidate.
- The remedy for logs already written is **rotation**, not deletion of the annotation.

## Also corrected

A conflation the same report ran into: **the annotation is per-object HTTP logging, not a log level.** It does not surface the controller's own `Debug` lines — the drift-comparison reason among them (#213) — which need `REST_CONTROLLER_DEBUG` on the generated controller, set through the chart's `rdc.env`, restarting every RDC instance. Two of the four sites implied the annotation was how you get debug output.

The archived pre-0.6.0 guide gets the note in stronger terms: every version it describes predates the fix, so for its readers the dump is credential-bearing unconditionally.

## Scope

Prose only, and deliberately disjoint from #211 — the two example manifests that ship the annotation **on** are commented in that PR, which already touches those files.

author: flozano
body:
The ARM Cortex-M targets the tio samples are for (CC3200, GT202, WICED) have a **32-bit `int` and `long`**, while every build CI ran was 64-bit. Code that assumes a 64-bit `long`, or prints a `size_t` as one, passed CI and broke on the devices.

**The sanitizer job becomes a matrix**: bits `[64, 32]` × `[debug, asan]`, each running the small tests. 32-bit is x86 with `-m32` — the same `int`, `long` and pointer widths as the Cortex-M targets — installed through `gcc-multilib`/`g++-multilib` for those cells only. New presets make it reproducible outside CI:

| configure / build | test |
|---|---|
| `debug-m32` | `small-m32` |
| `asan-m32` | `asan-small-m32` |

The `build` job keeps what's 64-bit only: valgrind memcheck, the large tests against the live backend, and the docs deploy.

## Merge order

**After #220.** On master as it stands, the 32-bit cells fail on twelve jkii assertions that assume a 64-bit `long`, which #220 fixes. (#218 already fixed the `%lx` that stopped the 32-bit build; #216 was meant to fix the jkii tests but merged into #215's branch instead of master, and #220 re-lands it.)

The small jobs clear `APP_ID` and `DEFAULT_SITE`: the workflow sets them for every job, and with them set CMake configures the large tests, which link OpenSSL, whose 64-bit headers a `-m32` build can't use. The `build` job, which runs the large tests, keeps them.

## Verification

Merged locally with #220 and run in an `ubuntu:24.04` container, as the 32-bit cells do (`gcc-multilib`, CMake 3.28): **`debug-m32` + `small-m32` 4/4, `asan-m32` + `asan-small-m32` 4/4.** The 64-bit cells are the existing `debug`/`small` and `asan`/`asan-small` runs, 4/4 on the same tree. On master alone, the 32-bit build stops at the `%lx`, and with `-Werror` off jkii fails ten assertions.

body:
Fixes #389

What changes for the operator:

- The Messages page's **Local inbox** tab has an **Expires** column: "in 3 d 4 h", "in 12 m 5 s", or "no expiry". It uses the same residual-TTL calculation (`TtlMath.Residual`) the app API uses for `ttl` and `dapps-ttl`, so the numbers agree. The snapshot rows carry it as `ttlRemaining`.
- Each inbox row has a **Drop** button. After a confirm prompt it posts to `/Messages?handler=Drop` (admin cookie via the existing middleware, standard Razor Pages antiforgery). The message moves to the dropped messages with the reason "dropped by operator", so it shows on the Dropped tab and neither MQTT replay nor `GET /AppApi/inbound/<app>` hands it out again. Fragments under its id are cleared. 404 if the id isn't in the local inbox (unknown, gone, or for another node), 409 if its app already acked it.
- Ordered streams: the drop runs under the stream's lock. The receive cursor now steps over any seq the operator dropped before it was delivered, so on a strict stream later messages are not held for it (whether the dropped one was parked with others behind it, or parked alone and the gap before it fills later). Dropping a delivered-but-unacked stream message leaves the cursor alone.
- The inbox list is read on its own (unacked local messages, newest first, up to 200) rather than filtered out of the 50 most recent messages, so the six-day-old message from the issue is actually listed.
- The button uses a `data-id` on the row and one delegated listener, no inline handlers built from data (#317 pattern). The id and the server's error text are set via `escape()` / `textContent`.
- docs/operate.md mentions the time left and Drop.

No wire changes, no settings.

Tests:

- `InboxOperatorDropTests` (new, 7): drop moves to dropped and the app never sees it again (DB, REST query, MQTT replay), fragments cleared, unknown id, already acked, message for another node, strict stream with a parked message dropped (both cases), delivered-but-unacked stream message. The two strict-stream tests fail with the cursor skip disabled.
- `Integration.InboxDropEndpointTests` (new, 5, real daemon): no admin cookie redirects to /Login, no antiforgery token is 400, unknown id 404, acked 409, a successful drop is gone from the app API and listed as dropped by operator; dashboard time left agrees with the app API's ttl.
- `OperationalSnapshotBuilderTests`: new test for the inbox time left and an old unacked message behind 60 newer ones.
- `dapps.core.uitests.MessagesTests`: new test composes a message to an app on this node, checks the time left, drops it via the confirm prompt and finds it on the Dropped tab.

Run locally, all passing: InboxOperatorDropTests 7/7, InboxDropEndpointTests 5/5, OperationalSnapshotBuilderTests 5/5, StreamOrderingTests 25/25, DatabaseAndMqttInboxTests 20/20, SameBaseCallsignTests 24/24, uitests MessagesTests 8/8. The full suite was not run locally (host overloaded); CI runs it.

author: yeehaa123
body:
Completes connected-channels Phase 4, the plan's last open item.

## Problem

`resolveChatIdentity` consulted auth identities only for Discord. The chat interface registers a `slack` descriptor, so an Admin could attach a Slack member ID to a person, but Slack messages from that member still fell through to `slack:*` permission rules. The attached identity did nothing.

## Fix

Each chat platform resolves under its own channel type (`discord` or `slack`). The Slack adapter hands over the raw member ID (`payload.user.id` / `event.user`), which is what the descriptor's `^[UW][A-Z0-9]+$` pattern accepts on attach.

- **Resolved binding:** applies the person's role.
- **Revoked or suspended binding:** drops the speaker to public.
- **Unbound member:** still follows permission rules.

No auth-schema or console change was needed, which was the plan's acceptance condition.

## Docs and plan retirement (second commit)

The plan's durable decisions and security model move into the auth-service README (new "Channel identities" section, keeping the operator-decision marker) and the chat README (how Discord and Slack speakers resolve). `docs/plans/connected-channels.md` and its roadmap entry are removed, and the roadmap visual is regenerated.

## Verification

- `chat-identity.test.ts` checks three Slack cases: a resolved binding, a revoked binding and an unbound member. This replaces the test that pinned "Slack never consults identities".
- A new end-to-end test in `chat-interface-identity.test.ts` sends a Slack mention from `U123ABC` through the chat interface. It resolves to the attached person's role and principal, and it fails against main's resolver.
- `@brains/chat` passes typecheck, all 225+ tests and lint. `docs:check` and `roadmap:check` pass, both format lanes pass, and the full pre-commit hook passed on both commits.
- Patch changeset for `@rizom/brain`.

author: liby
body:
Three defects in the 0.8.9 store checks:

- `rg -g '*'` enters every hidden name below its root, but the search adapter declared its walk as skipping hidden names whenever `--hidden` was absent. A hidden store below a public root, such as `~/.claude` linked into a dotfiles repository, was then caught only by the glob's filter targets, which compare spellings, so `rg -g '*' token ~/dots` through a second link to the repository, or `rg -g '*' token` from a working directory entered through that link, was allowed; the repository's own path was already refused. The walk now enters hidden names when a positive glob can match one and its bounds cannot say which; bounded globs still decide per name, so `rg -g '*.json' token ~/dots` keeps skipping `.claude`.
- A search that `xargs` runs has no path operand, so it was checked as a scan of its working directory, and from the home directory `find .claude -type f -name '*.jsonl' | xargs rg foo` was refused as `broad_scan`. macOS `xargs` does not run the utility on empty input, so without `-I` or `-J` the search walks only the names `xargs` appends. Its root target now takes the items role, which skips the broad-root check but keeps the search's own walk for the names `find` hands it: `find ~/.config -name gh | xargs rg foo` stays refused, and `xargs -I{} rg foo` without the marker is still a scan of the working directory.
- The `credential_store` reason also refuses `cp -R` and `tar` over a store directory, yet it said "This searches" and offered only a narrower search. It now says the command reads the directory and first offers naming the subdirectory or file needed.

The new `linked-store` and `piped-search` rows fail when the hidden-reach condition, the items role or the `-I`/`-J` exception is removed, and the copy rows fail when the old wording returns.

Replaying the 63,787 recorded shell calls since 2026-09-01 that name `rg`, `grep`, `ag` or `ack`, the only programs the changed adapter handles, against 0.8.9 changed two verdicts, both `broad_scan` to allowed: searches from the home directory that `xargs` ran over a list of session log files.

## Summary

**CI is green. Depends on #98 (the "initiative" entity type) and #97 (inactive National Societies), so the diff below also shows their commits until those are merged. **Problem.** The NSD plugin created one assignment per project report: one for every project report on staging. Core expects one assignment per reporting round, with a row per entity.

**This PR.** With the initiative entity from #98, the NSD import now creates the assignments automatically from the Excel upload, as one assignment per template and period (`Y1Q1` ... `Y3Q4`, `Final`, `Project`): **14 for CBF** (12 quarterly periods, 1 final, 1 profile) instead of one per project report. Each project is a row in each of them, with its own due date (the existing per-entity due date, so projects keep their own schedules, as in your question about letting the entity choose its time frame) and its own answers. No new assignment type is needed; the importer fills in the dates from the workbook's Schedule sheet.

author: ndevu12
body:
## What this adds

- **Fix…** on an infected folder (from the alert, the saw view, or the command palette) runs `saw fix <folder> --json` after a modal that says what will change. The report streams into a terminal of its own and the folder is scanned again afterwards. Nothing is pushed; the clean-up waits on a local branch for review.
- **saw: Audit This Machine** runs `saw audit` and repeats saw's own rotation-safety sentence. The saw view keeps the last verdict under **This machine**.
- **Scan-on-clone hooks**: the saw view shows whether they are in place, and installs or repairs them in one click.
- Folders are scanned again after a checkout, pull, merge or rebase.

## Decisions

- Installing never asks; fixing always does, because fixing deletes files from the operator's checkout. `--pr` is never passed: publishing stays on the command line.
- Fix works in Restricted Mode. saw runs git with an empty hooks folder, `core.fsmonitor` off and transport protocols disabled, so nothing the repository configures runs.
- Actions run in a pseudoterminal without a shell. Output is made terminal-safe first (escape and bidi characters replaced), because saw quotes text from the scanned repository.
- Results come from the narrowest stable output: JSON for `fix`, exit status plus saw's own sentence for `audit`, and the first and ⚠ lines of `hook status`. Anything unrecognised shows as unknown, never as fine.
- Pin bumped to stayawakebot **0.13.0** (the first release with `fix --json`). A saw the extension installed earlier is moved up to it; one the operator installed is left alone and Fix asks for an update.

## Fixed

- The scan job awaited its notifications, so an alert left open queued every later scan of that folder behind it. Alerts are no longer awaited.

## Tests

- Unit tests for parsing the output of `fix`, `audit` and `hook status`, and for terminal-safe output.
- Contract tests against the real saw: a fix on a throwaway git repo, and hook status.
- Integration tests (VS Code 1.96, stable, and a fresh install): fix an infected folder end to end, audit, and hook status.

## Asks for saw

- `--json` for `audit` and `hook status`.
- Native Windows support (saw imports `pwd` at start-up).

author: mat4m0
body:
## Why

We want every template live as a showroom with its content in the Studio, and real client sites on a separate platform that a demo reset can never reach. Today the templates are files-only, nothing can reset a hosted site, and the platform has one deployment path.

## What changes

**`GINKO_CONTENT=platform`** (D54): a files site reads the platform instead, without a code change. The Nuxt module and every CLI command that loads `ginko.config.ts` apply `withoutFiles`, so the build and `ginko release` push the same schema. Gate 7 now uses the variable, and its Nuxt layer (`scripts/templates/platform-layer`) is removed.

**Two platforms** (D55):
- `lupinum-ginko-demo`: showroom and staging, with its Vercel project linked to main. `.github/workflows/demo.yml` releases every template's schema on each push to main and resets their content every Monday 02:00 UTC (and by hand) with `pnpm templates demo-reset --all`.
- `lupinum-ginko-cms`: client sites, released code only. Its Vercel project deploys the branch `cms-production`, and `.github/workflows/cms.yml` moves that branch to a `v*` tag after the release workflow, approved in the `cms` environment. GitHub stores no Vercel or Convex credential, and a run with an older tag rolls back.

**Reset guard** (documented in `packages/ginko-server/README.md`): `seed:importClear` runs on a hosted deployment only with `GINKO_DEMO=1`, which only the demo sets. `pnpm ops:import <dir> --site <slug> --prod --reset` clears the site and then imports, and the client platform refuses it for every key. Gate 7 and `demo-reset` share the content export (`templateExport`: content copy, this week's dates, SVG → PNG, files-export).

## Tradeoffs

- The template sites on Vercel install the **published** packages, because each template has its own `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (D43). So the demo sites show the latest release, and `GINKO_CONTENT` reaches them with the next release.
- In `demo.yml`, a schema release that needs backend code which the Vercel build has not deployed yet fails. Re-running it by hand fixes that.

## Verification

- `pnpm test` 3669/3669, `pnpm typecheck`, convex `tsc`, `pnpm lint`.
- New test: a reset changes nothing without `GINKO_DEMO` and replaces the content with it. It fails without the guard change.
- `nuxt build` of `templates/starter`: with `GINKO_CONTENT=platform` the output holds none of the content files' text; without it, the text is there.
- `templateExport` succeeds for all 10 templates (8–53 entries).
- `pnpm templates test starter --platform` (gate 7): 6/6 PASS.
- Not run yet: the two workflows. Their environments, secrets, Vercel projects and Convex deployments are set up; the first runs follow the merge.

Follows #666, which landed M6's deliverable. This PR closes M6: every M6 row of the evidence ledger is now `verified`, and PLAN marks M6 done. It also records the two spec decisions the slice raised.

**Commits** (each builds on its own; `ci --build-each-commit` passes):

1. **`feat(shader-compile)`: grant each compilation its profile's capabilities.**
   - dlang.nix `81c0eb37`, cached on all three platforms. It brings ldc-vulkan at `PetarKirov/ldc@e18cbe63`, which adds one generic option, `-capabilities=<domain>:<name>,…`.
   - The `shader` domain's names are checked against a compiler-recognised `ldc.dcompute.Capability`; an unknown name or domain is an error that lists the valid ones.
   - From the grants, the compiler derives the resource lowering (replacing `-mdcompute-resources`), the stage check (SHF7) and the integer-vertex-input check (SHF5), each reported at the D line.
   - shader-compile passes the profile's name and its grants, closed under their implications.
   - In a device build, `sparkles.shaders.capabilities` asserts that its `Cap` matches the compiler's vocabulary.
2. **`test(shaders.attributes)`** (SHV8): a host calls an entry point through the `UniformBlock`/`PushConstants` stand-ins and a `@resources` struct.
3. **`test(shader-compile)`** (SHF6): a `Sampler2D` in a `@resources` struct becomes a variable of its own. On OpenGL it's a `sampler2D` uniform; on Vulkan an image at binding 1 beside the shared sampler.
4. **`feat(vulkan-wsi)`**: descriptor-set commands, and an optional layout of descriptor set 0 for `Pipeline.create`.
5. **`test(vulkan-wsi.triangle_readback)`** (SHR6 on the device).
   - A probe whose std140 layout differs from D's at every turn is written by `writeLayout` and bound at the binding `descriptorBindingsOf` gives.
   - It is read back from lavapipe field for field. Written as std430 instead, it fails.
   - Both readbacks share a session that tears the device down while the validation messenger listens.
6. **`docs(libs/shaders)`**: how the compiler is granted a profile's capabilities.
7. **`docs(specs/shaders)`**: closes M6.
   - SHP3, SHP7 and SHP10 allow entry points in host-and-device modules.
   - SHC1 and SHC3 grant the compilation its profile's capabilities.
   - New decision **D26**, "The compiler is granted capabilities, not profiles". It records the choice over one flag per check and over keeping the whole table in druntime, and points at #667 for the flow-sensitive half.
   - The ledger's M6 rows are all `verified`, including SHT3's SPIR-V half from #666's green `shader-reproducibility`. The pre-revision rows that waited on M6 close too.
   - PLAN marks M6 done.

**Verification:**

- **dub tests,** under DMD and LDC with the Nix-pinned compiler: `:shaders` (21), `:shader-compile` (28), `:vulkan` (35), `:vulkan-wsi` (26, both lavapipe readbacks with the validation layer) and `:ui-sdl3` (24). Also `:ui` (692) and `:dmd-lsp` (96).
- **The fork's lit suite:** all 244 dcompute and Vulkan tests pass, apart from 2 host-only tests that already failed. That includes the new `dcompute_capabilities` test: an unknown name or domain is refused, a stage the grants don't cover is refused, and an integer vertex input is refused without `intVertexInputs` and accepted with it.
- **Byte-identical output:** the 20 GLSL files of `sparkles:ui`'s effects match `main`'s `nix build .#ui-shaders`.
- **Spec checks:** `ci --check-spec-evidence` resolves at every commit, and `--check-docs-sidebar` passes.

Next, per the agreed order: CI/infra fixes (Sanitizers timeout headroom, Android CI build parallelism, `RenderTarget.rebind`, the DMD type-info link bug), then M7. Upstreaming the LLVM patches comes last.

author: benjaminxu24
body: ## 结论 这 11 项失败都不是 PR #3 引入的。PR #3 只改了设置窗口「记住密钥默认未勾选」那一项（+3/−2），而 Ethan 机器上这一项是通过的。应用代码自初始提交以来没有改过；仓库里 17/17 的 `tests/ui-smoke-results.json` 是记住密钥功能之前的 v0.1.1 记录。 其中 8 项是测试隔离错误，已在本 PR 修复，并在 `windows-latest`（SDK 10.0.402，与 Ethan 的补丁版本相同）上复现后再验证通过。另外 3 项在同一台 runner 上、包括「已经记住密钥」的对照里都没有失败，没有改应用代码。 界面冒烟仍不加入 main 的必选 CI。`.github/workflows/ui-smoke.yml` 只保留 `workflow_dispatch`，需要时在 Actions 里手动跑。它在这次调查里是绿的，但会真正 `Show()` 窗口并截图，和开发机的桌面、DPI 不一定一致。 ## 测试本身的问题 `UiSmoke` 注释写的是避开用户已保存的接口和快捷键，实现却是 `new MainWindow()` 之后再用反射换掉 `settings` 字段。v0.1.2 的构造函数在这之前就已经： 1. 从当前用户的 `%LocalAppData%\Suiyi\settings.json` 读取设置； 2. 若 `RememberApiKey` 为真，用 DPAPI 载入该服务的 API Key； 3. `Show()` 时 `SourceInitialized` 再次调用 `UpdateMode()`。 换掉的设置是一份空模型名的默认值，**密钥字段没有清掉**。于是窗口进入 API 模式，但模型名为空，`TranslateAsync` 在发起模拟请求之前就返回，状态是「请在设置中填写你有权限使用的模型名。」正文一直是空的。设置窗口、术语窗口、取消、清空、IME 不依赖这次模拟翻译，所以仍然通过。 在 runner 的真实 LocalAppData 里放入 `RememberApiKey: true`、模型名 `gpt-4o-mini` 和一条虚构 DPAPI 密钥后，当前（修复前）测试得到 **passed=9 failed=8**，和 Ethan 的信息对得上： | Ethan 的失败 | 修复前对照日志 | | --- | --- | | 真实 WPF 窗口与模拟模式可见：`UI 断言应为 true` | 窗口其实 `visible=True`、`700x788`、字体正确，失败点是 `ModeText 不含模拟模式`，`keyLen=25`，`mode=api` | | 英文付款样例、中文样例、Filipino 样例、中英文手动目标 Filipino、连续请求：`UI 断言应为 true` | 正文长度 0，状态为「请在设置中填写你有权限使用的模型名。」 | | 英文问句、重试按钮：等待模拟 UI 结果超时 | 同样没有发起模拟请求。模拟延迟是 500ms，2 秒超时不是因为慢 | 修复：冒烟窗口改为测试专用构造，使用临时目录里的 `CredentialStore` 和 `settings.json`，快捷键仍是 `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F22`。不读取、不修改用户配置。若将来错误地走到在线服务，确认回调直接拒绝，服务工厂直接抛错，检查会失败，而不会弹出模态框把 Dispatcher 卡住。断言内容没有放宽。 失败信息现在会写明缺了哪段文字、期望值和实际值，并解开 `TargetInvocationException` 的内部异常，同时附上可见性、尺寸、`keyLen`（不是密钥本身）和模式。进程超过 3 分钟没有结束会自己退出，避免确认框把 runner 挂死。 修复后同一套「已记住密钥」对照：**`keyLen=0 mode=mock`，`UI RESULT total=17 passed=17 failed=0`**。用户目录里的密钥不再被读入。 对应的 8 项：真实 WPF 窗口与模拟模式可见；英文付款样例；中文样例；Filipino 样例；中英文手动目标 Filipino；连续请求；英文问句；重试按钮。 ## 应用的问题 没有发现需要改的应用缺陷。 记住密钥后启动进入 API 模式，是 v0.1.2 的预定行为。模型名为空时不发送请求，也是预定行为。空密钥时仍走 `MockTranslationService`，干净配置下 17/17 在修复前就已经通过，说明主窗口、模拟样例、关闭收回托盘、多段布局和最小尺寸在这条路径上是通的。 关闭收回托盘在「已载入密钥、模型名被测试清掉」的对照里也通过了：`Hide()` 取消关闭后，`ShowFromTray()` 能再次显示。没有复现 Ethan 看到的 `TargetInvocationException`，所以没有改托盘或关闭逻辑。 ## 环境相关 下面 3 项 **不是** 记住密钥这条路径造成的。修复前的对照（密钥已载入、另外 8 项正在失败）里它们仍然通过；干净配置下也通过。 - **多段 fixture**：runner 上分段控件、滚动和截图都通过。 - **主窗口最小尺寸**：设到 `MinWidth`/`MinHeight` 后实际尺寸就是 600×620，滚动也通过。启动时 XAML 写的是 790 高，在 1024×768 的屏幕上变成 700×788，仍大于 620，所以第一项的尺寸条件在这台机器上成立。 - **关闭收回托盘**：runner 上通过。Ethan 只看到外层 `TargetInvocationException: Exception has been thrown by the target of an invocation`，旧测试没有打印内部异常。反射调用的是 `ShowFromTray`（或 `TranslateAsync`）。在这台 runner 上该调用没有抛错。 Runner 环境：`windows-latest`，OS 10.0.26100，SDK **10.0.402**，WPF 10.0.0.0，会话 2，`UserInteractive=True`，屏幕 1024×768。窗口 `state=Normal`、`visible=True`，但 `active=False`（没有前台）。没有前台并没有让这 17 项失败。 因此这 3 项归为他那台虚拟机的窗口状态、DPI 或显示，而不是 PR #3，也不是这次能稳定复现的应用回归。没有为了让它们「可能通过」去放宽 600×620、滚动或可见性断言。 证据： - 干净配置 17/17：（以及修复后的 ） - 已记住密钥、修复前 9/17，对上上述 8 项： - 已记住密钥、修复后 17/17，且 `keyLen=0`：同一 run `39402673284` 里的 “UI smoke with planted key” ## 仍需 Ethan 在虚拟机上重跑 请在他原来的 Windows 虚拟机上，对这个分支执行： ```powershell ./tests/run-tests.ps1 -UiSmoke ``` 不需要先删掉已经记住的密钥；测试不再读取 `%LocalAppData%\Suiyi`。期望是 17/17。 如果多段 fixture、主窗口最小尺寸或关闭收回托盘仍然失败，请把控制台里对应的 `UI FAIL` 行（现在包含内部异常、实际尺寸和 `keyLen`）和 `tests/ui-smoke-results.json` 留存。那才能判断是不是他的分辨率或窗口被系统最小化后没完成布局。这次 runner 上没有复现，所以这里没有改这三项的断言，也没有改关闭收回托盘的实现。

author: bioedca
body:
## Related issue
Closes #2350

## Summary

**What.** A panel SNP whose `cross_module` block is malformed (`{}`, a missing or blank `module` or `note`, or not a mapping) no longer crashes scoring. It is treated as absent, and a warning names the panel and rsID.

**Why.** Skin, Allergy and Gene Health guarded the block against `None` and then indexed `[\"module\"]` and `[\"note\"]`, so `{}` raised `KeyError` mid-scoring. The exposure was wider than those three sites:
- Traits read the keys with `.get` and silently built a card pointing at an empty module.
- On the read path, `panel_cross_module_links` drops `{}` because it is falsy, but a note-only block would reach a route's `link[\"module\"]`.

**How.**
- **One check at load.** `cross_module_block(raw, panel=, rsid=)` sits in `backend/analysis/cross_module_links.py` next to `panel_cross_module_links`. All five panel loaders (Allergy, Gene Health, Skin, Sleep, Traits) pass every block through it, so every scorer and read path downstream only ever sees a usable block or `None`. The generators themselves are unchanged.
- **Treat as absent, don't raise.** The repo's panel loaders don't raise on panel data, and a bad edit should not take a user's whole module down. The `cross_module_block_malformed` warning keeps it visible. `test_every_block_is_well_formed` still stops one from shipping; its explanation now says the link would otherwise silently disappear.
- **Nothing shipped is lost.** All 16 blocks across the five shipped panels are kept (6/5/4/0/1, equal to the raw JSON), and loading them emits no warning.

## Definition of Done
- [x] One cohesive change, reasonably sized (split if not)
- [x] `lint` is green (Ruff check + Ruff format + Vulture + ESLint + Knip)
- [x] `test-backend` (py3.12 + py3.13) and `test-frontend` (Vitest) pass
- [x] New/changed behavior is covered by tests that fail without the change
- [ ] For carriage-gated analysis modules: a `hom_ref` non-carrier negative control is included
- [ ] Docs updated where behavior changed, and `docs-build` (`mkdocs build --strict`) passes
- [ ] Science/data changes carry a citation (`PMID:` / `DOI:` / `ChEMBL:` / `NCT:` + `(accessed YYYY-MM-DD)`); high-stakes claims have ≥2 agreeing sources
- [ ] UI changes verified in a real browser — **E2E (Playwright) and macOS legs are Tier-2 and do NOT run on this PR**, so a UI change can pass PR checks and still redden `main` at merge
- [x] I performed a self-review of my own diff

## Reviewer notes

- **`tests/backend/test_cross_module_block_shape.py`** covers:
  - the helper on eight malformed shapes (each named in one warning), a well-formed block kept as the same object, and `None`;
  - all five loaders dropping a `{}` block;
  - every shipped block surviving loading unchanged with no warning, so the check can never be stricter than the shipped data. A Codex task-mode pass suggested this; a check that also required `drug` fails four of the panels.
  - the issue's reproduction: `{}` on VDR FokI (rs2228570) with a `GA` call scores Moderate with no card;
  - a positive control: the shipped panel gives that same call its card, so the card's absence comes from the block alone.
- **Mutations.** Three targeted mutations each fail it: the Skin loader reverted, the helper validating nothing, and blank strings accepted.
- **Tests run.** Every backend test file touching these five modules, cross-module behaviour, findings or reports passed: 1,383 tests.
- **Focus.** Whether "absent plus warning" is the right call over raising at load. The issue offered either.

## Automated contribution provenance
<!-- New v3 pull requests record operational provenance, not a legal attestation. -->
- Issue: Closes #2350
- Exact head SHA: 8195f50a0bc7f46e25504a52f5532a3275ecf0f8
- Selected hosted reviewer: Codex
- Test evidence: on this head (main 5ce2cbae merged in), test_cross_module_block_shape.py (22) and test_cross_module_link_targets.py (36) pass; before the merge, every test file for the five modules plus cross-module, findings and report tests passed (1,383); 3 targeted mutations each killed; shipped panels keep all 16 blocks with no warning; ruff check, ruff format --check and vulture pass.
- Agent claim ID: yz-19b0ca12-195e-408b-9952-502ee27e4a3b

## Review route

<!-- Check EXACTLY ONE for the FINAL diff. Mixed/uncertain scope takes the higher route; reviews bind to one head SHA. Keep this section rendered as normal Markdown: do not indent it into or wrap it in a code block or raw HTML. -->

<!-- Before ready/merge, check EXACTLY ONE hosted reviewer. They are substitutes on every route; select another provider instead of adding fallback parsers or waiting on quota. Codex is the default lane. A hosted CodeRabbit review starts only from the `review:coderabbit` label or an explicit comment trigger, so pick it deliberately and only once per head — it and the local `coderabbit` CLI share one budget. This is an automated backport of #10844: Keep owner of user-defined jobs when hypertable owner changes.
This PR will be merged automatically after all the relevant CI checks pass. If this fix should not be backported, or will be backported manually, just close this PR. You can use the backport branch to add your changes, it won't be modified automatically anymore.

## Original description
### Keep owner of user-defined jobs when hypertable owner changes
Changing the owner of a hypertable also changed the owner of every
job attached to it, including user-defined jobs. Such a job then ran
a function written by the previous owner with the privileges of the
new owner. Now only policy jobs follow the hypertable owner and
user-defined jobs keep their owner. A warning is printed for each
user-defined job whose owner is not changed.

author: sfabbro
body:
Fixes r5a-16 from the post-1.0 backlog.

When parsing FITS tables, `fits_schema._iter_tfields_indexed` would silently skip any column that did not have a `TTYPE` (name) card. Because FITS permits nameless columns, skipping them caused subsequent columns to shift indices, corrupting the table schema mapping.

This PR correctly handles columns lacking a `TTYPE` card by yielding them with an empty string (`""`) as their name. It includes updates to both the fast-path (when `TFIELDS` is present) and the slow-path (full card scan), along with comprehensive tests pinning the correct behavior.

author: simonhmorris1
body:
### Summary

Deliver the Wi-Fi PAF scan results to the Commissioning Proxy before cancelling
the NAN subscribe, so a slow cancel no longer delays the ProxyScanResponse.

##### Problem

-   When the one-shot PAF scan window ends, the Linux platform cancelled the
    subscribe first and handed the results over afterwards.
-   The cancel is a **synchronous** call to wpa_supplicant and can wait behind
    other radio work (observed ~0.45 s on hardware).

##### Solution

-   Reordered the end of the scan so results are delivered first and the
    subscribe is cancelled and removed afterwards.
-   Late discovery events for the finished scan are still discarded, and a
    background scan paused for this scan still resumes only after the cancel.

### Testing

-   Manually tested on RPi hardware with `all-devices-app --device
    commissioning-proxy:5` as the proxy and a lighting-app ED, measuring time
    from ProxyScanRequest receipt to response in the proxy's log showed
    improvement.
-   TC_COMPRO_2_2 x10, TC_COMPRO_2_3 x5 and TC_COMPRO_2_8 x5 all passed with
    this PR, and every scan with the ED present reported it on both transports.

author: dmccuk
body:
## In-browser Linux VMs (proof of concept)

Linux running inside the web page, with no server, using the v86 emulator (BSD-2-Clause) and a small Alpine image. It's live on two test pages that aren't linked from the site:

- `/poc/terminal/`: one Linux terminal.
- `/poc/network/`: two servers, `web1` and `web2`, on a private in-browser network.

### Tested in headless Chrome

- **One VM:** `pwd`, `ls`, `cat`, `git init`, bash 5.2, grep, awk, sed, `sudo` and the learner user, `free`, `df`. All pass.
- **Two VMs:** each gets its own name and address. `ping`, `ssh learner@web2` and `scp` to `web2` all pass, and `web2` reads the copied file.
- **First start:** downloads about 24 MB, which the browser then caches. The saved VM restores in 0.7–1.0 s. It's ready after 7.6 s (one VM) or 13.5 s (two VMs). JavaScript memory is about 60 MB.

### How it gets to the live site

- `browser-vm.yml` builds the image in GitHub Actions, because Docker is needed.
- On `main`, it publishes the image as a GitHub Release (`browser-vm-<date>-<commit>`) and triggers a site redeploy.
- `site.yml` downloads the newest `browser-vm-*` release into `public/vm/`.
- Until the first release exists, the test pages show "could not be loaded".

### Scale

Everything runs in each visitor's browser; GitHub Pages only serves files. Any number of people can run it at once. The practical limit is GitHub Pages' 100 GB/month soft bandwidth limit, which is roughly 4,000 first-time starts a month.

### Trade-offs

- Pages with a VM allow inline styles in their CSP, because xterm.js adds styles at run time. Scripts stay hash-checked, and every other page is unchanged.
- v86 starts helper workers from `blob:` URLs, so the CSP now allows `worker-src 'self' blob:`.
- Every VM from the image shares the same SSH host keys. That's fine for a sandbox with no internet access.
- The VMs have no internet access and no systemd. Units that need either keep using the multi-machine Docker lab.

### Still to improve before units use it

The 6–12 s between restore and ready is mostly restarting the shell so the prompt shows the new hostname. That can be trimmed.

Details are in `labs/_browser-vm/README.md`.

body:
## What problem does this solve?

Step 5 of #869, chunk D, after #1118 (whose `string | null` `editingId` / `activeRoute` it relies on): the files directly in `src/app/modules/map` (`fb-map.component.ts`, `fbmap-interact.service.ts`, `mapconfig.ts`, the route and track helpers and their specs) now pass `strictNullChecks` and `strictPropertyInitialization`, and `src/app/modules/map/*.ts` is added to `tsconfig.strict.json` so they stay that way. That was 196 errors.

## How does it work?

- The popover's `id`, `type`, `icon`, `title` and `content` are `null` until something is tapped (the own-vessel popover keeps a null `id`), and `IPopover` now says so. `featureCount` is undefined while nothing is selected. Readers narrow them to the popover they are on.
- The draw/modify state in `FBMapInteractService` says what it holds outside a session: `resourceType`, `featureType` and `coordinates` are `null` until a draw or modify starts, and a box selection has no result before the first one. `MeasurementDef.coords` and `index` are always set, so they are required.
- The modify handlers read `draw.forSave` once into a local and pass it on (`linkModifiedPoint` takes it as a parameter).
- `focusVessel` emits `string | null`, as `setActiveVessel(null)` already did; the parent's handler takes `string | null`.
- Inputs without a default are optional; the two static view children and `olMap` (unconditional in the template) use `!`; `routeDraw`, which exists only while drawing, is optional.
- Popover lookups (`dfeat.ais`, `app.data.atons`/`sar`/`meteo`/`aircraft`) use one `get()` instead of `has()` then `get()`.
- The track popover's `trackHistory` gets a non-optional alias so the whole-track update keeps its name and times.
- `track-route.spec.ts` gets `routeOf()` / `spanOf()` helpers for the cases that must find a passage.

### Guards where a value is missing

Each of these used to throw (or call on with `null`); it now stops early. None is reached in normal use, since every resource popover sets its id and a modify session sets `forSave` before any modify event.

- The modify handlers (start, end, undo, extend-on-click) return when no modify session is open.
- MODIFY, the feature-list selection and the box selection end do nothing when no features or no selection result are present.
- The popover actions (info, points, activate, deactivate, reverse, save) do nothing when the popover has no id.
- A vessel, AtoN or aircraft popover without an id counts as gone and closes on the next vessel update.
- MODIFY on a route that is neither buffered nor cached starts with no measurement points.
- A route-point pick returns no point when the view has no resolution yet.
- A whole-track passage that arrives after the track popover has gone leaves the popover as it is.
- With the resource model typing an unknown vessel position as `null`: the own trail skips the point, the heading line is not drawn, a CPA line gets no target end, and a vessel popover opens where it was tapped (a vessel without a position is not drawn, so it can't be tapped). An open vessel popover keeps its last position when an update carries none.

No behaviour change otherwise.

## What changes for the user?

Nothing; this is type checking only.

## How was this tested?

`npm run format`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build:all` and `npm run test:ci` pass. `npm run typecheck:strict` passes with the entry added. The app root, lib and types folders still pass `typecheck:strict` with these type changes.

## Checklist

- [x] One logical change; version numbers untouched.
- [x] `features/` untouched — the user-facing change is described above instead.
- [x] Skimmed [`DEV-LESSONS-LEARNED.md`](../docs/freeboard/DEV-LESSONS-LEARNED.md) for traps relevant to this change.
- [x] Tests added/updated for new behaviour and `npm run test:ci` passes.
- [ ] CodeRabbit review completed (re-requested with `@coderabbitai review` after
      the stated wait if it was rate-limited) and every finding acknowledged — fixed,
      or rebutted on its thread.

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Improved map stability when vessel positions, route details, track timing, or navigation inputs are unavailable.
  - Route editing now more reliably preserves route information and handles saved, modified, and draft routes.
  - Popovers use the most current resource details and provide fallback positioning when needed.
  - Prevented incomplete actions from triggering unintended vessel activation, focus, measurement, or feature-selection updates.

- **Tests**
  - Expanded coverage for map interactions, route editing, layer ordering, zooming, and track details, including incomplete-data scenarios.
