body:
## What

«Кредитные лимиты» is now the credit underwriter's workbench: one sidebar item with seven tabs, kept in `?view=`. «Портфель полисов» moves into «Полисы» as its «Обзор» tab, the same pattern.

| Tab | Content |
|---|---|
| Обзор | The limit portfolio that used to be «Портфель лимитов». |
| Очередь решений | Drafts, under review, escalation, decided and client-proposed buyers, as a segmented switch. New: a «Решение» column showing the rating band and whether *I* can decide the request alone, plus the filter «только то, что я решаю сам». |
| Действующие лимиты | Register of every in-force limit. Filters: buyer / policy / policyholder text, band, country and currency. Totals in UZS; a limit with no UZS rate is counted, never added as zero. |
| Мониторинг | Reviews due within 30 days or overdue; ratings worse than the band the limit was decided in; open overdue notifications (NOA) with the suspension status; groups over or near (≥ 90%) their cap. |
| Рейтинги | Rating worklist with four reasons: no financials, not rated, newer period than the one rated, older than 12 months. Each row opens the company on the tab where that work is done. |
| Группы | Corporate groups against their group limits, breaches first. |
| Мои полномочия | Credit authority per band in UZS (`my_authority_uzs`, the figure a decision is checked against) and the grants behind it. |

**Who sees what:**
- **Credit underwriters and admin:** all seven tabs.
- **Sales and commercial underwriting:** «Очередь решений» and «Действующие лимиты» only.
- **«Полисы» → «Обзор»:** commercial underwriting and admin only.

**Redirects:** `/portfolio/credit` and `/portfolio/policies` redirect to the new tabs. The old `/limits?tab=escalated` link still opens the queue.

## Schema — migration 0053

Three read-only views, all `security_invoker` and staff-only:
- **`tci.v_limit_request_queue`** — open requests with their rating band (from the buyer's latest assessment), the amount in UZS, and `decide_alone`. `decide_alone` is true for admin, or when the amount in UZS is within the caller's credit authority for that band.
  - One deliberate difference from `decide_limit_request`: a grant in a currency with no UZS rate is skipped instead of raising. This keeps one bad grant from emptying the queue. The view comment says so.
- **`tci.v_rating_worklist`** — buyers with live credit business and an ordered reason. The 12-month threshold is the Agenda's `rating_stale` rule, and the migration asserts that.
- **`tci.v_group_limit_status`** — exposure against the live group limit, with utilisation and `over_limit`. Only real groups appear: two or more members by `tci.entity_group`, or a live group limit.

The migration asserts its own grants and `security_invoker` setting. `tests/db/credit_workbench.sql` covers authority (one underwriter within authority, one with no grant, admin), the four rating reasons, group utilisation of 112.5%, and that a client sees nothing.

## Verification
- **Gates:**
  - typecheck;
  - lint (the same 2 warnings);
  - 783 tests, with and without `.env.local`;
  - build.
- **New tests:** the pure rules in `limits/workbench/model.ts`, contract-tested against the migration text. Also a test that every rating band the engine emits has an en/ru/uz label.
- **Local DB replay:** `credit_workbench`, `portfolio` and `definer_gates` pass.
- **Canonical:**
  - 0053 applied (ledger `20261020111938`);
  - live smoke with role impersonation (two credit underwriters, admin, client), rolled back;
  - users, entities, policies and decisions unchanged;
  - no advisor finding on the new views.
- **Headless check** with stubbed data, as credit underwriter, commercial underwriter and sales:
  - all tabs render;
  - tab counts are correct;
  - no untranslated keys and no console errors;
  - redirects work.

## Terminology to confirm (uz)
- «Qarorlar navbati» — decision queue
- «Ishlanadigan reytinglar» — rating worklist
- «Tayinlov» — an authority grant
- «Umumiy ko‘rinish» — overview

author: fallowlone
body:
## Summary

TASK-0212 (G13): "Encrypted sync and org policy take effect locally" — integration tests only, no production code.

Adds `org_sync_policy_quota_take_effect_between_two_daemon_stores` to `bins/agentctl/tests/execution_binaries.rs`: the first shipped-binary proof that sync crosses between **two independent daemon stores** (TASK-0211 covered a single daemon/store; the two-store case existed only in-process in `org_service` tests).

## What the test proves

- A MEMBER seals an `ORG_PROFILE` envelope locally on daemon A; daemon B (independently provisioned store) accepts it: exact plaintext returned, B head 0→1, sender head unchanged.
- Carrier view (seal output fields) contains no plaintext, org key, or account secret; ciphertext does not embed the plaintext (C-2).
- Tampered ciphertext refuses `bad_signature` and applies nothing (C-6); replay refuses `duplicate_envelope` (C-10); a second seal against the sender's stale head refuses `conflict` on the receiver (C-7).
- Org hard policy binds on the receiver: `OrgService` resolution over the receiver DB narrows and refuses `PolicyWeakening` with policy v1 unchanged (C-8); a MEMBER policy write through shipped IPC refuses `forbidden_role` (C-4).
- Quota binds locally: usage 900/1000 recorded, estimate 200 refuses `over_quota` pre-dispatch, 100 admits (C-9).
- Local sovereignty: a fixture-provider execution run on B completes `SUCCEEDED` while sync state is conflicted (C-1).
- Everything survives restart of both daemons, including the replay refusal.

Receiver provisioning seeds org facts (accounts, organization, memberships, current policy) through `OrgStorePort` before B starts — the ADR-0047 v1 out-of-band provisioning shape; no shipped import surface preserves minted IDs.

## Verification (observed this session)

- New test: green (first run RED on receiver data-dir mode, root-caused to daemon's exact-0700 admission in `data_dir.rs`; provisioning now sets 0700).
- `cargo test --locked -p agentctl --test execution_binaries`: 22/22.
- `cargo test --locked -p app-services --test org_service`: 8/8.
- `cargo test --workspace --locked --no-fail-fast`: exit 0.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Risk / known limits

- Test-only change; no public contract, schema, or production behavior changes.
- Layered policy weakening is not reachable through shipped IPC (no resolve command in `org_core`); it is proven via `OrgService` over the same SQLite DB daemon B serves, plus the shipped `forbidden_role` refusal. A shipped resolve surface would be a separate task.
- `check_quota` remains a pre-dispatch predicate (per TASK-0210/0211 design); it is not wired into provider dispatch, unchanged here.

author: daghostman
body:
Before: a module-level `const` had to fold to a scalar or string. `const TABLE = [10, 20, 30];` or `const A = compute();` was E0801 "must be a compile-time value; use `static const`", so there were two spellings for one idea: a name that cannot be rebound.

After: `const` is the only spelling. A module `const` that folds is still inlined. One that does not fold (an array, a call, another module's value) becomes the slot `static const` used to make: it is set once before `main`, it can be imported, and reassigning it is E0107. `static const` still compiles for this release, with an E0129 warning: "`static const` is deprecated / write `const X = …;` …; `coil fmt` rewrites it". `coil fmt` already writes it as `const`.

How:
- `const_fold::lift_startup_consts` runs right after parsing (`ast_cache`, in-memory `compile_src`, `parse_expand_check`). It folds the module's consts in order, using the same rule and env codegen uses, and turns each one that does not fold into `StaticDecl { is_const: true, lifted: true }`. Every later pass (checker, purity, HIR, codegen, GC static roots) then treats it exactly as a `static const`.
- `StaticDecl.lifted` tells a written `static const`, which gets the warning, from a lifted `const`.
- Purity: reading a lifted slot keeps a function pure, as a `static const` read did (`purity.rs` only counts `static let`). A unit test and an auto-par test cover it.
- E0801 stays as a fallback but no longer suggests `static const`.

Zero runtime cost: `coil dissect` gives identical bytecode for a program with `static const COMPUTED = four() + 2; static const TABLE = [10, 20, 30];` and the same program with `const`, at -O0 and -O2 (60 lines each).

Migrated: the tests in the design's P6 row (module_const_fold, static_const_read → const_startup_read, compile_fail static_const_reassign → const_startup_reassign, static_string_survives_gc, static_auto_par, overload_int_mul_after_float, instance_option_early_returns, local_shadows_static, static_init_expressions, imported_static_const_* → imported_const_*), `examples/src/{mod_state,static_then_branchy_fn}.hy`, `tests/hir_ffi_cli.rs`, and builtin keyword docs, the language skill and the internals docs. `compile_fail/module_const_not_folded.hy` is removed, because that program now compiles. Where a test checked a slot, its initializer now does not fold, so it still tests a slot.

Downstream already uses `const`: ardax-corp/coil-stdlib#44 and ardax-corp/coil-regex#15 (merged). No other repo writes `static const` in `.hy`.

Verification: `cargo test --release -p compiler --lib` (1390), `-p parser --lib`, pipeline `static_const_is_deprecated`, `coil test` for tests/{modules,codegen,functions,memory,syntax,traits}, corpora 21/21 (with the stdlib branch), `coil-fmt --check`, clippy on parser/compiler.

body:
Implements issue #1972 (archived as resolved): Iron/Jazzy matched and incompatible-type status events.

## ABI (header SSoT, append-only)
- `rmw_event_type_t` gains `NROS_RMW_EVENT_PUBLICATION_MATCHED` = 5, `_SUBSCRIPTION_MATCHED` = 6, `_PUBLISHER_INCOMPATIBLE_TYPE` = 7, `_SUBSCRIPTION_INCOMPATIBLE_TYPE` = 8. They are appended, not inserted at upstream's positions, because our enum was never value-compatible with upstream's.
- New payloads `rmw_matched_status_t {total_count, total_count_change, current_count, current_count_change}` and `rmw_incompatible_type_status_t`, with `uint32_t` counts. `rmw_event_payload_t` grows from 8 to 16 bytes. No new vtable slot.
- Bindings and C/C++ headers are regenerated.

## Producers
| Backend | Matched | Incompatible type |
|---|---|---|
| Cyclone | `dds_get_{publication,subscription}_matched_status`, polled through `*_take_event`. Changes are computed against the last report. | Builtin DCPS topics: same topic name, other type name. Not mapped to INCONSISTENT_TOPIC, because pinned 0.10.5 never raises it. |
| zenoh | `shim::matched`: graph-cache liveliness tokens of the opposite kind with the same name and type, like rmw_zenoh_cpp | Same walk, other type |
| XRCE, uORB | unsupported | unsupported |

`event_type_is_supported` (#1978) reports the four new kinds in the zenoh table, the Cyclone switch and the rust_adapter.

## Faces
- **Rust:** `EventKind` variants, `MatchedStatus`, `IncompatibleTypeStatus`, plus `MatchedCounter` / `IncompatibleTypeCounter` (no_std helpers that turn snapshots into reports). nros-node adds `on_matched` / `on_incompatible_type` on the publisher and both subscription handles.
- **C:** `rclc_{publisher,subscription}_set_{matched,incompatible_type}_callback`.
- **C++:** `rclcpp::MatchedInfo`, `IncompatibleTypeInfo`, `PublisherMatchedCallbackType`, `SubscriptionMatchedCallbackType`, `IncompatibleTypeCallbackType`, and `on_matched` / `on_incompatible_type` on `Publisher` and `PollSubscription`.

The C/C++ setters are wired all the way to the backend through a static `status_event_slots` table in nros-c (16 slots, generation-tagged, re-keyed when a C++ object is moved). The five Tier-1 C/C++ setters still return UNSUPPORTED; that is unchanged here.

Events are polled from each entity's data path. A publisher therefore sees a match on its next `publish` or `assert_liveliness` call.

## Ledgers
- rmw-api-map type-delta: the `type:` rows are now derived `same`; the enum and field rows are `re-mapped`.
- The five rclcpp `gap` rows are closed: they are `same` under Jazzy and Humble-scoped `divergence` under Humble.
- New items are added to the ledger, a feature-matrix row is added, and the support-status line is corrected (#1972/1974/1975/1978 are implemented).

## Tests
- Units in nros-rmw, nros-c slots and cffi `matched_event_poll`, plus a nros-node mock test.
- C/C++ declaration probes, run in `check c` and `check cpp`.
- Cyclone `matched_events` (matched count goes 0→1→0, then a second publisher type triggers incompatible-type) and an `event_type_is_supported` case.
- zenoh `matched_events_live`, against a peer running in a separate process (`just linux test-matched-events`).
- No interop cell against stock ros2.

The unsafe census grows, and that is intended; the commit message explains why.

Local gate: `just ci gate` passed on the final commit.

author: thesusort
body:
## Summary

Self-hosted visitor tracking in Supabase, replacing nothing (Hotjar was already removed in March). There is no third-party script, no cookies and no CSP change.

- **Browser:** one row per page view, recording:
  - the route pattern (`/ships/:shipId`, never the raw URL)
  - time the tab was visible, capped at 30 min
  - counts of clicks on elements labelled `data-track`
  - whether it was the entry page, the referrer host, the device class and the app version

  JS errors are recorded once per fingerprint per page load. Batches are sent with `fetch(..., { keepalive: true })` straight to an RPC, with no Netlify function involved.
- **Server:** `track_page_events` is a validating `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC. Invalid rows are dropped silently. Admin traffic is dropped server-side. Daily ceilings are 10k visit writes and 1k error writes. A nightly pg_cron rollup writes small daily tables and prunes raw rows after 7 days.
- **Admin Panel:** a new **Traffic** tab shows views, visitors, sessions, active time, a pages table with entry and exit rates, referrers, devices, clicks per page and top errors with sample stacks.
- **Profile:** a "Don't track my usage in this browser" opt-out that also works signed out, plus a docs section describing exactly what is recorded.

### Storage bounds (worst case under deliberate abuse ≈ 140 MB)

| What | Limit |
|---|---|
| Raw rows (`page_visits`, `client_errors`) | 7 days |
| Visit writes per day / error writes per day | 10,000 / 1,000 |
| Click labels per visit | ≤ 20, ids ≤ 40 chars |
| Error message / stack | 300 / 1000 chars, 600 / 2000 bytes |
| Rollups per day | top 200 pages, 1000 clicks, 100 referrers, 100 errors |
| Rollup retention | clicks and errors 90 days, others 400 days |

`serverLimits.test.ts` fails if the client limits and the SQL drift apart.

## Required after merge (you run these, before the next release)

1. Apply `supabase/migrations/20261020000001_page_tracking.sql`. It is written but not applied, and it relies on the existing `public.is_admin()` and `public.is_anonymous_session()`.
2. Schedule the rollup. Without it, raw rows are never pruned and past days are never rolled up:
   ```sql
   select cron.schedule('rollup-page-tracking', '15 3 * * *', $$select public.rollup_page_tracking()$$);
   ```
3. Optional check in the SQL editor:
   ```sql
   -- Valid visit, then a second snapshot of it: one row, active_ms 2000, clicks replaced.
   select public.track_page_events('[{"id":"11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111","visitor_id":"22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222","session_id":"33333333-3333-3333-3333-333333333333","path":"/gear","entered_at":"now","active_ms":1000,"clicks":{"autogear.run":2},"is_entry":true,"referrer_host":"www.reddit.com","device":"desktop","app_version":"1.81.0"}]', '[]');
   select public.track_page_events('[{"id":"11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111","visitor_id":"22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222","session_id":"33333333-3333-3333-3333-333333333333","path":"/gear","entered_at":"now","active_ms":2000,"clicks":{"autogear.run":3},"is_entry":true,"device":"desktop","app_version":"1.81.0"}]', '[]');
   select active_ms, clicks from public.page_visits where id = '11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111';
   -- Dropped silently: bad uuid, bad path, bad device.
   select public.track_page_events('[{"id":"x","path":"/gear"},{"id":"44444444-4444-4444-4444-444444444444","visitor_id":"22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222","session_id":"33333333-3333-3333-3333-333333333333","path":"<script>","device":"desktop","app_version":"1"},{"id":"55555555-5555-5555-5555-555555555555","visitor_id":"22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222","session_id":"33333333-3333-3333-3333-333333333333","path":"/ships","device":"phone","app_version":"1"}]', '[]');
   select count(*) from public.page_visits where id in ('44444444-4444-4444-4444-444444444444','55555555-5555-5555-5555-555555555555'); -- 0
   select public.rollup_page_tracking_day(current_date);
   select * from public.page_daily where day = current_date;
   -- Clean up.
   delete from public.page_visits where visitor_id = '22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222';
   select public.rollup_page_tracking_day(current_date);
   update public.tracking_ingest_counts set visits = 0 where day = current_date;
   ```

Until the migration is applied, the client fails silently (the RPC returns 404 and the error is swallowed) and the Traffic tab shows "could not be loaded".

## Notes

- **RLS:** every new table has RLS enabled, admin-only SELECT, and `REVOKE ALL` from anon and authenticated. There are deliberately no INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE policies, so writes go only through the definer functions.
- **Account link:** `page_visits.user_id` references `public.users` `ON DELETE SET NULL`, so deleting an account anonymises its visits. A partial index covers the FK action.
- **Click labels:** `data-track` was added to sidebar nav, import, autogear, both simulators, the save-loadout buttons, gear upgrade simulation and auth submit. The header "Sign in" is a `Dropdown.Item` that forwards no attributes, so it is not labelled.

## Test plan

- [x] Vitest: the full suite passes on every commit, and 85 new and affected tests pass in `src/services/pageTracking` and `trafficService`.
- [x] tsc and lint are clean.
- [x] Local run on :3021: the app renders with no console errors, the opt-out card shows signed out, the checkbox sets and clears `tracking_opt_out`, a visitor ID is created and no request is sent from localhost.
- [ ] After the migration is applied: run the SQL check above and open Admin Panel → Traffic.

author: artiz
body:
Closes #813

A `Figure N:` label printed above its figure never bound to the picture: the
picture arm of the caption pairing was geometric and only looked below the
figure, so the label stayed a loose `text` item and the picture had no caption
(DP-Bench 01030000000036/37 from the issue).

The three matchers (picture: below only; code: above only; table: reading-order
adjacency, #265) are replaced by one port of docling's
`ReadingOrderPredictor._find_to_captions` (`_rank_caption_candidates` +
`_match_caption`):

- a caption reaches the graphics (picture, table/document_index, code) in the
  unbroken run on either side of it in reading order, never across intervening
  text or the column gutter;
- candidates rank by the shortest box gap, equal gaps going to the preceding
  graphic;
- graphics are matched to captions by augmenting paths, a caption with a second
  choice yielding to one with none.

One deliberate deviation, recorded in `docs/PDF_CONFORMANCE.md`: a row of
side-by-side figures reads as a run of graphics followed by the run of their
captions, and upstream serves only the first caption. A caption still loose
whose only separation from a graphic run is other captions takes the nearest
unclaimed graphic it overlaps horizontally (the old geometric rule). A run
broken by text stays loose, as docling leaves it.

Conformance (docling-parse renderer, models): snapshots 94/98 exact before the
refresh, every drift intended; groundtruth 10/18 strict, 11/18
whitespace-normalized, 330 diff lines (2203.01017v2 19 → 17, 2206.01062
14 → 10, right_to_left_03 exact — its snapshot was stale since the bidi fix).
Four unit tests cover the issue's layout, gap ranking, displacement chains and
the side-by-side row.

## Summary

Admits `tool.ui_focus_kit_option` with the reviewed resource union `build_profiles`, `projects`, `source_docs` and `source-workspace`. This is the same union as `tool.ui_open_source`, because the handler uses the same plan and source lookups. Coverage moves from 27 reviewed / 416 unresolved to **28 reviewed / 415 unresolved** of 443.

Node stays the owner. Nothing calls the gate at runtime yet. `desktop_rebuild` behavior is unchanged.

## What the traces pin (`operation-resources.test.ts`)

- An integer-like `plan_id` reads tenant-owned `build_profiles` identity **before** input validation, so a missing `group_id`/`stl_filter` still reads that table.
- A nonblank `source_name` resolves through source summaries (`projects` and `source_docs` counts, plus not-found suggestions). It takes precedence over `source_id`, which is then forwarded without a lookup.
- An integer-like `source_id` reads only `projects` when not found, and adds the `source_docs` count when found.
- Trimming, labels, forwarded params, `plan_id` only when greater than 0, ID precedence, fallback after foreign IDs, tenant isolation, and database errors for each table.
- As a UI action it skips the dismissal lookup, so `plan_decisions` is never read.
- With the trusted policy there are zero filesystem calls. With the isolated policy the trace pins exact canonicalization/metadata probe sequences: workspace, missing, escape and root symlinks, root outside the workspace, and null. The STL filter is never opened.

## Rust (`pp-gateway`)

- New closed `ReviewedEntry::UiFocusKitOption` with the exact compiled union. It is added to the required-reviewed list.
- Partition counts are 28/415. Swap controls cover `ui_open_docs`↔`ui_focus_kit_option` and `ui_focus_stl_search`↔`ui_focus_kit_option`.
- `assert_workspace_tool_resources` covers Node ownership, the exact set, and incompatible SQLite/workspace rollback refusal. `assert_tool_invalid_admission` covers remove/duplicate/empty mutations, with refusal before effects.

Local, Node 22.23.3, VM 133.

- Main-fail/head-pass: with main's manifest, the trusted trace fails with `Missing kit option focus declaration`. It passes on this head.
- Mutation: adding an undeclared `ctx.repo.getSourceCategories()` call to the handler fails both new traces (`table:app_settings` observed). The handler was then restored.

The failure was `integrations/status-boundary.test.ts` hitting its 15 s timeout under full-suite load; it is unrelated and passed 3/3 when rerun alone. The remaining stages (workflow smoke, build, bundles, runtime, browser) exit 0.

Applying the proposal, the other 415 unresolved operations, and GRE-593 (full inventory, compatible rollback, cutover). GRE-402 stays In Progress.

body:
## Motivation

Captured Plain progress still emitted carriage returns/erase-line controls, and unconditional diagnostic styling polluted non-terminal stderr. Close that inherited carry while retaining terminal updates.

## What this changes

Non-terminal Plain uses complete throttled lines; terminal stderr keeps updating/flush behavior. Escape controls in retry causes. Gate the three shared diagnostic-style sites on stderr terminal capability. Document the bounded behavior without claiming CLI cutover, schema versioning or redaction.

## How it was tested

Original Plain renderer with new isolated child callback regression compiled and failed on actual CR/ANSI/raw remote controls. Corrected callbacks passed. The first real executable smoke caught remaining styled preamble labels; the final correction gates those labels too.

Actual compiled CLI transferred an exact4096-byte loopback payload to stdout in fresh empty cwd/TMPDIR. Exit0, byte-for-byte payload equality and equal SHA256; stderr C0-except-LF count0 and final newline. No remaining fixture artifacts. Captured evidence and a separate byte-scan receipt retained privately. Final exact prefix passed all44 default/S3/IPFS/all-feature tests/docs/strictClippy/fmt/sort/package gates over both actual dependency graphs. Independent bounded CLI/docs source and RED/GREEN receipt review GREEN. No TTY runtime exercise claimed; terminal branch was source-reviewed.

## Compatibility

Same human units, throttle and stderr destination. Payload stdout unchanged. TTY updating remains; captured logs intentionally become newline-delimited. Legacy expectation-after-publication behavior and non-versioned JSON schema remain unchanged. Escaping a cause is not secret redaction.

## Follow-ups

New CLI cutover, aggregate recovery/providers and final integrated six-role review remain separate approved work. Stacked on retry-JSON correction, not a release.

author: resident-x
body:
## Why

The layout practice catalogue's sensing item (keep precision sensing away from switching and drive nets) and the ground-return practice for connectors were left to a reviewer's eye. `REQ-ELECTRICAL-INSTALL-001.C8` needs sensing to hold its accuracy while the loads switch, and `OBL-VERIFICATION-DISCIPLINE-001.C9` needs each check shown failing on the defect it exists to catch. This adds two rules to the pre-order check, so a design that crowds a sensing net or short-changes a connector's ground returns fails before it is ordered, each rule proven on a seeded fault.

What it adds:

- A board rules record, `board-rules.yaml`, read the same way as the other records (nearest folder, synthetic marker in a proof design, undefined keys refused, silence fails, explicit `none` accepted).
- A **sensing-clearance rule**. A sensing and noisy class pair that does not involve `Mains` is written ahead of the signed Mains rule at the declared clearance. A pair that involves `Mains` is written after it, on a clearance constraint only, at the larger of the declared and signed figures, so it can only tighten. A pad or footprint clearance override below the sensing figure fails, since KiCad ranks overrides above every custom rule.
- A **ground-return rule**. Per connector, signal pins may not exceed `signal_pins_per_return` times its ground-return pins, compared exactly on whole pins, with the smallest ratio taken across several signal classes. A pin on a class declared none of ground, signal or non-signal fails.
- 15 seeded faults in the on-demand proof, the five proof designs' records, and the hardware notes and layout practice catalogue entries (new rule-kind item `SENSE-6`, with the method naming the record figure as a fifth rule form).

Two defects in the settled decision were found by the readiness pass and fixed in the graph before the build: the "larger of" figure for a Mains pair was written ahead of the signed rule, which wins when it matches last, so it would never have been enforced; and the ground-return ratio read the wrong way and named no keys. `DEC-BOARD-PRE-ORDER-RULE-READINGS` (v9 to v12) and `DEC-BOARD-SEPARATION-BASIS-RECORD` (v3 to v4) carry the corrected text, and the criteria C1, C2 and C5 follow it.

## Criteria resolved

- [x] C1: a sensing net closer to a switching or drive net than the declared clearance fails
- [x] C2: a connector with fewer ground returns than the declared ratio for its signals fails
- [x] C3: the rules extend the existing pre-order check and its record reader
- [x] C4: every failure names the rule, the design and the offending item
- [x] C5: each rule is shown to fail on a fault seeded for it in a copy of the throwaway proof design
- [x] C6: every tracked design passes the rules, which run in the build round for board changes and nightly on main
- [x] C7: the hardware notes carry an entry for each rule

The leaf is `finished` with 7 of 7 criteria covered. Evidence is 71 nodes, one per test function, because the accepted format is one `test_ref` per entry.

## Test evidence

- **Round gate (`task check:round`) passed** on `e875e6d` (exit 0, 79 minutes): host tier (`fw:build`, `fw:check`, `fw:test`, `fw:run`), emulation tier (`fw:emulate`) and board tier (`hw:verify`, `hw:test:round`). The mutation sweep was correctly skipped: none of the changed paths is a source the sweep draws mutants from.
- After that, three small commits changed pure-Python board tooling (a numberless-pad counting rule, an unconnected-net rule that now needs exactly one pad on the net, a doc link and its regression check). Fast tests pass on the merged head (`test_board_rules`, `test_board_check`, `test_board_voltage`: 554 tests). The two new regression tests were confirmed to fail on the old code. The PR's own gate re-verifies the final head in full.
- `main` moved while the branch was in review (the review fan-out solutions merged). The merge conflicted only in `hardware/README.md` (both sides added to the same two bullets, both kept) and the append-only events log (both sides kept).

## Review

- Brief review (WF-REVIEW, brief subject) confirmed the leaf. Output review (WF-REVIEW, run output) passed with change facts unavailable, so the diff was judged by reading it.
- Three cold-review rounds before submission found and fixed: a net class with an unreadable `track_width`, or defined only by a layout `net_class` block, fell into `Default` and escaped the undeclared-class guard (fixed structurally by resolving every class KiCad can resolve); and unnumbered connector pads each counted as a ground return (a pin is now a distinct pad number).
- The blind PR review found a broken README anchor for `SENSE-6` (fixed, with a check that pins the link to the heading), a guard that keyed on a net's name instead of whether anything else joins it (fixed in this rule: a pad is no pin only when its net carries no other pad), and asked that the pad-counting rules live in the decision (added) and a missing comment (added). A narrow re-check was clean.

## Notes

- The `ResourceWarning` lines in the board tier log (an unclosed file at `test_board_check_kicad.py:1532`) come from the earlier separation-floor commit `a27bdcf`, not this branch.
- The name-only `unconnected-(` convention is also used by three older rules (`board_check.py`: connectivity, the connectivity net list, and the generated-net filter). It is out of scope here and is raised with the operator as a maintenance candidate.

## Staged branches

### Already up to date with `main`

_Generated by `.github/scripts/merge-staging.sh`; the per-branch attempt log is in the job output._

## Pre-update triage

Held nixpkgs for a second week: the go-mockery Go 1.27 build breakage (PR `#565040`) is still open and no fix has landed in this week's 9 125-commit window. Held home-manager because PR `#10056` removes a large batch of deprecated option aliases across shell, terminal, and editor modules ahead of the 26.11 release; if any of those aliases are set in this flake the evaluation will fail. All other sources (catppuccin, dank-greeter, dankcalendar, danksearch, deploy-rs, dgop, dms, gaze, hermes-agent, nixpkgs-opencode, nixpkgs-stable, sops-nix, and the npin pins) show only features, fixes, dependency bumps, or CI changes with no evidence of breakage and are bumped.

**Not held after all:** home-manager -- the paragraph above was written before the check that drops a hold whose option or symbol nothing in this repo references, so these bump with everything else.

### Held at their current revision

| Input | Reason | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `nixpkgs` | nixpkgs head still fails to build go-mockery 3.8.0 under Go 1.27 (export data version 5 > 4) and typescript-language-server 6.0.2 hits a fixed-output hash mismatch; the tracked fix PR has not merged. | `NixOS/nixpkgs#565040` [open] — go-mockery Go 1.27 checkPhase failure and typescript-language-server pnpm derive hash mismatch |

### Held inputs

| Input | Held for | Since | Waiting on | Upstream |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `nixpkgs` | 2 weeks | 2026-10-13 | nixpkgs head still fails to build go-mockery 3.8.0 under Go 1.27 (export data version 5 > 4) and typescript… | `NixOS/nixpkgs#565040` (merged) |

#### What upstream recommends

- `nixpkgs`: Update the nixpkgs input to the revision that includes the merged PR `NixOS/nixpkgs#565040`, which fixes go-mockery under Go 1.27; the typescript-language-server hash mismatch cited in the hold reason is not addressed in this discussion. _(maintainer endorsed, as of 2026-10-20)_
  Maintainer t-monaghan (MEMBER) approved the PR, and it was merged on 2026-10-14. Maintainer 06kellyjac (MEMBER) initially requested the sesh: change be kept as a separate commit; the author consolidated to two commits and the request was subsequently dismissed. No competing suggestion appears in the thread. The only caveat is scope: this PR resolves the go-mockery / Go 1.27 export-data issue but does not touch the typescript-language-server fixed-output hash mismatch, so that part of the hold may still apply.


## What landed upstream

## Desktop

- **dms** (v1.6.3): lid-open fingerprint fix, refresh-rate reconciliation after resume, lock screen now appears on every display when none is selected, and touchpad scroll detection switched from `pixelDelta` to scroll-phase. Two behaviour changes to note: `fanout` is disabled, and the generated hyprland target no longer carries `Before=graphical-session.target` — if you relied on that ordering for a custom unit, add the ordering yourself.
- **dank-greeter**: now recognises `pam_gaze` in face-auth module detection (relevant if you use gaze at the greeter), honours `Hidden`/`NoDisplay` and XDG session precedence, and caps wallpaper decode to screen size. Breaking: `dms-hypr.conf` is removed and `dms-hypr.lua` command execution changed — check any custom greeter config that sourced the old file.
- **dankcalendar**: importing a `.ics` file now shows a conflict preview before committing; CalDAV `getlastmodified` dates that violate RFC 7808 are normalised instead of rejected; and `dcal.service` stops being restarted after repeated failures (systemd `StartLimitBurst` now applies).
- **danksearch**: the indexer exposes a `parents` field for the folder filter and an `info` method, so you can scope searches to a directory tree.
- **dgop**: `gops` now reports GPU usage, VRAM, power draw, and clock speeds; network interfaces with predictable names (e.g. `enp3s0`) are recognised correctly.
- **gaze**: falls back to RGB-only inference when no IR camera is present; new CLI subcommands `config get/set` and `doctor`; face auth is held across suspend/resume; `--no-pam` flag lets you install without touching PAM. PAM ordering is fixed so gaze runs before fprintd, and several hardening commits tighten daemon trust, template persistence, and model loading.

## AI

- **hermes-agent**: past the 300-commit noise cap, but the open PR "fix(nix): recognize externally provided runtime tools in PM health checks" is directly relevant if you run hermes under NixOS with externally-provided tools.
- **anthropic-skills**: the `claude-api` skill now lists Claude Haiku 5.5 as the current Haiku, adds Managed Agents and preserved-thinking fixes, and ships four workflow quickstarts with dynamic workflow support.
- **autoskills**: breaking — Deno support is dropped. New: an AI agent adjudicates flagged skills instead of requiring a human, and a `ui` command lets you browse installed skills interactively.
- **mattpocock-skills**: several skill behaviours changed: `chief-of-staff` keeps memory in a dated, commit-cited wiki; `diagnosing-bugs` now proves a forced mutation landed before trusting the red; `code-review` searches for standards files and foregrounds sub-agents; `grilling` rewords questions so "yes" accepts the recommendation.
- **nix-skills**: breaking — the plugin marketplace is renamed from `skills` to `nix-skills` and the stale `agent-skills-pack-` package prefix is dropped. Also fixes symlinked directories before resolving a `path:` flakeref.
- **odysseus**: past the noise cap; notable open PRs include generic OIDC single sign-on and project workspaces.

author: msgaihede
body:
Fixes #1169

## What
The card detail modal's quantity stepper read **one page of 200 rows** at the oracle grain (`collectionList({ oracleId, limit: 200 })`, and the same for `wishlistList`) and only then narrowed to the printing on the client. If a printing's rows came after row 200 (e.g. a basic-land collector with 200+ Island entries), the stepper showed 0 and + added a new row instead of stepping the existing one.

## Fix
Both stepper reads (collection and wishlist, which had the same bug) now page through with the export path's existing `sweep` (`features/transfer/export/scope.ts`). It reads 500 rows a page and stops on a short page, so almost every card still takes one round trip. The query now caches the row array directly; nothing else reads or writes those two keys.

I chose this over adding a `cardId` filter to Rust's `CardFilters`. That would have touched the shared search/collection/wishlist filter, the IPC mirror, the parity test and the fake DB, all for a `small` bug. Paging through was the issue's own second option.

## Tests
- New regression test: a full first page of other printings, then the printing's row on page two. The stepper steps row 42 (`collectionSetQuantity(42, 3)`), and `collectionAdd` is never called.
- Updated the two existing assertions from `limit: 200` to `SWEEP_PAGE`.
- `vitest` on `features/card` + `features/transfer` (1292 tests) passed, `pnpm lint` passed, `tsc -p packages/ui` is clean. No Rust changes.

author: seaavey
body:
## Summary

Adds the missing half of the SaaS shape: a **customer account** the operator creates, a
one-time **login token** handed to the customer, and a read-only **console** where the
customer sees only their own account, keys, and request logs.

```text
server/src/
├── features/users/
│   ├── model.rs      # User, token minting (sr-user- + 32 hex), id (usr_ + 24 hex)
│   ├── routes.rs     # /v1/users CRUD + POST /v1/users/{id}/token  (admin session)
│   └── portal.rs     # /v1/portal/login | me | logs | logout      (user session)
├── http/middleware/session_guard.rs   # renamed from admin_session.rs
│   ├── require_admin_session  -> SessionScope::Admin
│   └── require_user_session   -> SessionScope::User(user_id)
└── infrastructure/database/users.rs   # users + token_hash lookups

server/migrations/0005_users.sql  # users table, api_keys.user_id, admin_sessions -> auth_sessions

client/src/
├── routes/portal.tsx + components/portal/   # the customer console
├── routes/_authenticated/users.tsx + components/users/  # the operator's Users tab
└── routes/login.tsx                          # Password | Access-token mode
```

The credential split is the whole point:

| Credential | Prefix | Opens | Mounted on |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gateway API key | `sr-live-…` | `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/messages`, … | `api_key_auth` |
| Customer access token | `sr-user-…` | `/v1/portal/*` | `require_user_session` |
| Admin password | — | `/v1/users`, `/v1/keys`, `/v1/logs`, `/v1/quota`, `/v1/providers` | `require_admin_session` |

An API key is deliberately **not** a console credential (spec D1): rotating a leaked key
would sign the customer out, and one account with two keys would need two logins.

### Guard moves (owner-ruled 2026-10-20, D5a/D5b)

These read surfaces leaked installation-wide data to *any* valid key. They now require
the admin session, and the `Node parity` comments claiming otherwise were rewritten:

```diff
- create_providers_read_router().layer(api_key_auth)
+ create_providers_read_router().layer(require_admin_session)
- create_logs_router().layer(api_key_auth)
+ create_logs_router().layer(require_admin_session)
- create_quota_router().layer(api_key_auth)
+ create_quota_router().layer(require_admin_session)
```

`/v1/models*` and `/v1/settings` keep the API-key guard — they are per-key data, not
tenant data.

## Evidence

Full suite, server at the merge base of this branch:

```console
$ cd server && cargo test --locked
964 passed; 0 failed          # 48 test binaries
$ cargo fmt -- --check                          # FMT_EXIT=0
$ cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # CLIPPY_EXIT=0
$ cargo run --locked --bin export_ts && git diff --exit-code -- server/bindings.ts client/src/generated/typed.ts
BINDINGS_DRIFT_EXIT=0
```

New behaviour, exercised on the real path (a disposable SQLite file, a real listener,
real cookies — not mocks):

```console
$ POST /v1/admin/login {"password":"…"}                      -> 200, session cookie
$ POST /v1/users {"name":"Acme"}
201 {"id":"usr_c3d3cea4…","token_prefix":"sr-user-","token":"sr-user-bf4d9ac6…"}
$ POST /v1/keys {"name":"acme-key","user_id":"usr_c3d3cea4…"}
201 {"key_prefix":"sr-live-","user_id":"usr_c3d3cea4…","key":"sr-live-d9b3908d6…"}

$ POST /v1/portal/login {"token":"sr-user-bf4d9ac6…"}        -> 200, session cookie
$ GET  /v1/portal/me
200 {"user":{…},"keys":[{"id":"key_47fa247d…","user_id":"usr_c3d3cea4…"}]}
$ GET  /v1/portal/logs?page=1&limit=10
200 {"object":"list","data":[],"pagination":{"page":1,"limit":10,"total":0,"total_pages":0}}

# a customer key can no longer read installation-wide logs
$ GET /v1/logs -H "x-api-key: sr-live-d9b3908d6…"
401 {"code":"authentication_required"}

# the console session ends with the account
$ POST /v1/portal/logout                                      -> 204, cookie cleared
$ GET  /v1/portal/me                                          -> 401

# disabling the customer stops both surfaces at once, no restart
$ PATCH /v1/users/usr_c3d3cea4… {"enabled":false}             -> 200
$ GET  /v1/portal/me                                          -> 401
$ POST /v1/chat/completions -H "x-api-key: sr-live-d9b3908d6…"
401 {"code":"api_key_disabled"}
```

**Before:** `/v1/logs`, `/v1/quota`, and `GET /v1/providers` answered `200` to any valid
`sr-live-…` key, including one owned by a customer — installation-wide rows, other
tenants' data.

**After:** the same key answers `401 authentication_required`; the customer sees only
their own rows.

Migration is forward-only and refuses nothing that used to work: schema v4 → v5 adds the
`users` table, `api_keys.user_id`, and renames `admin_sessions` to `auth_sessions`.
`admin_sessions.user_id IS NULL` keeps meaning "operator session", so every existing
admin cookie keeps working. A pre-v5 export still imports — the transfer validates the
schema *after* migrating, not before.

`server/tests/users.rs` (17 new tests) pins the contracts, including the six conditions
this feature can break: a customer key cannot read installation logs, a pre-v5 export
still imports, disabling a customer stops both surfaces, an unowned key stays invisible
to every portal, a keyless customer sees empty states, and `/v1/portal/logs` counts the
tenant rather than the table.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** one-way.

Schema v5 is a forward migration (`PRAGMA user_version` 4 → 5) and the old
`admin_sessions` table is renamed, not copied. Rolling the binary back to a pre-v5
build will not start: it refuses a newer `user_version`. Recovery is a database restore,
not a redeploy. Merge with a database backup in hand.

**Blast Radius:** authentication.

The guard move is the widest part. Any client that read `/v1/logs`, `/v1/quota`, or
`GET /v1/providers` with an API key now gets `401`. That is the intent, and it is
breaking for anyone who relied on it — the operator's own tooling included. The
migration is also one-way in the sense that a customer token and an API key are
different credentials now: scripts that signed in to the console with a key need the
`sr-user-…` token the operator hands over.

Not verified here: `bun run typecheck` and `bun run build` (the owner runs both — the
machine rule is not to run them), and the client-side walkthrough of `/login` token
mode, `/portal`, and `/users` is owner-verified rather than machine-verified.

body:
Shiviti 2 only. Per Yosef, each Ana BeKoach block is now a square: every row is set to the same width by drawing out one or two letters, as a scribe fills a line, and the rows are spaced so the block is as tall as it is wide.

- **Width:** 1.12 × the widest row's natural width (`ana_square_pad`).
- **Which letters:** the traditional dilatable letters present in the row first (tav, he, lamed; alef has no straight stroke in Stam Sefarad and final mem too short a one), otherwise dalet, resh or chet. Up to two per row; the extra width is shared between them. Per row: אבג יתץ tav · קרע שטן resh · נגד יכש dalet · בטר צתג resh and tav · חקב טנע chet · יגל פזק lamed · שקו צית tav · בשכמל"ו lamed.
- **How:** the same three-slice method as the Name's he. Each letter's plain horizontal stroke was measured from the font (`STRETCHABLE`); only that slice is widened, so legs and tagin keep their shape. The method is now one helper, `stretched()`, shared by both; the Name area renders pixel-identical to before.

Checked: all four Shiviti 2 formats compile with no errors; on the poster each block measures about 143 × 140–145 px at 100 dpi. Shiviti 1 and the books are unchanged.

author: ekvargas
body:
## Summary
Closes F3c review follow-ups 3-8. One user-visible fix (the demo banner on `/app/nutrition/`), stronger e2e coverage, and spec wording brought in line with what the code does.

## Changes
- **3. Trailing slash (verified before fixing).** `/app/nutrition/` returns 200 with no redirect (`skipTrailingSlashRedirect: true`) and renders the live panel. The server resolves `/nutrition`, but the client `usePathname()` keeps the slash, so `AppShell`'s exact `liveRoutes` match missed. Result: the DEMO / MOCK DATA banner appeared over the live panel after hydration, and the server and client HTML disagreed. `AppShell` now strips trailing slashes once, which also fixes the same exact match for `/kiosk`. Production nginx (`location ^~ /app/`) passes the slash through, so this applies in production too.
- **4. `UNEXPECTED` log label.** Kept, not mapped. It flags an envelope the adapter contract never produces, and mapping it to `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` would hide that. The plan and unit tests already list it; the spec's vocabulary now does too.
- **5. Person ID echo.** In a document for `?person=PSN-00999`, the raw value appears 4 times: three from Next itself (canonical URL `c`, query `q`, page segment key) and once from the Suspense key. Changing the key would not make the invariant true, so the spec invariant now describes the echo.
- **6. Mint 401.** New e2e test: the panel asks to sign in, one mint, zero Nutrition calls.
- **7. Reverse staleness race.** One spec paragraph: server says current, client says stale, so there is one extra, unseen read and then one read for self.
- **8. Vacuous secret scan.** Every RSC response body read in Chromium fails (`Network.getResponseBody: No data found`), and `.catch(() => '')` hid it. So the retry and Back scans never covered the payloads they exercise. RSC fetches are now read through `page.route` and passed on unchanged; documents still stream. Each scan must find at least one body, and the retry and Back scans must find their own payload (`rscContaining`).

## Testing
Gates in the spec's order, all on this branch:
- `npm test` 147/147; `npm run lint` clean; `npm run build` (LIVE env) OK; `npm run test:startup-config` OK
- `npm run test:e2e` **44/44**. The new trailing-slash test failed before the `AppShell` change (banner count 1, expected 0) and passes after it.
- `npm run test:server-boundary` (run last) OK; `python -m pytest deploy/home-hub/tests -q` 8/8
- The capture tests (PRESENT, retry, Back) passed 9/9 with `--repeat-each=3`. A temporary log confirmed that the retry scan holds the refresh payload and the Back scan holds the subject-switch payload.

## Deployment
Item 3 changes `AppShell.tsx`, which is in the Hub image. Merging does not change production. The banner fix goes live only with the next Hub image rollout (operator-run Quadlet `Image=` change, as for R4).

## Not changed
`Sidebar` and `BottomNav` also compare `usePathname()` and may lose the active-link highlight on a trailing-slash URL. That is cosmetic and outside these follow-ups.

## Related
Follow-ups 1-2 are in #108.

body:
Roadmap phase 4 (`docs/roadmap.md`).

## What it adds

- **`shot -Baseline <folder>`**: compares each new screenshot with the earlier one of the same name. The comparison runs inside Godot at quarter resolution. Each shot gets `compare` (`changedPercent`, `sizeChanged`, `image`), and `<name>.compare.png` shows before, after and the changes in red. If `-Baseline` is the same folder as `-Output`, the run is refused with `invalid-arguments`.
- **`juice` runner**, detected when the project has a `juice.json`:
  - It plays the game headless at a fixed 60 fps for `frames` frames, with the bot's `args`.
  - It reads the game's `[juice] event <name> <ms>` and `[juice] feedback <name> <ms>` lines.
  - Each rule fails when an event had no listed feedback within `withinMs`, or when the event never happened.
  - Events too close to the end of the run to be answered are ignored.
- **`templates/STYLE.md`**: a style guide (palette, type, readability, motion, a log of choices) with a machine-readable `Resolutions:` line. `status -Json` now reports `look` (`styleGuide`, `resolutions`, `juiceRules`).
- **Skills:**

For a visual change it offers before and after as a multiple-choice question (keep before / take after / named tweak), with the comparison image, and records your choice under "Choices".
  - `godot-juice`: a feedback checklist (response under 100 ms, a sound on every action, hit-stop, shake, squash and stretch, flash, particles, telegraphs) with Godot 4 C# notes, and how to log events so the runner can check them.

author: adambelton
body:
Record canonical watched relationships through LibraryFilm STI, with one relationship per user and film. `Library::RecordWatched.call(user_id:, film_id:)` resolves an active user under its row lock and looks up the film inside the transaction. It creates an initial watched entry or converts a to-watch entry while preserving its ID, owner, film and creation time.

Models declare can_watch? (false by default, true for LibraryFilmToWatch); the service owns destination knowledge and STI mechanics. If permission is false, it raises Library::AlreadyWatched. Repeated or concurrent requests after success are failures without row changes, not idempotent successes. No model record_watched methods remain. Persistence errors propagate and roll back; retries after failed writes remain possible. Future system consumers must explicitly define duplicate handling without hiding unrelated errors.

Root construction is prohibited without enumerating subclasses. Type allowlists, redundant watched_at and speculative state-read projections are removed. The scoped user foreign-key cascade works with unchanged Identity cleanup/registration. No Film lock, Identity/Film implementation changes, watchlist UI, dismissal or reverse transitions. User transition refactoring is deferred.

Validation: 21 focused tests/102 assertions; full CI 219 tests/2,533 assertions, zero failures/errors/skips. RuboCop 121 files clean; dependency audits clean; Brakeman zero warnings/errors; application eager loading and whitespace checks pass. Real PostgreSQL lock waits verify transition/claim/cleanup races; rollback and failed-save retry are covered. The initial unmerged migration directly creates the final schema; redundant follow-up migrations are removed. Recreated the Library table from that migration in the test database only.

Ready for owner review. PR updates are authorized; acceptance and merge remain pending. Includes role/action/transition/testing conventions and the verified task 009 merge record.

author: turtiesocks
body:
## What this changes

- `[dog.deploy.release]` in the operator's `Flockfile.override.toml` names a command and its own `env`. It runs once per deploy, after the build and its artifacts and before `current` is swapped. A migration no longer has to end the build command.
- A non-zero exit, a signal or a timeout stops the deploy as a failed build does: `current` does not move, the old release serves, the sha is held in `state.failed`, and `shep deploy <sheep>` retries it.
- A committed `Flockfile.toml`, or an override the dog did not link in from the operator's checkout, that carries `[dog.deploy.release]` or `[dog.deploy.after]` is refused with `Error::Config` naming the file and the table. `after` has no reader yet; it is refused now so #37 needs no second change.
- The hook runs in the release as `app.user` through the build's group runner (`sh -c`, process-group holder, `build_timeout`, group kill). Environment is `BASE_ENV`, `passthrough`, the hook's `env`, then `SHEP_DEPLOY_SHEEP`, `SHEP_DEPLOY_SHA` and `SHEP_DEPLOY_RELEASE` last so the hook cannot override them.
- One stderr line, `shep-deploy: <sheep>: running the release hook`, precedes the run.
- A root dog with an app that has no build command still hands the release to `user` before the hook runs.
- `setup` parses the hooks and runs none.
- README says a rollback does not undo a migration and that a retried sha runs the hook again, so the command must be idempotent.

## Precise details

```
crates touched: shep-deploy
public API change: none (binary crate)
new or changed surface: Flockfile table `[dog.deploy.release]` (keys `command`, `env`); `[dog.deploy.after]` refused; `Error::Hook { name, ending }` exits 1; env vars SHEP_DEPLOY_SHEEP, SHEP_DEPLOY_SHA, SHEP_DEPLOY_RELEASE; `build_timeout` doc now says it bounds a hook (published schema description text only, no key change)
docs updated: README.md (hooks section, deploy steps, security list, hand-over text, build_timeout), CLAUDE.md (refused-fields gotcha), config.rs field docs
```

Decisions made without the maintainer:

- `build::runner::run_in_group` is the shared runner (no `run_command` exists). It returns `Error::Build` and `Error::BuildTimedOut`, which `hook::run` maps to `Error::Hook`.
- `root_warning` takes a `Step`. The build's text is unchanged and pinned by a new test. The hook has its own text, since its command comes from the operator.
- A root dog hands the release and the build cache to `user` before the hook when no build command ran, so a hook in an app with no build can write in its release. The hook always pins the `.git` pointer and writes it back afterwards, with or without a build, since the hook owns the directory and runs code the build put there. `build::drop_to` and `build::settle_pointer` hold that step for both the build and the hook. After a build the hook skips the hand-over but still pins. The hand-over itself needs root and is covered by `ownership`'s own tests; a new hook test covers both paths as the dog's own user, where the pin is a no-op.
- `hook::run` takes a `Context` struct instead of eight arguments.
- `deploy::tests::hooks` lives in `src/deploy/tests/hooks.rs`.
- IR-48: `src/deploy/mod.rs` grew from 780 to 796 lines and `src/hook.rs` is about 550 with its tests. No split was weighed worth it for either.
- `HookSpec` has a redacted `Debug` (IR-41) with an exact-string test.

Gaps:

- The integration tier did not run here. `shep start` fails in this sandbox with `daemon_unreachable: the daemon process exited before it started answering`, before the dog is reached. CI covers it.
- Only the unit tests for the touched modules ran locally. CI runs the rest.

## Before you ask for review

- [x] Every commit subject is a conventional one, `type(scope): summary`.
- [x] Nothing breaks a caller.
- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [ ] `cargo test --all-features` (CI runs it; integration tier not run locally, see Gaps)
- [x] `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --all-features`
- [x] No `web/` directory in this repo.
- [x] I can explain every line of this.

author: xgboosted
body:
API-uniformity item F2 (table "which flags read 0 and which NaN before they can know" in rmarcink's `test/api-consistency-map`). The maintainer decision: NaN until known.

## Problem

These flags returned int (`int8` for `cpr`), which can't hold NaN. So on bars where the comparison has no data (the warm-up, a missing bar, all-NaN input) they read 0, a definite "not increasing" or "no sweep":

| indicator | column(s) | made-up 0s on SPY_D |
|---|---|---|
| `increasing`, `decreasing` | `INC_1`, `DEC_1` | 1 bar each |
| `cpr` | `CPR_WIDTH_CLASS`, `CPR_POSITION` | 1 bar each (the documented exception) |
| `long_run`, `short_run` | `LR_2`, `SR_2` | 2 |
| `aobv` | `AOBV_LR_2`, `AOBV_SR_2` | 13 |
| `smc_sweep` | `SMC_SWEEP_15_1.5` | 15 |
| `amat` | `AMATe_LR_8_21_2`, `AMATe_SR_8_21_2` | 22 |

`squeeze`, `thermo`, `supertrend` and `qqe` already read NaN there.

## Fix

Each flag is float64 and reads NaN where its compared bars, swing window or CPR levels don't exist: `increasing`/`decreasing` track a `known` mask next to the comparison, `long_run`/`short_run` combine boolean `increasing`/`decreasing` and mask by both averages' diffs, `smc_sweep` masks by its swing window and the bar's own prices, and `cpr`'s helpers return float64 masked by the width or levels. `amat` and `aobv` inherit the change from `long_run`/`short_run`. `increasing(asint=False)`/`decreasing(asint=False)` still return booleans.

**BREAKING:** dtype int → float64, and those bars read NaN instead of 0. `flag.astype(bool)` turns NaN into True, which the CHANGELOG notes; use `flag == 1` or `fillna(0)`.

## Checks

- A bar-by-bar comparison of every registered indicator, main vs branch: only the bars counted above change (0 → NaN), plus the dtype. No other value differs. `squeeze(detailed=True)`, which uses `increasing()`, is unchanged.
- Strict xfails that now pass, so their exemptions are removed: `increasing`, `decreasing` and `smc_sweep` from `PUBLISHES_AT_THE_GAP` (interior NaN), and `amat`, `cpr`, `increasing`, `decreasing` and `smc_sweep` from the NaN-run and all-NaN exceptions. The `cpr` warm-up exception in `test_warmup_contract.py` and `docs/indicators.rst` is gone.
- `tests/fixtures/expected_values.json`: `non_nan_count` for the changed columns.
- Full suite: 16846 passed, 0 failed (zip-import test deselected locally). `black --check --diff pandas_ta_classic/`, `ruff check .`, `make typecheck`: clean; `cd docs && make html SPHINXOPTS="-W"`: exit 0.

author: moritzbrantner
body:
Long-running matches currently recover by replaying their entire history. Adds an opt-in canonical baseline so MMORPG #40 can restore an immutable checkpoint and replay only its post-checkpoint journal through the existing interpreter.

- `restore_checkpoint` defaults to rejection; `checkpoint_replay` captures state/session watermarks and starts a new replay suffix without I/O.
- Preserves retired identity ceilings, both command-lane clocks, trusted inputs and reconnect fencing; rejects malformed/repeated baselines and mismatched restores.
- Replay v5 is used only for baselines. Existing logs retain v1–4 bytes; client wire and outer recovery-image versions stay unchanged. Exhaustive `ReplayRecord` consumers must handle `Baseline`.
- Capture proves no durability: consumers retain prior durable recovery evidence until their new checkpoint/reference commits.

Validation: `coding-tooling run --tier fast --strict --json` passed (format, Clippy, all-target/all-feature tests). Production storage/publication integration remains MMORPG #40.

## Description

Running `dotnet new blazorwasm --help` displays the following malformed default for `--aad-b2c-instance`:

`https:////aadB2CInstance.b2clogin.com/`

The expected default is:

`https://aadB2CInstance.b2clogin.com/`

### Root cause

The `AAdB2CInstance` template parameter defines a four-slash `replaces` marker but does not define an explicit `defaultValue`. Consequently, the template engine exposes the replacement marker as the parameter's default in CLI help.

The marker matches the placeholder in the template's source configuration. Changing it directly would break that correspondence.

### Solution

Add an explicit `defaultValue` of `https://aadB2CInstance.b2clogin.com/`, following the existing pattern used by the adjacent `AADInstance` parameter.

Keep the four-slash `replaces` marker and source placeholder unchanged so template substitution continues to work.

### Test coverage

Add an integration regression test that uses the existing template-package installer and runs `dotnet new blazorwasm --help` against locally built templates in an isolated hive. The test verifies:

- The command exits successfully.
- The displayed default contains the correctly formatted B2C URL.
- The malformed four-slash URL is absent.
- Whitespace and terminal line wrapping between `Default:` and the URL
  do not cause a false failure.

Fixes #44894

author: spossann
body:
The PR docs preview (`build-and-deploy-preview` in `.github/workflows/docs-preview.yml`) is meant for inspecting the rendered docs, so it doesn't need to compile Struphy or run the notebooks. Skipping both makes the build much faster.

## Changes
- Removed the `Compile Struphy` step. `doc/conf.py` sets `nbsphinx_execute = "never"` when Struphy is not compiled, so the notebooks are no longer executed.
- New step `Disable per-notebook execution`: per-notebook `"nbsphinx": {"execute": ...}` metadata overrides the global setting. `tutorial_scope_profiling.ipynb` has `"execute": "always"` and runs a Poisson simulation, which would fail without compiled kernels. The step removes this metadata from `tutorials/*.ipynb` in the CI checkout only. The committed notebook is unchanged.
- Quickstart (`doc/sections/quickstart.rst`): added the missing figure of the 2D plot in step 8 (`doc/pics/quickstart_poisson_phi_2d.png`, generated with the quickstart script) and the matching `plt.savefig` in the snippet and full script.

## Notes
- Autodoc works without compiled kernels: kernel modules import as plain Python, and nothing checks for compiled kernels at import.
- Notebooks are stored without outputs (nbstripout), so the tutorial pages in the preview show code cells only.
- The main docs build (`docs.yml`) is unchanged: it still compiles and runs the notebooks.
- Running any `struphy` command before `make html` (even `struphy -h`) would write `state.yml`, and `conf.py` would then turn notebook execution back on. Nothing in the preview workflow does that.

author: abhishek-pandey7
body:
Adds `apps/worker`, which runs the whole app on Cloudflare's free plan: the web build as static assets, the API on Hono over `packages/core`, and market data precomputed by a cron trigger into Postgres (Neon via Hyperdrive). Design and trade-offs: `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 4.9. Steps: `docs/DEPLOY.md`.

**Market data without the Go gateway** (containers need the paid plan)
- Analytics, universes, AMFI parsing and screening ported from Go, with the Go tests ported alongside.
- Requests read `symbol_data` / `fund_data`; only missing instruments load inline, capped per request.
- One cron trigger every minute runs the most urgent job: SIPs, quotes, stock stats (4/run), AMFI catalogue (256 KB/run, ETag-pinned), fund stats (5/run). Batch sizes come from measured CPU (~1.6 ms per symbol, ~1.1 ms per fund) against the 10 ms limit.
- Instrument-specific failures are stored and backed off for 6 h; provider outages back the job off for 5 min.

**Verified locally under workerd (`wrangler dev`)**
- Every route returns the same shapes as the Nest API; the portfolio total matched to the paisa.
- All 141 curated symbols and 381 catalogue funds loaded, 0 failures. The one zero-NAV segregated fund is recorded as unavailable.
- Side by side with the Go gateway, every return, volatility and drawdown matched exactly for India large caps, US large caps and flexi-cap funds. An earlier spark-based version was up to 7 pp/yr off on high-dividend stocks (spark closes aren't dividend-adjusted), so spark is now only used for quotes.
- Bundle: 275 KB gzipped (limit 3 MB).

**Security**: Cloudflare Access in front; the Worker also verifies the Access JWT and email and fails closed. DB credentials only in Hyperdrive. Hyperdrive caching disabled so reads never lag writes.

Also in core: SIP catch-up skips dates already recorded, so a catch-up with nothing new is one query, not an mfapi call per SIP.

Tests: core 24, shared 54, api 17, worker 33 (incl. Postgres integration tests with faked upstreams).

author: craigbalding
body:
Scheduled CI and Native input jobs can now download matching production executables before compilation. The existing retained-artifact selector checks the exact source, architecture, compiler, profile, default features, build flags and output kind. Missing, expired, legacy or incompatible inputs keep the current-source build path. Invalid receipts, damaged bytes and API failures stop the caller.

Reference: #908, especially [the measured duplicate builds](https://github.com/craigbalding/safeyolo/issues/908#issuecomment-6287821046). This is a bounded CI increment. Parent acceptance remains 1/4, with the seven legacy Mattermost failures deferred.

The changes have these concrete reasons:

- Raw uploads lacked compiler and flag identity. `native-input.json` records the existing build settings, file checksums and original Actions producer. Downloads use the selector's existing fixed-name ZIP and digest checks. Reuse preserves the receipt bytes.
- Guest uploads name both executables, their version/checksum sidecars and the receipt explicitly. Cargo also leaves `safeyolo-guest.d` beside its binary; upload globs included that file and broke the selector's fixed-name check. The selector recognizes the known legacy shape without a receipt, including that depfile, as input that needs current-source compilation. Digest verification still runs first, and arbitrary extra paths still fail.
- CI tests require a successful default-branch scheduled/manual build job. Native package retention also requires successful whole runs for both the selected upload and its original producer. A failed CI run cannot become release-qualified input through reuse. There is no older-source or older-green fallback.
- Cross-run reads need `actions: read`. That permission is added only to the reusable input workflow and its two calling jobs. Linux host restoration follows guest compilation because the guest build also writes the host Coord binary. Native's distinct ARM64 host output is still built when missing and now has a reusable raw upload.
- Independent schedule admission, source-binding checks, guest-terminal tests, all consumer tests, Rust release test compilation, debug release generation, complete Native package assembly and publication/installed qualification remain in place. Compilation still uses one job and a 10 GiB reserve. No dependency was added.

Validation for `9307f3b98c60b0999216cc078a2f46d109d50fc9`:

```sh
uv run --frozen --no-sync pytest -q tests/test_ci_input_reuse.py --basetemp=/home/agent/pytest-908-depfile-fixed
```

74 passed in 51.00 seconds. Archive members come from the actual producer YAML paths while a Cargo depfile is present. The old producer patterns independently construct the known seven-member legacy ZIP. Fresh receipt-bearing reuse, legacy fallback, damaged ZIP refusal and arbitrary extra-path refusal pass. The two regression cases failed before the correction.

The probe uses the real selector, GitHub CLI command boundary, ZIP bytes and receipts with a controlled API. It runs the workflow's explicit Actions Bash commands and the build comparisons with the implicit success condition. Matching inputs skip compilation. Missing and incompatible inputs admit compilation. Corrupt input and API errors stop the caller. Both caller qualification modes, original-producer attribution and the Mac selection command are covered. The Mac command runs in the Linux fixture; this is not an actual Mac or hosted result.

```sh
uv run --frozen --no-sync pytest -q tests/test_retained_blackbox_inputs.py tests/test_workflow_action_pins.py cli/tests/test_host_setup_scripts.py::test_safeyolo_acceptance_graph_tool_hashes_match_sources --basetemp=/home/agent/pytest-908-depfile-consumers
```

49 passed, 1 skipped in 13.46 seconds. Configured Ruff, focused complexity checks, local Python Semgrep and commit/push hooks pass. Local Semgrep reports zero findings/errors on the changed selector. The CodeQL hook reports its supported Linux ARM64 skip; hosted checks for this head remain unverified. No product or image build was run.

Hosted saving remains unverified. With eligible inputs, the shared producer can omit the measured AMD64 guest (4m15s), AMD64 host (1m19s), ARM64 guest (5m35s) and Mac host (8m48s) compile steps. The diagnosed CI run failed overall, so its outputs do not qualify for Native package reuse. This PR claims none of that observed 19m57s as saved. Extra ARM64 host production, terminal/helper work, package assembly and Rust test compilation remain necessary when their own outputs are missing.

Relay/Sylab's next operation is to inspect the next appropriate same-source scheduled consumer after these receipts exist. Record the selected artifact and original producer, download/verification, unchanged consumer tests and skipped duplicate compile steps using ordinary job timestamps. CI test-only reuse can use a successful producer job despite a later whole-run test failure; Native package reuse needs whole-run success. If no eligible same-source output exists, retain normal production. No badge rerun or seed build is requested. Source acceptance, integration and natural recovery remain separate.

author: paudley
body:
Guard outputs previously became available only after the complete positive join, so a computed key could not constrain a later atom. `DlClause::with_ordered_body` now accepts `clause::BodyLiteral::{Atom, Guard}` and evaluates guards between movable positive segments. This supports the `at`, `pstep`, computed `pl` key and `pub` example without an intermediate relation.

Closes #643.

- Require guard inputs to be bound at their authored position and outputs to be fresh. Keep `with_guards` as the existing all-guards-at-the-end operation. Negated conjunctions remain attached separately.
- Keep SIPS and cycle certification within guard barriers. Binary, recursive and cyclic probes consume guard-produced bindings through the existing join kernels. Preserve original logical scan ordinals and authored positive provenance.
- Treat a computed key absent from the frozen dictionary as an absent binding for probes, rather than a free variable. Preserve early guard failures before empty later atoms while skipping unrelated-delta rounds.
- Admit the empty conjunction's unit binding before a guard-first callback. A zero-credit evaluation refuses before opaque code runs, including callbacks returning no rows.
- Encode early guard positions in version 3 clause identities. End-only guards retain their existing clause and reasoning-contract identities. Planner version 6 invalidates earlier physical plans; its frozen identity is pinned. Document the v4.0 API and identity changes and regenerate the hash-domain registry.

Validation:

- All 384 Datalog library tests, 26 public runtime cases, two structured-error cases and the allocation control pass locally. The new controls verify guard-produced predicate and graph keys, competing wrong-key rows, original provenance, absent fresh terms and zero/one-credit callback admission. Strict all-target Clippy passes.

author: rebelchris
body:
## Summary

Part 3 of 3 for the feed widget rail, on top of #6955 (the rail and its menu path) and #6963 (foundation), both merged. Split out of #6955 at review, so the editing layer can be reviewed and reverted on its own. Behind the same `feed_widgets` flag.

This PR replaces #6955's small `useRailEditMode` (deleted here) with `useRailEditing`:

- **Drag to reorder**: a short hold first on touch, so a swipe still scrolls. Swaps happen on the dragged widget's center, only toward the pointer's heading, with a settle window and a reversal distance, so neighbours don't flip back and forth. Auto-scrolls near the ends. Esc mid-drag restores.
- **Corner resize as a preview**: an outline follows the pointer, and a snapped footprint labelled with the size shows what letting go gives. Applied once on release, 16px of hysteresis at each boundary. Esc or a canceled gesture drops it.
- **Keyboard sorting**: Space lifts, the arrows move the preview, Space writes once, Esc drops it. The label reads the live position.
- **Touch**: widgets are `touch-pan-x`, so the rail still swipes in edit mode. A non-passive `touchmove` blocks scrolling only while a drag is live. A long press enters edit mode, with no callout.
- **Reflow**: FLIP measured on layout offsets (`offsetLeft/Top`), run only when order or size changes.

Every drag, resize or keyboard move works on a local draft and writes the settings once.

### Why not dnd-kit (raised in review on #6955)

`@dnd-kit/sortable` assumes moving item *i* to slot *j* lands it in *j*'s rect, and its strategies animate on that basis. Here the list order is fed through `buildRailPlacement`: first-fit packing on a two-row grid with mixed spans, the ad pinned to the third column, columns closing up, and gap slots. So one swap can repack everything after it, and a Large and a Small swapping does not trade rects. With dnd-kit we would still own the collision rule (center plus heading plus hysteresis, needed to stop flip-flopping), the preview transforms (our packer) and the whole resize. It would take over the sensors (pointer, touch delay, keyboard), the announcements and auto-scroll, roughly a third of `useRailEditing.ts`.

That partial migration, `DndContext` sensors with our layout and collision kept, is a reasonable follow-up if we want fewer lines to own. It didn't seem worth blocking this on. Happy to do it here instead if you'd rather.

## Test plan

- [x] Rail specs, including keyboard move writes once on drop and Esc drops a keyboard move without writing
- [x] Headless Chromium locally: sideways wheel smooth with zero stray animations, drag reorders, resize to Small holds, the widget menu opens with a real click, and Esc closes the menu without leaving edit mode
- [x] eslint, strict typecheck, webapp tsc
- [ ] **Real iPhone and Android**: swipe the rail in edit mode, hold to drag, and check the hold-to-edit against the link preview outside edit mode. Not verifiable headlessly.
  - Android: a long press on a widget link enters edit mode and no link context menu opens.
  - Both: after a hold-to-edit and Done, the next tap on a widget link opens it.
  - Phone: the menu offers Small and Tall only, and there are no corner grips.

author: cristianoveiga
body:
## Problem

The gather step builds its Connect Gateway endpoints from `GCP_REGION`, but its ref never declared that variable, so the `us-central1` default always applied while the e2e environment runs in `northamerica-northeast2`. Every region-cluster and management-cluster scope lookup 404'd (membership not found in us-central1), both scopes were marked `unavailable`, and the region archive — including the L7 load-balancer 5xx logs — was discarded on every run, passing or failing, since the step was introduced (#85782, after the region move in #86348).

This blocks diagnosis of the intermittent `request failed` platform API failures seen in `periodic-ci-openshift-online-gcp-hcp-infra-main-e2e-platform` (e.g. run [2112363469729697792](https://prow.ci.openshift.org/view/gs/test-platform-results-public/logs/periodic-ci-openshift-online-gcp-hcp-infra-main-e2e-platform/2112363469729697792), where `gcphcpctl cluster create` failed on `validating version "5.0.0-ec.6": request failed`): the LB 5xx logs that would identify the failing layer (GCLB/NEG churn, ESPv2, Cloud Armor) are collected but then thrown away.

## Fix

The commands script resolves the region in order of precedence:

1. `GCP_REGION` — optional override, declared in the ref with an empty default so it cannot shadow the provisioned region
2. the region recorded by `gcp-hcp-tf-provision` in `${SHARED_DIR}/region` — always matches the provisioned environment
3. `northamerica-northeast2` — e2e default fallback

Malformed values are rejected by a format check before they reach the Connect Gateway URL.

## Validation

- `bash -n` and YAML indentation check pass.
- Region resolution unit-checked: env override, SHARED_DIR value, missing and malformed inputs.
- Registry loads cleanly through the ci-operator configresolver image.
- Empty-default env follows the established optional-env pattern in the registry (e.g. `acm-tests-clc-destroy`, `addon-install`).

## Summary

- **Borrow checker:**
  - implicit reborrow when a `mutref` is passed to a `mutref` parameter (`inc(r); inc(r)`); reusing it in the same argument list conflicts, and calls whose result may carry a reference keep the move semantics;

author: oihwbba
body:
Part of SCRUM-161

## Why

Found in the 20 Oct audit. Since AC1, unavailability can be recorded over a booking that still stands (AC3 flags it but keeps its status). `availabilityByDay` (SCRUM-36's calendar) still assumed blockers never overlap. Take a booking 10:00–12:00 with maintenance 10:30–11:00. The calendar produced a maintenance stretch that ran backwards (12:00 → 11:00), drew 11:00–12:00 as **free**, and hid the maintenance.

## What changed

| AC | What changed |
|---|---|
| 1, 3 | Each day is cut at every boundary of what's on it. Each piece shows the blocker that matters most there: unavailability, then the booking, then its setup or turnaround. Neighbouring pieces of the same blocker are merged. The example above now reads booking 10:00–10:30, maintenance 10:30–11:00, booking 11:00–12:00. Days with no overlaps come out exactly as before. |

Calendar segments are keyed by their start time, so a booking drawn in two pieces keeps unique keys.

## Acceptance criteria → tests

| AC | Test cases | Covered by |
|---|---|---|
| 1, 3 | TC-161-17 (new) | unit (maintenance inside a booking; maintenance running past a booking's end; stretches always cover the day once, in order, never backwards) |

## How I verified it

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` on the changed files: clean
- [x] `npm run test:coverage` against the local database: 145 files, 2,671 tests passed, coverage thresholds met (the existing SCRUM-36 calendar tests are unchanged and pass)
- [x] Mutation check: with main's `lib/venue-availability.ts`, all three TC-161-17 tests go red
- [x] e2e: `e2e/availability.spec.ts`, against the local database, one worker: 8 passed
- [x] Went through "Before you open a pull request" in `CONTRIBUTING.md`

SCRUM-161 is Felicia's story. It was reopened for this fix (Sprint 3).

author: iziodev
body:
This KCC defines a six-level [BIP32](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/130b8e0fa7f30fa45532f080b87b8db27a79e46e/bip-0032.mediawiki) derivation hierarchy for Kaspa P2PK and multisig wallets.

Hardened levels separate spending conventions, networks, signature schemes, and accounts. Two non-hardened levels allow account extended public keys to derive receiving and change keys. For multisig wallets, the convention also specifies per-address public-key encoding and sorting, while leaving the script template to the wallet policy.
