Two pure wheels were sha256-checked and imported. ## Handoff queue (one item per agent) | Priority | Repo | Package | Difficulty | Approach | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | DRAgoWing | markdown | easy | CDN-fetch the pure wheel (Aoi PR 87). `render_md` fails with `ModuleNotFoundError` until the wheel is on `sys.path`. markdown 3.11.2 rendered the table / fenced-code / provenance sample. | | 2 | NagoyAction | polars | moderate | `polars_min.py` for `research_digest.collect` (`DataFrame`, `col`, `explode`, `filter`, `join`, `iter_rows`, `is_not_null`). The pure wheel requires `polars-runtime-32`. | | 3 | DRAgoWing | numpy | moderate | Port Aoi `shrink/numpy_min.py` (PR 89) for `load_overlap`, preloaded before sibling `rule_search`. Polars stays. | | 4 | Ironmate | pypdf | easy | CDN-fetch the pure wheel for `PdfReader.pages`. The `typing_extensions` requirement is marker-limited to Python <3.11. Playwright on the previous line is a separate, not-feasible dependency. | Aoi itself is not queued. Polars, numpy linalg, selectolax, and httpx are owned by other agents. QueRyu `ask/suggest.py` is byte-identical to Aoi `queryu/ask/suggest.py`, so it stays with the linalg work. markdown CDN-fetch and the overlap `numpy_min` are already merged in Aoi. ## What was classified as not feasible Native or wide numeric surfaces (PythDRagoras numpy, SakAnalytics and PythDRagoras polars, ortools), Pillow codecs, PyYAML 6.0.3 (no `py3-none-any` wheel), Gradio, Streamlit, FastMCP, Playwright, and the Ironmate exceljs/pptxgenjs writers. Ironmate numpy and ordinary PNG decoding already fall back to the stdlib when the package is absent. Vendored copies of archived GUI templates are inventoried and not handed off. pytest and coverage stay test harnesses. Dart pubspec dependencies are outside this Python/JS pattern. SheetJS in Ironmate and Plotly.js in DRAgoWing/Aoi are already CDN loads. ## Verification - JSON parses; the queue has four items at priorities 1–4 and the inventory covers all 23 surveyed repositories. - `python tools/parent_pin_check.py --skip-api --event pull_request` with the workflow's exclude globs reports `ok: true` and `inconsistent: false`. Checkout tips are stored as `head`, so they are not parent pins. - No workflow, dependency, lock, or vendored-file edits. ## Limitations One shallow clone of each public default branch on 2026-10-20. Dynamic import names that are not string literals are invisible. `python -S` proves the import fails; it does not run browsers, solvers, or GUI entry points. Parent CI audits recorded revisions. This survey does not block child merges.

author: prashantchothani
body:
## WA M1 reader: the Activity tab knows `conversation`

**Merge before mongodb#918** (migration 392). The api half is peakhour-api#1519.

### Why

mongodb#918 adds `conversation` to `plt_activity.outcome` and rewrites the stored `not_a_command` rows on dev (8 rows) to it. `OUTCOME_COPY` in `src/lib/control-plane-activity.ts` had no entry for it, so a rewritten row rendered through the unknown-outcome fallback: group "Activity", sentence "conversation".

### What changes

- One `CONVERSATION_COPY` serves both keys, `not_a_command` and `conversation`:
  - group **"Message"**, the group `not_a_command` already used. It is never "Blocked": chatter was refused nothing.
  - sentence **"Sent a message Peakhour did not take as an instruction"**.
  - `refused: false`.
- Why one copy: the api writes `not_a_command` until M3, during and after 392's run, so the tab holds both keys for the same event. Two sentences would show one event two ways.
- Why this sentence: it holds for every row either key can carry. Today `platform-inbound.ts` writes `not_a_command` for:
  - chatter;
  - a button tap;
  - any text while a question is waiting (Peakhour re-asks it);
  - a registered trigger the router declined.

  392 cannot tell the stored ones apart.
- Sentences rejected in review:
  - "Chatted with Peakhour — no instruction was run" (my first draft). "No instruction was run" was the api's write policy, not a fact the row carries.
  - "Chatted with Peakhour" (round 1). It read a declined trigger or a "did not understand" reply as a good exchange.
- The sentence names no trigger, because neither api return stores one. It has no second person (the ledger is org-wide), and it works beside a masked actor.
- There is no exhaustive outcome union in b2c: `ActivityRow.outcome` is `string`.

### Tests

- New tests:
  - "files a domainless conversation as a message Peakhour did not take as an instruction, under Message";
  - "reads a not_a_command row exactly as a conversation, so one event never shows two ways", with and without a trigger.
- The whole-map tests now walk one `STORED_OUTCOMES` list of twelve, which includes `conversation`.
- Mutations: 6 of 6 killed, each as "1 failed" with exactly 1 test selected:
  - drop the `conversation` key;
  - group "Blocked";
  - `refused: true`;
  - a reworded sentence;
  - drop the `not_a_command` key;
  - give `not_a_command` its old sentence.

  Two pass-direction mutants stay green across all 14 `activityCopy` tests: `not_a_command` as an equal literal, and the keys swapped.

### Gate (final tip)

- `npx tsc --noEmit`: exit 0.
- `npx vitest run`: 1697 passed.
- `npm run lint`: 27 problems (20 errors, 7 warnings) on both clean master and this branch. The problem lists are identical.
- `npx next build`: exit 0. It ran in the main checkout, detached at this tip, and the checkout was then put back on master.
- b2c has no PR CI.

### Review (2 rounds, medium)

- **Fixed:**
  - the two sentences for one event (R1);
  - the "nothing ran" claim (R1);
  - "Chatted" overclaiming (R2);
  - "392 rewrites every row" corrected to "the rows it finds" (R1);
  - "twelve" stated as current (R1);
  - a broken docblock wrap (R1);
  - the hand-copied outcome lists, now one constant (R1);
  - tautological assertions (R1, R2).
- **By design:** the merge order relative to #918. A domain-bearing row files under its domain, as every outcome does, and neither api return sets one.
- **Declined:**
  - an exact check on `OUTCOME_COPY`'s keys. The map is private, and the test's title predates this PR.
  - "Message" sitting near "Messaging". Those group labels predate this PR.

author: jonahangell
body:
## What changed

Remediation from the full codebase review, in eleven atomic commits.

**Deployment and CI**
- `Dockerfile`: `npm ci`, runs as UID 1000 with `--chown`, ships `.launch/` (migrations), health check on `/api/health`. `.dockerignore` keeps tests, docs, and bundles out of the build context.
- CI pins Node 22 (`.nvmrc`) and adds `npm run check` (new `tools/check-syntax.mjs` covering every first-party script), `version:check`, `css:check`, and `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high`. Playwright stays disabled: it needs an HTTPS preview URL and a headed MyID login.

**Security**
- New `src/http-security.js`: helmet with a same-origin CSP, per-token `/api` rate limits (600/min reads, 120/min writes, 10 per 15 min field-library uploads; `/api/health` exempt), 1 MB JSON default with 12 MB only on audit and review document routes.
- Static mounts 404 instead of falling through; client errors keep their 4xx status instead of becoming 500s.
- Escape audit and server ids interpolated into HTML attributes.
- Dependency fixes: `uuid` override (GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq), `ip-address` pinned patched, `compression` 1.8.2.

**Bugs fixed (all reproduced on `main` first)**
- A Postgres restart or dropped idle connection crashed the process (pool had no `error` listener).
- Excel export, qTest export, and workbook import reported "ExcelJS is not loaded" on a fresh page; they now lazy-load it.
- Review Feedback projection threw `escapeHtml is not defined` whenever a returned review carried feedback.
- A malformed `access_token` cookie threw `URIError`; it now reads as signed out.

**Performance**
- Gzip responses: initial load 1,961 KB → 470 KB transferred.
- Boot scripts are preloaded in parallel and still executed in order. Time to ready: 3.1 s → 1.1 s at 40 ms round-trip latency, 6.7 s → 2.2 s at 100 ms. Partials revalidate (`no-cache`) instead of bypassing the cache.
- `vendor/exceljs.min.js` had been reformatted by Prettier (2.1 MB); restored the exact 4.4.0 build (948 KB), excluded `vendor/` from Prettier, and a test ties it to the installed package.

**Cleanup**
- Removed unused `public/`, `updates/` diff archives, generated review bundles, `combined_html.txt`, `Audit Review Update/`, `js/.gitkeep`, and the stale `PROJECT_CONTEXT_NEW.md`.
- Package renamed to `atlas-align` and versioned with the app (3.1.7); `sync-app-version` now manages `package.json` and the lockfile.

## Why

Deploys ran as root without migrations, CI could not catch most regressions, the API had no headers or rate limits, several user-facing features were broken, and boot cost one network round trip per script.

## Testing

- `npm test`: 443 passing (new suites: `http-security`, `html-escaping`, `server-robustness`, `vendor-exceljs`, `boot-loader`; version-sync tests extended).
- `npm run check`, `version:check`, `css:check`, and `npm audit --omit=dev` all clean.
- Ran the app locally against Postgres 16 with all migrations and seed data, and drove it in Chromium: every view loads with no CSP violations or page errors; Excel export downloads; workbook import works; review feedback renders with HTML payloads shown as text; restarting Postgres no longer kills the server; boot timings measured with emulated latency (each boot script fetched once, no unused-preload warnings).
- Not run: `docker build` (no Docker daemon available) and Playwright (disabled in CI).

## Before merging

Deploy to a Launch preview branch and confirm migrations run from the image, MyID sign-in works under the CSP, and the rate limits don't affect normal use.

## Open items

- `templates/qtest-test-design-template.xlsx` has never been committed, so qTest export still fails (now with a clear message).
- Decide whether to keep `PROJECT_TREE.txt` and which of `.claude/rules` or `.cursor/rules` is the source.

body:
## 為什麼
第一次 Gateway 正式轉送的線上見證（Nexus-new #2803，2026-10-20）抓到的真實 bug：
- Gateway 是在自己的部署目錄裡呼叫 `cairnwork-route` 的，而那個目錄裡有一個同名的 `product` 套件。
- 背景執行程序原本用 `python -m cairnwork.route` 啟動，並繼承呼叫端的工作目錄。結果載入的是 Nexus-new 的 `product`，nexus-certify 的 `product.adapters.generic_verification` 匯入失敗。
- 任務因此一直停在 BOUND。我手動執行 `recover` 把它判為 FAILED（`INTERRUPTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH`），沒有重跑，部署器的在途任務數也回到 0。

## 內容
- 背景執行程序改用 `python -I` 啟動：工作目錄不會加進 import 路徑，也會忽略 `PYTHON*` 環境變數。
- 工作目錄改成 Cairnwork 自己的 state 目錄。

## 證據
- 新測試 `test_the_runner_ignores_the_callers_working_tree`：呼叫端的目錄裡放一個一匯入就報錯的 `product`，任務仍然照常完成。把兩層防護都拿掉時，這個測試會失敗（已實測），表示它確實重現了原本的 bug。只拿掉其中一層時測試仍然通過，因為兩層各自都足以擋住，這是刻意的雙重防護。
- 本機全套測試通過（sandbox 和專屬帳號都強制開啟）。

author: yasyf
body:
## Context

At 5:02 AM on Oct 20, in the monorepo drive, a lane ran `ccx vcs stack rebase --parent durable-step-6b-run-migration=durable-step-6a-fork-wiring --to durable-step-6b-infra` with thirteen `--include` flags. The run stopped on conflicts eight times. After the last `ccx vcs stack continue`, the publish refused:

```
ccx: stack rebase: --to durable-step-6b-infra cannot stop there: durable-step-6a-detach-route, durable-step-6a-fork-wiring, above it, is where a branch of the run was last published
```

Both named branches sit below `durable-step-6b-run-migration` once it is re-parented onto `durable-step-6a-fork-wiring`, so neither is above the `--to` tip. The lane replayed the resolved heads by hand and published with `stack submit`.

## Summary

`continue` replans a stopped run when one of its branches moved or landed during the stop (#433). That replan rebuilt the plan from gt's recorded parents and passed no `--parent` overrides. gt still recorded `durable-step-6b-run-migration` on `durable-step-6a-agent-cutover`, so the `--to` downstack skipped `detach-route` and `fork-wiring` and the check read them as stacked above the tip. A run now records the branches its `--parent` or `--linearize` re-parents. Its replan passes each one back as an override onto the parent the run gave it, so the `--to` check, the moving set, and the parent of every branch read the same topology as the original plan.

## Motivation

The replan already kept each replayed branch on its new parent through the branch's recorded `Parent`. Only the topology used for `--to`, the moving set, and the outside-branch check lost the override. Carrying the overrides on the run fixes all three with one field and no new flag. A re-parented branch that lands during the stop drops out of the overrides, since `--parent` refuses a landed branch.

## Details

- `stackRebaseRun` gains `reparented`, the sorted override children `stackPlan` resolved. A run saved by an older ccx has none and replans as before.
- `stackReplan` passes `<branch>=<parent>` for each live re-parented branch, using the branch's resolved `Parent`, so a parent that landed earlier in the run resolves to the branch below it.
- `TestStackContinueStopsAReparentedSubStackAtItsTipAfterAReplan` builds `a <- b <- c` and `a <- d <- e`, publishes all five, and runs `rebase --parent d=c --to e`. It stops on a conflict in `d`, moves `a` on the remote, resolves, and continues. It checks that the published `d` sits on `c` with the resolution, `e` sits on `d`, gt records `d` on `c`, and no run state is left.
- The changelog describes the fix.

The host-load guard blocked local Go runs, so nothing ran locally. CI runs the suite.

## Not in this PR

The lane also asked that a refusal at publish time keep the resolved commits instead of losing them at `abort`. That is a separate change.

author: rodloboz
body:
In a fresh checkout, `mix dev` failed with `cannot read asset ".../priv/static/tayori-admin.css"`.

The router embeds the admin's bundles when it compiles (PhoenixMountable's `Embedded` assets), and the bundles aren't in the repository. Nothing in `mix dev` built them first. CI didn't catch it because the e2e server runs `mix tayori.build` before `mix dev`.

## Change

- **`mix dev` builds missing bundles first.** When any of the six bundles is missing, it runs `mix tayori.build` before starting the server. That build also runs `npm ci` in `assets/` when needed.
- **The build runs in its own `mix` process.** This `mix dev` then compiles the router with the real files; a second compile in the same process would be skipped.
- **No change once the bundles exist.** The server starts straight away, with its watchers as before.
- **Docs:** the README's development steps are now just `mix deps.get` and `mix dev`.

Lotus Web has the same issue and solves it by hand: its README has contributors `touch` placeholder files, and its watchers and code reloader fill them in. That wouldn't work here. Tayori's watchers only rebuild the scripts, and the CSS bundles come only from `mix tayori.build`, so the admin would be unstyled.

## Checked

- In a fresh worktree (no `priv/static`, no `assets/node_modules`, no `_build`), `mix dev` printed `Building the bundles (mix tayori.build)`. It wrote all six bundles (admin script 882 KB, admin CSS 11 KB) and started `TayoriDev.Endpoint`.
- `mix format --check-formatted` and `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` pass.

body:
Closes #88

What shipped: `notifications(from:to:)` in `CarrierCore` compares two snapshots and returns one notification per epic that needs a person now and did not before (title names repo and issue, body is the reason) and one per epic new in the ready-for-test list (body names the PR). `NotificationWatcher` keeps the previous snapshot and feeds a `NotificationCentre` protocol; any state that is not a running Carrier (stopped, incompatible) forgets it, so the first snapshot after a restart only seeds, like the very first one. The app's centre (`SystemNotificationCentre`) touches `UNUserNotificationCenter` only when `Bundle.main.bundleIdentifier` is non-nil, asks for permission when the first notification is due (never at launch), queues notifications while it asks, and after a denial stops asking and drops them until the app restarts (the system itself remembers the denial across restarts). `AppDelegate.swift` changes by two lines only: the watcher call as the last line of the `watchCarrier` closure, and a `notifications` entry at the end of the self-test steps.

Verified: `swift build` and `swift test` in `macos/` pass (63 tests, 10 new: every case in the ticket, plus the watcher with a fake centre, plus same issue number in two repos). `pnpm typecheck` clean, `pnpm test` 41 files, 461 tests passing. `Carrier.app` built with `build-app.sh` and run with `--selftest` (against an empty temporary `CARRIER_HOME`, so it never saw a Carrier): every step ran and the last line says the process was still alive; the self-test entry reports `bundle dev.ashulab.carrier, centre touched on the first notification`. The bare SwiftPM executable (no bundle) also ran the self-test to the end and reported `no bundle identifier, centre never touched`. My own processes were stopped by pid afterwards and the built app removed.

Not checked, needs a person with a screen (no permission was requested and no real notification was posted from this session, and the "asked on the first notification, not at launch, not again after a denial" behaviour was verified by reading the code, not by seeing it):
- The permission prompt appears once, the first time an epic needs a person or is ready for test, and not at launch.
- The banner appears, also while the app is frontmost.
- After denying, nothing is asked again and the app keeps working.
- Whether re-signing after a rebuild makes macOS ask for the permission again.

author: hmdsefi
body:
Adds `chainlog.State`, the validator every log runs inside `Append`. It tracks the tip, the finalized ref F and the window of unfinalized blocks, and rejects any entry that may not follow the ones before it. Stacked on #94 (entries and the record codec).

- `chainlog/state.go`: `NewState`, `Check`, `Apply`, `CheckBatch`, `Tip`, `Finalized`, `Window` and `Clone`.
  - `Check` runs the shape rules (kind, zero fields, non-zero hashes, log fields), the 16 MiB record size, then the rules of the entry's kind:
    - a block is above the tip; a non-final block is the tip's child;
    - a `Final` block needs an empty window and becomes the tip and F;
    - a revert targets F or a window block;
    - a finalize is monotonic and links to the window and the tip;
    - the window holds at most the cap.
  - `CheckBatch` validates a batch against the state as it would be after each entry, then undoes every entry, so the state is unchanged when it returns. It keeps an undo record per entry, including a copy of the refs a revert drops. It grows the window's backing array once for the batch's blocks before it starts, so its cost does not grow with the window, and it allocates nothing for blocks or finalizes while the array has room.
  - Window lookups use the window's contiguous numbering. Numbers outside the window return at once; binary search runs only for windows with gaps, which only `Apply` alone builds.
- `chainlog/state_binary.go`: `MarshalBinary` and `UnmarshalBinary`, the form the WAL checkpoint stores. `UnmarshalBinary` treats its input as hostile: it bounds the window by the remaining bytes before allocating, checks the state's invariants, and leaves the receiver unchanged on any error.
- `BenchmarkStateBlock` and its `TestPerf` row.
- The plan's Deviations note an E2.7 spec fix: AT-LOG-04 and the conformance suite's `Rule2Linked` row said a non-final block more than one above the tip passes, which LOG-130 forbids.

How it was verified:
- The tests use the exact error texts for every rule: construction and the default cap of 100,000, rules 1 to 6 (including genesis and numbers at both ends of uint64), shape (21 rows, including first-failure order), size at exactly 16 MiB and one byte over, the apply sequence with its invariants after each step, clone and window isolation, and `CheckBatch`. The `CheckBatch` cases fail at entries 0, 1, 2, 4 and 19 (one batch is longer than the 8-entry stack buffer); after each call the accessors and the binary form equal the values before it. Also: a sparse backfill batch prefix by prefix, checked and replay-applied, and every `UnmarshalBinary` error with the receiver unchanged (in `state_binary_test.go`, with two 66-byte refs in exactly 132 bytes). 1,000 seeded random entries never make `Apply`, `Check` or `MarshalBinary` panic, and a seeded walk of 20,000 draws checks the invariants and the binary round trip after every accepted entry.
- `EVMSYNC_PERF=1 go test -run '^TestPerf$' ./chainlog` on an M-series Mac: StateBlock (check and apply of a linked block and a finalize, window of 99,999) 96 to 111 ns/op, 0 allocs (target 300 ns, 0). Its 396 B/op is the amortized copy when the window's array grows, about every 25,000 blocks.
- Coverage of the module with `-race`: 99.6% (CI requires 95%).
- Gate: gofmt, `go mod tidy -diff`, `go vet`, build and tests with and without `-race`, golangci-lint v2.14.0. All clean.

Risk: a wrong rule lets a bad entry into the log or rejects a good one, and every consumer's state depends on it. The rule tests and the batch undo tests guard against that.

Closes #79

author: forayconsulting
body:
## Summary

Adds three sections to `ea/calendar`.

- **Reading other people's calendars.** In a shared workspace a colleague's email often works as the calendar ID. Event search matches attendee addresses, so one person's calendar plus a second person's address lists their shared meetings. Private events show only as busy.
- **Reading the record carefully.** An untitled busy block is a hold, not a meeting. An invite or acceptance does not prove attendance.
- **Changing events.** Never move or delete without a yes for that event. An RSVP is a send.

Also adds See Also links and vocabulary. The vocabulary terms `focus-time`, `window`, and `hold-a-window` fix a golden probe that fails on upstream main ("i need an hour to focus tomorrow ... can you hold a window" scored below threshold).

## Why

The upstream way covers creating events on the user's own calendars. Many scheduling questions are about other people: when is Dana free, have we met before, is there already an invite. The attendance rule stops a briefing or timesheet from treating every accepted invite as a meeting that happened.

## Trade-off

Calendar ID and search behavior differ by provider. The text says "often" and names the shared-workspace case so it does not promise behavior every provider has.

## Test plan

- `ways author lint --check`: 0 errors. The 3 warnings are pre-existing and on other ways.
- Golden probes for `ea/calendar`: 2/2 pass. On upstream main the situational probe fails. It now fires at rank 2.
- Personal-marker scan: none.

## Not in scope

- Sibling links dropped because they land in other PRs: the send gate (`meta-trust-delegation-send-gate`), record writes (`meta-trust-delegation-record-writes`), and time tracking attendance rules (`ea-tasks-time`).

First item on the new stage-2 route (stacked on #323): original → intent → `image_gen` concept → model built in Blender → own baked atlas → bench.

- `scripts/content/mesh3d/blender/bake_atlas.py` + `barrel-atlas.json`: new atlas UV; stage-1 tiling materials baked through their tile UVs into a 1024² atlas with per-part tone, plank seams, worn edges (Bevel), bleached tops, wet bottom and AO; each zone gets local contrast and is scaled back to its measured mean colour. GLB keeps only the atlas UV and two materials (WOOD / METAL).
- `scripts/content/mesh3d/pack_prop.py`: atlas to DDS once (stage-1 compressor), one `materials.json` key per GLB material, mesh index.
- `scripts/content/mesh3d/blender/compare.py`: one light, one camera, configurable views and wireframe.
- `scripts/content/mesh3d/iron_material.py`: seamless procedural forged iron at the measured mean colour (old iron read as moss).
- `concepts.py import --view {34,front,top} --edit-of <id>`; variants 1..9. Three concept views registered as `mesh3d-pilot-barrel-v3-*`, backed up on dev-ubuntu.

**Crate** (second item): `scripts/content/mesh3d/blender/crate.py` + `crate.json` builds frames, planks with gaps, a dark core, L-shaped corner plates and sunk nail heads (1410/1500 tris, 174 parts, bbox exact; the only open edges are the 102 hidden nail bases). Each part writes `_part`, which `bake_atlas.py` now uses for tones; bakes filter with 16 samples per pixel; crate atlas 2048². `scripts/content/mesh3d/prop-survey.cpp` prints only numbers: where a visual stands in NewWorld and the mean colour of its texels. New bench `own-mesh-crate`; concepts `mesh3d-pilot-crate-v3-{34,front,side,top}` (orthographic views need only 10% transparency). Report `reports/content/2026-10-crate-from-concept/`. New bench `own-mesh-table`; the table is in the shared index and in game reads as planks, apron and splayed legs, the top 14% darker than the original. The bench is built and baked but not in game: the GLB loader replaces only static `.3DS/.MRM`, the bench is a MOB model. Report `reports/content/2026-10-table-bench-from-concept/`.

author: vaibhav-sf
body:
## Overview

This PR implements the Assignment 15 security and authentication enhancements for the Book Management System (BMS), including JWT authentication, role-based access control (RBAC), a generic OAuth/OIDC integration using the Strategy design pattern, and GitHub Actions CI/CD checks.

## Changes Implemented

### 1. Authentication and Authorization
- Implemented a dedicated Auth Service with user registration and email/password login.
- Added bcrypt password hashing and JWT-based authentication.
- Enforced JWT validation and role-based access control at the API Gateway.
- Restricted administrative write operations to authorized ADMIN users.

### 2. OAuth/OIDC and Strategy Design Pattern
- Added a reusable external authentication strategy interface and OIDC strategy using `openid-client`.
- Implemented authorization-code flow with PKCE, state and nonce validation.
- Added authentication login and callback routes with API Gateway forwarding.
- Added external identity mapping using the provider issuer and subject.
- Ensured externally provisioned users receive the USER role by default and are not automatically linked to existing accounts based only on matching email addresses.

### 3. OAuth Transaction Security
- Added PostgreSQL models and repositories for external identities and OAuth transactions.
- Protected transaction state and browser-binding values using hashing.
- Encrypted nonce and PKCE verifier values at rest.
- Implemented transaction expiry checks and one-time consumption to prevent replay and concurrent reuse.

### 4. Testing and CI/CD
- Added automated tests for OIDC token validation, OAuth transaction security, external-user provisioning, and API Gateway authentication forwarding.
- Updated the Assignment 15 GitHub Actions workflow for Auth Service and API Gateway builds, tests, linting, and database migration checks.
- Documented the security implementation and remaining provider configuration requirements.

## Verification

- **Auth Service:** 22 tests passed.
- **API Gateway:** 27 tests passed.
- TypeScript build, linting, and formatting checks passed locally.
- Database migration and schema verification completed.
- Docker Compose configuration validation passed.
- GitHub Actions completed successfully for the committed changes.

## Remaining Configuration

The generic OIDC flow has been tested using a mock provider. Live Arc Authentication MS sign-in still requires the actual provider issuer/discovery URL, client registration details, registered callback URI, and required scopes. Production security hardening, including rate limiting, explicit CORS policy, security headers, TLS configuration, and managed secret rotation, also requires further review.

## Related Assignment

**Assignment 15 — Security and Authentication**

Deliverable: Secure application with OAuth authentication, RBAC, and design-pattern-enhanced security flows.

body:
Closes #2. Closes #3.

The repository is public. This brings it to the shape of `judgment-pack-agent`, adapted to a bash kit, and fixes the two open issues. Version stays `0.1.0`.

## What it adds

- **Contributor files**: `CONTRIBUTING.md` (running `tests/run.sh` and `shellcheck`, the DCO sign-off, one pull request per issue, the agent docs), `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` (the same text), `SECURITY.md` (the same reporting path, scope adapted: a manifest is code), `NOTICE`, `.gitattributes`, `.gitignore`, `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`, `.github/dependabot.yml` (github-actions only), and `thank-merged-contributors.yml` copied as is.
- **The kit on itself**: `dev.json` (steps `diff-check`, `local-paths`, `agent-docs`, `bash-n`, `json`, `shellcheck`, `tests`), `scripts/dev/check.sh` (a copy of the template), `AGENTS.md` (the template plus a "This repository" section) and `CLAUDE.md` generated from it. `ci.yml` keeps its `lint` and `tests` jobs, which branch protection requires, and runs them through `scripts/dev/check.sh --only ...`; it also gains `workflow_call`. The `json` step is the old "JSON documents parse" lint step, moved into the manifest.
- **README**: a "Public" paragraph, install from a release or a clone, and the release and verification pointers. `docs/releasing.md` is new.
- **#3**: `lib/wrap.sh` puts the manifest's venv first on the PATH for every step, whatever its toolchain (the toolchain still decides the cap). A kit test runs a `node`, a `go`, a `shell` and a `python` step that each import a module installed in the venv, and a run without the venv fails all four. `templates/check.sh` line 2 is `# from judgment-pack-devkit v0.1.0 (templates/check.sh)`; a test holds it to `jpdev --version`, and the release workflow asserts it; `docs/adopting.md` says a vendored copy keeps the line.
- **#2**: the `go` toolchain takes an optional `version` (`1.26` or `1.26.5`) in `dev.schema.json`. `templates/ci-check.yml` reads it and passes it to `setup-go` as `go-version`, falling back to `go-version-file` when the manifest names none. `jpdev setup` and `jpdev check` select a Go that matches it (the go on PATH, else `sdk/goX.Y.Z/bin/go` under the new setting `JPDEV_GO_SDK_DIR`, default `~/sdk`) and say so when none is installed, then run with the go on PATH. `examples/judgment-pack-agent.dev.json` names `1.26.5`; the agent repository's own manifest is a change in that repository.

Public surface: the manifest schema (`toolchains.go.version`), a new setting (`JPDEV_GO_SDK_DIR`), the PATH a step sees, and line 2 of `templates/check.sh`. Tests and documentation changed with them.

## Release workflow

`release.yml` runs on a `v*` tag (`vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`) and is modelled on the agent repository's, without the Go module tag and the mutation-table gate.

| Job | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `admit` | The tag is in the grammar, annotated, names the commit the run was started for, and that commit is on `main`; `docs/releases/<tag>.md` exists, is not empty and ends its first line with the tag; the `release` environment has a required reviewer. |
| `verify` | Calls the tagged commit's own `ci.yml` (`lint`, `tests`). |
| `package` | `bin/jpdev --version`, line 2 of `templates/check.sh` and the tag agree, and `scripts/dev/check.sh` is the template. `git archive` of `bin/ lib/ templates/ config/ scripts/ docs/ README.md LICENSE NOTICE` into `judgment-pack-devkit-<version>.tgz` (gzip -n, so the bytes are reproducible), `checksums.txt`, one run of the unpacked kit, the files uploaded as an artifact. |
| `attest-and-draft` | The tag still names the commit and no release exists under it; both files are attested with `actions/attest-build-provenance`; a draft release is created with the notes from `docs/releases/<tag>.md` and its id recorded. |
| `publish` | Behind the `release` environment (the gate: a maintainer approves). The tag is compared once more; the draft is read by id and must hold the run's notes, title and asset digests; it is published by that id; the published assets are read again and must match. |

`docs/releasing.md` describes the steps, the gate, what to do when a run fails, and how to verify a release: `gh attestation verify <file> --repo ... --signer-workflow Judgment-Pack/judgment-pack-devkit/.github/workflows/release.yml --source-ref refs/tags/<tag> --source-digest <commit> --format json`. The `release` environment exists with a required reviewer. The workflow has not been run: `actionlint` is clean, and the package steps were run by hand on the commit (the tarball is reproducible and unpacks to a kit that reports its version).

## Checks

`scripts/dev/check.sh --all` from the clone root, once. `shellcheck` 0.10.0, the native binary (release tarball), in the CI form `shellcheck -x -P ".:SCRIPTDIR" ...`.

```
== check summary (dev.json) ==
PASS     diff-check               0s
PASS     local-paths              0s
PASS     agent-docs               0s
    sync-agent-docs: CLAUDE.md matches AGENTS.md
    sync-agent-docs: CLAUDE.md matches AGENTS.md
PASS     bash-n                   0s
    bash -n: every script parses
PASS     json                     0s
    parsed 5 JSON documents
PASS     shellcheck               1s
    shellcheck: clean
PASS     tests                    20s
    102 passed, 0 failed
== 7 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 0 not run ==
```

Also: `actionlint` (native, with `shellcheck` on PATH, under `lib/rsscap.sh 6000 600`) reports nothing; `git diff --check` is clean; no `/home/` or `/tmp/` path and no personal name in tracked text. Mutation checks on a scratch copy: restricting the venv to python steps fails the four venv tests; removing the Go selection fails six; a stale line 2 fails two; a prefix match of the Go version (1.7 matching go1.77.5) fails one.

## Not in this PR

- The DCO required status context: the maintainer re-adds it once the DCO app covers the repository.
- The next version's release notes and version bump (`docs/releases/`, `JPDEV_VERSION`, line 2 of the template): the maintainer's, per `docs/releasing.md`. The `v0.1.0` tag predates the workflow and has no release.
- Turning on immutable releases in the repository settings (the maintainer's).

## What changed
Michael's decision, 2026-10-20, verbatim:
- "Når de først er gået igang med at skyde på en fjende kan man ikke stoppe dem igen ved at få dem til at køre væk. Det skal være muligt at sige de skal køre væk fra et mål"
- "Hvis jeg vælger enheden og siger den skal køre til en anden position så skal den stoppe angrebet og køre til den valgte position."

**What a ground tap does now** (with units selected): it sends a **MOVE** Command instead of ATTACK_MOVE. The sim already supports MOVE:
- A MOVE row drops its target every tick and never acquires a new one.
- `Combat.fire` skips MOVE units, so they stop firing and drive to the point in formation.
- On arrival they go IDLE. An idle unit fires at enemies within weapon range without moving.

**What stays the same:**
- A tap on an enemy is still ATTACK.
- The rest of the gesture set is unchanged: select, double-tap, long-press box, groups, All army.
- Scenario and AI orders may still use ATTACK_MOVE.

**Consequence:** no gesture issues an attack-move any more. Starting a fight is one tap on an enemy, and idle units defend themselves.

**Size:** 70 lines outside tests/:
- game code 27: `PlayerController.gd`, plus a comment-only edit in `MoveMarkerLayer.gd`;
- docs: CLAUDE.md, touch-ui-rules, HOW_TO_PLAY, ADR 0004 and 0009 notes, plan.

399 changed lines in total.

**Code:** `game/input/PlayerController.gd` sends `Command.move(...)` with the same selection and target. The marker stays the amber chevrons. The art lens judged that they still read right for a move and stay distinct from the red attack diamond. STYLE.md's "Attack-move marker" name is to be renamed by art-director.

**Tests:**
- New `tests/input/test_player_controller_move.gd`, run at 1280x720, 2400x1080 and 2048x1536 with real touch events, a real queue and a real sim:
  - **Disengaging:** units engaged by a tap on an enemy (ATTACK) or by an ATTACK_MOVE get a ground tap. From the tick the MOVE applies they fire no further SHOT. They reach the point and become IDLE. An enemy that then comes within weapon range is fired at without the unit moving.
  - **Re-engaging:** a later tap on an enemy gives ATTACK again.
- Changed assertions, all because a ground tap is now MOVE:
  - `test_player_controller.gd`: 3 assertions and a helper.
  - `test_controls_flow.gd` (qa's file): one line, ATTACK_MOVE becomes MOVE. The 450-tick idle-slot checks are unchanged and green.

**Docs** (lead-approved lines, Michael's words quoted verbatim):
- CLAUDE.md Mobile UX: "tap ground = move (stops an attack)".
- touch-ui-rules: the ground-tap row.
- HOW_TO_PLAY:
  - the Orders row "Move: ... also out of a fight";
  - the Combat rows: standing units fire, units on a move order do not;
  - the "Moving without fighting (retreat)" not-yet row is removed.
- ADR 0004 §5 and ADR 0009: dated status notes. The "players cannot disengage in Phase 2" limitation is lifted.
- Plan:
  - row P43c added;
  - dated notes in "Out of scope", answer 2, the Command section and risk 11.

**Open for later:**
- STYLE.md marker rename (art-director).
- ROADMAP line 22, the Phase 1 box about attack-moves, is historical and left as is.
- A MOVE leaves a stale `order_target` on the row, which is harmless: only the ATTACK branch reads it.

## How it was verified
Final independent check at fb9c59c (one fix round): GREEN, 1403 test cases.

After merging main (P44a, P44b, P48, P26aa) at 078de2e, run by the lead:

```
===== VERIFY SUMMARY =====
godot: 4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf
commit: 078de2e
RESULT: GREEN
gdUnit4: 1484 test cases, 0 errors, 0 failures, 0 orphans
```

The merge was clean, and the delta against main is exactly the PR's own.

## How to test it on the phone
1. Select tanks that are firing at red tanks.
2. Tap the ground **at least 5 tiles behind them**, beyond the 4.5-tile weapon range.
3. They stop firing and drive there. A shell already in the air may still land.
4. At the point they fire again, without moving, only at enemies that come within weapon range.
5. Tap a red tank to attack again.

- **Container page**: pills under the breadcrumb; Inspect puts the raw JSON beside 400 px CONFIGURATION / STATE / LIMITS field cards; Exec gets captioned USAGE / NETWORK / MOUNTS / CONFIGURATION cards and a status pill with the terminal size; Stats cards are captioned.

author: christianparpart
body:
Adds `SqlConnection::Borrow(SQLHDBC)`: a `SqlConnection` over an ODBC connection handle that another data layer allocated, connected and keeps owning. Lightweight statements then run in that layer's session and inside its open transaction — useful while migrating an existing ODBC code base onto Lightweight piece by piece.

| Behaviour | Borrowed connection |
|---|---|
| Server type, query formatter, driver name | detected as `Connect()` does |
| Session settings (string truncation, SQLite pragmas, post-connected hook) | none applied |
| `StringTruncationMode()` | on MS SQL read from the session (`@@OPTIONS & 8`), so `ScopedAnsiWarnings` restores the owner's real setting |
| `Close()` / destructor | detach; never `SQLDisconnect` / `SQLFreeHandle` the handle |
| `Connect()` | fails |
| `HandleOwnership()` | `SqlHandleOwnership::Borrowed` |

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The lent handle must stay valid until the borrowed connection is closed or destroyed (both free the statement handles cached on it). On MS SQL without MARS, borrowing while the owner has unread results fails with "connection busy".

Tests: `src/tests/SqlConnectionBorrowTests.cpp` — 9 cases (statements on the lent handle, shared transaction, owner survives destruction and move-assignment, session settings untouched, truncation mode adopted, `Connect()` refused, null handle rejected, move keeps borrowing). Run locally on SQLite and MS SQL with cl and clang-cl; PostgreSQL via CI.

The budget workspace replaced FinFlow’s original visual dashboard with a simpler layout, and its native month input was difficult to operate. This restores the emerald/slate styling, icon navigation, colored KPI cards, and responsive chart layout while retaining the current local budget and import workflow.

The dashboard shows twelve indicators, recorded income and net spending, savings rates, investment valuations and credit balances, real wealth snapshots, outflows by envelope, planned versus actual allocations, active project progress and recent transactions. Missing forecasts and incomplete actual spending remain explicit; no historical values or expense trends are fabricated. Charts and panels follow the saved light/dark preference.

A monthly salary breakdown shows each envelope separately, with planned and recorded amounts and percentages. Both use the regular income reference from the selected month’s budget, excluding exceptional receipts and other months. The reference is explicitly labeled and editable through Budget mensuel; it is not inferred from bank descriptions. Missing/zero income leaves percentages unavailable, and totals may exceed 100%. Actuals use booked transactions assigned to that budget month, including salary received in a preceding bank month.

The budget month control has labeled month/year dropdowns and previous/next buttons, with December/January rollover. Changing the displayed month does not move transactions or forecasts.

Verified refunds, savings, pending/transfer exclusion, actual history, goal progress, month controls and rollover, saved month/theme after reload, mobile navigation and no horizontal overflow at 320/390px, with no runtime errors.
- Salary breakdown checks: the same €300 envelope gives 10% against October’s €3,000 reference and 20% against November’s €1,500 reference; exceptional income is excluded; missing December and zero January references remain unavailable.

No storage schema, personal financial data, deployment workflow, or import engine changes. Draft ready for review before merging and publishing.

## Worum es geht

M4-18 (Stufe B). Ottos Freigabe vom 20.10.2026: F1–F6 und F8 je Option 1, K1–K8 angenommen, F7 mit Beleg [P] und zwei Auflagen. Dieser PR ist **M4-18a**; M4-18b (Kette in der Kachel, Vorschau) und M4-18c (Panel) folgen je als neue Session nach dem Merge. Klassennamen nach SentiWiki Table 3; die Collection veröffentlicht `earthx:mask`.

## A cup session has a name

**From Ajay's post-cup list** ("sessions can't be named in the UI"), and a fault found reading the code behind it.

**The fault**: a session added with **Add round** (not by the cup template) takes the round type's own sentence as its description, and `sessionName` printed whatever the description held — so the cup board, the players and now the final report would have titled that session "A session of the team cup: the captains' lineup, every match worth a point." `sessionName` now goes through `roundKicker`, the rule every other label slot uses (no closing full stop, at most 24 characters), and falls back to "Session N".

**The feature**: **Rename** beside each session's title on Team cup opens a **Session name** box (24 characters, a label's length); **Save name** stores it, an empty name hands the session back to "Session N", and a refusal is said beside the box. Not behind the setup lock — like the lineup, the captains settle it on the day. Staff only, narrowed to this event's cup sessions, one audit line (`nameCupSession`).

**Tests**
- `a-cup-session-is-named-not-described.test.ts` — the type's own sentence is never a name (with a control that the sentence exists); an organizer's name is kept; an empty one falls back. Reverting `sessionName` turned it red.
- `e2e/team-cup.spec.ts` — the organizer renames "Sunday singles" to "Final day singles" on Team cup, and the lineup, the public board and the final report all call it that. Phone, desktop, 320px. With the save removed, red.

body:
## Wat

Vervolg op #12. Vervangt de schaalfactor in het kostenmodel door een model op basis van een referentieofferte, en voegt stilstand bij stackwissels toe.

## Kostenmodel

- CAPEX = prijs per kW × vermogen + vaste kosten per module (gelijkrichter, transformator, besturing, leidingwerk).
- Afgeleid van een referentieofferte, standaard 60 M€ voor 50 MW in 10 units van 5 MW. Met 1 M€ vaste kosten per module (plaatshouder) volgt 1.000 €/kW.
- Nieuwe uitkomst per aantal modules: de **maximale vaste kosten per module** waarbij opsplitsen per kilo goedkoper blijft dan één module. Op de pagina als grafiek met de aangenomen waarde als lijn, en in tabel en CSV.
- 10 modules toegevoegd aan de keuzes.

## Stackwissel

- Stilstand per wissel (standaard 4 weken), naar rato van de gemeten slijtage verdeeld over het stackleven en gepland in het windarme voorjaar. Elke configuratie wordt daarvoor twee keer gesimuleerd: eerst de slijtage meten, dan met de bijbehorende stilstand.

## Controle

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`: 50 tests geslaagd (offerte → prijs per kW en CAPEX, snijpunt vaste kosten, stilstand uit slijtage).
- Pagina in Chromium gecontroleerd: geen consolefouten; nieuwe berekening circa 25 s, uit cache direct.

body:
## 拉取/合并请求描述：(PR description)

[

#### 为什么提交这份PR (why to submit this PR)

关联 issue #8143。

`RT_SERIAL_EVENT_RX_TIMEOUT`（0x05）在 `components/drivers/include/drivers/dev_serial.h` 里已经定义，但 `rt_hw_serial_isr()` 的 switch 只处理 0x01~0x04，且**没有 default 分支**。所以驱动发出这个事件时，框架不做任何事——事件被静默丢弃。

仓库里正好有两个驱动依赖它，都是拿芯片的接收空闲超时中断来切分数据帧：

```c
/* bsp/wch/arm/ch579m/board/drv_uart.c:335 */
case UART_II_RECV_TOUT:         // 接收超时，暂时一帧数据接收完成
    rt_hw_serial_isr(serial, RT_SERIAL_EVENT_RX_TIMEOUT);
    break;

/* bsp/synwit/libraries/SWM341_drivers/drv_uart.c:287 */
if(UART_INTStat(uart_cfg->UARTx, UART_IT_RX_TOUT))
{
    UART_INTClr(uart_cfg->UARTx, UART_IT_RX_TOUT);
    rt_hw_serial_isr(serial_device, RT_SERIAL_EVENT_RX_TIMEOUT);
}
```

这两个 BSP（`bsp/wch/arm/ch579m`、`bsp/synwit/swm341-mini`）都用 V1 框架，结果是"一帧收完"的通知永远到不了应用层，帧边界实际丢失，只能退化成按 FIFO 水位由 `RX_IND` 上报。

#### 你的解决方案是什么 (what is your solution)

把超时事件并入 `RX_IND` 分支处理：排空硬件 FIFO，然后按软件 FIFO 中已缓存的长度回调 `rx_indicate`。这正是"用超时作为帧结束标志"的驱动所期望的语义，也与我之前在 issue 里建议的方案 A 一致。

只改了 `components/drivers/serial/dev_serial.c` 一行 case（+5 行含注释），没有新增字段、不改 ABI。

#### 关于 V2

V2 框架**未做改动**，原因是我在编译验证时确认：

- `components/drivers/include/drivers/dev_serial_v2.h` 只定义了 0x01~0x04，**没有** `RT_SERIAL_EVENT_RX_TIMEOUT`
- V2 下驱动引用该宏会直接编译失败，因此不可能发出这个事件（我试着在 V2 的 isr 里加 case，编译报 `'RT_SERIAL_EVENT_RX_TIMEOUT' undeclared`，已撤回）

也就是说这个坑纯粹存在于 V1。V2 若将来需要该语义，应当走它自己的读侧超时机制（`RT_SERIAL_CTRL_SET_RX_TIMEOUT`），那是另一个话题。

#### 请提供验证的bsp和config (provide the config and bsp) 

- BSP: bsp/qemu-vexpress-a9（V1，`RT_USING_SERIAL_V1`）；另用 bsp/renesas/ra6m3-hmi-board（V2）做回归，确认未影响 V2 编译
- .config: 均为 BSP 默认配置，未改动
- action: 本地编译（xpack arm-none-eabi-gcc 15.2.1），未使用 GitHub Actions

验证情况：

| 项目 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| V1 编译（vexpress-a9） | 通过 |
| V2 编译（ra6m3-hmi-board） | 通过，未受影响 |
| 行为验证 | **已完成**，见下 |

行为验证一开始做不了：这个事件由芯片的**接收空闲超时中断**触发，QEMU 的 pl011 没有该中断，我也没有 ch579m / SWM341 硬件。

后续改为用**伪 serial 设备**绕开硬件依赖，新增 utest `components.drivers.serial.v1.uart_rx_timeout`：注册伪设备并用 `RT_DEVICE_FLAG_INT_RX` 打开，让框架自己分配软件 FIFO，伪 `getc()` 从脚本缓冲区模拟硬件 FIFO，直接调用 `rt_hw_serial_isr` 注入事件。

同一个用例在 master 与本分支上的结果相反：

```
master 1c801efa : RX_TIMEOUT -> callbacks=0（事件被丢弃），用例 FAILED
本 PR          : RX_TIMEOUT -> callbacks=1, size=9，三个场景全部 PASSED
```

边界结论：缓冲区为空时超时事件不回调（实现并入 `RX_IND` 分支，该分支仅在 `rx_length != 0` 时上报）。

这个用例已经补上了（commit `dcadd964`），不依赖硬件、可直接进 CI。如果维护者认为"超时事件等价于一次 RX_IND"这个语义方向不对（比如希望超时走独立回调、或空超时也应回调），请直接说明，我按结论调整或撤回。

]

author: nigelblount
body:
## Problem

The `security` job ran `npm audit --audit-level=high || true`, so a vulnerable web dependency never stopped a merge or develop's deploy. #509 made pip-audit blocking and left npm advisory.

Dropping `|| true` on its own would fail CI today on **GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm**. That advisory is in `braces`, which comes in through eslint-config-next's lint tooling, and it has no fix: every published `braces` (latest 3.0.3) is in its range `<=3.0.3`.

npm audit has no way to accept a single advisory. `--omit=dev` would stop checking the dev tree altogether. Nigel chose to block on both prod and dev dependencies, with one dated, justified exception.

## Approach

- **`apps/web/scripts/audit-gate.mjs`** (Node, no new dependency) reads `npm audit --json` and fails on every high or critical advisory in production or dev dependencies, unless `audit-allowlist.json` accepts it. An entry accepts an advisory only when:
  - the GHSA id and the package both match;
  - and its `recheck` date has not passed.
- **Matched by id, never by package name.** A new advisory in `braces`, or the allowlisted id reported against another package, still fails.
- **Expiry.** Once its recheck date passes, an entry stops counting. CI fails from 2026-11-21 until someone looks again, and the failure names the expired entry.
- **Fails closed.** These cases exit 2 rather than passing:
  - npm's own error report;
  - an unknown report shape;
  - counts of high or critical with no advisory read;
  - an allowlist entry missing its id, dates, reason or approver, or holding a malformed id or date.
- An entry that is no longer reported is printed as `unused`, so it can be removed.
- Severity is judged per advisory. `--audit-level=high` judges a package by its highest advisory, so the gate blocks exactly what that flag did.
- **`apps/web/audit-allowlist.json`** has one entry: `GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm` in `braces`, with
  - path: eslint-config-next › @next/eslint-plugin-next › fast-glob › micromatch › braces;
  - added 2026-10-20, recheck 2026-11-20;
  - reason: dev-only lint tooling, not in the image, no fixed version;
  - approved by Nigel.
- **CI:** the step is now `npm ci && node scripts/audit-gate.mjs`.
- **Tests:** `src/lib/audit-gate.test.ts` has 10 tests. They run the script as CI does, over stored reports, with no network. They cover:
  - an allowlisted advisory passing;
  - the recheck date passing and the next day failing;
  - a new id in an allowlisted package failing;
  - the allowlisted id in another package failing;
  - critical and high failing while moderate passes;
  - a blocking advisory next to an allowed one failing;
  - an unused entry being named;
  - three kinds of unreadable report being refused;
  - three kinds of malformed entry being refused.

## Trade-off accepted

One known high advisory in dev tooling is accepted for a month, by name, rather than leaving npm advisory-only or gating production alone.

## Measured

- On develop's lock: `node scripts/audit-gate.mjs` → `allowed high GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm in braces until 2026-11-20` → `nothing blocks (1 allowed)`, **exit 0**.
- On a throwaway lock with next 16.3.6 (develop before #509; not committed) → **exit 1**, naming `next GHSA-cjq9-62q9-8jv4`, `sharp GHSA-wq5f-xc86-pv6w` and `source-map-js GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q`. next's other five advisories are moderate or low, so they don't block. `--audit-level=high` treats them the same way.
- `make test-web`: 108 files and 2448 tests pass. `npm run lint` and `npx tsc --noEmit` are clean.

## Deliberately not done

- No allowlist mechanism for pip-audit beyond its own `--ignore-vuln`. It has no exception today.
- No change to `prototypes/research-lead-v2` or `legacy/`.

## Doc follow-up

`ARCHITECTURE.md` §8, CI tiers table:
- The `npm audit --audit-level=high` row becomes **blocking**, with this text:
  > `npm audit` gate (`apps/web/scripts/audit-gate.mjs`): every high or critical advisory, production and dev, blocks unless `apps/web/audit-allowlist.json` names its GHSA id for that package before its recheck date. An entry carries the path, the date added, the reason, the approver and a recheck date at most a month out. After that date it no longer counts.
- The `pip-audit` row becomes blocking too, if #509's follow-up hasn't been applied yet.

`ARCHITECTURE.md` §8, "Pending cleanup" table:
- Remove the `npm audit` row and the `pip-audit` row.

## Checks

- [x] `make test-web`, `npm run lint`, `tsc --noEmit` pass. The Python half of `make verify` was not run: no Python changed
- [x] Parity suite: n/a
- [x] No shared file edited
- [x] Plan file: n/a
- [x] The new script has tests
- [x] No test skipped, disabled, quarantined or loosened

---

author: tttmmmyyyy
body:
Closes #887 ## 概要 `fix docs` が書く文書で、トレイトの実装の見出しとトレイトのメンバの型から、関連型に対する制約 (`Item it = a` の形のもの) が抜けていました。 ```fix impl [it : Iterator, Item it = a, a : Format] Joined it : Format { ``` この実装の見出しは、`std_doc/Std.md` では次のようになっていました。 ``` ### impl `[it : Std::Iterator, a : Std::Format] Std::Format::Joined it : Std::Format` ``` `Item it = a` が無いので、`a` が `it` の要素の型であることが読み取れません。言語サーバーは、ファイルのアウトラインとワークスペースのシンボル検索に実装を `impl [...] ...` という名前で出します。この名前も同じ文字列から作るので、同じく制約が欠けていました。 この PR で、制約の並び `[...]` を 1 つの関数 `constraints_to_string` が文字列にするようにしました。この関数は、カインドの注釈 (`f : * -> *`)、トレイトの制約 (`a : Eq`)、関連型に対する制約 (`Item it = a`) の順に出力します。上の見出しは次のようになります。 ``` ### impl `[it : Std::Iterator, a : Std::Format, Std::Iterator::Item it = a] Std::Format::Joined it : Std::Format` ``` ## 不具合の仕組み 制約は、コンパイラの中で次の 2 つの型が持っています。 - `QualPred`: トレイトの実装の、実装する型とトレイトの組 (`Array a : Eq`) とその制約 (`[a : Eq] Array a : Eq`)。フィールド `kind_constraints`、`pred_constraints`、`eq_constraints` に、カインドの注釈、トレイトの制約、関連型に対する制約を持ちます。 - `QualType`: 型シグネチャとその制約 (`[a : ToString] a -> String`)。同じ 3 種類をフィールド `kind_signs`、`preds`、`eqs` に持ちます。 どちらの `to_string` も、ソースに書かれた形の文字列を返します。`fix docs` は、実装の見出しを `QualPred::to_string` から、トレイトの節のメンバの型を `QualType::to_string` から作ります。言語サーバーも、実装のシンボル名を `QualPred::to_string` から作ります。 **元のコードの処理の流れ。** 上の `Joined` の実装では、`pred_constraints` が `[it : Iterator, a : Format]`、`eq_constraints` が `[Item it = a]` です。`QualPred::to_string` は次の手順で文字列を組み立てます。 ``` s = "" pred_constraints か kind_constraints が空でなければ s += "[" s += (kind_constraints と pred_constraints を ", " でつないだもの) // eq_constraints は使わない pred_constraints か kind_constraints が空でなければ s += "] " s += 実装する型とトレイトの組 ``` 制約の 3 種類のうち `eq_constraints` だけを使わないので、`Item it = a` がここで落ちます。括弧を開くかどうかも残りの 2 種類だけで決めるので、関連型に対する制約しか持たない実装では `[...]` ごと消えます。`QualType::to_string` も同じ手順を `kind_signs` と `preds` で行い、`eqs` を使いません。2 つの `to_string` は互いの複製で、同じ抜けがありました。 **修正後の処理の流れ。** 2 つの `to_string` は、自分の 3 つのフィールドを `constraints_to_string` に渡し、返った文字列の後に実装する型とトレイトの組 (または型) をつなげます。`constraints_to_string` は 3 種類を順に文字列にしてつなぎ、1 つでもあれば `[...] ` で囲みます。`eq_constraints` もここで使われるので、`Item it = a` が `[it : Std::Iterator, a : Std::Format, Std::Iterator::Item it = a] ` の末尾に入ります。括弧を開くかどうかも、3 種類を合わせた並びが空かどうかで決まります。 値の型 (`fix docs` の `Values` の節とホバー) は `Scheme::to_string` が文字列にしており、こちらは元から関連型に対する制約を出力していました。そのため、同じトレイトのメンバの型が、`Values` の節では `Item it = a` を含み、トレイトの節では含まない、という食い違いもありました。 ## 変更した項目 ### [`constraints_to_string`](https://github.com/tttmmmyyyy/fixlang/blob/da313775c346beb943a3865f673bf289a8b218c9/src/ast/qual_type.rs#L157-L172) (追加) 型や、実装する型とトレイトの組の前に置く制約の並びを、ソースの形の文字列にします。カインドの注釈、トレイトの制約、関連型に対する制約をこの順につなぎ、`[...]` で囲んで後ろに空白を 1 つ置きます。制約が 1 つも無ければ空文字列を返します。 **Examples** ``` kind_signs = [], preds = [it : Iterator, a : ToString], eqs = [Item it = a] -> "[it : Iterator, a : ToString, Item it = a] " kind_signs = [], preds = [], eqs = [] -> "" ``` **利用箇所**：`QualPred::to_string` と `QualType::to_string`。
constraints_to_string のコード ```rust pub fn constraints_to_string( kind_signs: &[KindSignature], preds: &[Predicate], eqs: &[Equality], ) -> String { let constraints = kind_signs .iter() .map(|c| c.to_string()) .chain(preds.iter().map(|c| c.to_string())) .chain(eqs.iter().map(|c| c.to_string())) .collect::>(); if constraints.is_empty() { return String::new(); } format!("[{}] ", constraints.join(", ")) } ```
### [`QualPred::to_string`](https://github.com/tttmmmyyyy/fixlang/blob/da313775c346beb943a3865f673bf289a8b218c9/src/ast/qual_pred.rs#L78-L84) トレイトの実装の、実装する型とトレイトの組を、制約の並びとともにソースの形の文字列にします。`fix docs` の実装の見出しと、言語サーバーの実装のシンボル名がこれを使います。 **変更**：制約の並びを自分で組むのをやめ、3 つのフィールドを `constraints_to_string` に渡します。 **目的**：関連型に対する制約 `eq_constraints` も出力するため。 ```diff pub fn to_string(&self) -> String { - let mut s = String::default(); - if self.pred_constraints.len() > 0 || self.kind_constraints.len() > 0 { - s += "["; - } - let mut constraints = vec![]; - constraints.extend(self.kind_constraints.iter().map(|c| c.to_string())); - constraints.extend(self.pred_constraints.iter().map(|c| c.to_string())); - s += &constraints.join(", "); - if self.pred_constraints.len() > 0 || self.kind_constraints.len() > 0 { - s += "] "; - } - s += &self.predicate.to_string(); - s + constraints_to_string( + &self.kind_constraints, + &self.pred_constraints, + &self.eq_constraints, + ) + &self.predicate.to_string() } ``` ### [`QualType::to_string`](https://github.com/tttmmmyyyy/fixlang/blob/da313775c346beb943a3865f673bf289a8b218c9/src/ast/qual_type.rs#L55-L57) 型シグネチャを、制約の並びとともにソースの形の文字列にします。`fix docs` のトレイトの節で、メンバの型 (`Type: ...`) がこれを使います。 **変更**：`QualPred::to_string` と同じく、3 つのフィールドを `constraints_to_string` に渡します。 **目的**：関連型に対する制約 `eqs` も出力するため。 ```diff pub fn to_string(&self) -> String { - let mut s = String::default(); - if self.preds.len() > 0 || self.kind_signs.len() > 0 { - s += "["; - } - let mut preds = vec![]; - preds.extend(self.kind_signs.iter().map(|p| p.to_string())); - preds.extend(self.preds.iter().map(|p| p.to_string())); - s += &preds.join(", "); - if self.preds.len() > 0 || self.kind_signs.len() > 0 { - s += "] "; - } - s += &self.ty.to_string(); - s + constraints_to_string(&self.kind_signs, &self.preds, &self.eqs) + &self.ty.to_string() } ``` ### `std_doc/Std.md` (生成し直した文書) 関連型に対する制約を持つ Std の実装 12 個の見出しが変わりました。`Joined` のほかは Iterator の実装で、たとえば次のとおりです。 ```diff -### impl `[i : Std::Iterator] Std::Iterator::MapIterator i a b : Std::Iterator` +### impl `[i : Std::Iterator, Std::Iterator::Item i = a] Std::Iterator::MapIterator i a b : Std::Iterator` ``` 同じ形で変わったのは `AppendIterator`、`ConsIterator`、`FilterIterator`、`FilterMapIterator`、`FlattenIterator`、`IntersperseIterator`、`ProductIterator`、`ReverseIterator`、`TakeWhileIterator` です。Std のトレイトのメンバには関連型に対する制約を持つものが無いので、トレイトの節は変わっていません。 ## テスト `src/tests/test_docs.rs` の `test_docs_comprehensive_output` は、テスト用のプロジェクト `src/tests/test_docs/cases/comprehensive_docs` に `fix docs` を走らせ、出力を `expected_docs/Main.md` と 1 文字ずつ比べます。このプロジェクトに次の 3 つを足し、期待する出力を更新しました。 - 関連型に対する制約を持つトレイトのメンバ `my_append_elems : [it : Iterator, Item it = a, a : ToString] it -> c -> String` (トレイト `MyAppendElems`)。トレイトの節に `QualType::to_string` の出力が `Type: [it : Std::Iterator, a : Std::ToString, Std::Iterator::Item it = a] it -> c -> Std::String` として出ることを固定します。 - 関連型に対する制約を持つ実装 `impl [it : Iterator, Item it = a, a : ToString] MyIterHolder it : ToString`。見出しに `QualPred::to_string` の出力が `Std::Iterator::Item it = a` を含んで出ることを固定します。 - カインドの注釈、トレイトの制約、関連型に対する制約を全部持つ実装 `impl [f : * -> *, it : Iterator, Item it = f I64] MyIterHolder it : MyTrait`。`constraints_to_string` が 3 種類をこの順に出力することを固定します。 この変更が無いと、テストは期待する出力との食い違いで落ちます (`Generated documentation does not match expected output.`)。修正を外して走らせ、落ちることを確かめました。カインドの注釈を出力しないように `constraints_to_string` を書き換えた場合も、3 つ目のケースでこのテストが落ちます。この書き換えでは、他の docs のテストは 8 本すべて通りました。 `test_generate_documents` は `std_doc/Std.md` を生成し直すテストで、上の Std の見出しの変化はこのテストが書いたものです。 ## 利用者に見える文 **CHANGELOG** (Fixed / Tool): > - #887, #894: `fix docs` now writes the constraints on associated types, such as `Item it = a`, in the heading of a trait implementation and in the type of a trait member, as in `impl [it : Iterator, a : Format, Item it = a] Joined it : Format`. It used to leave them out. The language server now shows them too, in the names of trait implementations in the outline of a file and in the workspace symbol search. **`fix docs` の出力と言語サーバーのシンボル名。** 制約の並びは、どの表示でも同じ 1 つの形に変わります。 ``` 変更前: [it : Std::Iterator, a : Std::ToString] Main::MyIterHolder it : Std::ToString 変更後: [it : Std::Iterator, a : Std::ToString, Std::Iterator::Item it = a] Mai

body:
📌

Replace the README launch video with the new mascot product demo, and add the mascot explainer video under the presetter.dev hero. Both videos are hosted as GitHub attachments on this PR, so no video bytes enter the repository.

## 🎯 Goal

A README visitor sees Presetter working in a 90-second product demo, and a presetter.dev visitor can watch a 90-second explainer of how one config flows from `presetter.config.ts` to generated files, without leaving the page.

## ✅ Requirements

- The README shows a thumbnail of the mascot product demo that opens the video with sound, and renders the same way on GitHub and npmjs.
- The presetter.dev homepage shows a "Follow one config from start to finish." section directly under the hero, with the explainer as a click-to-play video with sound.
- The homepage video shows the map frame as its poster and downloads nothing until the visitor presses play.
- The section reads correctly in light and dark mode and on mobile widths.

## 🧵 Context

The 77-second launch video predates the Presetter ghost mascot. The new mascot videos (product demo, explainer, comedy, and an X musical) were storyboarded, scored, and rendered from the real `presetter.config.ts` model and real `presetter bootstrap` output. This PR places two of them: the product demo in the README and the explainer on the homepage.

## 🛠️ Implementation

- The README replaces its `<video>` block with a linked thumbnail image (`[![…](thumbnail)](video)`), because npmjs strips `<video>` tags; the thumbnail is the closing tagline frame with a "Watch the demo" badge.
- `ExplainerVideoSection` follows the homepage's existing local-section pattern and reuses its `sectionIntro`, `sectionEyebrow`, `sectionTitle`, and `sectionDescription` styles; the new `explainerFrame` uses the same border, radius, and shadow tokens as the proof cards.
- The video uses `preload="none"` with a poster, so the 9 MB file loads only on play, and fixed `width`/`height` attributes plus `aspect-ratio` reserve its space without layout shift.
- The web copies are 1280×720, 24 fps, H.264 two-pass with AAC 128 kb/s and fast start, about 9 MB each so GitHub accepts them as attachments; audio is mastered to about −14 LUFS with peaks at or below −2.4 dBTP.

## 🖼️ Screenshots

**presetter.dev — explainer section under the hero, poster frame shown before play · desktop · 1280 wide**

![presetter.dev explainer section, desktop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4b24e8ef-b263-47d6-a481-a274b609d613)

**presetter.dev — explainer section · dark mode · desktop · 1280 wide**

![presetter.dev explainer section, dark mode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/06537539-46fa-4150-8470-3d368df2908c)

**presetter.dev — explainer section · mobile · 390 wide**

![presetter.dev explainer section, mobile](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b9360cc0-f895-4b30-87ec-d84fbe49ad7a)

**README — product demo thumbnail (links to the video below)**

![Presetter product demo: stop haunting your configs, watch the demo](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a5b05247-c814-4fcf-b92e-9e8ffcdcd52f)

**README — product demo (89 s, click to play with sound)**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/45376166-d2c6-420a-a6d4-8dfc309644e9

**presetter.dev — explainer (89 s, click to play with sound)**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/67375ea6-baa6-4363-803c-e2757ae02766

**presetter.dev — explainer poster, the map frame at 13 s**

![Explainer poster, the map frame at 13 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d7942d49-9236-40b6-9c61-e9aea6df145a)

## ⚠️ Risk

R1: documentation and one presentational homepage section, with no runtime or API change. If an attachment URL ever stops resolving, the README shows the thumbnail alt text as the link and the homepage shows an empty player under the hero; the rest of the page is unaffected.

## 🧪 Verification

- [x] `pnpm --dir website run typecheck` passes at 8c007ae on a clean frozen-lockfile install.
- [x] `pnpm --dir website run build` passes at 8c007ae.
- [x] ESLint passes on `website/src/pages/index.tsx` and Prettier passes on all three changed files at 8c007ae.
- [x] The built homepage renders the section in light, dark, and mobile layouts (screenshots above, with the poster injected locally).
- [x] The attachment URLs replace the placeholders in `README.md` and `website/src/pages/index.tsx` at 8c007ae; each attachment matches its local web copy by SHA-256.
- [x] The README video and the homepage video play from their attachment URLs (Chromium: 1280×720, 89.08 s and 88.88 s, no media error); the homepage video fetches nothing before play.
- [x] At 8c007ae, `README.md` passes Prettier, GitHub renders the demo line as an image linked to the video, and the thumbnail attachment matches its local file by SHA-256.
- [ ] Hosted CI passes.

## 🚫 Boundary

- The mascot production sources (HyperFrames projects, music plans and masters, render receipts) are not part of this PR.
- The comedy and the X musical are not placed on the README or the site.
- The launch-video source package under `assets/videos/overview/` is unchanged.

## 📋 Additional Notes

Publish review findings and the verdict as a separate PR review or comment. Never append them to the main PR description.

This PR stays draft until hosted CI passes and review is complete.

M0 parity tooling: the ledger, the coverage check and the identifier extractor from the goal's "finish line" section.

## What's in it
- `scripts/parity.py` (stdlib only) parses the `docs/parity.md` table and only accepts `done`, `hand-test`, `confirmed`, `impossible`, `n/a` and `todo`. It fails when:
  - an inventory F-ID is missing from the ledger, or the ledger has an ID that is not in the inventory;
  - a `done` cell has no evidence (a backticked test name plus `#PR`);
  - an `impossible` cell has no doc URL;
  - an `n/a` cell is not `n/a <category>: <reason>` with an allowed category (billing, subscriptions, referrals, telemetry, remote-flags, ab-tests, account-admin).
  It prints automated coverage and confirmed coverage. `--completeness MAP IDENTIFIERS_DIR` fails on any extracted identifier the map leaves unmapped, on any map entry whose identifier is not in the extracted lists, on `internal` entries with no reason, and on map targets that are not ledger F-IDs. The map covers all 1639 identifiers, so the second rule catches a truncated or partial identifier dir as well as a stale map line. `--self-test` is assert-based.
- `docs/parity.md` has one row for each of the 124 inventory rows, with every Mac, Linux and iPhone cell set to `todo`. The exceptions are the inventory rows that are n/a in an allowed category: F85, F103 and F104 (account-admin), F105 (subscriptions), F106 (telemetry) and F107 (remote-flags).
- `scripts/extract_identifiers.py` (run it with `python3 -I`) reads `/Users/sorcecoder/shepetal-re/asar` and writes chunks of at most 250 names to `/Users/sorcecoder/shepetal-re/identifiers/`. It refuses any output dir inside the repo, so no identifier list is committed. It exits 1 when `~/Library/Application Support/Wispr Flow/config.json` is missing, because without it the 23 settings keys that exist only there would be dropped. `--self-test` checks that and the settings-key merge.

## Completeness check
The identifier map is at `/Users/sorcecoder/shepetal-re/identifier-map.tsv`, outside the repo, and is never committed. It joins the 11 mapper chunks in `/Users/sorcecoder/shepetal-re/identifier-map/` and adds the category column that `parity.py` expects (`category<TAB>identifier<TAB>F-ID|internal<TAB>reason`). Every one of the 1639 extracted identifiers is mapped.

| Category | Identifiers | Mapped to a feature | internal |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| settings | 202 | 198 | 4 |
| helper-requests | 102 | 92 | 10 |
| helper-responses | 28 | 22 | 6 |
| flags | 203 | 143 | 60 |
| events | 1064 | 878 | 186 |
| windows | 9 | 8 | 1 |
| shortcut-actions | 31 | 29 | 2 |
| **total** | **1639** | **1370** | **269** |

The mapped identifiers point at 119 distinct F-IDs. Five inventory rows have no Wispr identifier and come from the docs alone: F35, F41, F44, F57 and F90. Every `internal` entry gives a reason.

**New features added: 11 (F114 to F124).** The mappers proposed 13 new features. Two slugs came from two chunks each and describe the same feature, so they were merged: the meeting-recorder hotkey (settings and shortcut actions) and the mic quiz (settings and events). None of the 11 that are left duplicates an existing row, so each one got a new ID:

| F-ID | Feature | Pri | Map entries |
|---|---|---|---:|
| F114 | Creator mode: an on-screen dictating label for screen recordings | P2 | 1 |
| F115 | Microphone advice quiz | P2 | 13 |
| F116 | iPhone Action Button dictation with a setup guide | P2 | 11 |
| F117 | Bulk import of dictionary words and snippets from a file | P2 | 3 |
| F118 | Share usage stats as an image card | P2 | 6 |
| F119 | Meeting recorder from the keyboard (triple-tap or a rebindable shortcut) | P1 | 4 |
| F120 | Meeting notes library with tabs and search | P1 | 2 |
| F121 | Keep or discard a very short or accidental meeting recording | P2 | 1 |
| F122 | Warning when the call app's mic differs from the recorder's | P2 | 4 |
| F123 | Latin-script view of non-Latin meeting transcripts | P2 | 3 |
| F124 | Prompt to move the app into Applications | P2 | 1 |

All 49 `NEW:<slug>` entries in the map now point at their final F-IDs.

**Why the new IDs start at F114 and not F113.** This branch now merges the current head of its base, `re/wispr-flow-full` (#6). #6 split F104 into F104 (accounts, SSO and team administration, n/a account-admin) and F113 (team dictionary and snippets, P2), so F113 was already taken. In the ledger that means:
- F113 gets a row.
- F104 is now n/a account-admin.
- The stale review notes on F58, F63, F77 and F95 are gone, because #6 gave each of those rows a local-first P2 plan.

Four map entries for team dictionary and snippet sharing moved from F104 (or `internal`) to F113. They are `department-scoped-snippets`, `department-scoped-dictionary`, `snippet_shared_with_team` and `dictionary_word_shared_with_team`.

$ python3 scripts/parity.py --completeness /Users/sorcecoder/shepetal-re/identifier-map.tsv /Users/sorcecoder/shepetal-re/identifiers
automated coverage: 4.8% of 372 cells
confirmed coverage: 4.8% of 372 cells

missing <empty dir>/Library/Application Support/Wispr Flow/config.json: the settings keys that exist only there would be dropped   exit 1

Break checks on the real map: a map with one entry left as `NEW:x` fails (`FAIL map line 1: 'NEW:x' is not an F-ID in the ledger`, plus that identifier is reported as unmapped, exit 1). A plain `cat` of the chunks without the category column fails too: every identifier is reported unmapped, exit 1.

## Deliberate-break check
I broke each rule once in a copy of the script and ran `--self-test` on it. All 15 mutations fail with exit 1:
- inventory F-ID missing from the ledger
- ledger F-ID not in the inventory

- extractor skipping a missing `config.json` instead of failing (`extract_identifiers.py --self-test`)

author: clickbitau
body:
This fixes the night-time bedroom LED: a running ramp kept overriding manual changes, and switching the automation off didn't stop it. It also covers the rest of the bug report. Hub 0.7.140.

## Commit 1 (already reviewed)
- **Hands-off after a manual change:** once a person changes a device during a run (from the app, the assistant or undo), that run's sets and ramps leave it alone. A ramp with no devices left ends.
- **Switch-off and delete:** switching an automation off or deleting it cancels its live runs. A disabled automation run by hand isn't ended just for being off.
- **Stop API:** `POST /api/automations/:id/stop` (needs the `automate` permission).
- **Restarts:** runs cut off by a restart are saved as cancelled at startup.

## Commit 2
- **Late runs (1d):** a run starts at the last "wait until after X" whose time has come. "Evening lights" run by hand at 23:52 no longer sets 30% or ramps to 100%. A delay or ramp after that wait keeps to the wait's time:
  - a ramp whose window has passed goes straight to its end value;
  - a ramp whose window has half passed eases over the time that's left.
- **Stop button and night confirm (1c, 2):**
  - A running automation shows Stop instead of Run now, in the web app and the phone app.
  - Run asks for confirmation between 21:00 and 06:00.
  - The toggle is a separate control and never runs anything. I checked this on both.
- **Restarts (3):**
  - A run a restart cut off starts again: within 30 min, or within 6 h for a run laid out over the day (that one picks up where the day is). Otherwise it records why it didn't.
  - The trigger is kept, so a prayer call plays its own adhan.
  - Stopping the hub saves its runs as cancelled straight away.
- **Clearer skip reasons (3):**
  - A skipped run reads like "Didn't run 23:10: Theatre TV isn't on HDMI 4 (it's on TV)".
  - An offline device says what Kova last heard from it.
  - A cancelled run says why it was cancelled.
- **The device readings behind the skips (3):**
  - A Helix box whose screen is asleep counts as off. Before, it stayed "on" while a paused title was still loaded.
  - A TV's input comes from the last change Kova saw, ahead of a lagging read-back (for example, SmartThings missing an HDMI-CEC switch).
  - The old input read back just after Kova switches it is dropped from state.
  - A TV that's off is on no input.
  - A Samsung TV in standby must report "on" twice in a row, within 3 polls, before Kova believes it.

## Tests
- Hub: 666 pass, 3 fail (group sync, seamless loops, Warden link). Those 3 also fail on main.

**What changed**
The aft stair's outer wall and its two end walls in `src/transit.js` are now built one storey per box instead of as single boxes running the full height of the ship. Their size and position are unchanged.

On the aft stairs at Deck 2, the outer wall beside the landing showed an opening onto the hallway behind it. author: ajmcneil
body:
## Problem
`tsfit` of an order-2 `sdvinecop` v2p model (VIX residuals, ast base) ended at the linear fit (ll 147.90, kappa1 = kappa2 = 1 exactly, gradient about +22.7 / -18.0) with convergence 0. Starting from the order-1 estimates reached ll 159.39.

## Cause
The staged linear fit leaves a kpacf free-scale parameter on the edge of the feasible box (`z1 = 8`, lambda1 = 0.9997). Any positive step in that coordinate is infeasible (`dv_negll = 1e10`), and the negative gradient has a tiny positive component there, so every steepest-descent step, however short, is infeasible; BFGS's line search never recovers and stops. (Coordinate probes alone, as in the joint remedy, move one kappa at a time and the BFGS restarts keep failing; the Nelder-Mead fallback then needs ~100 s.)

## Fix (`R/sdvinecop-fit.R`, v2p only)
After BFGS in `fit_fixed`, if the exact gradient is not near zero (`dv_stalled`: max |g| > 0.1; converged fits have ~1e-3), continue with L-BFGS-B inside the feasible box (`dv_bounds`), and if still stalled with `tm_joint_optim` (probes, coarser restarts, Nelder-Mead; convergence 10 if still stalled). The result is kept only if it improves the value; convergence/message are stored in the `sdvinecopfit`. K and L rules are untouched.

## Results (optimised install)
- VIX repro, default start: ll 159.397, kappas 0.668 / 1.430, convergence 0, 19.8 s (was 8 s at the stalled 147.90).
- Cold order-1 Joe-free check on VIX order-1 ast v2p: 8.0 s vs 9.7 s before (one extra gradient per optimisation; noise).
- Simulated order-2 v2p, n = 1500: seeds 14, 15, 21, 23, 27 stalled at kappa = (1, 1) before; fixed (e.g. seed 21: 170.0 -> 183.7, seed 27: 162.0 -> 179.7).

## Tests
New `skip_on_cran` test (simulated order-2 v2p, seed 21) fails on main and passes here. Full suite with NOT_CRAN=true passes; `R CMD check` Status: OK (vignettes not built). NEWS entry added.

Not addressed: some simulated series error out at the linear stage ("starting values are infeasible ... BB1"), a separate issue.

author: v4ndr
body:
Avant : `/api/compose`, `/api/note` et `/api/locus/*` étaient ouvertes à tous, sans authentification ni rate limit. N'importe qui pouvait dépenser des appels de modèle et des crédits Locus, avec un `maxDuration` jusqu'à 300 s. `/api/locus/logic` relayait n'importe quel `mku_key` avec la clé du serveur, et `/api/locus/status` exposait l'URL de core.

Après : en production, ces routes répondent 403 sauf avec l'en-tête `x-studio-live-token` égal à `STUDIO_LIVE_TOKEN`. Le navigateur bascule alors sur le scénario rejoué : il renvoie la requête avec `x-studio-replay: 1`, et la route répond avec les règles et Locus simulé, sans aucun appel externe. Le Studio reste donc entier sans compte. Un rate limit par IP sert de filet de sécurité.

## Comment
- `src/lib/server/guard.ts` : `guardLive(req)` renvoie `{ ok, replay }` ou une réponse prête (403 `live_locked`, 429 avec `Retry-After`). Le module contient aussi `mkuAutorisee()` et `donneesReelles()`. La PR Accès remplacera le verrou par Clerk et un quota par compte, au même endroit.
- `src/lib/live.ts` : `fetchLive()` côté navigateur. Sur un 403 `live_locked`, il rejoue la requête en mode rejoué, et les appels suivants de l'onglet partent directement en rejoué.
- Rate limit : fenêtre fixe d'une heure par IP. 20 requêtes live et 200 rejouées par défaut. Le compteur est en mémoire de l'instance, ou dans Upstash Redis via l'API REST (`fetch`, sans SDK) quand `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL` et `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN` sont posés. Si Upstash est injoignable, on retombe sur la mémoire. Le jeton interne est exempté.
- `maxDuration` passe à 60 sur toutes les routes live.
- `/api/locus/logic` n'accepte que les `mku_key` d'une liste blanche (`score:cha2ds2vasc`, `score:cha2ds2va`, `score:hasbled`, `score:findrisc`, `score:score2`), extensible par `STUDIO_MKU_ALLOWLIST`. Toute autre clé reçoit un 400.
- `/api/locus/status` renvoie seulement `{ ok: true }` en production.
- `/api/note` refuse avec un 422 un transcript qui contient un NIR (13 ou 15 chiffres, mois et département plausibles) ou une date de naissance complète (« née le 12/03/1958 », « DDN 1958-03-12 »…). L'éditeur de note rappelle de ne pas saisir de données réelles.
- Les entrées de `/api/locus/retrieve` et de `/api/locus/specialite/[cis]` sont bornées.

## Choix par défaut
- **« Production »** veut dire `VERCEL_ENV === "production"`. Hors Vercel (`VERCEL_ENV` absent), c'est `NODE_ENV === "production"`, donc un `next start` local. Les previews Vercel et `next dev` restent ouverts, pour que Romain teste sans jeton. `STUDIO_LIVE_LOCK=1|0` force le verrou dans un sens ou dans l'autre.
- Le rate limit ne s'applique pas sous `next dev`. Le compteur live est commun à toutes les routes live d'une même IP.
- Le refus pour donnée réelle renvoie un 422 (et non un 400) avec `code: "donnees_reelles"`. La date de naissance n'est détectée qu'avec un marqueur (« né·e », « naissance », « DDN »), pour ne pas bloquer « bilan du 12/03/2025 ».
- La clé du NIR n'est pas vérifiée : un NIR mal recopié reste un NIR.

## À vérifier en recette
- Sur la prod, ⌘K et la synthèse de note doivent répondre en scénario rejoué (le plan affiche « simulation · règles »), sans aucune erreur visible.
- Avec l'en-tête `x-studio-live-token`, la prod doit répondre en live.
- Variables à poser sur Vercel : `STUDIO_LIVE_TOKEN` (production), et éventuellement `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL` et `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN`.
