author: forayconsulting
body:
## Summary
Adds `ea/comms/recap/notes-message`, a way for pulling the full transcript out of an auto-generated meeting-notes email. The agent follows the email's link to the notes document, fetches every tab, and saves only the transcript tab verbatim. Google Meet's note-taking feature is the worked example.

## Why
Meeting tools that email AI notes put only the summary in the email. The transcript sits in a linked document, often on a second tab that a default API fetch does not return. Agents stop at the summary, search file storage for a transcript file that does not exist, or save the notes tab and call it done. The way gives the steps, the check that tells a transcript from notes, and the fallbacks.

## Trade-off
The steps name the Google Docs API's `includeTabsContent` flag and the Meet conference records endpoint because they are public and are the case most users hit. The way tells the agent to map the steps to other tools.

## Test plan
- `ways author lint --check hooks/ways`: 0 errors. The 3 warnings are pre-existing on other ways.
- `ways author probe` on the way's two golden prompts: 2 of 2 fire, both top-1, with no domains disabled.
- Personal-marker scan: none.

author: rennf93
body:
Release 0.2.2. It closes four gaps between how murmur behaved and what it was built for: one message to many sessions, everyone in the thread seeing every reply, and `/murmur` working as "me, through this session".

## What changed

1. **`/murmur` is from renn via the session it was typed in.**
   - Before, `/murmur` registered as the owner only (`src/cli.ts:254`), and reply fan-out (`src/core.ts:378-383`) sent replies to `renn`, which has no session. The session I typed in never saw the answers.
   - Now the owner register carries the process ancestors. The broker finds the live session among them and keeps it on the connection as `via`. Every send and reply on that connection stores it in a new nullable `messages.via` column.
   - The tag reads `[murmur m<id> t<t> s<s> from renn via <session> ...]`. Replies go to everyone in the thread plus every `via`, so the typed-in session gets them pushed.
   - From a plain terminal (no session among the ancestors) nothing changes.
2. **Claude session titles become handles.**
   - Claude writes `/rename` into the transcript as `{"type":"custom-title","customTitle":"..."}` entries, repeated as the session goes. Each hook reads the last 256 KB of `transcript_path` and sends the latest `customTitle` as `title`.
   - The handle becomes the slug (`Ledger, Implementer, Companion - Claude 3` is `ledger-implementer-companion-claude-3`), and the display becomes the full title. `HANDLE_RE` goes from 32 to 48 characters so these fit.
   - An explicit name (`murmur_name`, `murmur name`, `MURMUR_HANDLE`) pins the handle against later titles, using a new `sessions.pinned` column. If another live session holds the slug, the handle stays.
   - A rename now rebinds every live connection on the old handle (the session's MCP server, an adapter). Before, the MCP server kept sending as the old name.
3. **The MCP instructions ask for one send.** `INSTRUCTIONS` (409 chars) and the `murmur_send` description tell agents to send ONE `murmur_send` to all the sessions they consult, not separate `SendMessage` calls.
4. **`murmur prune`** and a `prune` protocol request. They remove peers that are not the owner and have no session, message, delivery, group membership or live connection. These are the v0.1 `claude-<8 hex>` leftovers; my bus has 7 of them.

5. **Review fixes** (second commit), from an adversarial review of the first:
   - A rename keeps pending delivery proof and batched notifications. Before, a push to `alice` whose session was renamed to `bob` before the proof landed stayed `sent` forever, because the proof watch and the notify batch were keyed by the old handle (`src/proof.ts:48`, `src/broker.ts:986`). `rebind` now moves both when the whole identity moved.
   - The column migration runs in an immediate transaction, so a second process opening the same old database waits instead of failing with `duplicate column name`.
6. **The murmur icon** (third commit): a vector redraw of the M icon as `docs/assets/murmur.svg`, plus `murmur-512.png` and a 64 px `favicon.png`. It is the docs logo and favicon and heads the README. Docs only, nothing in the npm package changes.

Schema: `messages.via` and `sessions.pinned` are in `CREATE TABLE` for new databases. An existing database gets them through `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` when `PRAGMA table_info` lacks them.

Behavior change: handles may now be up to 48 characters, and a Claude session renamed with `/rename` changes its handle at its next hook unless it was named explicitly.

## Verification

- `make coverage`: `Tests 474 passed (474)`, `All files | 100 | 100 | 100 | 100`. `tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- `migrates a 0.2.1 database by adding the via and pinned columns` (`test/store.test.ts`) opens a 0.2.1-shaped file twice and reads the old rows back.
- `a title joining an existing peer still moves the MCP connection when only an ended session keeps the old name` (`test/broker.test.ts`) fails on the first rebind check (`expected 'claude-proj' to be 'live-peer-a'`) and passes now.
- The two review-fix broker tests time out without the `src/broker.ts` change (`timed out waiting for proof delivered after rename`, `timed out waiting for notification after rename`) and pass with it.
- `mkdocs build --strict` exits 0 with the logo and favicon.
- Live check, `make verify CLI=claude` (haiku, two real sessions in tmux, isolated broker), run on the first commit and again on the final code, both `RESULT: PASS`:

  - `/rename Live Peer A` and `/rename Live Peer B` became handles `live-peer-a` and `live-peer-b`, displays `Live Peer A` and `Live Peer B`.
  - Owner ask to both: `replied` with transcript proof (2503 ms and 2239 ms), and each reply fanned out to the other session and `renn`.
  - `/murmur-live live-peer-b ...` typed in A: stored verbatim as `sender renn, via live-peer-a`. B's reply has deliveries to `["live-peer-a","renn"]`.
  - `RESULT: PASS`, 7 of 7.

Not run: the Codex, opencode, Hummin and zcode live checks. The Hummin adapter change is one line (`ancestors: [process.pid]`), and I didn't run it against Hummin.

## After merge

Tag `v0.2.2`; `release.yml` publishes it as `latest`. My running broker is on 0.2.1 code, so via, titles and prune need a broker restart before they show up.

body:
## Summary
Queue-1 row 8 (uniform lists), using Native #293 (`349d4857`). Native now reports a block of bare values (`tags = { a b }`: a `ReadUniform<T>` list, or a key-reference list) as `FieldMembers::Items { reader }`, where `reader` reads one value.

- **Field value form:** a field with `Items` members has value form `block`, whatever its own reader kind is. A key-reference list's own reader is a `Reference`. This fixes review group 7: the 12 key-reference-list claims compare `block` against `block`.
- **Established members:** `assemble_block` counts `Items` as established members, so the "neither family nor members" `nested_grammar` gap goes away.
- **Item subject:** each list gets one new subject `field:R/<path>/$item`, with three entries:
  - `value_form`: the item reader's form, via `scalar_form` (`string`, `reference`, `number`, …). A gap when the kind has no form.
  - `repeat_behavior`: `Accumulate` (each value is appended), so `$item` `cardinality_maximum` compares as `inf`.
  - `occurrences.minimum`: a gap. Native does not establish how many items a definition needs; a post-read check can require a non-empty list.

  The subject also takes the field's read `conditions`, so SDK-716 reaches items under subtypes.
- **Projection:** the claim index also files each claim under its path with `$item:N` read as `$item`, as does the subtype index, so the item subject answers every `$item:N` claim.
- `docs/coverage/ledger.md` adds the "List items" contract and narrows the listed-field gap reason 1 to lists without established items.

### Self-review (unknown accepted by default)
- Only `Items` creates an item subject. `Unresolved` members keep the existing list gap.
- An item reader kind without a mapped form (keyword, unknown) gives a `value_form` gap, not an answer.
- The item minimum is never answered.

## Pin and measurement
`pin-native-ec3342f` (#56, Native `ec3342f3`) is merged in, and the local patch is removed. CI can pass now.

**Measured.** The capture's `rules.json` (ec3342f) was assembled by #56's Atlas, which has no item subjects. On it, #55 gains 0 and loses 0, and the committed baselines (`covered-claims.txt`, gate fixture) are unchanged; `full_config` passes.

To measure the join itself, I re-assembled the snapshot from the same capture's recording (`snapshot --recorded <capture>/m452`) with #55's code, and gave its sources the capture's live bases and keys. The re-assembled snapshot has every rule of the live one, plus 451 new `$item` rules. Measured on it, as an estimate until a capture is made with #55:
- **+321 covered, 0 lost** against the capture's `covered-claims.txt`:
  - 123 `$item` value forms;
  - 102 `$item` cardinality maxima;
  - 96 list-field value forms (the list's own value form, no longer blocked by the `nested_grammar` gap).
- Most gains are in `traits` (49), `governments` (31), `starbases_consolidated`, `zones` and `species_consolidated` (20 each).
- **Review group 7:** all 12 key-reference-list claims now compare `same`.

## Tests
- `a_list_of_bare_values_answers_its_items`: item value form covered and agreeing, item maximum covered, item minimum not covered.
- `a_list_of_keys_is_a_block_of_references`: a `Reference`-read key list compares as `block`, and its item is covered.
- Both use authored `Items` fields and fail without the change.
- `cargo test`, clippy `-D warnings`, `fmt --check` pass with the local patch.

## 1. Asistente con botones de opciones
Pedido del usuario: que se pueda tocar opciones en vez de escribir todo.
- Debajo de cada pregunta del asistente aparecen **botones de respuesta rápida** del dato que está pidiendo: 😢 La perdí / 🙌 La encontré, 🐶 Perro / 🐱 Gato, colores, Macho / Hembra / No sé, Chico / Mediano / Grande, **📍 Usar mi ubicación actual**, **📷 Adjuntar foto**, señas (collar, chapita, mancha…), Hoy / Ayer.
- `/api/chat` devuelve `pending`: el primer dato que falta según `missingFields` (ahora con claves estables). Es el mismo dato que el prompt le pide preguntar al modelo, así que los botones siempre coinciden con la pregunta.
- "No sé" / "Ahora no" saltean ese dato (`context.skipped`, validado en el servidor) para que no lo vuelva a preguntar.
- "Usar mi ubicación actual" marca el punto en el borrador y le pasa al asistente solo el barrio/ciudad, nunca la dirección exacta.

## 2. Arreglo de "Dictar" en celulares
- **Causa**: el header `Permissions-Policy` tenía `microphone=()`, que bloquea el micrófono para el propio sitio, así que el dictado fallaba siempre. Pasa a `microphone=(self)`: solo felpus.com puede usarlo, ningún iframe ni tercero.
- El botón ahora se puede frenar: antes quedaba deshabilitado mientras escuchaba.
- Cada error explica qué pasó: permiso bloqueado y cómo habilitarlo, no se escuchó nada, no hay micrófono, no hay conexión.

## Verificación
- `npm test`: 367/367 (10 nuevos). `next lint` limpio. `next build` OK.
- Probado en local (celular, con Claude simulado): aparece el botón del dato que falta, al tocarlo se manda la respuesta, el dato salteado queda guardado y aparecen los botones del siguiente.
- El header nuevo se verificó en local. No probado: hablar al micrófono desde un celular real. Hay que comprobarlo en felpus.com después del merge.

author: ewen-poch
body:
## Problem

The installed-Skill import view preselects every available Skill, but submits the selection as one
request. Selecting 257 Skills therefore fails with `Cannot import more than 256 installed skills at
once.` even though discovery and the installed catalog support that many Skills. Refs #3618.

## Proposed change

Submit selected Skills sequentially in batches of at most the existing 256-item limit. Aggregate
per-item outcomes; stop after a rejected request, preserve confirmed results, and rescan actual
state. Stop submitting remaining batches when the user switches frameworks or leaves the view.

## Scope and non-goals

Only the existing import view changes. Keep backend resource limits, validation, replacement
behavior and per-Skill transactions. External directory monitoring/automatic synchronization in
#3618 remains a separate feature request.

No new data fields, enums, schema, endpoints, historical migration or compatibility layer.
Imports still persist through existing Skill files and `.source.json`; completed imports remain
committed if a later batch fails. Source directories and existing imported IDs are unchanged.
The generated consumer index adds the real-catalog regression to the durable-files consumer set.

## Acceptance criteria and validation

Checks below ran after the last material edit; independent code and test reviews found no actionable
issues. No full local suite was run, as requested by the maintainer.

| Behavior/check | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reported failure before the fix | `npm test -- src/renderer/src/pages/settings/SkillsPanel.render.test.tsx -t 'preselected installed skills through the bounded catalog'` | 256 passed; 257 failed with the exact reported limit error, reproduced twice |
| Boundary, multi-batch errors and navigation | `npm test -- src/renderer/src/pages/settings/SkillsPanel.render.test.tsx` | 98 passed |
| Renderer module and consumers | `OPEN_SCIENCE_TEST_MAX_WORKERS=4 npm run test:module -- settings_extension_presentation` | 221 files / 5,851 tests passed |
| Import-module extra consumer | Initial `settings_skill_import` module selection | `provider-icons.render.test.tsx` passed; all other 100 files are included in the successful broader module run |
| Store, host catalog, workflows, command/IPC contracts and i18n | `npx vitest run src/renderer/src/stores/settings-skills-slice.test.ts src/main/skills/catalog.test.ts src/main/settings/workflows.test.ts src/main/settings/integration-application-commands.test.ts src/main/settings/ipc.test.ts src/renderer/src/i18n/resources.test.ts` | 6 files / 985 tests passed |
| Registration | `npm test -- scripts/ci/validate-module-impact.test.ts scripts/ci/check-module-ownership.test.ts scripts/ci/module-consumer-coverage.test.ts` | 74 passed |
| Ownership and generated consumers | `node scripts/ci/audit-module-ownership.mjs`; `npm run generate:module-consumers`; `npm run check:module-consumers` | Passed; existing tracked test extended, no new source/test file |
| Types and style | `npm run typecheck:web`; `npm run lint`; Prettier on changed files; `git diff --check` | Passed |

The public UI regression uses real temporary directories, catalog validation and filesystem writes;
only the renderer transport is replaced. No production test seam was added. Worktree-local locked
dependencies, generated Prisma client and local package builds were prepared and resolution checked.
Direct Vitest contract checks used that prepared environment.

The first module run under default parallelism plus concurrent checks exceeded the regression's
20-second filesystem wait (100 other files passed). The supported four-worker rerun passed without
changing timeouts or assertions. This earlier failure is not counted as a passing module run.

The committed-head `test:affected:explain -- --base origin/main --head HEAD --tier pr` falls back to
full selection because the generated consumer manifest is a global gate input. The actual PR Gate
applies an additional policy: full portable tests/coverage are deferred to scheduled/manual
acceptance. Its selected bundles are policy, static, Linux runtime, Windows core and Windows E2E;
the skipped portable/module jobs are not passing evidence. This PR does not change that policy.
Local testing was macOS/jsdom, not a packaged Electron end-to-end run. Backend/ACP implementations
and persistent formats are unchanged; no live provider certification or historical data migration
tests are claimed.

## Review focus

Preserve request bounds, partial-success reporting and stale-view cancellation. The error summary
reports confirmed outcomes only: a rejected request may already have committed writes, so rescan
reconciles state instead of claiming rollback.

author: suleimansh
body:
👤 **Suleiman's picks**
- No live comment. A new comment sends an email; an edit sends none.
- 👀 on each comment at once; the answer as a new comment.
- When the work takes more than about 5 minutes, a short comment first: what the agent will do, and that it will comment when finished. The agent decides, no timer.
- Each comment opens with the coding agent's logo, the model and the effort: `<logo> sonnet-5-5 · high effort`.

🤖 **What changed**
- `replies` (skill-github) puts 👀 on each comment and review it hands an agent, in one GitHub call. A 👀 that fails does not stop the agent from waking.
- `comment` (skill-github) writes the first line from the agent's run record: the logo (Claude Code or Codex, from this package's own files on jsDelivr), the model (a Claude model without `claude-`), the effort. With no run record: the 🤖 line.
- A run's record says the effort in force when none was picked. Codex reports it, or its model list gives the model's default. For Claude Code, its settings may set one; with none set, Claude Code does not say, and the line shows the model only.
- The `reply` skill: the agent posts with `comment`, each time a new comment, and answers in its main comment only.
- The live comment is removed from the runner, with what only it used: the coding agents' `plan` event, `run --resume --from`, the git host's comment and branch page, `comment --edit`, `home --branch`. The runner no longer posts on a pull request, so the reply loop works without the dashboard.
- Kept: the row's `check-every: 15s` and the 5-minute quota reading.

🤖 **Tried**
- On suleimansh/test-project #20: 👀 in 34s, an answer as a new comment in 46s; a bigger ask finished in 54s, so no note was posted.
- On #21: the answer opened with `<logo> sonnet-5-5 · high effort`, the effort read from Claude Code's settings. The logo shows once skill-github 0.1.3 is published.

author: royanrosyad85
body:
## Summary

Update the QA protocol and dashboard to show current evaluation evidence, keep print-inquiry follow-ups in context, and document local setup with Python venv and pip.

```diff
 QA evaluation
- annotated retrieval metrics on new runs
+ Faithfulness, Answer Relevancy, Contextual Recall, Contextual Precision
+ ranked calculation traces; historical checkpoints and exports retained
 Dashboard
- fixed retrieval baseline; queue mode shown as a stopped worker
+ latest completed QA summary with run link; queue-aware processing status
 Customer conversation
- short approval/numeric replies can lose the inquiry context
+ preserve specifications, summarize the inquiry, and guide branch selection
 Documentation
+ Windows/PowerShell venv + pip setup, metric guide, and inquiry runbook
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** the dashboard used a fixed retrieval baseline; Vercel queue mode could display a stopped local worker. Short approvals and branch numbers could take shortcut/menu paths.
  **After:** regression coverage verifies latest completed QA selection, missing versus zero scores, queue-aware status, historical recipe continuation, contextual metric arithmetic, and inquiry/branch routing.
- Full offline backend suite: **224 passed, 11 skipped** against disposable PostgreSQL; no production database used by tests.
- Frontend logic tests: **5 passed**. Frontend lint and TypeScript/Vite build passed with existing lint warnings. Staged credential scan and `git diff --check` passed.
- Paid model evaluations and native Windows execution were not run. Print-inquiry behavior is covered with mocked providers; its production answer quality is not established by these tests.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Code can be reverted; no database migrations, embedding changes, or reindex are required. Saved historical evaluation evidence remains unchanged.

**Blast Radius:** chatbot

The core prompt and history routing affect WhatsApp, Playground, and evaluations. New QA runs use four LLM-judged metrics, while existing checkpoints retain their original recipe. Merging may trigger the repository's configured deployment pipeline.

author: shuko83
body:
Closes #79

## Résumé

Les exemples suivent maintenant l'usage normal : un plugin a des composants, chaque composant crée lui-même ses objets et les relie aux autres par les interfaces qu'il fournit et consomme ; la classe du plugin ne les connaît pas.

**Core** : `build(<composant>&)` disparaît. `Plugin::add()` enregistre `create<T>()`, qui ne fait que créer le composant ; une classe de plugin qui déclare encore un `build()` pour un composant ne compile plus (`static_assert` avec un message qui dit quoi faire), pour que ce qu'il créait ne manque pas sans un mot. La signature du `Builder` change : un plugin compilé contre le Core d'avant plante à la création d'un composant, comme pour tout changement de `Plugin.h` (voir Pièges de CLAUDE.md) ; il faut le recompiler.

**Anciens exemples** (gardés, comme demandé) : `ExamplePlugin` et `ExternalPlugin` ont des classes de plugin vides ; `Greeter`, `Ticker`, `ProfileSelector` et `Window` créent leur classe `*Logic` dans leur constructeur. Même chose pour les composants de test.

**Nouveau plugin `WidgetsPlugin`**, dans `plugins/` (NebulaStudio le liste au démarrage), des composants nommés `<Nom>Component` dont les objets sont des membres :

| Composant | Fournit | Consomme |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MainWindowComponent` (`title`, `width`, `height`) | `mainWindow` : sa `QMainWindow`, montrée pendant l'exécution | `centralWidget` : `QWidget` |
| `TopBarComponent` (`title`, `movable`) : une `QToolBar` en haut de la fenêtre | — | `mainWindow` : `QMainWindow`, **Mandatory** ; `action1` à `action4` : `QAction` ; `widget1`, `widget2` : `QWidget` |
| `ActionComponent` (`text`, `shortcut`) | `action` : sa `QAction` | — |
| `CounterComponent` (`count`, `text`) | `display` : son `QLabel` | `action` : `QAction`, **Mandatory** ; compte ses déclenchements pendant l'exécution |

La barre montre ses actions dans l'ordre de leurs interfaces, puis ses widgets, chacun à sa place, les emplacements vides ne laissant pas de trou. Faute de consommation de liste (#67), le nombre d'emplacements est fixe. Ce qu'un composant prend d'un autre (widget central, barre, widget de la barre) lui est rendu sans parent quand l'interface part, pour qu'aucun ne détruise le membre d'un autre ; une `QToolBar` possédant les widgets qu'on y ajoute, la barre range les widgets consommés dans des supports à elle.

## Vérifié

- Debug (MSVC, Qt 6.11.2) : compilation sans avertissement, `ctest` 14/14, dont le nouveau `TestWidgetsPlugin` (fenêtre montrée pendant l'exécution, widget central rendu sans parent, barre qui exige la fenêtre, ordre des actions et des widgets, action liée deux fois, raccourci, compteur pendant l'exécution seulement et remis à sa valeur d'édition à l'arrêt, texte sans `%1`, aller-retour d'un projet), et `TestPluginManager` / `TestPluginModel` mis à jour.
- Release : compilation sans erreur ni avertissement, `ctest -C Release` 14/14.
- Le `static_assert` : un `build(Greeter&)` remis dans `ExamplePlugin` ne compile plus, avec le message attendu.
- `ExampleApp` (build) : liste les quatre composants et fait toujours tourner le `Greeter`, dont la logique est créée par le composant.
- Un programme jetable (hors dépôt) qui ouvre un `.nbp` assemblant les quatre composants, démarre, déclenche les actions et capture la fenêtre : barre et compteurs comme attendu ; à l'arrêt, fenêtre cachée et comptes remis à 0.

## Pas vérifié

- NebulaStudio à la main : glisser les composants, les lier, **Start** (seulement par les tests et le programme jetable).
- `ExampleUniverseApp` sur un vrai écran, dont la fin de l'application à la fermeture de la fenêtre principale.
- `clang-tidy` n'a pas été lancé.
- Dans le paquet, `ExampleApp` (console) n'a pas `Qt6Widgets` : il affiche que `WidgetsPlugin` n'est pas chargé et continue (le `Greeter` tourne). Noté dans les Pièges de CLAUDE.md.
- Aucun projet d'exemple `.nbp` n'est ajouté au dépôt.

author: ethancharpentier667
body:
## Summary

The ECS `Transform` and the Jolt body now agree every fixed tick: gameplay drives kinematic bodies and teleports,
the simulation drives dynamic bodies. Until now each copy lived its own life after the body was created.

Closes #242. Part of stack #266: #264 → #265 → #267 → #268 → #269 → this PR, merge in order.

## Who moves what

| `BodyType` | Moved by | Sync |
|---|---|---|
| Dynamic | Jolt (gravity, contacts) | body → `Transform` after the step; `Transform` → body only when gameplay moved it (teleport) |
| Kinematic | gameplay, through `Transform` | `Transform` → body before the step, every tick |
| Static | nobody | `Transform` → body when gameplay moved it (teleport) |

Fixed tick order: `SyncBodies` (#241) → **`SyncToPhysics`** → `Step` → **`SyncFromPhysics`**, then `PostUpdate`
propagates `GlobalTransform` for rendering as before.

## Changes

- **`PhysicsWorld`**
  - `moveKinematic(entity, transform, dt)`: Jolt's `MoveKinematic`, which gives the body the velocity that reaches the
    target in one tick, so a moving platform pushes dynamic bodies instead of passing through them. Called every tick,
    so the body also stops when its `Transform` stops.
  - `teleport(entity, transform)`: `SetPositionAndRotation`, waking the body up (a sleeping body teleported into the
    air must fall). Keeps the velocity.
  - `collectMovedBodies()`: the active dynamic bodies (`GetActiveBodies`) whose pose changed, with their entity.
  - `isOutOfSync(entity, transform)`: whether the `Transform` differs from the last pose given to the body or read
    from it.
- **`PhysicsPlugin`**: `rtype.Physics.SyncToPhysics` and `rtype.Physics.SyncFromPhysics`, ordered around
  `rtype.Physics.Step`; the class documentation lists the four systems in order.

## Design points for review

- **Our own writes are not teleports.** After the step, `SyncFromPhysics` writes the `Transform`, so `Changed<Transform>`
  fires on the next tick for every moving body. Each body entry remembers the last pose given or read, and only a
  `Transform` that differs from it counts as a move by gameplay. The comparison is exact float equality on purpose:
  the `Transform` holds exactly the floats read from the body.
- **No change marked for nothing** (replication sends changed components): only active bodies are read, only
  changed poses are written. Bodies at rest, which Jolt puts to sleep, leave their `Transform` untouched.
- **Kinematic bodies are not read back:** gameplay owns their `Transform`.
- **Conversion** through `JoltMath` (`unitsPerMeter`, Y flipped, angle around Z negated); `Transform::scale` untouched.

## Tests

`PhysicsSyncTests.cpp`, 8 tests:
- a falling body's `Transform` follows it (~490 units in one second, equal to the body position);
- a `Transform` written by the physics is not taken for a move by gameplay;
- moving the `Transform` of a dynamic or a static body teleports it;
- a kinematic body follows its `Transform`, then stops; a kinematic body pushes a dynamic one;
- change detection, counted by a test system with `Changed<Transform>`: a body at rest marks nothing over 60 ticks, a
  falling body marks its `Transform` every tick.

"Z stays at 0" is guaranteed by `Plane2D` (#241); the 2D API does not expose Z.

Locally on macOS (Apple Silicon, Clang): `xmake build -y` OK, `xmake test` 6/6 suites pass (132 plugin tests),
`clang-format` and `clang-tidy` clean on every changed file. Linux and Windows left to CI.

author: terminills
body:
Use the classic peer's IO capability to distinguish Just Works confirmation from numeric comparison. A no-input/no-output peer cannot compare a displayed number: locally requested pairing already has consent, while peer-initiated pairing needs a consent prompt.

Keep the capability when IO Capability Request follows the peer's response, and clear it on pairing completion or link loss. This fixes the event-order bug in the pairing change previously included in #1727 and keeps pairing separate from audio support.

Native x86_64 build passes. This is a draft pending runtime coverage of both local- and peer-initiated pairing; saved-key audio reconnects do not validate fresh pairing.

author: sqhc
body:
## 问题

在 macOS/Linux 上这个插件的**主链路是静默失效的**，不是报错。

`lib/index.js` 和 `lib/scheduler.js` 解析 node 运行时把文件名写死成 `node.exe`（仅 Windows）。
macOS/Linux 上是 `node`，两个候选全部 `existsSync() === false` → 回退到 `process.execPath`
→ 在 DSH Desktop 里那是 **Electron 主程序**，spawn 它不会执行脚本：**退出码 0、stdout 空**。

所以每个 `execFile(NODE_EXE, …)` 都拿到「空输出 + 无异常」：生物钟 `night plan`、
评论区/私信/直播间监听、依赖体检、待审回复批准 —— 全部哑掉，用户只看到「装好了但什么都不干」。

## 验证

| | `bili.mjs deps` |
|---|---|
| 修复前 | stdout **0 字节**，退出码 0（脚本从未执行） |
| 修复后 | stdout **366 字节**，退出码 3（缺 cookie，预期） ✓ |

环境：macOS 26 arm64 / DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` / node `v24.21.0`

---

The node runtime candidates in lib/index.js and lib/scheduler.js hardcoded the binary name as `node.exe`, which only exists on Windows. On macOS/Linux the binary is `node`, so both candidates failed existsSync() and the resolver fell back to `process.execPath`.

In DSH Desktop `process.execPath` is the Electron main binary. Spawning it with `[script.mjs, ...args]` does not run the script as node: it exits 0 with an empty stdout (only Chromium sandbox noise on stderr). Every caller of `execFile(NODE_EXE, ...)` therefore got empty output and no error, so the scheduler, comment/DM/live-danmaku listeners, deps check and pending-reply approval silently did nothing on macOS/Linux.

Changes:
- add NODE_BIN (platform-aware binary name) and nodeBinDirs() helpers
- add resolveNodeRuntime(), used by both modules
- stop falling back to process.execPath: record the reason instead, and report it through the existing call sites (settings deps route shows it; scheduler logs it and disables its loops) rather than returning an unusable path
- guard every spawn: lib/index.js routes execFile through a small execNode() wrapper that invokes the callback with an error when no runtime resolved; lib/scheduler.js guards runBili() and the live-danmaku child process

Verified on macOS arm64 / DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 / node v24.21.0:
- before: `bili.mjs deps` -> 0 bytes stdout, exit 0 (script never ran)
- after:  `bili.mjs deps` -> 366 bytes stdout, exit 3 (missing cookie, expected)

Both modules still import cleanly and pass `node --check`.


## 追加：第二个 bug 也已修好（本 PR 现在含 2 个 commit）

`997b464` — `fix(tools): resolve DSH home from DSH_HOME instead of hardcoding ~/.dsh`

### 问题

宿主半边 `lib/index.js` 用的是 `process.env.DSH_HOME || ~/.dsh`，
但 `tools/` 下每个脚本各自拼 `path.join(HOME, '.dsh')`，**完全不读 `DSH_HOME`**。两边分叉后：

    宿主   读写  $DSH_HOME/bili-whale.config.json
    工具链 读写  $HOME/.dsh/bili-whale.config.json

配置、作息计划、两本日记、事件日志会分裂到两个目录。`DSH_HOME` 非默认时（自定义 profile 根、
便携安装、多实例、CI）表现成 EPERM/ENOENT，或者更糟——静默读写一份过期副本。
这个问题在第一个 commit 修好 node 运行时**之后**才会真正暴露。

### 改动

新增 `tools/lib/paths.mjs`（`HOME` / `DSH_HOME` / `dshPath()` / `homePath()` / `configPath`），
语义与宿主半边一致。10 个文件改走它：whale-night、diary、fav、feed、selftest、config、ffmpeg，
以及 debrief / subtitles / bili-watch 的 shots 目录。

### 兼容性

- USERPROFILE 仍优先于 HOME
- BILI_WHALE_CONFIG 仍可覆盖配置路径
- **两者都不设时，解析结果与改动前完全相同**（无回归）
- 凭据仍在 $HOME/.bili-ai（属于用户，不跟 profile 走）

### 验证（macOS arm64 / node v24.21.0）

| 场景 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| 默认环境 | DSH_HOME === ~/.dsh ✓ 无回归 |
| DSH_HOME=/tmp/iso → night plan | 写入 /tmp/iso/，真实 ~/.dsh 未被触碰 ✓ |
| DSH_HOME=/tmp/iso → diary | 读 /tmp/iso/whale-diary.md ✓ |
| USERPROFILE=/fake/win | DSH_HOME === /fake/win/.dsh ✓ |
| BILI_WHALE_CONFIG=/tmp/o.json | configPath === /tmp/o.json ✓ |
| 全量 | 11 个文件通过 node --check ✓ |

两个 commit 相互独立、可分别回滚。建议一起合——单独合第一个会让第二个 bug
从"看不见"变成"看得见的报错"。

author: seanthimons
body:
## Problem

`start_mirai_bootstrap()` passed an anonymous worker to `mirai::mirai_map()`. That closure was created inside `start_mirai_bootstrap()`, so its environment was that function's frame, which holds every task (`inputs`) and `batches`. mirai serializes a function together with its environment, so each batch job carried the full task list. Dispatch cost therefore grew with the total replicate count (quadratic overall).

This blocks the calling R process. A Shiny app that calls `bootstrap_dose_response_async()` freezes during launch, and the default `analyze_dose_response(bootstrap_times = 10000L)` with the mirai backend is affected too.

## Fix

- The worker is built by an internal `bootstrap_worker()` whose environment is `globalenv()`. Its body uses only namespaced calls (`pkgload::`, `dplyr::`, `singlehit:::`), so it needs no free variables from the creating frame.
- Source references are removed with `utils::removeSource()`. Under `pkgload::load_all()` the worker otherwise serialized the whole package source file (about 213 KB) with every batch. It now serializes to under 1 KB.
- The `dev_path` branch is unchanged. The worker is not given the namespace as its environment, so dev-loaded workers still load the same checkout.
- Replicate output is unchanged. The same seed gives identical results before and after.

Task generation (`generate_bootstrap_tasks()`, about 1 ms per replicate) is not changed here.

## Measurements

`bootstrap_dose_response_async(fit, times, seed = 42, workers = 2)` on the Ward rotavirus data with a `beta_poisson` fit, using 2 local daemons. "Returns" is the wall time of the async call. Task generation is included in that time and dominates the after case. Collection time is refit compute and did not change beyond run-to-run noise.

| replicates | before: call returns (2 runs) | after: call returns | before: collect | after: collect |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000 | 1.30 s, 1.26 s | 1.00 s | 6.47 s, 6.12 s | 6.13 s |
| 4,000 | 7.33 s, 7.20 s | 3.13 s | 20.33 s, 19.45 s | 20.24 s |
| 10,000 | 34.89 s, 32.98 s | 7.64 s | 40.99 s, 39.54 s | 44.83 s |

Task generation at 10,000 replicates takes 7.2 to 7.5 s, so after the fix the call returns in roughly task-generation time plus about 0.4 s of dispatch. Before the fix, dispatch took about 25 s of the 33 to 35 s. Before the fix, the call took 33 to 35 s on this machine, not the 47.8 s seen earlier.

Replicate output was compared with `identical()` between the pre-fix and post-fix code for 1,000, 4,000 and 10,000 replicates at seed 42. All three matched.

## Regression test

`tests/testthat/test-bootstrap-dispatch.R`, which needs no daemons and no timing:

- The worker's environment is `globalenv()`, and its serialized size is under 10 KB.
- The worker refits a batch exactly like `run_sequential_bootstrap()`.
- `start_mirai_bootstrap()` passes the detached worker to `mirai_map()`. This uses a mock of `mirai_map` and `daemons_set`. The test fails on the pre-fix code (2 failures) and passes with the fix.

## Verification

- `testthat::test_local()`: 297 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped. Two of the skips are mirai tests that need an installed namespace.
- `R CMD build` and `R CMD check --no-manual`: 305 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (the slow exact-model oracle), including the two mirai-gated tests. Status is 1 NOTE: `singlehit:::bootstrap_refit` is flagged as a `:::` call to the package's own namespace. This is the same call that existed before this change.
- The dev-loaded snippet from the "Development-loaded mirai bootstrap" CI job passes locally under `pkgload::load_all()`.

## Not in this PR

- `generate_bootstrap_tasks()` could be made lazy as a follow-up. Task generation is now the dominant cost of the async call.
- `local_mocked_bindings()` needs testthat 3.1.7 or later, but DESCRIPTION declares `testthat (>= 3.0.0)`. I did not change DESCRIPTION.

author: flotob
body:
Design 0007 step 4: requests, streams, credit, cancel, deadlines and admission ("PR 3a"). Budgets and `ipfs.stats` follow in 3b.

## Commits

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `485ffe0` | **The pin.** freedom-ipfs moves from aad6126 to b5485ee on `integration/rust-core`: the builder, parser, owned instances, store options, build info, and item 8's limits, reservations and caches. The dependency set is unchanged, so THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES is unchanged and `cargo deny` is clean. The store's new `StoreError::PageCap` gets a fixed log name. |
| `0bc819d` | **fc-protocol and fc-service: settling a request** as a panic or a teardown requires. See below. |
| `696d87b` | **freedom-ipfsd: `ipfs.request`** (`src/requests.rs`). |
| `0c151ad` | **Design 0007:** the decisions made at `ipfs.request`'s edges, where 0007 was silent. |

### `Sender::settle(id, error, abort)` (fc-protocol), exposed as `Connection::settle` (fc-service)

| State of the request | What `settle` does |
|---|---|
| No head queued | The error is the only reply. |
| Head queued but not written | The head and body are dropped, as for a cancel, and the error is the only reply. |
| Stream open | An abort purges queued data, including a queued `end`. |
| Already settled | Nothing changes. |

`Connection::settled(id)` resolves once the request's terminal is written, or the connection ends.

## How 0007 maps to the code

- **Parsing:**
  - `params::request` checks `instance`, `method`, `path`, `headers` and `headers_ms`, and refuses unknown members.
  - Upstream's `parse_native_request` then gets `request_id` set to the envelope ID and `top_level_path` set to `path`, as main does today.
  - A refusal is `invalid_argument` with a fixed message.
- **Admission:**
  - The reader thread checks admission. An instance that isn't live is `stopped`; past 512 admitted requests, the reply is `busy`.
  - Each request holds a slot until its work has ended and `settled(id)` has resolved, so heads, open streams and work still ending after a cancel all count.
  - The request is recorded before its work is spawned, and the spawn happens outside the service's locks.
- **Work:**
  - It runs as `instance.context().spawn_request(child token, Labeled(REQUEST, serve))`.
  - Each instance has one `GatewayCore`, built at start, so its header permits and queue are shared. Upstream's `gateway_core()` would build a new limiter on every call.
  - The head is `{status, headers, body}`, with no body for HEAD, 204, 205 or 304.
  - The body goes out through `conn.send`, under credit, coalesced by the `Sender`. A failing body aborts with `body_stream_error`.
- **`headers_ms`:**
  - A watcher per request runs from admission. With no head queued by then, the reply is `deadline` and the token is cancelled.
  - There is no deadline after the head.
- **Cancel:** fc-service queues `cancelled` or the abort, then the request's token is cancelled.
- **A request panic** is caught at its join handle. Then, in order:
  1. `fence_after_panic` retires the instance and arms the 5 s bound;
  2. the request is settled `internal`;
  3. the rest of the teardown runs;
  4. `ipfs.instance_retired { reason: "panic" }` is sent after quiescence.

  An instance already stopping is left to that teardown.
- **Teardown:** step 3 settles each of the instance's requests `stopped` before cancelling. As a backstop, work cancelled without an outcome is also settled `stopped`.

## Design decisions (recorded in 0007 by `0c151ad`)

- **0006's bounds:** main checks the URL and header bounds (64 KiB each); the service doesn't. Main measures UTF-16 units and the service would see bytes. The 1 MiB frame bound still applies.
- **The method:** the parser decides it, in any case, as the add-on does.
- **`headers_ms`** is from 1 to 30,000, the Bounds table's 30 s. Anything else is `invalid_argument`.
- **Refusal order:** `invalid_argument`, then `busy`, then `stopped`.
- **In a teardown, "in flight" means not yet written.** A queued but unwritten head is dropped and answered `stopped`, even a complete bodiless one. A stream is open until its `end` is written.
- **Deadlines:** a head queued, though not yet written, by `headers_ms` is in time.
- **Admission slots:** a slot is held until its work has ended and its terminal is written.

## Tests through the binary (`tests/requests.rs`)

These use a persistent store seeded with raw blocks, offline routing, and request hooks behind `FREEDOM_IPFSD_TEST_REQUEST_HOOKS=1`. The harness decodes stream frames, sends credit, and can pause reading.
- **A 600 KiB body:** exactly the 128 KiB window without credit, then the rest and `end`. Also a range request (206), and HEAD (`body: false`, no stream).
- **Admission:** the 512 bound, with a cancel before the head freeing its slot; and an open stream keeping its slot until its `end` is written, with the pipe paused.
- **Cancel and deadlines:** a cancel after the head (`abort cancelled`), with the work ending; and deadline expiry, with no deadline after the head.
- **Instances:** unknown and stopped instances, including a stop aborting a stream whose work had already ended.
- **Panics:**
  - before and after the head: `internal`, the other requests `stopped`, the event, the fence, a new instance serving, and stderr with only the fixed line;
  - in the ephemeral process: HTTP failures arrive as heads, and a panic retires one instance only.
- **Malformed params.**

Each test fails with its part reverted. One exception: the `stopped` backstop alone isn't caught, because `stop_instance` covers every reachable case. It is caught together with `stop_instance`, and kept as defense for "every admitted request gets one terminal".

## Gates

- **Root workspace:** `cargo fmt --check`, clippy (all targets and features, `-D warnings`), and all tests (all features).
- **`services/freedom-ipfsd`:** fmt, clippy (all targets and features, `-D warnings`), and all tests (10, 12, 10, 10); `cargo deny --locked check`; and `scripts/third-party-notices.py --binary freedom-ipfsd --check`.

author: liamnwhite1
body:
## Summary

Prepare reviewable release bumps from Conventional Commits while enforcing the MAJOR ceiling of `2`. Keep `version.json` authoritative and make CMake and Nix agree on prerelease/build suffixes.

## Related issues

Closes #320

## Details

- Add schema, cap, monotonicity, transition, and release-tag validation plus a dry-run-first release command with explicit overrides and guards against overwriting version edits.
- Infer one bump from commits since the latest eligible stable tag, including the repository's existing release-branch merge history. Order prereleases correctly and support promotion to stable.
- Require an explicit MINOR override and compatibility/migration note for breaking changes at MAJOR `2`.
- Add a release-preparation workflow that creates a version-only PR, refuses to overwrite an existing release branch, and explicitly dispatches CI. Gate packaging jobs with version validation.
- Add focused tests and contributor/release documentation.

## Impact

Medium risk: this changes release automation and rejects malformed versions that previously passed unchecked. `version.json` remains `2.1.0`. CMake's numeric project version stays numeric; runtime and Nix package versions share the full SemVer string. author: cbeck88
body:
## Motivation

PR #3565 changed two things that break some dev targets:

- `snarkvm-parameters` fetches SRS powers files and shipped key files only with the `filesystem` feature. Without it, the crate does no I/O.
- Its dev-dependencies no longer turn `filesystem` on for every bench and example. The no-`filesystem` tests need it off.

Builds that depend on `snarkvm` with default features still get `filesystem`. The targets below did not ask for it, so they stopped:

- The `varuna` and `varuna_verifier` benches build circuits larger than the embedded powers. They panic with `MissingPowers` in `circuit_setup`.
- The `inclusion`, `setup` and `translation` examples fail with `MissingPowers`. `srs_shared_keys` fails with "Filesystem access is disabled".

This PR adds `filesystem` to the `required-features` of each of these targets. Cargo then names the missing feature instead of failing at run time. The usage comments and the key-generation scripts in `parameters/scripts` pass the feature.

**Commits**
- `29c0de3`: require `filesystem` for the varuna benches.
- `b5c269a`: require `filesystem` for the parameters examples.

## Test Plan

- `cargo bench -p snarkvm-algorithms --features test,filesystem --bench varuna -- --warm-up-time 0.1 --measurement-time 0.1` runs all 11 bench functions without a panic.
- `cargo bench -p snarkvm-algorithms --features test,filesystem --bench varuna_verifier -- --generate` generates and verifies the proof. A run without arguments times verification. `-- --clean` deletes the artifacts.
- Without `filesystem`, each of the four examples fails as described above. With it, `translation testnet` runs to completion.
- `cargo build -p snarkvm-parameters --example setup` without features stops with cargo's required-features error.
- `cargo clippy -p snarkvm-algorithms --all-targets --features test,filesystem -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p snarkvm-parameters --examples --all-features -- -D warnings` pass.
- `cargo +nightly-2026-04-02 fmt --all -- --check` passes.

## Documentation

The benches and examples now need `--features filesystem`. The usage comments and the `parameters/scripts` show it.

## Backwards compatibility

This PR changes only bench and example targets, their comments and the key-generation scripts. It does not change library code, consensus or tests.

A `cargo check --examples --benches` without features now skips these targets. CI's lint job runs clippy with `--all-features`, so it still checks them. The Windows job's `cargo check --examples --benches --tests` in `parameters` no longer compiles the four examples.

author: rodloboz
body:
Automation for Tayori. Changes that shipped go into an inbox, digests turn them into entries, and the entries are published and emailed on schedules you choose. Each step is configurable and can also be done by hand. Without the new options, nothing changes.

```
sources ──► inbox ──► digest ──► entry ──► page, panel, feeds
CI, GitHub,  waiting    plain or   draft or     emails: each one
your code               by the AI  published    or by period
```

## The inbox (`Tayori.Inbox`, `tayori_changes`)

The table is added to `Tayori.Migrations.V1` directly; there's no V2 because Tayori is unreleased.

- A change has a title, a Markdown body, a kind, a category, an audience (`public`/`internal`), segments, highlight, version, url, author and time.
- It is identified by its source and ref, so reading a source again only adds what's new.
- States are new, drafted (linked to the entry it went into) and hidden.

## Sources

**In the app** (`:inbox` config, read at start):
- `Tayori.Sources.Changelog` reads a Keep a Changelog file. A trailing `<!-- audience: internal; category: x; highlight -->` comment sets those fields for an item.
- `Tayori.Sources.Fragments` reads a folder of Markdown fragments, including Changesets and towncrier files.
- A title taken from a change's text is removed from its body, so the text isn't repeated.

**From CI:**
- `POST <api>/changes` with a bearer token. Only its SHA-256 is stored.
- `mix tayori.ingest`, in the app or as `--url`/`--token` from CI.

**From GitHub:**
- A signed webhook (`Tayori.GitHub`), using `body_reader:` to keep the raw body for signature checks.
- Pull requests merged into the default branch use their `## Changelog` section.
- Published releases add one change per item in their notes.
- `changelog:` labels mark a PR to skip, internal, highlight, category, segment or kind.

**From code:** `Tayori.Inbox.add/2` and `add_many/2`.

## Digests (`Tayori.Digest`)

- **Plain:** one change becomes its own entry. Several make an entry titled with the date, with a section per category and highlights first.
- **With AI:** the model writes the entry from public changes only. It gets titles, bodies, categories and highlights, never refs, links or authors. If the model fails, or Tayori refuses its entry, the digest falls back to plain. `translate: true` adds the other languages.
- **Schedule:** `:manual`, `:ingest`, `{:weekly, day}`, `:monthly` or `{:days, n}`, at a set time, with a `minimum:`. It runs as an Oban job when Oban is configured, otherwise as a task.
- **Publishing:** drafts by default; `publish: :publish` when you trust the output.
- **Slugs:** a slug derived from a title that's already taken gets a number (`20-october-2026-2`). A slug you set explicitly still errors if taken.

## Emails

`emails: [every: :each | {:weekly, day} | :monthly | {:days, n}]`. A period sends one email listing its entries, with `List-Unsubscribe`. The default is still one email per entry. The subscribe form's text no longer promises one email per entry.

## Admin

- An `/inbox` page:
  - tabs, filters and search;
  - a count of new changes in the nav;
  - select changes, then "Draft an entry";
  - edit, hide or restore a change;
  - "Read the sources now".
- Settings → Automation: the sources, the digest schedule (next and last run), the CI token and the GitHub secret, each shown once.
- The editor shows the changes an entry was made from.
- Fixes found along the way:
  - The Embed card picks the embed mount.
  - Bar links keep their button colours (the Sumi "New entry" button was blank).
  - On a phone, the bar's labels are visually hidden but still read by screen readers.

## MCP (`Tayori.MCP`, optional Sake)

The host mounts it in its own server with `mount Tayori.MCP, prefix: "tayori"`, next to Lotus.

- **Scopes:** `tayori:read` and `tayori:write`.
- **Access:** the app's resolver decides, as in the admin. With no resolver nobody gets in.
- **Tools:** `list_entries`, `get_entry`, `list_changes`, `list_categories`, `add_change`, `hide_change`, `draft_entry`, `create_entry`, `update_entry`, `publish_entry`, `unpublish_entry`, `request_upload`, `upload_image`.
- **Screenshots from a browser agent:**
  1. `request_upload` returns a single-use URL valid for 10 minutes. Only its hash is stored.
  2. The agent `curl`s the file to that URL. The bytes must be an image, up to the editor's limit.
  3. The agent puts the returned `[alt](url)` in an entry, where it becomes a Kotoba figure.
  - Nothing is ever fetched from a URL.
- Sake is left out of the oldest-dependencies (Phoenix 1.7) job, since Sake needs Phoenix 1.8. The fix is a separate Sake PR.

## Dev app and docs

- The dev app reads `dev/CHANGELOG.md` and `dev/news/` as real sources and mounts the machine API.
- New guides: one `guides/automation.md` (inbox, sources, CI, GitHub, digests, schedule, emails) and `guides/mcp.md`. README, CHANGELOG (0.1.0, unreleased), the AI guide and the notifications guide are updated.

## Checks

- `mix test` on SQLite and PostgreSQL: 523 passing.
- `mix format --check-formatted`, `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`, `mix credo --strict`, `mix dialyzer` and `mix docs` are clean.
- e2e in Chromium: 10/10, including the new inbox spec.

author: shunkakinoki
body: ## Summary - Removes the settings-level `WorktreeCreate`/`WorktreeRemove` hooks. The enabled worktrunk plugin already provides both, and it reads the created path from `wt switch --format=json`. - `rtk-rewrite.sh` no longer rewrites git commands when `agent_id` is present. Claude Code refuses `rtk git ...` inside a worktree-isolated subagent, so every rewritten git command failed there. Non-git rewrites in subagents are unchanged. ## Postmortem: worktree-isolated agents could not start or run git ### Impact - Every `isolation: 'worktree'` agent (Workflow or Agent tool) launched from a linked worktree failed at startup with `WorktreeCreate hook returned a path that is not a directory`. - A 4-lane implementation workflow failed instantly. It was relaunched without isolation, using hand-passed worktree paths. - After the startup fix, isolated agents still could not run git: every `git ...` came back as `rtk git ...` and the isolation guard refused it. ### Root causes 1. **Wrong path echoed.** The settings hook echoed `$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.worktrees/`. From a linked worktree, that is the linked worktree's root. worktrunk's `worktree-path` template uses `{{ repo_path }}`, the main checkout, so wt created the worktree somewhere other than the echoed path. 2. **Two creators per event.** The worktrunk plugin also registers `WorktreeCreate`/`WorktreeRemove`, so both hooks ran for every agent. - The plugin hook omits `--yes`, so the unapproved project `post-start` command failed non-interactively. - That failure cancelled the sibling hook mid-`git worktree add`, which left a half-initialized worktree locked as `initializing`. 3. **Rewrite vs guard.** The rtk PreToolUse rewrite turns `git ...` into `rtk git ...`. Claude Code's worktree-isolation guard cannot prove which checkout a wrapped git command targets, so it refuses the command. ### Detection - The first isolated workflow launch failed for all lanes. - Live probes then exposed the next layer each time: - a direct hook invocation from a linked worktree; - a 1-agent isolated Workflow, which failed on the plugin approval; - a second probe, which failed on the rtk guard; - a final probe, which passed. ### Fix - One owner for worktree lifecycle: the worktrunk plugin hooks. The duplicate settings hooks are deleted rather than patched. - The project's worktrunk commands are approved once with `wt config approvals add --yes` (machine-local `approvals.toml`), so the plugin hook runs without a prompt. - `rtk-rewrite.sh` passes git commands through unchanged for subagent calls (`agent_id` present). It still compresses them in main-thread calls. ### Verification - An isolated Workflow agent started in the main checkout's `.worktrees/`. - In that worktree it ran `pwd && git branch --show-current && git status --short` successfully. - `shellspec spec/rtk_rewrite_spec.sh spec/sync_rtk_rewrite_spec.sh`: 22 examples, 0 failures. `shellcheck` is clean. ### Follow-ups - When a project changes its worktrunk `post-start`/`post-create` commands, the approval goes stale. The plugin hook then fails again non-interactively until `wt config approvals add --yes` is re-run in that project. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes worktree-isolated Claude agents (Workflow and Agent tools) that failed at startup and could not run git commands. - Removes the settings-level `WorktreeCreate`/`WorktreeRemove` hooks, which duplicated the worktrunk plugin's hooks and echoed the wrong worktree path from linked checkouts. The plugin now owns worktree lifecycle. - `rtk-rewrite.sh` no longer rewrites git commands to `rtk git ...` in Claude subagent calls, since Claude Code refuses the wrapped command in isolated worktrees. Non-git rewrites are unchanged. **Migration** - Approve the project's worktrunk commands once with `wt config approvals add --yes`; if a project later changes its `post-start`/`post-create` commands, re-run the approval or agents fail non-interactively. Written for commit 6bc8154960e6956f45af428f632410b084acf916. Summary will update on new commits.

author: avatarsd
body:
## What

A slot server named each session `p<slot>`, which depends only on the slot's position. A session that lands in a reused slot therefore got its predecessor's name. If node A forwarded a subscription for the old session to node B, B kept a return route ending in A's `p<slot>`. After the slot was reused, B's deliveries along that route reached the new session, and B's edge was never reaped.

The session name now includes the tenancy generation that the slot's handle already held: **`p<slot>~<gen>`** (for example `p0~1`, then `p0~2`). I used `~` because `path::valid_segment` rejects `.`, and many existing peer names already contain `-`. Now, when B delivers along a route made for an earlier session, A finds no live peer with that name and refuses the delivery. The existing refused-route reclaim then removes B's edge.

## How

- `slot_server_t` (the tcp and ws listeners) and `httpd_ws_link_t` each use one formatter, built from the handle, both for the name they stamp at accept time and for `peer_name()`.
- `bus_link_t::peer_link(name)` matches only the exact current name. A name with a departed session's generation, or with no generation, resolves to nothing. This uses the exact string compare that was already there, so no branch was added.
- Session anchors stay keyed by **slot**: `fwd_router_t::session_anchor_id` applies the new `net::session_slot_of`. One slot still keeps one anchor however many sessions pass through it (the ADR-0044 amendment bound; `session_anchor_test` is green and unchanged apart from the expected names). The anchor revives in place, and its own generation still refuses an element minted for a departed session.
- New `bus_link_t::slot_link(slot)` is what an anchor uses to send to the slot's current session. By default it calls `peer_link`, which is correct for kinds whose names carry no generation. CAN's `n<node>` is unchanged; its peers have no tenancy to count.
- `child_registry_t::resolve_peer` now takes which bus lookup to use (default `peer_link`), so the router gains no branch. Core CCN total is 542 before and 542 after (`tools/check_ccn.py --base origin/main`).

## Test

`slot_reuse_reaps_forwarded_sub_test` is new. A runs a real peer-named TCP listener, and B is reached from A over an in-memory pipe. Session S1 subscribes to B through A, a control delivery reaches S1, then S1 hangs up and S2 lands in the same slot. The test checks:
- S2's name is fresh but has the same slot part;
- B's edge is reaped after B's next delivery;
- S2 receives **0** deliveries.

On unpatched code the test fails 4 checks: both sessions are named `p0`, S2 receives the deliveries meant for S1, and B's edge stays.

Tests and examples that expected the old `p<slot>` spelling were updated to the new one. Two cases inverted, because what they assert changed: a recycled slot used to keep its name and now gets a fresh one (`peer_handle_seam`, `httpd_ws_close_peer`).

## Checked locally

- default config: full ctest, 318/318
- bus-closed: ctest `-LE bus`, plus the new test skipping cleanly
- self-heal-closed: ctest `-LE selfheal`
- minimal module set
- `check_ccn.py`
- `check_doc_citations.py`
- `doxygen core/Doxyfile`
- `sphinx-build -n -W`

Not built here:
- gcc15: no toolchain on this host.
- TSan: left to CI.

## Perf

Not measured yet. The local A/A and A/B run was stopped before it started, because the host ran low on memory. The per-frame change is on the bus inbound path: `peer_name()` now formats two integers instead of one. Name lookups cost the same as before. Per-session RAM is unchanged on host (`kPeerNameChars` was already 24); the ESP slot name grows by 2 B per slot (22 to 24). A stored return route grows by `~<gen>`, typically 2 B. The in-process gate rows do not go through a slot server.

## Docs

Updated:
- core and ESP-IDF CHANGELOGs (Fixed);
- the reference pages, the module page, the multi-peer listener example and its page.

- ADR-0073 §2 has an amendment note for the `p<slot>~<gen>` spelling, and the ADR-0044 amendment's churn-bound row now says anchors are keyed by the slot part (`session_slot_of`).
- Leftover `p<slot>` comments in core, ESP and bench now say `p<slot>~<gen>`.

No conformance vector pins the spelling. Two things did depend on it:
- The TypeScript testbed checks (`mesh-testbed.test.mjs`, `topology.test.mjs`) matched `/^p\d+$/`. They now accept `p<slot>~<gen>`, and the `topology.ts` comments say so. Both run only in the `mesh-testbed` CI job, not locally.
- RFC-0031 §1 names the anchor by the peer name `p<slot>`. That text is left as written here and is handled separately.

RFC-0020 §3 reasons that "a segment naming a departed session is indistinguishable from one that never named anything". With a generation in the name that holds without exception, so the text is left as written.

## Arrival and late departure (#1609 follow-up)

- An arrival in a reused slot now evicts the edges, labels and pending awaits filed under the predecessor's name, `p<slot>~<gen-1>`. The bus spells that name from the arriving handle one generation down, which matches both slot servers (each claim advances the generation by one).
- `bus_peer_down` retires the slot-keyed anchor and drops the cached token only while the slot still belongs to the departing session: `slot_link(slot) == peer_link(name)`. A departure reported after a successor claimed the slot evicts its own name and leaves the successor's anchor alone.
- `edge_eviction_test` covers both with real `p<slot>~<gen>` names.
- Not done here: the anchor route still resolves its egress by slot (`slot_link`), not by the exact session name. Doing that needs per-anchor mutable storage for the name and is left as a follow-up.

author: zxsleebu
body:
On Plasma, `register()` rewrites `tokativ-input-method.desktop` whenever the running binary's path changes, but KWin never hears about it. KWin reads the entry's `Exec` only when `[Wayland] InputMethod` in kwinrc changes, and writing the same value sends no notification. So after a move (a build in `/tmp` replaced by the package after a reboot, or a switch from a source build to a package), KWin keeps running the old command, or runs nothing at all if that file is gone. The daemon then logs "KWin has not started Tokativ's input method yet" and pastes through the clipboard until someone toggles the virtual keyboard in System Settings.

Now, when the entry is rewritten and KWin has it selected, the daemon clears the setting and selects the entry again, both with `--notify`. KWin's `setInputMethodCommand` sees a different command and restarts the input method. A user who picked another virtual keyboard or none is left alone, because this only runs while ours is selected.

Tested on Plasma 6.8: with `/usr/bin/tokativ input-method` running, I started a build from `/tmp/tokativ-test`. The entry was rewritten, KWin started `/tmp/tokativ-test/tokativ input-method`, and the daemon connected to it within a second.

author: ah-merii
body:
In a project with a Rust crate under a pyrefly root, an ERROR toast "LSP[pyrefly]: file watcher failed: Couldn't watch new directory …/target<random>/: No such file or directory" could appear the first time the crate's `target/` was built, though nothing had failed. It also made the regression suite's `lsp_attach` check flaky: 5 of 10 runs failed on that toast on origin/main, through the harness's rule that any ERROR notification fails a check (`tests/regress/README.md:190`).

The cause: cargo creates `target/` under a temporary name and renames it (cargo `crates/cargo-util/src/paths.rs:748-784`). When inotifywait sees the new directory before the rename and tries to watch it after, it prints that line to stderr and keeps watching; the renamed `target/` is watched from its move event (inotify-tools 4.23.9.0 `src/inotifywait.cpp:426-441`). Neovim's inotify backend hands every stderr line to the watcher's `on_error` (`$VIMRUNTIME/lua/vim/_watch.lua:500-512`), and `vim.lsp._watchfiles` reports anything but `ENOENT:` as an ERROR (`lsp/_watchfiles.lua:93-108`). The config turns file watching on for Linux (`nvim/lua/lang/python.lua:31-33`), so the fix lives here: the watcher function is wrapped so that line alone never reaches `on_error`; any other inotifywait error is still reported.

The first commit only moves the existing watcher adjustment (6e53fce) into `nvim/lua/lsp/watchfiles.lua`, so a unit test can set it up without enabling every server. `tests/unit/lsp_watchfiles_test.lua` runs a server through the real `vim.lsp` with a fake `inotifywait` that prints errors, then a change: a vanished directory raises nothing and the change still reaches the server, while any other error in the same output is still one ERROR. All 4 cases failed before the fix.

Checked: `tests/unit/run.sh` (14 files); in the test image, `lsp_attach` 10 of 10 runs passing (5 of 10 before), and the full unit tier and suite passing.

Known effect: `:checkhealth vim.lsp` names the watcher backend "Custom" rather than "inotify", since the backend function is wrapped (`$VIMRUNTIME/lua/vim/lsp/health.lua:160-170`).

author: orengithub
body:
First step toward analyzing DSpace (Spring): get Java method annotations into the knowledge base.

## What changed

- **dhscanner-bitcode 2.2.0** — `Annotation` is now just a `Location`; `MethodContent` gains `methodAnnotations`. (Hackage revision 1 widens `dhscanner-ast` to `>= 1.4.0 && < 1.5`.)
- **dhscanner-kbgen 2.1.2** — exports the `CallableAnnotation` / `ClassAnnotation` / `Annotation` constructors; allows bitcode 2.2 and ast 1.4.
- **dhscanner-kbapi 1.1.3** — requires `dhscanner-ast >= 1.4.0 && < 1.5` (the `< 1.4` cap was blocking queryengine).
- **codegen 1.0.37** — each annotation is lowered as an ordinary call at its own location, so the annotation's FQN and args come from the existing call facts.
- **kbgen 1.0.43** — emits `kb_callable_has_annotation( Callable, Annotation )` for function and method annotations.
- **queryengine 1.0.64** — dependency bounds only.

## Resulting query shape

```prolog
kb_callable_has_annotation( Method, Annotation ),
kb_call_resolved( Annotation, 'org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping' ),
kb_arg_i_for_call( Url, 0, Annotation )
```

## Side effects

- Annotation calls appear as `kb_called_from( Annotation, Callable )`. Auth predicates require a 1st-party callee, so they are unaffected; `utils_control_flow_reaches_sink_fqn` may list annotation FQNs, which its callers already filter.
- Python / TS decorators that are calls (e.g. `@app.route("/x")`) now also produce call facts.

## Not yet verified

No end-to-end run on a DSpace controller yet: the KB output for a real `@RequestMapping` method has not been inspected.

author: jorgemenadev
body:
Each Projects ticket proved its own part, but nothing proved the whole loop, from a chief's request to a verified pull request. Review round 1 found the loop also stalled: after the engineer opened its draft PR, nothing woke the project agent, so a person had to say "Verify task #1" and then "Mark task #1 done". The README also read as if a repo needs a committed project file, and called engineers "workers" in places. #65 asks for one end-to-end proof, offline and by hand, and a docs pass.

Part of #57. Closes #65.

```
chief:        send_to_project ──▶ task #1 (Accepted)      message_project ──▶ same task, same chat
coordinator:  update_task in_progress (Working)           dispatch_worker #1 (its brief has the follow-up)
engineer:     clone → setup → push (approved) → create_pull_request (approved) → draft PR (Pull request opened)
control:      system line "Engineer for task #1 ended: opened <PR>. Continue the task: …"
coordinator:  dispatch_verifier → fresh computer, checkout <head> → report_verdict pass (Verified PASS @head)
control:      system line "Verifier for task #1 ended: PASS for <PR> at <sha>: …. Continue the task: …"
coordinator:  update_task done → done rule: PASS for the current head → Done
restart:      the cards replay the same; handoff_status → done, PR link, engineer and verifier, PASS @head, not stale
```

## What changed

- **The task goes on by itself.** When an engineer or a verifier ends (finished, blocked or failed; not stopped), control queues one turn for the coordinator in the chat of the member who requested the task. It is paid as that member's own turns are, so it follows the workspace's billing mode: their seat, or the organization's Copilot. The chat shows it as a system line, not as their message.
  - The text says how the worker ended: the PR it opened, its report, `blocked: <reason>`, or the verdict with its PR, sha and summary. Then: "Continue the task: dispatch the verifier on its PR, send fixes for ISSUES, or mark it done after a current PASS."
  - One turn per ending, keyed by the worker id in a new `task_continuations` table. A restart neither repeats nor loses it: `recover` queues the endings a stop cut short. When the table is first created, the workers that had already ended count as continued, so an upgrade starts no burst of turns.
  - At most 6 per task. After that, each ending sets the task to **Needs input** with "Automatic steps used up: tell the project how to go on."
  - Nothing is queued for a task that is done or abandoned, or whose requester left the workspace.
  - A queued continuation never reopens a closed task. A member's **Mark done** (or any close) ends the task's queued continuations. The scheduler also ends any whose task closed before it claims a turn. Coordinator turns record the task a system turn continues (`coordinator_turns.task_number`).
  - A member's message is refused only while one of their own messages is unfinished. Behind a continuation it queues, and the composer stays free while the continuation waits.
  - Contracts: a `system-message` chat event. The desktop folds it into a notice, which the project chat shows as a muted line with an info icon, and which starts a new turn in the chat's tool folding. The coordinator's instructions say what these turns are.
- **Offline end-to-end test**, `apps/control/src/chiefToVerifiedPr.test.ts`. It runs the loop above on the existing fixtures: `startTestControl`, the fake Copilot, fake computers, the fake GitHub, and real git through control's git proxy. It sends no "Verify" or "done" message: the continuations reach Done on their own. It has no sleeps: after the restart it waits for the final card.
- **README manual check "a chief's request ends in a verified PR"**: the six acceptance steps in one run of 9 live calls on a throwaway repo, plus a 3-call verifier on a real web app. That is 12 in all, and the check states its exception: it is the spec's single end-to-end run, so it may go over the handful-per-ticket rule. The push that makes the verdict stale lands while the verifier works, so the verifier's own continuation finds it and the task stays open. Deleting the project is then checked with the engineer's and verifier's computers still there: 9 Docker objects, then 0.
- **Docs pass**:
  - What the project agent can and cannot do, as two bullets.
  - A "who uses each key" table, covering how the file, the settings and the secrets combine.
  - **The task goes on by itself**, a new paragraph.
  - A "Not yet" list: repo hosts reached with a personal token, token sign-in, and proxy and CA settings. It says a public repo can be read without the repo app, while private access and every write need it.
  - The handoff check uses the member's **Mark done** override instead of asking the coordinator to close an unverified task.
  - The engineer, verifier, watch and deploy checks account for the turn after each ending.
  - "Worker" becomes engineer or verifier wherever people read it. Code names (`dispatch_worker`, `chiefbot-worker_…`) stay.

## Text removed or moved

- The "two members" check no longer commits a `chiefbot.project.yaml`. The file is optional.
- "Engineers run on the standard computer image: rebuild it…" is gone: the setup paragraph already says an old image blocks the engineer.
- "…and its last message becomes its result" is gone: the setup paragraph says the task shows its last message.
- "A task has one worker at a time…" is now one sentence in **Engineers**.
- The verifier paragraph's "arrives stale" sentences moved into **The done rule**.
- "`handoff_status` gives the same verdict" is folded into the sentence that lists what `handoff_status` returns.
- The coordinator paragraph's tool list moved into the "can" bullet. That list said "four worker tools", but there are five.
- The prose on which agent uses which key became the table. Every key and every reader in it is unchanged.
- The chief-to-PR check's second full run on a real app is now the verifier only, and its status and stale steps cost no extra call.

## Evidence

- `bun run check` passed twice in a row on `df1b0c6`, which includes `integration/projects` at `3232036`. Typecheck is clean. 580 tests pass, 2 skip and 0 fail, across 92 files (572 before this PR's reviews). check-public is clean. Neither run printed the teardown "fatal: '.' does not appear to be a git repository".
- New tests, written red first:
  - `taskWorkers.test.ts`:
    - An engineer's ending wakes the agent in the requester's chat, paid as their turns are, as a system line, and not in another member's chat.
    - One ending wakes it once across a restart, and an ending a stop cut short is queued when control starts.
    - Seven endings give six turns, then **Needs input**.
    - In an org-paid workspace the continuation runs on the organization's Copilot.
    - The review's case: a continuation is queued, then the member clicks **Mark done**. The agent never gets the continuation, and the task stays done.
    - The member's only unfinished turn is a queued continuation, and their message is accepted and runs after it.
  - `chatRows.test.ts`: a notice starts a turn, so the continuation's tool calls don't fold into the turn before. `chat.test.ts`: a `system-message` folds into a notice and leaves the composer free.
- One existing restart test lets the verifier's continuation run before control stops, so the next held turn is the member's own.
- Hardening:
  - The fake GitHub removes its repos only once every in-flight `git http-backend` run is over, which ends the teardown "fatal".
  - `task_continuations` is created and backfilled in one transaction.
- The end-to-end test passed 15 runs in a row, and the three continuation tests 10 in a row.
- Project chat with both system lines, light and dark: `/tmp/chiefbot-ui/continuation-chat-light.png`, `/tmp/chiefbot-ui/continuation-chat-dark.png`. They come from the real renderer with a stubbed `window.chiefbot`.
- The manual check was not run: it needs

author: agulaya24
body:
Stability fixes, one per commit, each with a test that failed on the old code first.

**Similarity**
- `chromadb_dist_to_similarity` reads Chroma's l2 distance as squared (`1 - d/2`) and ip as `1 - dot`. The old l2 formula inflated every similarity (30 degrees apart: true 0.866, reported 0.964); ip inverted the ranking. Checked against real in-memory Chroma collections of each space.
- `semantic_search.search_conversations` converted with a literal `1 - distance`; it now goes through the converter with `collection_space`. A grep of `src/` for every distance-to-similarity conversion found no other literal.

**Behaviour change to know about:** a collection created with `hnsw:space=cosine` is unaffected. A `memory_facts` store built before that metadata existed has no `hnsw:space` and reads as l2, so on those stores AUDN dedup now reports lower similarity (the true cosine) and keeps more facts as new instead of folding them into an existing one. Messages and summary collections of that age change the same way.

**Spend and batches**
- Batch submit honours `BASELAYER_SPEND_CEILING_USD` against the batch's worst case.
- `distill_batch --resume` refuses requests whose serialized hash differs from the submitted batch (`--leaf-spans` and similar flags changed prompts without changing any checked field).
- `convergence` submits its batch with retries off and writes `batch.json` atomically.
- `estimate_cost` prices from the dated spend table; the stale `llm_provider.PRICING` table is removed.
- Model-staleness findings: authoring and compose calls go through the per-model sampling filter; the freshness check derives the newest model per family from the dated rate tables; `spend.py` moves to the 2026-10-20 price table (a billed run asks the operator to confirm it).

**Traceability, MCP, consolidation**
- Traceability step 5b embeds missing fact vectors (it called the message embedder before).
- MCP tool output kept off stdout; first stdio end-to-end test of the server.
- `trace_claim` hides facts the user forgot.
- Consolidation API backend streams, so 32K-token builders can run.

**Test infrastructure**
- pytest imports this checkout's `src/` (pyproject `pythonpath`), and `tests/conftest.py` refuses to run when `baselayer` resolves elsewhere; child processes inherit `src` on `PYTHONPATH`. CI installs with `pip install -e ".[dev]"` from the repo root, so the editable target is this checkout and the guard passes.
- Batch-test fixture fakes `chromadb.config`, so that test passes run alone.

- The MCP stdio test keeps stdin open until every reply arrives (mcp 1.30 cancels in-flight requests on EOF, which failed the first CI run). Holding stdin open exposed a defect also present on main: on Windows the first `recall_memories` call stalls until stdin receives more input. Not fixed here; pinned as a strict xfail on win32 (it passes on Linux CI).

Full suite locally with API keys unset: 1801 passed, 7 skipped, 2 xfailed (at the commit before the stdio test change; that test file passes under mcp 1.26 and 1.30). CI: 1802 passed on 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12.
