body:
## What and why

The after-scan workflow (record the scan, refresh smart collections, raise events, tell profiles of new titles, ask for subtitles) and the picture backfills lived in `cmd/photon-server/tasks.go`, untested, while every other job handler lives in its package. The job is now `(*scan.Scanner).Job`, taking a small hub interface declared in `scan`, and the backfills are `(*artwork.Cache).FetchUnfetched` and `HashUnhashed`, beside `Sweep`. `cmd` only wires them. Behaviour is unchanged.

## How it was verified

- `TestAScanThatAddsTitlesTellsProfilesAndAsksForSubtitles` (integration) covers the job. `TestEveryUnfetchedPictureIsFetched` and `TestEveryUnhashedPictureIsHashed` each run one item past a batch, so a backfill that stopped after its first page fails.
- `go test -race` and the integration runs of artwork, scan and cmd pass. `golangci-lint fmt` and `golangci-lint run` are silent.

## Checklist

- [x] It needs to exist now: no code for a future need, no knob nobody turns, no interface with one implementation.
- [x] It is not already here: the repo and the standard library were searched, and nothing now does the same job twice.
- [x] The shape is idiomatic: concrete returns, consumer-side interfaces, ctx first, enums for modes.
- [x] Each error is handled once: handled or returned, wrapped only where the words help.
- [x] Every goroutine has an owner and a stop; tests pass under `-race`.
- [ ] A test fails without this change, and it tests behaviour a client or operator would notice, not the code restated. A refactor, so behaviour is unchanged; the new tests cover what had none.
- [x] It is one concern and small; refactors are in their own PR.
- [x] Comments only where something is surprising; every `//nolint` names its linter and says why.
- [x] Any new dependency is justified in this description.
- [x] Nothing here needs a later PR to undo or complete it.

## Out of scope

Nothing.

author: rickybusse15
body:
Third slice of R2 (vegetation) in `docs/WORLD_REALISM_PLAN.md`. **Stacked on #261 → #258**: until those merge, this diff includes their commits. The new work is a32cd1b.

## What it adds
- **Line of sight through trees** (`visibility::los_with_trees`; without trees it is exactly `los`).
  - A trunk stops the ray like a building, with `blocker_type` `"trunk"`.
  - Each crown crossed dims the ray by its Beer–Lambert optical depth. The dimming multiplies into the forest stands' transmittance, and the crown counts as vegetation for the first hit, so three dense crowns in a row fall under the hard-block threshold.
  - The run's `SharedVisibility` carries the trees, so every sight line (bearing sensors, follow controllers) sees them.
- **Range scanner returns from trees** (`SharedVisibility::first_return`).
  - A trunk returns as structure.
  - At each crown a ray enters, in order, one uniform draw `u` stops it `-ln(1−u)/(k·d)` metres in. If that point is inside the crown and short of anything harder, the ray returns **canopy** there; otherwise it continues.
  - So a crown returns with probability 1 − T, where T is the transmittance `los` gives along the same ray. A test over 20,000 draws agrees to within 1 %.
  - The draws come from their own stream, keyed by node and tick, and none are drawn in a world without trees.
- **Belief: canopy as soft structure.** Per cell, the belief keeps the highest canopy return and a count. The cell counts as seen but is never occupied, so nothing collides with a crown.
  - The canopy arrays are allocated at the first canopy return, so a run without trees checkpoints byte for byte as before.
  - The replay carries `canopy_updates` (`[i, j, top_cm]`, written when first seen or when the top moves 10 cm), range-scan `canopy` points and `mapping_state.belief.canopy_cells`. Each is written only when there are some.
  - `structure_precision` counts a believed structure on a trunk's cell as right. Recall still covers buildings and walls only.
- `docs/migration/UNKNOWN_WORLD.md` is updated: canopy is no longer dropped.

## Measured
Before is #261 at 8ec018d; after is this PR. All runs are release builds on this Mac.

**Line of sight.** The canonical target scenarios were run with `trees: true`; observations over the run:

| scenario | seed 7 | seed 42 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| intercept_stress | 2810 → 2776 | 2888 → 2852 |
| sar_person_search | 205 → 193 | 104 → 52 |
| search_acquisition | 1246 → 1246 | 1013 → 1013 |

`search_acquisition` is unchanged: it is urban, and its trees stand on scrub away from the targets.

**No-prior mapping.** Tree scenario (medium, default terrain, 3 drones, 8 POIs, `trees` + `tree_inspection` + `safety_blocking`), efficient_v1, `--world-knowledge none`:

| | seed 7 | seed 42 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| canopy cells (of 15,246) | 0 → 6,936 | 0 → 7,012 |
| trunk cells believed structure | 0 → 40 (precision 1.0) | 0 → 30 (precision 1.0) |
| ground RMSE | 0.17 → 0.22 m | 0.18 → 0.21 m |
| POIs inspected | 8/8 | 8/8 |
| world contacts | 0 | 0 |

**With a prior map and no targets,** every frame is identical.

## Evidence
- `scripts/replay_hashes.py --check` against a record taken on main (2522930): **14/14 identical**.
- Tests:
  - `cargo test -p argusnet-sim -p argusnet-world`: all pass. Clippy on the whole workspace with `-D warnings`, and `fmt --check`: pass.
  - New tests: crowns along a ray; line of sight through crowns, the threshold, trunks, and a nearer wall against a trunk; `first_return` covering no draws without trees, the Beer–Lambert share and the stop depth, trunk against crown, and nothing returned or drawn past a trunk; the scanner's classes and its canopy stream; the belief canopy rows and checkpoint, and that it is never occupied.
  - An integration test runs a no-prior jungle map with trees. Canopy rows, points and cells appear, trunk-structure precision is 1.0, and a resume from a checkpoint matches the straight run frame for frame.
- **Mutation round:** 20 hand-applied mutants. 10 were killed at first; the tests above were added for the survivors, and a second pass killed 8 more. Two survive:
  - Keeping an empty tree layer as `Some`. This is equivalent: an empty layer meets nothing.
  - The trunk-radius filter in the trunk-cell truth used for the precision figure. Every generated tree has a trunk.

## Next
- Flight: trunks are hard to physics, crowns are a soft keep-out for efficient_v1, and crown contacts are recorded. This is ready on a stacked branch.
- Drawing in the viewer.

author: raghavs6
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"raghavs6"} -->
_Requested by **Raghav** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01ELPZ4JAABYwAEhXpr3dMRd?thread=cmsg_01ELPZ4JAABYwAEhXpr3dMRd1NZZdrcJr9kNDPJv432Yns)_

Before: agents sharing one token kept sending to the fake GitHub after the budget was gone, with 8–202 primary-limit 403s per bench run at 1× load and above. The repo also had no license.

After: `bin/quotad -upstream <api>` is a proxy that agents point their base URL at. It learns each token's budget from `x-ratelimit-*` headers and holds requests once the budget is gone. In the bench through quotad, **primary 403s are 0 in all 50 runs at every demand**, and utilization stays at 99–100%. Results: [docs/step2-results.md](docs/step2-results.md). Design (signed off): [docs/governor-step2.md](docs/governor-step2.md). The repo is now Apache-2.0 (`LICENSE`).

As the design said up front, step 2 doesn't fix secondary-limit 429s. Header-aware agents end up with *more* 429 violations through quotad (924 against 802 at 2×), because quotad's `Retry-After` sends every turned-away agent back at the same reset moment, where they trip the concurrency limit. That's step 3.

## How

- **`internal/budget`** (reserve, then correct): a request takes a unit before it's sent, and the response's headers correct the count. Within a window, the lowest `remaining` seen wins, so a late response can't raise it. Before any headers have been seen, one request goes out and the rest wait for it. Held requests are released in arrival order at reset + guard, and turned away with `Retry-After` once they can't be served within the max hold. A request that fails without an answer stays counted. Time and timers are injected, so the tests are exact.
- **`internal/proxy` + `cmd/quotad`**: `httputil.ReverseProxy`, with one budget per `Authorization` header. `ModifyResponse` corrects the budget, `ErrorHandler` marks a request failed, and quotad answers its own 429 without touching the upstream.
- **`cmd/bench -proxy`** starts quotad between loadgen and fakegithub. Violations are still counted by fakegithub. The max hold is `window/120` (GitHub's 30s per hour, scaled down).
- **Utilization fix** (51ff565): the first bench through quotad showed exactly 75% in many runs. A 4th window opened in a run's last seconds was being charged a full window's budget. Utilization now counts only windows that reset inside the run. I reran the baselines with the fix, and `docs/step1-baselines.md` is updated.

## Verification

- `gofmt -l .` is empty, `go vet ./...` is clean, and `go test -race ./...` passes.
- The budget unit tests cover the step 2 doc's checks: learning first, holding when reservations use up `remaining`, stale responses not raising the count, release order at reset, too-long waits turned away (`Retry-After` rounded up), a client giving up and leaving the line, failed requests staying spent, and a failed probe letting the next request learn.
- The proxy tests put quotad in front of the real fake server. 8 concurrent requests on a budget of 3 all succeed with 0 violations, and a too-long wait gets quotad's 429 without reaching the upstream.
- Full bench: 50 runs through quotad and 50 baseline runs, all at 60s windows.

author: villebase
body:
Closes #897.

## What changes

- The run document carries the config's warnings as text (`warnings_text`, never serialised). `report_config_warnings` fills it and `diagnostics[]` together, and replaces `config_diagnostics` at all 17 call sites.
- The emitter prints them under every verb's text, before the hints, in the same block shape (`notices.render_warnings`). The config views (`config show`, `config validate`, `target list`) no longer print their own copy, so they print it once. `config validate` still counts the warnings in its summary, and its install warnings go in the same block.
- A run that fails prints the warnings to stderr before the error line. The verbs report warnings after their I/O, so when a verb raised first, the warnings come from the loaded file. A run that cannot reach the store is the usual case: W051 is often the reason it failed.
- A declined `account reset-password` prints its text and then aborts. It sets `warnings_shown`, so the warnings are not printed a second time.
- `03-json-output.md` has a new section, *Config warnings in text output*.

## Real run (tier-1 stack)

```
$ VAULT_ADDR=http://localhost:8200 sopuli --config sopuli.yaml lock status
config: sopuli.yaml
mode:   cas

LOCK                     STATE     HOLDER              COMMAND      SINCE                        EXPIRES
vault-dev:acme/dev/acme  released  ville@Awesominator  creds apply  2026-10-20T17:29:33.829030Z  2026-10-20T17:44:33.829030Z

0 of 1 declared lock paths held

1 warning:
  VAULT_ADDR sets the address of vault 'vault-dev' to http://localhost:8200, not http://127.0.0.1:8200, which vaults.vault-dev.addr declares
    hint: unset VAULT_ADDR if it is left over from other work; to choose the address for this tool on purpose, use SOPULI_VAULT_ADDR or --vault-addr
```

```
$ VAULT_ADDR=http://127.0.0.1:8399 sopuli --config sopuli.yaml lock status
1 warning:
  VAULT_ADDR sets the address of vault 'vault-dev' to http://127.0.0.1:8399, not http://127.0.0.1:8200, which vaults.vault-dev.addr declares
    hint: unset VAULT_ADDR if it is left over from other work; to choose the address for this tool on purpose, use SOPULI_VAULT_ADDR or --vault-addr
sopuli: could not reach the store: [WinError 10061] No connection could be made because the target machine actively refused it
  hint: check `addr`, and `tls.ca_file` if the certificate is your own CA
```

`creds status` and `config validate` print the same block once. With no `VAULT_ADDR`, the output does not change.

## Not in this PR

With `--output json`, the document of a run that fails before the verb reports its warnings has no W051 in `diagnostics[]`. The cause is the same, but the change is to the JSON, so it is a separate issue.

## Tests

`tests/test_config_warnings_text.py`: a non-config verb prints the warning; each config verb prints it once, including when a selector matches nothing; the JSON document carries the warning and no `warnings_text`; a failing run prints it on stderr, both before and after the verb reports. The view-level test that `render_target_list` renders warnings is removed, because the view no longer renders them. The full suite passes locally.

author: ecarlste
body:
Drops the external "living design doc" and its export step: `docs/DESIGN.md` becomes the source of truth for the agreed design, edited through PRs like everything else. Every design change needs Erik's sign-off, whoever proposes it; only then does it go into `DESIGN.md`. Erik no longer has to copy changes over and re-export.

## Changes

- **`docs/PROJECT.md`**:
  - `DESIGN.md` is the source of truth (overview and "Planning docs").
  - New workflow rule: ideas move through three stages. Brainstorming stays in research notes and the plan's "Ideas and maybe"; agreed choices go into `DESIGN.md`; features about to be built get a spec. Undecided ideas don't go in `DESIGN.md` or specs.
  - Erik signs off every design change, whoever proposes it (Claude, another developer, a research spike). Proposals go in a "Design proposals" section of the PR description or in chat; `DESIGN.md` is edited only after explicit agreement, and a PR that changes it says so, so design changes are never buried in other work.
  - Erik decides each piece of a proposal: **accept** (into `DESIGN.md`), **keep iterating** (stays in research or "Ideas and maybe"), or **reject** (moves to `docs/rejected/`, with a rejection notice at the top of its file: date, one-line reason, links to the full reasons and to the reopening steps). Reopening a rejected idea needs Erik's approval, then it moves back into research. Check `rejected/` before proposing an idea.
  - "Planning docs" lists `rejected/`; "Keeping docs in sync" gains rows for rejecting and reopening an idea.
  - Design discussions happen in chat, not in an external doc.
  - "Keeping docs in sync": an agreed design choice updates `DESIGN.md` in a PR, replacing "list the changes for the living design doc". A new row: design changes not yet signed off go in the PR's "Design proposals" list, not `DESIGN.md`. The key-decisions row points at `DESIGN.md` too.
- **`docs/DESIGN.md`**: header no longer says it's an export; it says changes need Erik's sign-off, and where unsettled ideas live. No design content changed.
- **`docs/rejected/README.md`** (new): steps for rejecting an idea and for reopening one (needs Erik's approval, drops the notice), and the index of rejected ideas (empty for now).
- **`docs/rejected/_template.md`** (new): the file layout for a rejected idea. The rejection notice sits at the top, so moving the proposal back into research in a PR means visibly deleting it, which makes accidental moves hard to miss.
- **`docs/research/README.md`**: notes' ideas become design proposals in the PR description, and go into `DESIGN.md` only once Erik signs off.
- **`docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`**: the spike 1 item "reflect findings back into the design doc" now says `DESIGN.md`.

## Review closely

- The sign-off wording in `PROJECT.md` (Workflow): does it cover other developers' proposals the way you want?

## Not done

- The "For the living design doc" lists in earlier PRs (e.g. #24) aren't applied to `DESIGN.md`; they're still ideas, not agreed choices.

author: vilenarios
body:
## Summary

Layout **`l2-2`** for `parquet-l2` bands: two files derived per band for tag names the publisher chooses, so an app-level client (the ArDrive explorer) stops scanning whole bands.

- **`lookup_key.parquet`**: for each value of the index's `keyTags` (`Drive-Id`, `Parent-Folder-Id`, …), the heights at which items carry it and how many (`name8, val8, height, items`, sorted by key). A drive spread over a year is found in a row group or two, then only the `tags` row groups at those heights are read. `lookup_tag` gave only first and last height, between which a wide drive cost the whole band (43% of drives with ≥ 20 records span > 10k blocks).
- **`stats.parquet`**: items and bytes per 1,000 heights, in all (empty `name`/`value`) and by each value of the index's `statTags` (`App-Name`, `Content-Type`, `Entity-Type`). "Bytes a month by app" over the whole index is then a read of the small files alone.
- Configured per index in `INDEX_EXPORT_L2_INDEXES` (`keyTags`, `statTags`, optional, each name once in UTF-8 byte order, at most 16), recorded in `band.json`, left out of the band's id.
- **Upgrade in place.** Every band built is `l2-2`. A published `l2-1` band, or an `l2-2` band derived for other tag names, has the two files derived from its own tables in the work directory, checked, moved in, and its `band.json` replaced by a rename: same id, no file already in the band touched, no source read, no header check, before any build and outside the time budget (`derived` in the report, `index_export_runs_total{kind="derive"}`). Mirrors `runL1Derive`. Held to `--range`; a dry run derives and changes nothing.
- Readers accept `l2-1` and `l2-2`; the subscriber footer-checks the two files by the band's tag names; `index-l2-verify` checks them as it checks the other lookups (`files`, `lookups`).
- Docs: `index-publication.md` (layout + SQL), `index-export.md` (config, derive, upgrade order), `envs.md`, CHANGELOG.

Band dates needed no change: `band.json` `createdAt` is already the top block's time.

## Rollout (turbo-gateway.com)

Subscribers first (an `l2-1`-only sidecar refuses `l2-2` bands and keeps its copy), then gw1's `index-swarm` and `index-export` with `keyTags`/`statTags` set. The next run upgrades all 23 `ardrive-l2` bands in place: two `tags` sorts per band, about an hour for h1.8M. Subscribers fetch the two files and `band.json` per band.

## Test plan

- [x] `src/lib/parquet-l2/*` (layout, lookups, verify-bands), `src/index-export/kinds/parquet-l2/*`, `config.test.ts`, `service-l2.test.ts` (derive in place: same id, tables untouched, before builds; tags changed; dry run; `--range`), `service-l1.test.ts`, `service.test.ts`, `index-swarm/kinds/parquet-l2.test.ts`, `l2-end-to-end.test.ts` (an `l2-2` band publishes, installs byte for byte, lookups verify): 171/171
- [x] eslint + prettier on every touched file
- [ ] After merge: dry run on gw1 (`--once --dry-run --range 1300000-1399999`) reports `derived` for h1.3M; then the real run and `index-l2-verify` clean

body:
Finding f-ff4ce040. Stacked on #328 (fix/seed-teaches-core-rule).

**Problem.** BIBLE s9.6 item 3: the Seed "teaches the boss's core rule with no stakes". A floor Window's field Combo fires onto the Payoff actor itself (`Payoff.TryClosePayoffOnFloor`), and the frozen `content/data/combos.json` row `seedbloom-field` ("Death Bloom (field)") is 120 physical damage, so the player who closes the Seed's Death Bloom is hit for 120.

**Fix (content, not a sim rule).** A C#-only row in `game/content/data/combo-riders.json` replaces `seedbloom-field`'s effects with none. Riders exist for exactly this: BIBLE effects the frozen oracle root `combos.json` cannot say. The Combo still fires, so the Seed bonus is still awarded. The field-Combos-apply-to-the-closer rule is unchanged, and so are the Warden's Lock Combos (`lock-*`, damage on the boss). `content/data/` is not touched, so the oracle fixtures do not move.

**Tests.** `game/sim/Keyrun.Sim.Tests/Encounter/SeedBloomNoStakesTests.cs` builds the ComboTables from the real content files the same way `HostRunSetup.ToComboTables` does (riders replace effects, and a `*` row fans out over the other classes):
- closing the seedbloom Window does no damage to the closer, and the Combo still earns the Seed bonus (red before the fix);
- control: the boss's Lock Combo (`lock-cinder`) still deals 200 to the Lock carrier;
- control: a player floor Window's field Combo (`hymn-field`) still applies to its closer.

`ComboRiderTests`' rider inventory now includes `seedbloom-field`, and a new case asserts that its rider is empty while the `combos.json` row stays verbatim.

author: cristianorevil
body:
## Problem
With `cursor-agent` 2026.07.23, every Cursor turn fails with:

> error: Cursor rejected model "grok-4.7-low" via session/set_model: Invalid params

Newer CLI builds accept only their own ACP ids in `session/set_model` (e.g. `grok-4.7[context=256k,reasoning_effort=high,fast=true]`) and answer `-32602 Invalid model value` to the slugs from `cursor-agent models`, including `auto`.

## Fix
The model is already pinned through argv `--model`, and that still works. `session/set_model` was meant to be best effort, so `-32602` is now ignored like `-32601`. A model that doesn't exist still makes the spawn fail, so this hides no real error.

## Tested
- Raw ACP probe against `cursor-agent` 2026.07.23: `set_model` rejects slugs, while `--model` selects the model (`currentModelId` changes).
- `swift build`, plus the ACP/Cursor tests (`swift test --filter "ACP|Cursor"`).
- Not tested: a live turn through the fixed engine, `parity/all.sh`, the full `swift test` suite.

## Known gap
With `--model grok-4.7-low` the CLI reports `reasoning_effort=high`. Over ACP, `set_model` accepts only one variant per model, so the effort level can't be set that way.

author: renanabade
body:
## What

- Difficulty and friction weights on every order, a tier on every restriction, and a budget per difficulty
  and length; candidates are drawn with a weighted shuffle biased by difficulty.
- The accumulated curse is built in layers, one per difficulty.
- `generateGroup` and `--players`: one challenge for players of different skill, same orders, eased numbers.
- Deaths range 60-90 / 20-35 / 6-12 / 0-2; 0 reads "Do not die".
- The manual writes milestones as actions ("until you defeat Taurus Demon") and defines its key words.

## Why

Product decisions are now judged by player profile. The easy level could draw the heaviest orders, the
extreme level could not ask for a deathless run, and friends of different skill could not share one run.
ADR 0004 has the alternatives.

## How it was tested

- Budget: easy challenges have a lower mean order weight than extreme ones, light-only curses, capped friction.
- Group: for four seeds and all four difficulties, same orders, every number never harder for an easier
  player, nested curses, each challenge valid; the hardest player gets exactly the solo challenge.
- Manual: "Do not die" for 0 deaths, definitions only for the words the challenge uses, milestone phrasing.
- The 40-seed phase C test still passes. Checked a group manual by hand.

## Checklist

- [x] `pnpm check` passes
- [x] Commits follow Conventional Commits
- [x] Docs, schema or ADR updated, if this changes them

body:
CAUSE ETABLIE EN EXECUTANT `classify()`, et non en relisant le source : sur les
trois fiches que `ab` a rapportees depuis la SORTIE, `route_none_of`, `route_of`,
`excluded_of` et `refusal_of` rendent tous `None`, `content` est la chaine vide,
et la chute `if measured: return "faisable"` rend ('faisable', '2026-09-11').
Les trois declarent leur fait dans `witness:`, un champ que `classify()` ne
consulte JAMAIS, et `refusal_of()` ne lit que des lignes portant un 403/429/451 :
ni un NXDOMAIN ni un `Disallow: /` ecrit n'y matchent. La page envoyait donc
construire un adaptateur sur deux noms qui ne resolvent pas et sur un hote que
la borne 1 ferme a TOUTES les voies, navigateur compris.

DISTRIBUTION DE LA BRANCHE SUR LE CORPUS, 550 fiches : 106 `faisable`, dont 89
declarent `content: measured …`, 12 declarent `content: out-of-domain …`, et 5
n'ont AUCUNE ligne `content:` — bestjobs-mg, emploimali, jobmada, plus
saudi-labour-platforms et wantedly, deux de plus sur la meme branche. Le compte
recoupe celui d'`ab` a l'unite : ses cinq cellules sont ESP 2, deja
`indetermine`, plus MDG 2 et MLI 1.

LE PLANCHER EST POSITIF ET IL PORTE SUR UN CHAMP : `faisable` exige une ligne
`content:` declaree, son absence rend `indetermine`. Pas la prose — #1136 l'a
retiree expres, une exclusion etant une DECLARATION et jamais une INTERPRETATION
— et pas une fermeture : ecrire `route: none` sur un hote que NOUS jugeons mort
est un verdict reserve au proprietaire (§2 sexies), et un indetermine n'est pas
un renoncement mais une mesure a refaire. Le cas SANS date reste `reverifier`.

MOUVEMENT DES DEUX TERMES, lu en lancant les DEUX versions du generateur sur les
pages touchees : quatre pages bougent (ML, MG, SA, JP), cinq cellules, et AUCUN
denominateur ne bouge — `fait / faisable` reste 1/4, 2/4, 5/6, 7/8 et
`fait / total` est intact, parce que les indetermines COMPTENT dans faisable. Ce
qui bouge est la ligne `mesure sans refus` (-1) et le `dont N indetermine(s)`
(+1). CZ sert de temoin : zero ecart.

ET LA MESURE A TROUVE UN SECOND FAUX QUE CE CORRECTIF ALLAIT AGGRAVER : la ligne
`INDETERMINES` glosait « refus consigne avec sa date », ce qui est faux des cinq
fiches neuves — elles n'ont aucun refus. La phrase etait DEJA fausse avant ce
commit, pour une autre raison : la fixture `shell` declare
`content: indeterminate` et ne consigne aucun refus, et un test EPINGLAIT la
phrase sur elle. Une glose fausse sur un verdict juste ne contredit rien, donc
elle se corrige dans le meme geste : la ligne nomme desormais ses TROIS sources,
dans le rendu Markdown et dans la docstring de tete qui les enumere. Les deux
assertions sont mises a jour ; les fixtures, elles, atteignent toujours leur
branche et ne changent pas.

LA GARDE PORTE SA PREUVE D'EXERCICE : trois cas, rouges tous les trois avant le
correctif — corpus, fixture et GLOSE lue par `status_of()`, puisque le defaut
rapporte est une PHRASE dans une cellule publiee. Le cas du corpus compte la
population des fiches muettes et rend NON EXERCE si elle est vide, au lieu de
passer par vacuite (§4 ter, cinquieme espece).

**Mutations, sur une copie et jamais dans l'arbre partage — chaque rouge vient d'une assertion NOMMEE :**

```
M1  le plancher RETIRE (etat d'avant)      3 rouges : corpus, fixture, GLOSE de cellule
M2  le plancher TROP LARGE                  3 rouges : `declare` cesse d'etre faisable,
                                            et DEUX tests de page preexistants tirent aussi
M3  la glose d'AVANT restauree              2 rouges : les deux assertions de la ligne
```

*M3 est instructive en sens inverse : mon cas de glose n'y tire PAS, parce qu'il asserte la cellule rendue par `status_of()` et non la ligne des cinq nombres. Deux surfaces, deux gardes, et c'est la classe preexistante qui tient la seconde.*

author: mjcarroll
body:
## Description

`__rmw_send_response` waits for the response writer to match the client's response reader before replying, because a response sent before the match is lost. The reader is discovered independently of the request, but the wait was only the writer's `max_blocking_time` (100 ms by default). On a loaded system that is not enough, and the response is dropped with `client will not receive response` while the client waits forever.

This waits up to 10 seconds instead. The wait ends as soon as the reader matches or the client's endpoints go away. `endpoint_erase_if_exists` did not notify the condition variable, so a client that left would not have released the wait. It does now.

I hit this as a nightly flake in `launch_ros` (`test_load_node_with_param_file`, ros2/launch_ros#572). To check the change in isolation, I ran a script that creates a fresh context, node and client for each call against a long-lived service server, and counts calls with no response after 3 seconds. 10 parallel workers under `stress-ng --cpu 16`, `ros:rolling` with `rmw_fastrtps_cpp`:

| | calls | lost |
|---|---|---|
| master | 1500 | 7 |
| this PR | 1500 | 0 |

This is a bounded workaround, not the Enhanced Service Mapping from the TODO in `__rmw_send_response`. A server can now block for up to 10 seconds in `send_response` if a client's reader is slow to appear, which stalls a single-threaded executor for that long. I chose that over losing the response.

Related to #842

### Is this user-facing behavior change?

Yes. Service responses that were dropped when the client's reader was discovered late are now delivered.

### Did you use Generative AI?

Yes, Claude Sonnet 5.5

author: fw-bot
body:
Before this commit, `mail_html_composer_test_tour` could fail on a loaded runbot at the step "The italicized text is in the full composer":

```
Element (.o_mail_composer_message em:contains(Hello)) has not been found.
```

This happens because the chatter composer keeps its selection when the full composer opens, so its toolbar stays open behind the dialog. That toolbar closes after the click in the full composer, but only once a few timers and a render have run. Until then, the `.o-we-toolbar` steps can match it, and bold and italic go to the chatter composer. The tour engine does not stop it, as it skips its modal check while a toolbar is open.

One solution could have been to wait for the chatter composer toolbar to close, but that wait would be a negative one, with nothing positive to pair it with.

This commit fixes the issue by acting only on a toolbar whose overlay comes after the overlay of the modal.

Note that saas-19.2 avoids this in the tour engine: a step never acts on an overlay behind the modal (6879444930375, https://github.com/odoo/odoo/pull/245680).

author: omattsson
body:
## Summary

GORM logged every lookup that found no row as a red, error-level line (14,927 lines in a 5-minute soak test). This PR builds the GORM logger in one helper, `newGormLogger` (`backend/internal/database/gorm_logger.go`). `NewFromAppConfig` and `NewFromDBConfig` both use it.

- `IgnoreRecordNotFoundError: true`: a lookup that finds no row writes no log line. The repositories still map `gorm.ErrRecordNotFound` to `dberrors.ErrNotFound`; they are unchanged.
- `Colorful: false`: no ANSI codes.
- **Writer:** a dedicated `log.New(os.Stderr, "", log.LstdFlags)`. It does not use the `log` package default, which writes through slog after `slog.SetDefault`, so the GORM output cannot become part of the slog/log chain that CLAUDE.md warns about.
- **Levels:**
  - `APP_DEBUG=true`: `Info`, every statement with its values (as before).
  - `APP_DEBUG=false` (Helm): `Warn` (was `Error`). Real SQL errors are still logged, and **slow queries (200 ms or more, the GORM default threshold) are now logged too**. Release mode sets `ParameterizedQueries: true`, so these lines show `?` placeholders instead of values. Without it, slow-query and error lines could hold user data or secrets.
- `schema/migrator.go` gets its logger from the `*gorm.DB` that the factory builds, so the migration version checks are covered too. No other code builds a GORM logger. No new environment variable.
- `backend/CLAUDE.md` describes the GORM logging next to `LOG_LEVEL`.

## Tests

`gorm_logger_test.go`, table-driven with `t.Parallel`:
- `Trace`: record-not-found is not logged (also when wrapped), a real SQL error gives exactly one entry, slow queries are logged in release mode and fast ones are not, debug logs every statement, no ANSI codes.
- `Info`, `Warn` and `Error` levels for each mode.
- End to end through GORM with SQLite in memory: `First` without a row writes nothing in release mode. A SQL error is logged with placeholders in release mode and with values in debug mode.

Local checks: `gofmt -l .` is empty, `go vet ./...` passes, `go test -p 2 -short ./...` passes, `make gosec` finds 0 issues.

Closes #646

author: justinperea
body:
Follow-up to #99, closing its three review items. The adversarial review found and fixed five more bugs.

## 1. A failed node keeps its error across a reload, a project switch and a restart
- **Before:** the graph the page loads had no error state. `_cli_node_to_rf` always wrote complete or idle, and opening a project overwrote the saved state with that.
- **Now:**
  - **Where errors live:** node errors are kept per project in `node-errors.json` in the state dir. It's written 0600, like every other state file, because a provider's error text can repeat the prompt.
  - **What carries them:** graphSync, `GET /api/projects/{id}` and the switch snapshot carry `state: "error"` with the error, friendly line and category.
  - **On the card:** it shows the error even before the node has an output, unless this tab has queued or started that node again since. A sync sets the friendly line and category together, so an older 429's line can't sit beside a newer error.
- **When an error clears or is forgotten:**
  - Running the node again clears it.
  - Deleting a failed node keeps its error, so an undo brings it back (ids are never reused within a project).
  - An undo that swaps one node for another under the same id forgets it.
  - Clearing the canvas, loading a graph over the project, and purging or emptying trash forget it. Recently deleted keeps it, so a restore brings it back.
- **Why errors survive a restart:** run history can't rebuild them. A run record has no per-node message, and agents' runs aren't in it.

## 2. The readiness warning names each surface's own lister
The HTTP reply says `GET /api/agent/nodes`, MCP `propose_change` says `find_nodes`, and `nebula propose` says `nebula context`. `nebula propose --json --wait` now includes the warning too.

## 3. The ~20 s Accept: found and fixed
- **Cause:** every stalled Accept waited behind a project autosave. `save_project` ran `validate_file_references` over the whole snapshot, run history included, on the event loop. That took 10.6 s on a real snapshot, and every request and canvas event waited behind it.
- **Fix:**
  - each distinct string is checked once (10.6 s → 0.73 s);
  - the check runs in a worker thread before the catalog lock;
  - the per-event workspace read is cached until `catalog.json` changes.
- **After:** all 40 Accepts started, at 1-6 nodes on 100-125-node canvases. The median from click to first run event was 0.8-1.4 s (before: up to 24 s, and one never started). Backend ping during Accepts: p95 74-138 ms.

## Tests (fail first)
- `test_node_errors_reload.py`: page-level `'idle'/'complete' == 'error'` before the fix; undo after delete; id swaps; 0600.
- `test_project_save_event_loop.py`: 4 of 5 failed before the fix.
- Two new readiness-wording tests in `test_canvas_proposals.py`, plus `--json --wait`.
- `graphStore.agentRunErrors.test.ts`:
  - an error shows on a node with no output yet;
  - a sync sets the friendly line and category together.

## Live check (isolated backend and Vite on 878x/578x; a real stdio MCP client, the `nebula` CLI and Puppeteer)
- **Errors persist:** a canvas Run failure and an agent `run_nodes` failure both kept "Missing API key: OPENAI_API_KEY" through a reload, a project switch and back, and a backend restart. `look_at_canvas` agreed each time.
- **Isolation:** 0 canary hits; nothing paid; no keys set.

## Checks
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Backend, isolated (after merging main through #108) | 7,366 passed, 61 skipped |
| Frontend | Full run under heavy load: 40 timeouts in 9 files; those 9 rerun: 166/166 |

body:
## Change

The data side of **"Your emoji"**: a personal image pack ([MSC2545](https://github.com/matrix-org/matrix-spec-proposals/pull/2545)) that users own and can use in every room. Nothing changes in the UI yet. The Settings screen and the entry points follow in stacked PRs.

- **`image-pack.model.ts`** holds the pack constants, `ImagePackUsage`, the usage parsing and `isValidMxcUri`, moved out of `image-pack.service.ts` so the new modules don't import each other. `image-pack.service.ts` re-exports them, so existing importers are unaffected.
- **`AccountPackTarget`** (`image-pack-target.ts`):
  - It reads account data `m.image_pack`, falling back to the legacy `im.ponies.user_emotes`, and writes only `m.image_pack`.
  - It keeps entries the reader rejects verbatim on write.
  - It sits behind a small `PackTarget` interface, so room packs can reuse the editor later.
- **`prepareImagePackImage`**:
  - Still images are resized to a long edge of 256 px for emoji and 512 px for stickers or both. This is a hard cap, through a new `force` option on `downscaleImage`; existing callers are unchanged.
  - Animated GIF/WebP is kept as-is up to 1 MB.
  - Only PNG, JPEG, WebP and GIF are accepted.
  - WebP and PNG never become JPEG, so transparency survives.
- **`ImagePackEditorService`**:
  - It adds, renames, changes usage and removes images.
  - Shortcodes are validated and unique, and the pack holds at most 500 images.
  - Each queued edit reads the pack from the server first, as `ImagePackManagementService` and `RecentEmojiService` do. A stale sync echo or a legacy event can't drop an earlier edit.
  - It checks the server's upload limit before uploading.
  - A retry after a failed save reuses the upload.
  - The first save copies a legacy-only pack and names it "Your emoji".
- **Pickers:** `ImagePackService` now lists the personal pack first, as "Your emoji", and updates live on either account-data type.

## Related issue

Part of #1280 (image packs).

## Validation

- `data-access-media`: 572 tests pass.
- `node .agents/skills/validate-change/validate-change.mjs --run` passes.
- New specs cover:
  - stale-echo safety, including a legacy-only variant;
  - preserving unknown entries;
  - account isolation across two accounts;
  - the hard pixel cap and keeping alpha;
  - the 1 MB animated cap.

author: ayagmar
body:
UX wave 2, PR I: session, session timeline and context tables.

- Session list, `--by-repo`, `--timeline` and context tables use the fit ladder from #283. They abbreviate token counts first, then hide minor columns (session: Models, Duration, Last Activity, Source; repo: Sources, Last Activity; timeline: Cache Write, Running, Input, Cache Read). Rows are listed only when even the last step is too wide. The wrapped column is sized to its content rather than a fixed 32.
- One shared `describeTableFit` (`src/render/table-fit-note.ts`) writes the `Fitted the table…` / `Listed rows…` stderr note. The usage and efficiency reports now use it too, so the efficiency note no longer leaves a dangling "and" when one column is hidden. `renderUnicodeTableWithFit` returns the step it took, and the note mentions abbreviated counts only when a cell that is shown actually changed.
- Color roles: headers bold, money yellow, sources in their hue, secondary models, folded timeline rows and the context aggregated note dim. Headers are sized with `terminalWidth`, and stdout notes are wrapped.
- Listed rows print long model names and events on whole lines, broken at name breaks rather than mid-word.
- Context headers are now Title Case (`Tier Extra`, `>80% Limit`), which shows in the terminal and in markdown.
- `session --json` and `--by-repo --json` add an envelope-level `rowCount` (rows before `--top`). The change is additive: `data` keeps its shape and `schemaVersion` stays 1. The schema and docs are updated.

Shared files: additive changes only. `unicode-table.ts` gains `renderUnicodeTableWithFit` and `table-text-layout.ts` gains `measureWrappedColumnWidth`. Screenshots are not regenerated; a later PR refreshes them all.

## Validation
- `pnpm run verify` passes, and the full vitest suite passes with `CI=1`.
- Real data (`--no-sync`) in a pty at 44, 80 and 120 columns for session, `--by-repo`, context, `context --by-session` and `--timeline`: no line is wider than the terminal; tables stay boxed at 80 and 120 and become lists at 44, each with the matching stderr note.
- An independent review found no high or medium issues. Its low findings are fixed (abbreviation note accuracy, docs claims, shared cell styling, whole-line lists, extra tests), and a re-review found no new issues.

## What does this pull request do?

`KORNIA_CHECK_SHAPE` documents that it validates tensor inputs, but a non-tensor currently leaks an implementation `AttributeError` before the check can report a useful validation error. For example, on `origin/main`:

```python
KORNIA_CHECK_SHAPE([1, 2], ["N"])
# AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'shape'
```

This PR runs the documented tensor guard before reading `.shape`, returns `False` when `raises=False`, documents the `TypeCheckError`, and adds a focused regression test plus changelog fragment.

## Related issue or discussion

No matching open issue or pull request was found for this exact failure.

body:

_Requested by **Vanya** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01VTb61sDWjuB3G8ni12iGSE?thread=cmsg_01VTb61sDWjuB3G8ni12iGSE4xHhMM1tijZjUjtPU1peDT)_

## Summary

Finding a4-26: every scroll view published a slider labelled with the hard-coded English "Scroll position", so screen readers in other locales read English.

```diff
 scroll_semantics(...)
-  .label("Scroll position")
+  .label(position_label)     # BoxedWidgetsLocalizations::maybe_of(ctx), Default as fallback, like PageView's page label
```

`WidgetsLocalizations` gains a required `scroll_position_label`. `DefaultWidgetsLocalizations` and `GlobalWidgetsLocalizations` return the English string.

## Evidence

`page_view::the_page_label_comes_from_the_widgets_localizations` now also asserts the German localization's "Bildlaufposition" is published and "Scroll position" is not. With the production change reverted the test does not compile, because the trait method is missing, and before the trait method existed the label was English for any locale. `cargo test -p flui-widgets --test widgets_it -- page_view` passes (21 tests); clippy on `flui-widgets --all-targets -D warnings` is clean.

author: zinin
body:
## What failed

The first run of `deps-latest` on master (run 39487703620, dispatched by hand right after #7) failed in the `python-floor` job at its `uv venv` step:

```
Creating virtual environment at: .venv
error: Failed to create virtual environment
  cause: A virtual environment already exists at: .venv
hint: Use the `--clear` flag or set `UV_VENV_CLEAR=1` to replace the existing virtual environment
```

`python-latest` (3.10 and 3.14) passed. The workflow file came in with #7 and had never run on GitHub: `workflow_dispatch` and `schedule` fire only from the default branch.

## Why

- `astral-sh/setup-uv@v5` with `python-version` sets `UV_PYTHON`, **creates `.venv` and activates it** (its v5 README; the failed job's env shows `VIRTUAL_ENV=…/.venv`).
- uv refuses to replace an existing venv without `--clear` (reproduced locally with uv 0.11.7: exit 2, then `uv venv --clear` exits 0).
- The local floor runs before the merge used a venv in a fresh directory, so they never met setup-uv's venv.

## Fix

`uv venv` → `uv venv --clear`, with a comment saying why. Dropping the step instead would break after a Dependabot bump of setup-uv: in later majors `python-version` only sets `UV_PYTHON` and a venv appears only with `activate-environment: true`, so `uv pip install` would find no venv. With `--clear` the step works under both.

## Verification

`deps-latest` dispatched on this branch (run 39488400454, head `cc2ffce`): all three jobs green.

| Job | Result |
|---|---|
| `python-floor` | CPython 3.10.22, mcp 1.30.0, pydantic 2.11.0 — 213 passed, 1 skipped |
| `python-latest (3.10)` | success |
| `python-latest (3.14)` | success |

body:
## What
Dose times anchored to daily events (S08z): a dose can be tied to waking, a meal, a daily prayer or bedtime instead of a clock time. The patient sets each anchor's time (nothing computed from location or calendar); "my day has shifted" moves chosen anchors for up to 45 days then stops by itself. Days already lived never move (anchor times are versioned by date). Reminders stay generic and never name a medicine.

- Migration `20261021011847_s08z_dose_time_anchors.sql` (additive tables + RPCs; rewrites the four slot-expanding functions from their live definitions and aborts if the expected text is not found; DO-block assertions).
- Pure rules in `packages/medicines` (100% branch coverage, 429 tests), phone and web screens, outbox kinds, printed adherence report.
- DB proof `s08z_dose_anchors.sql` (103 checks, 3 sabotages that flip), run as a rolled-back transaction against live; CI replay is the first real run.

## Review notes (code-review high, run in the parent session)
1. **Privacy gap to decide before merging:** anchor tables are readable only by the person and an acting guardian, but the anchor id (for example `night_prayer`) is also stored in `medications.schedule_spec`, which tied clinicians and caregivers read. The self-check only inspects the new tables.
2. The four functions are patched by regexp over `pg_get_functiondef`; a concurrent edit to one of them could be rewritten against an unproven body.
3. Per-slot anchor lookups in the reminder queue are unmeasured at scale.
4. `anchor_day_has_answers` only checks yesterday to tomorrow.

## Not verified
No device, simulator or browser run. Open questions OQ-S08z-1 to 6.

author: samuelalvesg
body:
Fixes #276

## Problem

`Session::wait_for_connection()` only watched a state channel that the event loop updates while it's running. When the loop ends for good (out of retries, session closed, task dropped or aborted) nothing updates it again, so the call waited forever. `disconnect()` had the same problem, and after an abort `wait_for_connection()` even returned `true` for a session that was already dead.

## Fix

A final `SessionState::Terminated`, set from `Drop for SessionEventLoop` so it covers every way the loop can end. `wait_for_state` stops on it: `wait_for_connection()` returns `false`, and waiting for a disconnect returns `true`. The doc comment on `wait_for_connection` now says that, instead of "this method will never return".

## Tests

Two new tests in `session_lifecycle.rs`, both time out on master and pass now:

- the loop gives up (closed port, `session_retry_limit(0)`): `wait_for_connection()` returns `false`
- the loop task is aborted after connecting: `wait_for_connection()` returns `false` and `disconnect()` comes back

I ran the same things as the CI on stable and beta: `cargo check --locked`, `cargo test --locked --all-features`, `cargo clippy --locked -- -D warnings` (default features, `--no-default-features`, `xml`, `json`) and `cargo fmt --check`. All of them passed (476 tests with `--all-features`, on both toolchains). I did not run the .NET external-server test or the generated-code check locally, so those are left to the CI here.

---
Following up on the issue: I called this a bug there, but `wait_for_connection` not returning when the loop has ended is documented, so this is really a proposal to change that contract (and the abort / disconnect cases are the parts that aren't documented). If you'd rather keep the contract, I can narrow the PR to the abort and disconnect cases. One thing worth knowing: callers that ignore the returned bool, like the samples, would now continue on a dead session and get errors from the next call, instead of hanging.

author: giove-a
body:
"Julia 1 - ubuntu-latest" has failed on most runs since the PositionVelocityTime 7 update in 5.1.1 (on `main` at 5.1.1, 5.1.2 and #48), always in "At an epoch the data's record may come before or after the pilot's". It is the test's tolerance, not the code.

## Cause

The test requires the scalar fixes of its three runs to agree to 1e-6 m. In one run the satellites register in another order, so the least-squares solve sums them in another order. The solve stops at a step of ~2 µm (PositionVelocityTime's `x_tol` of 1e-13 against the ~2e7 m clock bias), so the fixes may legitimately differ by a few µm.

Whether they do depends on the BLAS kernels OpenBLAS picks for the runner's CPU:

| Forced OpenBLAS kernels | Gap at the seeding fix | 1e-6 m test |
|---|---|---|
| Haswell / Zen (AMD EPYC runners, no AVX-512) | 4.7 µm | fails, 7 passed / 1 failed, as on CI |
| SkylakeX / native AVX-512 (Intel runners) | 1e-8 m | passes |

That is why the same commit passed once (#47) and failed otherwise. Julia's own CPU target, the Julia patch version and the resolved package versions made no difference. The run that only shifts the records' timing matches exactly (0.0 m), and the measured satellites match in every run, so the snapshots themselves agree.

## Change

The tolerance goes from 1e-6 m to 0.1 mm, far below what a differing snapshot would move the fix by, with a comment explaining the bound.

Checked locally on Julia 1.13.2: with `OPENBLAS_CORETYPE=Zen`/`Haswell` the old tolerance reproduces the CI failure and the new one passes. The full suite passes with the Zen kernels and coverage.

Test-only (`test(vector)`), so no release.

author: morluto
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->
## Summary

Fixes #5670. Reverse, pcap, and SQLite application admission were dropping the caller's abort reason, and a reverse-engineering digest or command failure could be reclassified as cancellation whenever the caller signal was already aborted.

## Problem and expected behavior

`docs/tool-design.md` requires the exact caller abort reason as `AnalysisCancelledError.cause`, including cancellation observed after provider completion, and requires a recognized primary failure to keep its classification.

On `40428da1dd6308f6f407547fd23b0a912232895a`, an injected probe with `AbortController.abort({ requested: "stop" })` observed:

- `inspectWithObjdump` before launch returned `AnalysisCancelledError` with `cause` absent and did not run the provider.
- The same call, aborted after the command returned stdout, kept partial Evidence and still omitted `cause`.
- An injected digest that aborted and then rejected `EACCES` returned `AnalysisCancelledError` whose cause was that `EACCES` error.
- `PcapAnalysisService.execute` and `SqliteDatabaseService.inspect` did the same at admission: `cause` absent, provider not called.

## Change and scope

Cancellation is now published with `signal.reason`. A recognized physical code (`EACCES`, `EPERM`, `ETIMEDOUT`, `ENOENT`, and the other host failures already classified by this service) stays that failure when a late abort is also observed. A non-physical rejection while the signal is aborted, including the existing plain `digest cancelled` case, remains cancellation and now carries the caller reason.

A command `ABORT_ERR` remains cancellation, which is the previous command contract, and uses the caller reason when the signal is aborted. A digest or stat `ABORT_ERR` without an aborted signal stays `ProviderAdapterError`.

Follow the [contribution scope](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#contribution-scope). This is an ordinary classification fix inside existing reverse, pcap, and SQLite boundaries. Not applicable: no new provider, target execution, injection, mutation, or protection recovery.

Intentionally not included: GDB, native command, owned-command, pcap command, SQLite provider, and EVM cleanup bugs in the same audit cluster. Those already preserve the caller reason or primary failure on this main. Other application services that still omit `signal.reason` at admission are left for a separate change.

## Contract and boundary impact

- Semantic owner and earliest changed stage: application admission and reverse-engineering failure projection, before provider launch or after a settled command/digest result.
- Contribution scope fit and linked maintainer decision: ordinary fix within existing boundaries; not applicable.
- CLI and MCP/tool-catalog contract: no schema or catalog change. Typed cancellation `cause` now carries the caller reason for these three services.

author: fallintoplace
body:
## What
Speed up `CountSetBits` for bitmap ranges with a nonzero offset.

## Why
The previous path scans up to 63 leading bits one by one before using a word-based popcount.

## Implementation
- Count the leading partial byte with a mask and `bits.OnesCount8`.
- Reuse the existing word-based path for the rest.
- Add boundary tests and a benchmark.

## Benchmark
Isolated old/new microbenchmark, Go 1.23.2 on AMD EPYC 7763, 0 allocations.

| Range | Before | After | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 5 bits, offset 3 | 15.5 ns/op | 5.9 ns/op | 2.6x |
| 32 bits, offset 3 | 40.6 ns/op | 16.2 ns/op | 2.5x |
| 32 bits, offset 8 | 40.1 ns/op | 12.9 ns/op | 3.1x |
| 128 bits, offset 37 | 42.4 ns/op | 21.7 ns/op | 2.0x |
| 8192 bits, offset 3 | 135.1 ns/op | 95.3 ns/op | 1.4x |

A 1024-bit range at offset 63 was roughly unchanged (28.8 to 29.2 ns/op). These are isolated microbenchmarks, not full-package measurements.

This fork PR uses an upstream-main snapshot as its base to avoid unrelated commits from the older fork main.

author: luizparreira
body:
The founder asked to drop macOS from CI on 2026-10-20, because it costs too much. bip does the same in bipa-app/bip#1014.

### Change
`ci.yml` `cross-platform`: the matrix goes from `[macos-latest, windows-latest]` to `[windows-latest]`.
- This job ran on `push`, `pull_request` **and** the nightly `schedule`, so the macOS leg ran on every one of them.
- The "Test publishable crates" step ran only on macOS (`if: runner.os != 'Windows'`), so it is removed rather than left dead. The full suite still runs on Linux in `test`.
- The comment above the job now says why macOS is not in the matrix.
- The `all` aggregator, the required check in the `main` ruleset, needs the `cross-platform` job by its id, not a matrix leg, so it is unaffected. Branch protection's required checks are `Test (nextest)` and `Postgres integration`. Neither is touched.

### Other workflows
None uses macOS. `grep -n macos .github/workflows/*.yml` is empty on this branch.
- `claude.yml` runs on `blacksmith-2vcpu-ubuntu-2404`.
- `release-gates.yml` (its nightly `schedule` included), `release-plz.yml` and `mirror-buzz.yml` run on `ubuntu-latest`.

### What Windows costs, for the decision to keep it
The billing timing API (`/actions/runs/<id>/timing`) returns 0 billable ms for this org's runs, so these figures come from job wall time over the last 30 completed `ci.yml` runs:

| Leg | Avg per run | Est. per month (~476 runs so far in Oct) | Est. cost at GitHub's list multipliers |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `Cross-platform (macos-latest)` (removed) | 4.4 min | ~2,100 min | ~$167 (10x Linux) |
| `Cross-platform (windows-latest)` (kept) | 2.0 min | ~950 min | ~$15 (2x Linux) |

These are estimates: billing rounds each job up to a whole minute, and Windows runs on 2-vCPU runners. Dropping Windows too would save roughly $15 a month, and lose the only check that the published crates still build on Windows.

### CI on this PR
- `all` passes, and so do `Cross-platform (windows-latest)`, `Test (nextest)` and `Postgres integration`. No macOS leg ran.
- `cargo-audit` and `cargo-deny` fail on advisories published 2026-10-19/20, which are unrelated to this change. They are RUSTSEC-2026-0382 (`rustls-webpki` 0.103.15), RUSTSEC-2026-0383 (`webpki-root-certs` 1.0.9), the matching `webpki-roots` 1.0.9 advisory, and RUSTSEC-2026-0381 (`unsafe-libyaml` unmaintained).
- `main`'s last release-gates run passed before those advisories were published, and neither check is required. Any agent-sdk PR now hits them until the dependencies are bumped.

body:
Adds `src/content/posts/tsrs-speedup-decomposed.md`.

**Topic:** tsrs, the Rust port of the TypeScript compiler announced today by Cloudflare/VoidZero (HN front page).
**Score:** 8/10. The announcement gives headline speedups, and this post measures where they come from. It benchmarks TS 6 / 7.0 / 7.1β / the matched Go nightly / tsrs on two codebases (the TS repo and type-fest), then switches tsrs's optimizations off one at a time (`--singleThreaded`, `--noLazyMembers`, `--checkerAssignment go`) and reads the work counters and page-fault numbers. Findings: 10× on type-fest = ~3.2× per core × 1.1× lazy members × 2.7× parallel scaling. Instantiation counts are identical, while Go's 4-checker run spends ~30% of its CPU in the kernel. A 3,000-file conformance sample produced byte-identical diagnostics.

**Runners-up**
- DeepInfer (DeepSeek inference framework): SWA bounded replay / batch-invariant inference. 6, because it needs SM100/Ascend hardware, so the post could only reason about it, not measure.
- Futhark "Making all divisions slower to fix a rare bug": 5
- Pocket TTS 1.9M-param voice cloning on CPU: 5
- Google TorchTPU (PyTorch backend for TPUs): 5, needs TPUs
- SlopCodeBench 10/2026: 4, a benchmark recap
- Voxtral 3: 4, an announcement

**Sources**
- https://blog.cloudflare.com/typescript-rust-port/
- https://github.com/oxc-project/tsrs (README, docs/USAGE.md, docs/COMPATIBILITY.md, bench/RESULTS.md, notes/perf-round3.md, notes/perf-icount-round4.md)

body:
Closes #199 --- ## Agent summary The app polled every found project. A start sent hundreds of tracker requests and held the first poll for minutes. The configuration now holds a `tracked` list, and the app polls only those projects. Only a tracked project gets ticket, PR and branch requests, and only a tracked project shows on the overview. Settings still lists every found project from membership and the checkout scan, so the user can pick what to track. With no tracked project, a start sends only discovery requests: the membership requests, plus one Linear lookup for each ticket key the checkout scan finds. Old configuration files still load: `pinned` becomes `tracked`, and the app drops `hidden` and `activityWindowDays`. This is not marked as a breaking change, but found projects that are not tracked leave the overview. Design notes: - Untracking a project clears its good-poll record in `project_polls`, so a re-tracked project gets a full poll and does not miss older open tickets. `project_errors` stays in place. - `poll()` and `settingsProjects()` share the domain `matchesRef` and `refKey`, so one copy of the ref rule decides which tracker requests go out. The copies in `src/app.ts` are gone. - `projectViews` matches stored rows to tracked refs through `sameProjectRef`, which handles repo, Linear and GitHub board refs. - The overview loses the pin star, the Pinned menu and the `pinned` filter, because every overview project is tracked. A stored `"pinned"` filter loads as `"all"`. - Settings renames the Pinned switch to Tracked and removes the Hidden switch and the Activity window field. This overlaps the switch in #200; #200 keeps the empty state. - `GLOSSARY.md` adds **Tracked project**, removes **Pinned project** and **Hidden project**, and rewrites **Found project**. It removes the **Activity window** term instead of rewriting it, because no rule or key uses it now. Test changes: dropped the two activity-window tests and the hidden-only source test because their rules are gone; test/tracked.test.ts covers tracked-only polling. ## Caveats
1 departure - The issue asks to rewrite the **Activity window** term. The branch removes it, because no rule or configuration key uses it now.
1 loose end - An untracked project keeps its `project_errors` rows. Only its good-poll record goes.
4 assumptions - The overview loses the pin star, the Pinned menu and the `pinned` filter, and a stored `"pinned"` filter loads as `"all"`: every overview project is tracked. - Settings renames the Pinned switch to Tracked and removes the Hidden switch and the Activity window field: the old configuration keys are gone. - Untracking a project clears its `project_polls` good-poll record, so a re-track gets a full poll. It leaves `project_errors` in place. - The change is not marked breaking: old configuration files load, but found-only projects leave the overview.
## Conceptual Changes The `tracked` list replaces `pinned`, `hidden` and the activity window as the one rule for which found projects get polled and shown. No overlaps with existing concepts. ```mermaid flowchart TB found["Found project
membership and checkout scan"]:::changed settings["settings projects
lists found projects"]:::same tracked["tracked
configured projects to poll"]:::added poll["poll()
ticket, PR and branch requests"]:::changed overview["overview
tracked projects only"]:::changed pinned["pinned and hidden
always or never show"]:::removed window["activityWindowDays
show recent found projects"]:::removed found -->|lists| settings found -->|picks| tracked tracked -->|scopes| poll poll -->|feeds| overview pinned -->|filtered| overview window -->|filtered| overview classDef added fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,color:#14532d classDef changed fill:#fef9c3,stroke:#ca8a04,color:#713f12 classDef removed fill:#fee2e2,stroke:#dc2626,color:#7f1d1d,stroke-dasharray:4 3 classDef same fill:#f3f4f6,stroke:#9ca3af,color:#374151 linkStyle 1 stroke:#16a34a,stroke-width:2px linkStyle 2 stroke:#16a34a,stroke-width:2px linkStyle 4 stroke:#dc2626,stroke-width:2px,stroke-dasharray:4 3 linkStyle 5 stroke:#dc2626,stroke-width:2px,stroke-dasharray:4 3 ``` #### Legend 🟩 added | 🟨 changed | 🟥 removed | ⬜ unchanged ## Proof 1. ✅ With no tracked project, a start sends only discovery requests: the membership requests, plus one Linear lookup for each ticket key the checkout scan finds. `test/tracked.test.ts` "a start with no tracked project sends only the membership requests" passes, and the full suite has 451 pass and 0 fail. The test asserts the exact set of requests the fake fetch records: user, user/repos, ViewerProjects, MemberProjects and viewer. The checkout in this test names no ticket key, so it sends no Linear lookup. The overview is empty. A start with `{"tracked":"acme/repo-3","pinned":5}` prints "invalid configuration: tracked, pinned" and exits with code 1. 2. ✅ `test/tracked.test.ts` "only the tracked 2 of 10 found projects get ticket and PR requests and show" passes. Settings lists 10 found projects (5 repos and 5 Linear projects). Issue, PR, branch, label and ProjectIssues requests go only to acme/repo-3 and board-1. The overview shows only those 2 projects. 3. ✅ `test/tracked.test.ts` "a configuration file with pinned and hidden loads and its pinned projects are tracked" passes. The file has `pinned`, `hidden`, `activityWindowDays` and `filter: "pinned"`. Settings returns `tracked` with acme/repo-2 and no pinned, hidden or activityWindowDays key. The overview shows only acme/repo-2. 4. ✅ `git diff origin/main -- GLOSSARY.md` removes **Pinned project**, **Hidden project** and **Activity window**, and adds **Tracked project**. Found project is rewritten. The old names stay only on the _Avoid_ line of the Tracked project term. ## Merge Danger **Door:** ➡️ one-way - A configuration file that settings saves holds `tracked` and no `pinned`. The reverted app's strict schema refuses that file until the user renames the key. **Blast Radius:** 👥 users - Found projects that are not tracked leave the overview, so a user with no `pinned` entries sees an empty overview until they track a project. - A wrong ref match in `sameProjectRef` or `matchesRef` would skip polls for a tracked project. --- Implemented by a workcell manager running Claude Opus 5.5 implementer, verifier and reviewer workers 🤖 Generated with Claude Opus 5.5 via [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: ivanzugec
body:
## Summary

**Image props without a Canvas dependency**

Replaces `"$ref": "json-schema-definitions://canvas.module/image"` with the equivalent inline schema in `card` (`image`), `hero` (`image`), `section` (`background_media`) and `site_logo` (`logo_light`, `logo_dark`). The `json-schema-definitions://` stream wrapper comes from Canvas, so these components depended on it. Canvas matches the inline shape to its own image definition (`PropShape::standardize()`), so the editor is unchanged. Approach from [Canvas tips & tricks: declaring images in SDCs](https://penyaskito.com/articles/2026/07/18/canvas-tipstricks-declaring-images-sdcs).

**Link props use `uri-reference`**

- `badge` and `button` `url`: `iri-reference` → `uri-reference`, matching what other Canvas themes use (see [byte_theme !30](https://git.drupalcode.org/project/byte_theme/-/merge_requests/30)).
- `site_logo` `url`: adds `format: uri-reference`. It was a plain string, so Canvas showed a plain text field and the prop couldn't map to link fields in content templates. It now gets the link widget.

## Canvas impact

- Image props: Canvas generates identical prop field definitions and keeps the same component versions. Existing content is unaffected.
- Link props: Canvas creates a new version of `badge`, `button` and `site_logo`. Stored link values don't change, and existing instances keep working. Links saved with unencoded non-ASCII characters (e.g. `/café`) would fail `uri-reference` validation the next time that component is edited.

## Testing

- [ ] After `drush cr`, `card`, `hero`, `section`, `site_logo`, `badge` and `button` are enabled in Canvas.
- [ ] Image props still use the media library widget (image and SVG image), and existing pages with images render.
- [ ] Button, badge and site logo links use the link widget and accept both `/about` and `https://example.com`.
- [ ] Existing pages with buttons, badges and the site logo still render.

Checked locally: Canvas field definitions as described above, home, card, hero and buttons/badges pages render, and `pnpm run format:check` passes.

author: canonix-nikolay-s
body:
Existing Redis-based PoC installations cannot use the ordinary 0.2.0 upgrade because its migration guard correctly blocks replacing live Redis with empty Valkey. This adds an explicit `install.sh --discard-redis-state` path for the customer to accept that tradeoff and complete the update independently.

The helper pauses the rendered Phoenix Deployments, waits for their Pods to exit, refuses active sandbox/job/remote clients and autoscaling, upgrades only the existing Redis Helm release, checks Valkey via the existing endpoint, and restores original replica counts. It retains the old PVC, records a private retry journal, and never flushes either server. Repeated execution does not reset existing Valkey. The default guard remains unchanged.

Release 0.2.1 changes the installer and instructions only: every application/infrastructure image digest and chart version is identical to 0.2.0. The customer procedure includes optional backups and explicitly states which Redis-held state is not carried over.

Validation: full static BYOC suite; ShellCheck; 21 Python tests covering compliance and cutover failure/retry cases; isolated local Kubernetes cutover from Redis 8.8.0 to pinned Valkey 9.1.2 with the published 1.6.18 chart and two clients. Original Redis PVC UID/binding and Service UID/IP stayed unchanged, both clients resumed, and a Valkey key survived a repeated invocation. The unchanged application images retain the earlier EKS qualification; customer GCP workflow acceptance is still required.

Named profiles can save `agent/launch-memory.json` with a `sources` array of persistent text files. `npi --profile work` reads only that profile's manifest and preloads the selected contents into the initial system prompt. `/launch-profile` shows the profile name, resolved paths, and exact loaded snapshot. The snapshot is also recorded in the session transcript.

**Rollout: direct**. This adds optional context and a read-only slash command. It does not change menu navigation, key handling, the composer, live mode, or control-socket behavior. Without a named profile, the manifest is not read. Existing named profiles without a manifest keep their current startup path.

## Why

Fixes #65

The conservative design reuses the existing named-profile selector and its established directory isolation. It selects file-backed memory sources rather than adding configuration presets or making remote retrieval calls. Relative paths resolve against the manifest directory; absolute paths can select existing persistent files elsewhere. Remote memory IDs must first be exported to text. Normal memory-backend retrieval and other context discovery remain unchanged.

The core integrations are narrow: CLI startup loads the optional selection, and the SDK adds its snapshot while assembling the first prompt. An extension-only implementation cannot guarantee this behavior when extensions are disabled. Explicit append prompts, system-prompt templates, and chat mode retain the selected memory.

## Testing

All commands ran through the polite relay under the exclusive light lock, with a 600-second command timeout and a 60000 ms Bun per-test timeout.

- `bun test --timeout 60000 packages/coding-agent/test/launch-profile.test.ts packages/coding-agent/test/cli-service-tier-flag.test.ts packages/coding-agent/test/profile-alias.test.ts packages/coding-agent/test/discovery/profile-isolation.test.ts`: 36 pass, 0 fail, 100 assertions.
- `bun test --timeout 60000 packages/coding-agent/test/sdk-system-prompt-template.test.ts packages/coding-agent/test/system-prompt-template.test.ts packages/coding-agent/test/slash-commands/session.test.ts`: 31 pass, 0 fail, 91 assertions.
- `bun --cwd=packages/coding-agent check`: passed lint, formatting, and typecheck, with existing warnings outside the changed files. Two initial feature type errors were corrected before the passing run.

The new tests use real persisted `Settings.init` initialization. They compare default startup options and complete initial system-prompt blocks with and without a broken, ignored manifest; check named profiles without manifests; verify work/personal isolation before any conversation messages; exercise snapshot inspection after a source edit; preserve chat and append prompts; and reject malformed manifests or missing sources.

No binary build, compiled CLI launch, interactive TUI session, or live-provider request was run. Dependencies were removed from the worktree after verification.

author: shahroz16
body:
Refs MBL-2397

## Why
GitHub removed Node 20 from hosted runners on 2026-09-23 ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-09-19-deprecation-of-node-20-on-github-actions-runners/)). Actions that still declare `runs.using: node20` are force-run on Node 24 with a warning. This repository had 21 such references in 9 files. Every SDK repo consumes these composites and reusable workflows `@main`, so **merging this changes all of them at once**. A dry run is below.

## Change
Every pin below was checked with `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/contents/<path>/action.yml?ref=<sha>`.

| File | Action | From → To | `runs.using` at the new SHA |
|---|---|---|---|
| `github-actions/ios/setup-ios/v1` | `maxim-lobanov/setup-xcode` | v1.6.0 → v1.7.0 `ed7a3b1` | node24 |
| `github-actions/slack-notify-sample-app/v1` (×2) | `slackapi/slack-github-action` | `@v2.0.0` (tag) → v4.0.0 `dcb1066` | node24 |
| `github-actions/android/setup-android/v1` | `actions/setup-java` | v4 → v5.7.0 `b6effb0` | node24 |
| | `android-actions/setup-android` | v3.2.2 → v4.0.4 `be39fa8` | node24 |
| | `gradle/actions/wrapper-validation`, `setup-gradle` | v4.3.1 → v5.0.2 `0723195` | node24 |
| `.github/workflows/ios-test.yml` | `actions/checkout` | `@v4` → v7.0.1 `3d3c42e` | node24 |
| | `maierj/fastlane-action` | v3.1.0 → v3.2.0 `182983d` | node24 |
| | `codecov/codecov-action` | v4.6.0 → v7.1.1 `303a32d` | composite (inner `github-script` v8 = node24) |
| | `actions/upload-artifact` | `@v4` → v7.0.2 `cf430e0` | node24 |
| | `mikepenz/action-junit-report` | v4.3.1 → v6.6.1 `6ef3fdc` | node24 |
| `ios-lint.yml`, `ios-lint-linux.yml`, `ios-actions-test.yml`, `android-publish-ci.yml`, `android-publish-release.yml` | `actions/checkout` | v4 / v4.2.2 → v7.0.1 | node24 |
| `ios-lint-linux.yml` | `actions/cache` | `@v4` → v6.1.0 `55cc834` | node24 |
| `ios-actions-test.yml` | `actions/upload-artifact` | v4.6.2 → v7.0.2 | node24 |

### What changes behaviour, and what does not
- **setup-xcode v1.7.0**: the diff from v1.6.0 is only `runs.using`. Version resolution is unchanged.
- **slack-github-action v4**: v4 parses `payload` with js-yaml 5 (stricter multi-line indentation). I rendered both payloads in `slack-notify-sample-app` with realistic inputs. They parse identically with js-yaml 5.2.1 (what v4 bundles) and 4.3.2. `errors` already defaulted to `false` in v2, so failure handling is unchanged. The webhook inputs were already the v2+ form.
- **setup-java v5, not v6**: v6 moves Zulu resolution to the Azul Metadata API, and this composite installs Zulu. v5.7.0 is the same choice as customerio/customerio-android#946.
- **gradle/actions v5, not v6**: v6 moves caching into `gradle-actions-caching`, a proprietary component under Gradle's Terms of Use. Upgrading is a team decision, as in customerio/customerio-android#946.
- **android-actions/setup-android v4**: default `packages` changes from `tools platform-tools` to `platform-tools` (the obsolete SDK Tools package is no longer installed). Default cmdline-tools also moves from 12266719 to 15859902. Neither the android-publish plugin build nor customerio/jist (the only external consumer of this composite) calls the legacy `tools/` binaries. I kept the default instead of re-adding `tools`.
- **checkout v7**: credentials are persisted to a `$RUNNER_TEMP` file included from `.git/config` (since v6). Plain `git push` keeps working, which matters for the tag push in `android-publish-release.yml`. v7 also refuses fork-PR checkouts under `pull_request_target`/`workflow_run`. No caller of these workflows uses those triggers: the consumers are `pull_request`, `push`, `schedule`, `workflow_dispatch` and `workflow_call`.
- **codecov-action v7**: a composite around the Codecov CLI. It reads the `CODECOV_TOKEN` env this workflow already sets, and `files:` is the v5+ input name already in use.
- **action-junit-report v6**: v5 simplified the job-summary format. `github_token` is a deprecated alias, so it is renamed to `token`. `fail_on_failure` and `require_tests` are unchanged.
- **upload-artifact v7**: `archive` defaults to `true`, so the artifact is still a zip with the same name.

### CI coverage added
- `android-publish-ci.yml` now also runs when `github-actions/android/setup-android/**` changes. It is the only CI that exercises that composite, and jist consumes it `@main`.
- `ios-actions-test.yml` runs `setup-ios` with its default Xcode at the end of the macOS job and asserts `xcodebuild -version` is 26.6.x. Nothing else in this repository ran `setup-ios`.

## Dry run
Merging rolls out to every consumer at once, so before merge:
1. **This PR's own CI** covers `setup-ios`, `setup-android` (android-publish-ci), `report-toolchain` and `launch-simulator-app` (ios-actions-test).
2. **customerio/customerio-ios-fcm#22** (throwaway draft, will be closed) points fcm's `test.yml` and `lint.yml` at `@ci/node24-actions`. That exercises the real Scan run, test-report artifact and JUnit check through `ios-test.yml`, plus `ios-lint.yml`. Codecov is covered by a customerio-ios run (below). fcm is the smallest caller of both. Note: inside `ios-test.yml`, `setup-ios` is still referenced `@main`, so (1) covers that piece.
3. **Not dry-run: `slack-notify-sample-app`**. Running it posts to the team's Slack build channels. It is covered by the payload parse check above. Its first real run after merge will be the next sample-app build in any SDK repo.
4. **Not dry-run: `ios-lint-linux.yml`**. It has no caller yet.

### Results (2026-10-20)
- **This PR's CI: all green.**
  - [`build`](https://github.com/customerio/mobile-ci-tools/actions/runs/39488579630/job/118855350051) ran the android-publish plugin build through `setup-android` (setup-java v5.7.0, setup-android v4.0.4, gradle/actions v5.0.2).
  - [`macos-bash-tests`](https://github.com/customerio/mobile-ci-tools/actions/runs/39488579597/job/118855349731) ran the new `setup-ios` steps (setup-xcode v1.7.0), and `xcodebuild -version` reported 26.6.x.
- **Dry run customerio/customerio-ios-fcm#22: green**, with `ios-test.yml` and `ios-lint.yml` resolved from this branch at `27c9394`.
  - [Test run](https://github.com/customerio/customerio-ios-fcm/actions/runs/39488492455/job/118855051756) went through checkout v7.0.1 → Setup iOS → setup-ruby → **Scan via fastlane-action v3.2.0** → **test-report artifact via upload-artifact v7.0.2** (`xcode-test-report`, 872 bytes; `main`'s is 864) → **JUnit via action-junit-report v6.6.1** ([check](https://github.com/customerio/customerio-ios-fcm/runs/118901160898): "26 tests run, 25 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed").
  - [Lint run](https://github.com/customerio/customerio-ios-fcm/actions/runs/39488492503) passed on checkout v7.0.1.
- **Codecov upload (`codecov-action` v4.6.0 → v7.1.1): verified** by a [customerio-ios run](https://github.com/customerio/customerio-ios/actions/runs/39555794131/job/119075141866) through `ios-test.yml@ci/node24-actions` (`27c9394`). It ran with `--fail-on-error`, and the upload returned 200 ("Upload queued for processing"). fcm passes no token, so its dry run skipped these steps.

## Codex review
Codex (gpt-6.1-sol, high) reviewed the diff adversarially:
- **No consumer-breaking regression found.** It checked Slack and jist inputs, artifact defaults, JUnit inputs, `checks: write`, and the tag push with checkout v7 credentials.
- **Verification gap: green CI here cannot prove that Scan, Codecov and JUnit still work.** Accepted. That is the fcm dry run (step 2).
- **Correction: codecov's inner `github-script` step always runs**, not only with OIDC. It only requests an OIDC token when `use_oidc` is set, so no `id-token: write` is needed. The step is node24 (v8.0.0).

author: czarcas7ic
body:
Replaces the common IWPROOF1 witness file with a companion witness PIR table per payment table, as the wallet-libraries companion witness change defines it. Records carry a witness ordinal, `/v1/receiver/init` serves the payment and witness sessions together, and wallets read a payment's 512-byte lower path over PIR by that ordinal. The witness file route, `--witnesses`, `--max-witness-commitments` and the 2^24 commitment limit are gone.

Witnesses are now built per Ironwood shard. The store keeps every commitment, records each completed shard's root and completing block with its payments' final payloads, and a rewind past that block drops them. Only the filling shard's paths stay in memory and extend each publication; a restart or rewind rebuilds them from that shard's own commitments, so no publication rereads the full history. `Store::correct` replaces a stored block's payments on an unchanged chain under a higher correction revision, and a payment it adds to a completed shard rebuilds only that shard. The probe reads the fixture's payload over PIR and checks it against the node's Ironwood subtree root (`z_getsubtreesbyindex`), which the monitor's node must now answer.

This is the first of two stacked PRs; sealed Receiver shards and inventories follow on top. The wallet-libraries pin is the library PR's current head and will move with its review.
