author: luisgf
body:
Part 3 of #325, as scoped in the 2026-10-20 comment on the issue.

## What changed

- `ENVIRONMENTS` gains `EbsiEnvironment("preprod", None)` and `EbsiEnvironment("prod", None)`: the Trusted Nodes List's own spellings for EBSI Core API v1, whose hosts are the nodes of a signed list, not a name (`fixed_host is None`, `.base is None`).
- `EBSI_HOSTS` and `EBSI_BASE` keep exactly their four keys, values and order (`fixed_hosts()` already filters rows with no host). The dict-equality pin gains an assertion that neither new name is in either dict.
- New `NodeDerivedEnvironment(UnknownEbsiEnvironment)` in `errors.py` (so also an `EbsiError` and a `ValueError`). `for_ebsi("preprod")` and `for_ebsi("prod")` raise it **before any `httpx.Client` exists**; the message says the name has no fixed host and names `verify_node_list`, `for_nodes` and the wiki page `EBSI-Node-Trust`. The branch reads the row (`fixed_host is None`), not a list of names.
- The unknown-name path is unchanged: `for_ebsi("nope")` is still exactly `UnknownEbsiEnvironment`, and its "known:" list (read from `EBSI_HOSTS`) still names only the four fixed-host names. The match is the exact name, so `"Prod"`, `" prod"` and `UserString("prod")` are plain unknown names.
- `nodes.py` and `node_client.py` are untouched. `environments.py` still imports no HTTP library; no new dependency; EBSI stays read-only.

## Which host each of the six names seeds or refuses

| Name | `for_ebsi` |
|---|---|
| `legacy-pilot` (default) | seeds `{api-pilot.ebsi.eu}` |
| `pilot` | seeds `{api-pilot.ebsi.eu}`, with its `DeprecationWarning` (Part 2, unchanged) |
| `conformance` | seeds `{api-conformance.ebsi.eu}` |
| `production` | seeds `{api.ebsi.eu}` |
| `preprod` | refused: `NodeDerivedEnvironment`, no client, no host |
| `prod` | refused: `NodeDerivedEnvironment`, no client, no host (not `production`) |

Pinned by `test_each_of_the_six_names_seeds_its_host_or_is_refused`. Nothing that built a client before stops building one; the only behaviour change is that two names that raised `UnknownEbsiEnvironment` now raise its subclass (`except UnknownEbsiEnvironment` / `ValueError` still catch them; code comparing the exact class for those two names must compare `NodeDerivedEnvironment`).

## The adapter pairing is dropped from the table

The issue text proposed `didr_adapter` / `tir_adapter` fields on the row. `for_nodes(result, ..., didr="core-v1", tir="core-v1")` already takes both and validates them against `DID_REGISTRY_ADAPTERS` / `TIR_ADAPTERS`; a second copy in `environments.py` would be a second source of truth for the same fact. The row stays name + `fixed_host` (pinned: `dataclasses.fields` is exactly `["name", "fixed_host"]`). `nodes._ENVIRONMENTS` stays where it is: the TNL's `pilot` is the node-derived ledger and the table's `pilot` is the deprecated alias of `legacy-pilot`, so the two cannot share one tuple before the MAJOR. There is no node-derived `pilot` row; the 2.0 end state is the one recorded on #74.

## Tests (`tests/test_ebsi_environments.py`, new section D)

Negatives first: exact class for both names, `isinstance` of the three parents, message names `for_nodes`/`verify_node_list`/`EBSI-Node-Trust`, raised before any client (`httpx.Client` patched to fail, with a control showing the patch fires), silent under `simplefilter("error")`, `str` subclass / `(str, Enum)` read by characters, the "known:" list pinned to the four names, `environments.py` imported with `httpx` blocked (now also asserting the two rows).

- On `origin/main` plus a bare `NodeDerivedEnvironment` class (so the file imports): **25 tests fail**.
- Six mutations of this branch, each caught by named tests: remove the `preprod` row (16 fail), remove the `prod` row (15), remove the `fixed_host is None` branch (18), give `prod` a host so it is projected (25), hard-code the two names in `for_ebsi` instead of reading the row (2, the two table-driven tests), make `.base` never `None` (3).
- Existing pins moved by the new rows, each marked `MOVED`: the "known:" loop now iterates `EBSI_HOSTS`, the table-shape test is six names, the fixed-host test filters rows with a host, the httpx-blocked output lists six names.

Local gate: exit 0 (flake8, mypy, 21283 passed / 41 skipped, coverage 95.6%, build + twine).

## Beyond the letter of the brief

- `wiki/EBSI-Node-Trust.md`: besides the one table row, the heading `## The three names today` became `## The names today` (it already read "three" over four rows; nothing links to it).
- `http.py`: only `for_ebsi` and its docstring changed, plus two names added to the existing import block (`ENVIRONMENTS`, `NodeDerivedEnvironment`); that import block is where a sibling PR on `http.py` could conflict (trivially).
- No adversarial review (additive, no parser or verify path), per the scoping comment.

Closes #325

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>supercorp-ai/supergateway (harbor.cloud.traunseenet.com/ghcr.io/supercorp-ai/supergateway)</summary>

### [`v4.2.0`](https://redirect.github.com/supercorp-ai/supergateway/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#420)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/supercorp-ai/supergateway/compare/v4.1.0...v4.2.0)

Upgrading from 4.1.0. No breaking changes: everything new is behind a new flag or a config file, and a 4.1.0 command line runs as it did.

##### New

- **Several servers from one config file.** `--config servers.json` reads the `mcpServers` file Claude Desktop and other clients use, and serves each server at `/<name>` on one port. Any option can be set per server or as a default. `--checkConfig` validates a file, and `--printConfig` prints the resolved one.
- **Servers combined on one URL.** An entry with its own `mcpServers` is served as one MCP server: tools, prompts and resources of all of them, with requests from the servers to the client (sampling, roots, elicitation) passed through. A combined entry can also be the one stdio server a desktop client launches.
- **Remote servers over any transport.** `--sse` and `--streamableHttp` servers (and `url` entries) can be served over SSE, WebSocket or Streamable HTTP, not only bridged to stdio. One remote entry may stay on stdio beside servers on the port.
- **`--toolPrefix` and `--tools`**: put a prefix before a server's tool names, and expose only the tools listed.
- **`--healthCheck server`**: the health endpoints start the MCP server, initialize and ping it, and answer 503 with the reason when it does not respond.
- **`--apiKey`, `--apiKeyFile`, `SUPERGATEWAY_API_KEY`**: require clients to present a key, as `Authorization: Bearer` or `X-API-Key`.
- **`--host`**: the address to listen on.
- **`--logFormat json`**: one JSON object per log line.
- **`--exitWithProcess <pid>`**: shut down, stopping the server, when the launcher exits.
- **Standalone executables and a Homebrew formula**: Supergateway with Node built in, for macOS, Linux (glibc and musl) and Windows.
- **MCP 2026-07-28** is now also served for a remote Streamable HTTP server and for combined servers, when they speak it; otherwise clients fall back as before.
- Unknown options and stray arguments are warned about at startup.
- `--printConfig` replaces every `env` value and the whole query of every URL, so a printed config carries no secrets. Command lines (`args`, `stdio`) are printed as written.

##### Fixes

- A client that reconnects to an SSE or WebSocket gateway without initializing again (as the TypeScript SDK's SSE client does after a dropped stream) no longer has its calls refused by servers that enforce the handshake. A 4.1.0 regression.
- A client that retries after a slow server's start timed out now gets the server already starting, instead of starting a new one each time and timing out forever. A 4.1.0 regression.
- The `--sse` and `--streamableHttp` bridges stop reading the remote server while their client is not reading, instead of holding its output in memory.
- The bridges pass an upstream application error through with its own code, as before 4.0.0.
- `--stdio=cmd` and `--streamable-http url` start the gateway instead of "stdio→undefined not supported".
- A call's progress on a stateful session rides that call's own response stream when several calls are in flight.
- A stateful session whose server fails at startup no longer logs a counting error.
- A `--header` given as one word with no colon is no longer written to the log.
- On macOS, stopping a server no longer logs `Failed to signal child ... kill EPERM` with a stack trace when the server has exited but is not reaped yet.

</details>

author: coral-coder
body:
## What changed

Myna becomes **a Bee companion**, as you asked — no microphone, no listening. It imports your Bee conversations and parses each transcript for the things you actually want out of them — shopping lists, appointments, dates, contacts, phone numbers, to-dos — and surfaces each as an **accept / dismiss suggestion** in a new **Inbox**. Nothing is acted on until you tap Accept.

### Parsing (the core of it)
- `TranscriptParser` uses **`NSDataDetector`** for dates → appointments, phone numbers, addresses and links, plus **deterministic keyword heuristics** for shopping items and to-dos (speaker-label aware, word-boundary aware).
- **Deliberately does *not* use the on-device LLM** — that was the thing giving you your calendar when you asked for the weather. Plain pattern-matching is predictable, and you're the one who accepts each suggestion anyway.
- The heuristics are Foundation-only and **unit-tested** (13 new tests).

### Inbox
- New default tab (replaces the mic-first "Listen" screen). Each suggestion shows its kind, the text, the sentence it came from, and which Bee conversation.
- Accept routes into the existing machinery: shopping/to-do/reminder lists, calendar for appointments (falls back to a dated reminder with no calendar access), memo for contacts/numbers/links.
- Dismissed suggestions are remembered so the same thing is never offered twice.
- Pull-to-refresh pulls fresh Bee conversations.

### Mic off
- The iPhone microphone is **off by default** — no auto-start, nothing recorded on the phone. Still toggleable back on in Backstage for anyone who wants it. Bee import keeps running in the background regardless.

### Backstage lag
- Cached the installed-voice enumeration. `AVSpeechSynthesisVoice.speechVoices()` was being called on every render (once for the label, once per picker row), which is what made the screen lag.

## Testing
- 13 new `TranscriptParserTests` covering shopping/to-do extraction, speaker-label stripping, word-boundary matching, clause tidying, and dedup. Builds on the neural-voice work (#19) already on main.

author: mrousavy
body:
Explicit module builds can preprocess C++ headers for the SDK target and then emit their inline code for an older Swift deployment target. For example, `std::make_exception_ptr` can reference `__cxa_init_primary_exception` in an iOS 15.1 build. Header constants can also retain values selected for the newer target.

This draft adds a deployment-target Clang AST for Swift imports and code generation. Separate SDK and producer ASTs supply compatible declarations missing from that AST. Existing deployment definitions keep their own bodies, initializers and attributes. References that fail compatibility checks produce diagnostics.

The scanner exports each context's primary target, secondary target, native Clang hash and resolved `cc1` arguments, including the optimization and debug settings applied by Swift. This mode enables Clang's strict context hashing to distinguish header search paths and VFS overlays. Serialized Swift references retain their originating context, including references forwarded through another Swift module. The companion driver plans explicit PCMs for these contexts and includes them in Swift module dependencies and cache invalidation.

The entry point is the experimental driver flag `-experimental-clang-codegen-target-context`. This requires [swiftlang/swift-driver#2239](https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-driver/pull/2239). The serialized metadata bumps the Swift module format from 1039 to 1040, the dependency scan cache minor version from 9 to 10, and the scanner C API minor version from 4 to 5.

This is a draft for the import model and its rollout. The implementation rejects adding executable definitions or default/member initializers from another context, as well as declarations from hidden modules. New special, virtual, operator and template members are unsupported. Binary reconstruction requires saved configuration and access to the recorded headers and SDK paths. Conflicting saved relative-path configurations are rejected. CAS, incremental compilation, root target variants, bridging headers and PCH are outside this draft. The ABI checks cover record layout, bases and virtual declaration structure; complete vtable equivalence remains unproven. Supplemental bridge annotations and derived conformances also need further coverage before general use.

Validation is limited to macOS and iOS targets. Full Swift CI and compile-time measurements have not been run.

author: e-lo
body:
Three small follow-ups from the re-review of #248. That PR merged before they landed.

- **The undo side of the reconcile race is now closed** (the add side was closed in #248). A route reads `host.pending_edits` outside the session lock. A read taken before an `undo_change` still lists the undone edits as pending, so reconciling with it put the undone change back for a moment.
  - `CardsState` keeps a generation counter. `pop` bumps it under the plugin lock and stores it on each undone entry (`Undone.popped`).
  - `flow.pending_seqs` captures the generation before reading `host.pending_edits`.
  - An undo newer than the read is never restored. A real rollback of an undo still restores it, because the next read is taken after it.
  - New test: add, stale read, undo, `sync(stale)`. Together with the add-side test from #248, a stale read can now neither drop an add nor resurrect an undo.
- **`host.dispatch` is refused from a rollback callback.** `dispatch_recorded` now raises `RuntimeError("host.dispatch cannot be called from a rollback callback")`, like `mutate`, `derive`, `undo` and `on_rollback`. Otherwise history would record an Action the rollback hides. Docstrings, the cookbook and the CHANGELOG are updated, and `"dispatch"` is added to the parametrized test, using a non-mutating Action so the dispatch guard itself is exercised.
- **Stale comment:** `plugin.py`'s `REQUIRES_API` comment now says `assistant_compact`.

author: atulya-srivastava
body: ## Overview This pull request introduces native moved code block detection and visualization to the px0 diff viewer for both split and unified view modes. When refactoring code (e.g., reordering functions or relocating logic blocks), standard git diffs represent relocated lines as disjoint deletions and additions. This implementation identifies identical blocks across hunks, isolates them from unrelated adjacent modifications, provides source/destination navigation bars, and renders non-overlapping orthogonal connector paths across a dynamically sized middle gutter. This feature is inspired by Visual Studio Code's moved code detection and split-diff connector visualization (`diffEditor.experimental.showMoves`), adapted for px0's lightweight, dependency-free web architecture. This PR closes #257 and is a continuation to PR #253 ## Moved Code Detection The diff viewer detects code that was cut from one place and pasted in another, and shows it as a move instead of an unrelated delete and add. ### Features - **Moved block detection**: matches runs of deleted lines against runs of added lines across all hunks. Matches must be at least 3 lines, longest blocks first. - **Trivial line filtering**: ignores blank lines, lone brackets, punctuation, and delimiters (`{}[]();,/\*`) to avoid false positives on structural syntax. - **Per-document numbering**: moves are labeled `move-1`, `move-2`, ... and reset on re-render, so state never leaks between tabs. - **Clean split-view pairing**: moved lines are isolated from normal add/delete pairing, so they never line up beside unrelated changes. Remaining changes keep token-level Myers highlighting. - **Adaptive middle gutter**: - No moves: gutter is hidden (`display: none`), keeping a 50/50 split with a single 1px divider. - With moves: a sweep-line pass assigns each overlapping move its own lane (greedy interval coloring), so connectors never overlap. - Width scales from 28px to 84px with lane count via `--diff-gutter-w`. - **Orthogonal SVG connectors**: right-angle paths (`M x1 y1 L xTrack y1 L xTrack y2 L x2 y2`) with arrowheads, confined to the gutter. - **Live tracking**: connectors recalculate on pane resize, window resize, and sash drag using `ResizeObserver` and `mousemove` throttled with `requestAnimationFrame`. - **Native scrolling**: the SVG layer sits in `#diffcontent` coordinate space, so the browser compositor scrolls it without layout thrash. ### Navigation and Feedback - **Move headers**: `Code moved to line X–Y` on the deleted side and `Code moved from line X–Y` on the added side, each with a jump control. - **Scroll-settled highlight**: jumping smooth-scrolls to center the target, waits for `scrollend`, pauses `FLASH_PAUSE_MS` (180ms), then flashes the destination. - **Overlay flash**: an `::after` pseudo-element fades opacity from 1 to 0 over 1.0s. This avoids per-row line artifacts and leaves syntax backgrounds intact. - **Unified hover**: hovering the source header, connector arrow, or destination block highlights all three together. ## Inspiration & Prior Art The design, UI placement, and navigation model in this PR are inspired by the moved code detection architecture in Visual Studio Code (`diffEditor.experimental.showMoves` / Monaco Editor's `linesDiffComputers`), adapted here to operate directly on parsed unified diffs within px0's vanilla JavaScript and CSS runtime. --- ### Implemented Feature --> https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e5956dfc-9465-4b6b-8ba9-281d6a121247 ## Performance Optimizations | Subsystem | Issue Addressed | Implementation Detail | |---|---|---| | **Move Detection** | $O(N^3)$ sub-slice explosion on large diffs | Added an $O(1)$ prefix check to skip redundant suffix sub-slices, evaluating only maximal common substrings. | | **DOM Queries** | Querying all code row elements for move identifiers | Scoped queries specifically to `.diff-side-move-header` and `.diff-move-bar` instead of all row nodes. | | **Scroll Pipeline** | SVG reconstruction on every scroll event | Removed the scroll event listener; the SVG layer is positioned in content space and scrolls natively. | | **Event Bubbling** | Mouse event thrashing over descendant syntax spans | Added `e.relatedTarget` checks to ensure hover recalculations trigger only when crossing move block boundaries. | | **Animation Rendering** | Background override snapping back abruptly | Implemented `.diff-row-flash::after` overlay fading, preventing layout redraws and background overrides. | --- ## Files Changed - **`web/src/diff.js`**: - Implemented `detectMoves`, `computeMaxConcurrentTracks`, and `isValidMoveSlice`. - Implemented `drawMoveConnectors`, `jumpAndFlash`, and `flashMoveSection`. - Updated `pairRows`, `splitTable`, and `unifiedTable` for move segmentation and intra-line diffing. - Added corridor visibility and counter reset handling in `renderDiff`. - **`web/style.css`**: - Added `.diff-move-bar`, `.diff-moved-row`, and `.has-diff-moves` styles. - Implemented `.diff-split-gutter` corridor layout rules with conditional activation. - Added SVG path and hover state styling. - Updated `.diff-row-flash` to a borderless overlay animation. --- ## Verification - Verified moved block detection and connector generation across multiple hunks in split layout. - Verified moved block rendering and intra-line pairing in unified layout. - Verified that diffs without moved blocks render with zero middle corridor width. - Verified sweep-line interval lane allocation when moves overlap vertically. - Verified that jump controls scroll to destination and trigger synchronized highlight upon arrival. - Verified that switching tabs between diff and source views does not trigger spurious row flashing. - Verified connector geometry tracking during layout and sash resizes. - Verified frontend checks via `node --check` and clean compilation via `make build`.

author: pcbeingused333
body:
## What

`generateSolution` creates one `context.WithTimeout(..., 30*time.Second)` before the loop and uses it for every issue. The requests run one after another, so they share a single 30 second deadline: with a handful of issues, or one slow model (a thinking model can take 20 seconds or more for a single answer), the deadline expires part way through. The next request fails with `context deadline exceeded`, `GenerateSolution` returns the error, `main` only logs it, and every remaining issue is reported without an autofix.

## Fix

Create the timeout per request (`generateWithTimeout`), so each issue gets the full 30 seconds. Nothing else changes: the cache, the empty-response check and the error wrapping are the same.

## Tests

`TestGenerateSolution_EachIssueGetsItsOwnTimeout` records the context deadline of two consecutive requests and checks that the second one is later than the first. On master both are the same shared deadline and the test fails; with the change it passes. `go test ./autofix/`, `go vet ./autofix/` and `gofmt` are clean.

This change was made with Claude Code.

author: johnnymo87
body:
#### Description

Phase 1 of cross-machine swarm messaging (epic `pigeon-k0qn`, spec `docs/plans/2026-10-20-cross-machine-swarm-design.md` §1–§2). A swarm message to a session on **another machine** now fails within one arbiter tick and says why. Before, it retried for minutes, wrote a phantom routing placement, posted a Telegram notice into the wrong chat, and ended in an unexplained `delivery.failed`.

- **Locality check before delivery (daemon).** The arbiter now decides whether the target is local, remote or unknown before it builds a delivery client (`routing/locality.ts`):
  - **Local:** the session has a local session row, or any serve on this machine answers 200 for it.
  - **Remote:** it has no local row, no serve answers 200, and at least one serve answers 404. A `gse_` id with no row is also remote; serves are never probed for `gse_` ids, because they answer 500.
  - **Unknown:** anything else. It is retried as an outage, never treated as remote.
  - The check is read-only, so a remote id never reaches the router path that writes a placement.
- **Remote fails on the first attempt.** The sender's `delivery.failed` says the message was not received and not to resend via swarm. When the worker answers within 2s, it also names the machine the session is registered to.
- **New worker route (`pigeon-k0qn.1`).** `GET /sessions/:id/owner` returns `{machine_id, last_seen}`, or 404. It is read-only and used only to word that failure message.
- **No foreign Telegram notice (`pigeon-qioa`).** The outbox holds a swarm notice whose session has no local row, and drops it after 60s. Another machine's session never gains a row, so its notice is never posted. A session that was reaped and is then revived by the message normally re-registers within that window, so it still gets its notice.
- **Docs (`pigeon-k0qn.3`).** AGENTS.md and the swarm and daemon skills describe the above. The references to the removed `pigeon-send` / `opencode-send` CLIs are replaced with the `swarm_send` tool.

**Deploy:** deploy the worker and restart the daemon on each machine, in either order. A new daemon against an old worker just omits the machine name.

#### References

- Epic `pigeon-k0qn`; beads `pigeon-qioa`, `pigeon-k0qn.1`, `pigeon-k0qn.2`, `pigeon-k0qn.3`
- Implementation plan: `docs/plans/2026-10-20-cross-machine-swarm-phase1-plan.md`
- Incident: `pigeon-533h` (#183)

These tests read fixture repositories, not this corpus, and their Git calls have a 5-second limit, so slow runs can fail them.

- No spec is written here. The six reset intents still need their decomposition recorded when their specs are written.

body:
Delivers the Responses portion of M7.11 with reusable generic and closed-shape API-key request fakes.

- Scripts JSON, exact SSE and raw responses, including benign, obedient, schema-breaking, refusing, slow, authentication, rate and quota cases. Supports controlled Date headers, finite chunking, abort/cancel and common faults.
- Exposes `handler(request)` and `recorder` for unchanged-request composition. Direct handler calls retain defensive byte/chunk/error controls; ordinary `fetch` and loopback `listen` apply shared capped intake, recording and faults.
- Caps requests at one MiB before handler admission. Tests received-prefix refusal hashes, fault ownership, incomplete-slot discard, custom recorder receivers, raw targets and loopback behavior.
- Bounds queued response payloads to 64 MiB, prepared incrementally and atomically, released at app admission. Caller data, headers, serialization temporaries and active responses remain separate. No original-ingress chunk-count, duration or global-memory limit is claimed.
- Carries #140 minor 1: adds `on-demand.test.ts` to both M7.4's required command and the EXEC command reference.

Validation:

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passed.
- From `packages/fakes`, `pnpm exec vitest run --reporter=default --exclude '**/*siwc*/**' --exclude '**/*siwc*' --exclude '**/*dynamic-agent*' --exclude '**/*dynamic_agent*' --maxWorkers=1`: 252 tests passed across six files, including 165 Responses tests.
- `pnpm --filter @draftyak/fakes typecheck` and `build` passed. Workspace and built root/subpath export smoke passed, including handler/recorder behavior.
- Changed-file Biome, whitespace checks, `pnpm guard` and `node tools/verify/verify.ts --profile docs` passed; guard reported zero findings and all nine ADRs passed.
- Twenty targeted mutations failed and were restored exactly: shared intake, raw target, queue byte cap/release/atomicity/reentrancy/UTF-8 accounting, step/event/name/actual-yield/response-chunk limits, direct byte/chunk limits, malformed-input and abort cancellation, closed fields, store, stream and fatal UTF-8.

Not run: vendor/live/device checks, native pin/credential/schema/consent authority or native provider/corpus execution. Messages and compatible/native composition retain their existing M7.11/M7.6 ownership and acceptance. These synthetic scripts establish none of those gates.

Self-check:

- Scope is the Responses fake and tests, its single root export/README section, and the two carried acceptance-command corrections. Shared server/recorder/faults and package configuration are unchanged.
- Independent literal wire fixtures and positive boundaries accompany hostile and mutation controls. Event names retain exact ASCII boundaries; schemas remain opaque fixture data and JSON uses ordinary last-member semantics.
- Actual yielded events are counted before observing an excess entry's properties, with atomic rollback and no later event/step preparation. Caller JavaScript and serialization remain trusted fixture configuration, with no runtime sandbox claim.
- No new owner decision or dependency is required for this synthetic slice. Native and owner-session prerequisites remain explicit.

author: raj-codal
body:
### Description

`asFieldRefsByTypePath` built its lookup with `reduce((acc, ref) => ({...acc, [ref.key]: ref}), {})`. Spreading the accumulator copies every key collected so far for each new ref, so the cost grows with the square of the number of refs.

It runs from `createFieldRefCache` when `AssistDocumentLayout` mounts. That happens the first time each document type is opened, whether or not Assist is used on the document. Page-builder schemas produce a lot of refs at the default `maxFieldSelectionDepth` of 6, because each array member type adds its own subtree.

On a production Studio, a document type with two page-builder arrays of about 90 block types each produces about 26,000 refs, and the first open blocked the main thread for about 50 s. Page types with one builder blocked for about 10 s. `options.aiAssist.exclude` doesn't help, because `getObjectFieldRefs` still walks into excluded fields.

This PR:
- builds the lookup in a single pass;
- removes the file-level `oxlint-disable no-accumulating-spread` from `helpers.ts`, which was only covering this `reduce`. `pnpm lint` passes without it.

### What to review

- `asFieldRefsByTypePath` returns the same object: the same keys in the same order, and the last ref wins on a duplicate key, as with the spread.
- `translate/paths.ts` and `helpers/conditionalMembers.ts` keep the same file-level disable for `[...acc, ...]` array spreads. Those walk document values per action rather than on mount and didn't show up in our profiles, so they're left for a follow-up.

### Testing

- New `asFieldRefsByTypePath` tests in `helpers.test.ts`:
  - The lookup matches `getFieldRefs` output key for key.
  - A 10,000-ref lookup finishes in under 1 s. It takes about 7 ms with this change and about 11 s with the previous `reduce`, so the test fails on a regression.
- `vitest run --project @sanity/assist`: 10 files, 65 tests pass.
- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm knip` and `pnpm --filter @sanity/assist build` pass. `oxfmt --check` is clean on the changed files.
- Standalone repro using `@sanity/schema` 6.16.0 with a synthetic 90-block page builder, at default depth: 16,998 refs, 32.9 s with `reduce` and 10.3 ms with the loop, identical lookups.
- Same change applied as a `pnpm patch` to `@sanity/assist` 6.2.1 in a production Studio (`sanity` 6.16.0), measured on the same document:

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Form ready | 58.4 s | 7.5 s |
| Longest main-thread task | 50.2 s | 0.53 s |
| Total blocking on load | 53.8 s | 4.0 s |

### Notes for release

`@sanity/assist`: opening documents with large page-builder schemas no longer freezes the Studio while Assist builds its field lookup.

body:
Ruler Alertmanager basic\-auth password stored as plaintext config string and disclosed by unauthenticated \/config

## Risk assessment

**Severity: High**

**Likelihood: Moderate · Impact: High**

| Dimension | Recorded assessment | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reachable from attacker | Yes | Finding |
| Configuration required | Yes | Finding |
| Access required | None | Code |
| User interaction required | No | Finding |
| Attacker gains | Read | Finding |
| Blast radius | Cross\-tenant | Finding |
| Target value | High | Finding |

<details>
<summary>Assessment reasons and what could change this assessment</summary>

### Reachable from attacker

The \/config endpoint is on the same HTTP listener tenants use for push\/query \(per finding\/validation\)\, registered with auth\=false \(pkg\/api\/api\.go\:220\)\. Cortex authenticates nothing by design — tenants\/clients on the network reach the port directly\. Operators are instructed to front it with a reverse proxy but the component itself accepts untrusted inbound\. In typical multi\-tenant Cortex deployments the port is reachable by tenants \(external\) with no credentials\.

**What could change this assessment:** Confirmation of the specific deployment\'s network topology — if \/config is strictly behind an internal\-only load balancer\/VPN with no tenant\/internet exposure\, this would flip to false\.

### Configuration required

Both the ruler Alertmanager basic\-auth password and alertmanager\_url userinfo default to empty\. The validation explicitly lists as a precondition\: \'Operator configures ruler\->Alertmanager basic auth via \-ruler\.alertmanager\-client\.basic\-auth\-password \.\.\. both default to empty\, so a default install discloses nothing\.\' A non\-default operator config must be in place for the password to be leaked\.

**What could change this assessment:** Evidence that the ruler is deployed in a mode where Alertmanager credentials are set by default \(e\.g\.\, a specific distribution\/helm chart that pre\-populates them\) would flip this to false\.

### Access required

pkg\/api\/api\.go\:220 registers \/config with the auth flag set to false\; pkg\/api\/api\.go\:138\-181 conditionally wraps with AuthenticateUser only when auth\=true\, so no identity check sits in front of the handler\. The validation confirms \'auth flag \= false \-> AuthMiddleware not wrapped\' and that even an empty X\-Scope\-OrgID is accepted on this route\. The endpoint is reachable with no credentials\.

**What could change this assessment:** Evidence that the deployment places a mandatory authenticating reverse proxy \(e\.g\.\, mTLS\, OIDC gateway\) in front of \/config would raise this to any\_authenticated or privileged — but no such in\-process control exists\.

### User interaction required

Steps to reproduce are a single unauthenticated GET \/config by the attacker\, parsing YAML for the plaintext password\, then using it against the Alertmanager\. No other user action\, click\, or triggered event is required\.

**What could change this assessment:** A scenario where \/config only emits the live config after an operator\-triggered reload would introduce interaction — not the case here \(it marshals live config on every request\)\.

### Attacker gains

Unauthenticated GET \/config returns YAML containing the ruler\->Alertmanager basic\_auth\_password and any userinfo in alertmanager\_url in cleartext \(util\.BasicAuth\.Password is a plain string with no MarshalYAML masking\)\. The direct\, demonstrated capability is reading an operator\-owned credential\. Follow\-on use of that credential against Alertmanager \(injecting\/silencing alerts\) is a separate downstream action enabled by the leak\, but the finding\'s primary technical impact is credential disclosure\.

**What could change this assessment:** Evidence that \/config can also be written via the same unauth path would elevate to modify\; absent that\, disclosure is the demonstrated gain\.

### Blast radius

Cortex is a multi\-tenant system where tenant identity is asserted via X\-Scope\-OrgID\. The leaked credential is for the operator\-owned Alertmanager that serves ALL tenants\; with it \(and an arbitrary X\-Scope\-OrgID\)\, an attacker can post\/resolve alerts and read Alertmanager state for arbitrary victim tenants \(confirmed by proof\-of\-exploit source walk in pkg\/alertmanager\/multitenant\.go\: tenant resolved solely from header\, no binding to basic\-auth identity\)\. The leak itself is a single shared operator credential affecting all tenants\' alerting integrity\.

**What could change this assessment:** If deployed as single\-tenant \(no multiple customer orgs\) and the Alertmanager served only one org\, blast radius would drop to own\/other\_users\_in\_tenant\.

### Target value

The disclosed data is a live outbound basic\-auth credential \(and potentially URL userinfo\) used by the ruler to authenticate to the operator\'s Alertmanager\. Credentials\/secrets are explicitly high\-value per the rubric\, and the finding and validation confirm the value is a real credential \(consumed as config\_util\.Secret at pkg\/ruler\/notifier\.go\:193\)\.

**What could change this assessment:** If the field were documented as unused\/placeholder rather than a live credential\, this would drop to medium\.



</details>

## Remediation

Masked the ruler→Alertmanager basic\-auth password on YAML marshalling and redacted userinfo from \`alertmanager\_url\` so unauthenticated \`GET \/config\` no longer discloses the operator\'s Alertmanager credentials\.

<details>
<summary>Recorded change details</summary>

Changes\: \- pkg\/util\/http\.go\: \`BasicAuth\.Password\` retyped to \`flagext\.Secret\` \(yaml tag \`basic\_auth\_password\` unchanged\)\. \`flagext\.Secret\.MarshalYAML\` renders non\-empty values as \`\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\`\, matching the s3\/consul pattern\. Flag registration switched from \`StringVar\` to \`f\.Var\(&b\.Password\, …\)\`\; flag name and help unchanged\. \`IsEnabled\` checks \`\.Value\`\. \- pkg\/ruler\/notifier\.go\: pass \`BasicAuth\.Password\.Value\` into \`config\_util\.Secret\(\.\.\.\)\`\; outbound auth unchanged\. \- pkg\/ruler\/ruler\.go\: added \`Config\.MarshalYAML\` that returns a \`type plain Config\` copy with \`AlertmanagerURL\` run through a new \`redactAlertmanagerURLsCredentials\` helper \(parses each comma\-separated URL and strips \`url\.User\`\)\. Load path\, \`\-ruler\.alertmanager\-url\` flag\, and in\-process use of \`AlertmanagerURL\` \(including \`buildNotifierConfig\`\) are unchanged — only YAML output is sanitized\. \- pkg\/ruler\/notifier\_test\.go\: updated the one literal using \`Password\: \"test\"\` to \`flagext\.Secret\{Value\: \"test\"\}\`\.

Follow\-ups a human must decide \(not in this patch\)\: \- Authenticating \`\/config\` \(pkg\/api\/api\.go\:220 registers with auth\=false\) — contract change\; disclosure is already mitigated by this patch regardless\. \- Password\-file support preferred over inline value — operator policy decision\.

Verification\: grep shows no other call sites use \`util\.BasicAuth\.Password\` as a string\. No Go toolchain in sandbox\; changes reviewed by inspection\.

</details>

## Proof

**Recorded evidence level: Static proven.**

Recorded source analysis; patch execution results are not included in this evidence.

<details>
<summary>Recorded source analysis</summary>

Source artifact: 01a15b43ee337750a865527c3ce87cce · Issue 01a15b339d2d7363ba8b2ee2f7297dbf.

```python
# Annotated entry->sink walk (SOURCE_ONLY, infra level 1)
# Finding 01a15b2eb35071ada3bdb78224f12fdf — layer 2 (credential USE / cross-tenant Alertmanager compromise)
# CWEs: 522 (leaked credential) enabling 284 / 668 / 807 (untrusted X-Scope-OrgID in a security decision)
#
# ATTACKER BOUNDARY: an HTTP request to the operator-owned Cortex multitenant Alertmanager,
# authenticated with the ruler->Alertmanager basic-auth credential stolen in layer 1, carrying an
# attacker-chosen X-Sc

body:
Operators cannot easily tell whether their node's libp2p port is reachable from outside: a closed forward, a firewall and a wrong listener all look like silence.

Add `qclient node diagnostics dial <multiaddr> [--peer <id>] [--timeout <secs>]`. It dials one TCP or QUIC v1 address as a throwaway Ed25519 identity over the network's stack (PQNoise sntrup761 and yamux, or QUIC with the sntrup761 TLS fork), verifies the peer ID named by `--peer` or `/p2p`, and prints the peer's identify answer (agent, protocol version, protocols, listen addresses with public/private reach, observed address), connect time and one ping. Failures name their cause: refused, no answer, failed or stalled handshake, peer ID mismatch. It contacts only that address; under torsocks (TCP) the peer sees a Tor exit.

Tests: `cargo nextest run --workspace` 4696 passed, including in-process TCP and QUIC listener tests; a mutant skipping the peer check fails two; release build of `quil-node` and `qclient`; dialed live mainnet nodes through Tor.

author: shaan-shoukath
body:
The second half of ticketing extras, after purchase, plus refunds when an event is cancelled.

## Refunds when an event is cancelled
- **"Cancel event"** (owners and admins, in the event's Manage section):
  - registration closes and the page shows it's cancelled;
  - every paid order is refunded in full and cancelled, and the buyer gets the refund email;
  - orders still being paid for are released, and open requests are declined;
  - free guests are emailed.

  Running it again only finishes what's left, so nobody is refunded twice. An order someone already checked in on is counted for the organiser to settle by hand.
- **Deleting a paid event or series is refused** ("Cancel it instead, which refunds them in full"). Before, deleting an event left its paid orders without tickets or a refund.
- **Complimentary or unpaid cancellations** now email the buyer ("Your order was cancelled… nothing to refund"). Before, they got no email.

## Disputes (chargebacks)
- Razorpay `payment.dispute.*` and Stripe `charge.dispute.*` webhooks are parsed into a new `PaymentDispute` row (status, amount, reason, respond-by). Each dispute is matched only to a payment of the same organisation and provider.
- A new dispute, or a change of status, emails the owners with the deadline and what to do. Nothing is cancelled automatically.
- The guest list shows "Disputed", and the payment dialog explains it.

## Transfers
- Organisers allow transfers per event or series, until N hours before the start (each date's start for a series).
- Buyers press "Transfer" on the order page and enter a name and email:
  - the ticket gets a new link, so the old one stops working;
  - the new holder is emailed their ticket, and the old address is told;
  - a pass moves every remaining date together;
  - checked-in tickets never move.

## Pay at the desk
- A ticket type can allow it. When every chosen ticket does, the form offers "Pay online now" or "Pay at the desk".
- Desk orders are confirmed straight away with one pending offline payment, and the buyer gets a "pay at the desk" email.
- The guest list shows "To pay ₹X at the desk". "Mark as paid" records it and sends the receipt.
- Cancelling closes the payment (`CANCELED`).

## Payment reminders
- One reminder, about 3 hours before a day-long payment link runs out (after approval, a waitlist place, or an organiser's link). The order is claimed first, so it's never sent twice.

## Schema
Migration `20261028000000_after_purchase`; defaults keep today's behaviour and no rows change.
- `PaymentDispute`, with checks.
- `Order.paymentReminderSentAt`.
- `Event` and `EventSeries` get `allowTransfers` and `transferCutoffHours`.
- `TicketType.payAtDesk`.

The schema contract and the migration-safety test are updated.

## Not included
Changing a booked guest's ticket type with a price difference. Today the organiser refunds and rebooks.

## Verified
- New DB tests in `after-purchase.db.test.ts` (7):
  - the complimentary-cancel email;
  - the reminder sent once;
  - Razorpay and Stripe disputes through signed webhooks (opened, then won);
  - paying at the desk: reserved, collected, cancelled, and refused for online-only tickets;
  - transfers: not allowed, a new link, the old link gone, and too close to the start;
  - cancelling an event: refunds, emails, a released hold, delete refused, and safe to repeat.
- The full DB suite passes 160/160; tsc, eslint and the catalog are clean.
- The payments browser suite passes 14/14 locally, including a new test: reserve to pay at the desk, then transfer the ticket from the order page.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: alefranz
body:
## Summary

Ordinary `/work` and `/autonomous` activations now finalize routing with a single mechanical helper call. The mechanical startup work — preference-location discovery, installed-default resolution, and the OpenCode agent-profile comparison — moves into a new packaged `routing.mjs startup` subcommand, and the bootstrap is rewritten around a quiet short path: no narrated pre-dispatch routing, nothing created when preference files are absent, and the snapshot fixed for the activation (including compaction).

## Why

On a fresh install every part of the bootstrap's routing work was already deterministic, yet the workflow still discovered locations, resolved defaults, and (on OpenCode) read and compared installed agent profiles in context before the first dispatch. `startup` does that mechanical part and prints the finalized snapshot (`policy`, `routeProvenance`, `profile`, and on OpenCode the per-role `agents` comparison), so the workflow can dispatch immediately. The in-context interpretation paths remain only for the cases that genuinely need them — a discovered preference file, or invocation-level preferences — and they are the only two paths that ever write a temporary layers file.

## Reviewer-relevant semantics

- **Missing preference files are normal.** No creation, no clarification, no fallback investigation, no retry. An unreadable file is a genuine, actionable error on every path (exit 1), and is distinguished from absence.
- **Invocation-preference path:** `startup` serves only as the file-existence probe. Its results — including an unknown-profile failure — are provisional and unreported; profile availability is validated by the final `resolve --input <file> --profile NAME --explain`, which also accepts a profile defined by the invocation Markdown itself.
- **OpenCode agent comparison:** from the startup output on the short path; in context against the final snapshot on the interpretation paths. A missing, stale, or mismatched profile blocks only its own role's dispatch; an unused unavailable role never blocks.

## Compatibility

- Ships in plugin 0.11.0 (minor bump for the new capability); plugin and both marketplace catalogs regenerated.
- No migration for existing installs; the documented no-Node path is preserved, and ordinary activation never needs an AgenticAle source checkout.

## Validation notes

- The deterministic routing tests cover the full startup contract, including provisional-vs-final unknown-profile behavior and the agent-comparison statuses (match / mismatch / missing / unreadable, including the duplicate-frontmatter ambiguity case).
- Fixtures 16–18 are evaluation fixtures for the interpretation boundary, not live-model runs; live verification on a real host (named-set identifier acceptance, live model availability) remains open.

body:
MIGRATION-TASK: APP-PRINTING

Triaje: VÁLIDA — premisa verificada contra origin/main@b5135e4 (mergeado en la rama: hub#104, #106, #107, #103 y #105): la app `printing` tenía 4 flujos `no hecho` (F02, F10, F11, G01), 9 `parcial` y 7 `hecho` por revisar; desde la vuelta 1 del carril cash_register+invoice+kitchen+printing+reservation+sale+table+verifactu, las FIX de Ventas y Facturación hacia Impresión son de esta tarea (PLAN-MIGRATIONS §20). Sin PRs abiertas sobre `apps/printing`, `apps/sale/services.py` (sección «Paper») ni `apps/invoice`; `requires = []`; ninguna ronda posterior de los PLAN cambia Impresión (PLAN-HUB «El cobro y la comanda llaman a la cola dentro de su propia transacción»). Síntomas reproducidos con su test rojo antes de cada arreglo (`invoice.invoice.print` → `UnknownOperation`; «Search again» → `expected 'clear' to be 'outline'`; el cobro sin `printed`) y con `curl` el de `/ws/print` (fuera del carril, abajo).

## Qué cambia

### Vuelta 1 (carril nuevo: Ventas y Facturación piden su papel)

- **PRINTING-F07, F13 (Ventas):** el cobro pide su tique a Impresión **por nombre** (`printing.job.create`, sin `requires`), en un *savepoint* de su propia transacción (`apps/sale/services.py`, sección «Paper»): sigue los ajustes de Impresión (`automatic`) y la orden del cajón va **solo si entró efectivo** (`open_drawer`, nuevo en `printing.job.create`, por defecto `true`: nadie más cambia). La respuesta del cobro trae `printed` (`queued`, `job_id`, `printer`): el TPV dice «Enviado a <impresora>.» y el papel en pantalla pasa a ser copia. Sin Impresión encendida, sin impresora de tiques, con el documento fiscal aún pendiente o si Impresión lo rechaza, no se encola nada (el trabajo sin impresora se deshace: esperaría para siempre) y el cobro sigue: el tique sale por el diálogo del dispositivo. Repetir el cobro no saca otro tique. El papel lo compone Ventas (`apps/sale/paper.py`, puro: lo mismo que el papel de pantalla, con el QR de VeriFactu).
- **PRINTING-F08 (Ventas y Facturación):** `sale.sale.print` (Imprimir del Documento de venta y «Reimprimir» de la lista: copia «DUPLICADO») e `invoice.invoice.print` (nuevo: la página A4 de la factura para la impresora del sistema, en el idioma de quien imprime y con el QR de VeriFactu; si su registro no se puede leer, no se encola: nunca un papel sin su QR, VERIFACTU-F19). Las pantallas preguntan primero a la cola y, si no se encoló o la cola no responde, imprimen con el diálogo como antes.
- **PRINTING-F09 (Ventas):** `sale.order.print_bill`: la cuenta de la mesa va a la cola desde «Imprimir cuenta».
- **PRINTING-F17:** `hecho`: Caja ya imprime X/Z por la cola en `main` (hub#106), comprobado con su test de integración y su e2e en esta rama.
- **PRINTING-F02:** «Search again» del modal «Search printers» era `fill="clear"` y se leía como texto suelto (captura F02-834 de la vuelta 0): ahora es un botón con contorno e icono, con su test.
- **e2e:** `printing-sale.spec.ts` (nueva): cobro en efectivo en el TPV → tique en la cola con el cajón; cobro con tarjeta → sin cajón; «Imprimir» del documento → copia; «Reimprimir» de Ventas → copia; «Imprimir cuenta» → `prebill`; «Imprimir / PDF» de una factura → A4 en la impresora del sistema (y nunca en la de tiques). `invoice-sale.spec.ts` espera al diálogo (la impresión ahora pregunta antes a la cola).
- **Higiene e2e (causa de dos rojos de `printing-queue.spec.ts` al correr detrás de las specs que cobran):** los cobros dejaban en la cola hojas de cocina sin impresora y `printing.job.claim` de la spec siguiente se llevaba la más antigua. `cleanSales()` y la limpieza de `cash-register-flows.spec.ts` borran ahora los papeles de sus ventas y cuentas por su `job_key` (`sale-<venta>-…`, `sale-order-<cuenta>-…`, `kitchen-<ticket>-…`) antes de borrar los tickets; tras cada tanda, `select count(*) from printing_printjob` → `0`.
- **WORKBOOK:** PRINTING-F07, F08, F09, F17 → `hecho`; F13 `parcial` solo por la parte del dispositivo (hub#2724); «Quién la usa» y el estado de la app al día. SALE-F01 (paso 6), SALE-F21 y SALE-F29 dicen que el papel va a la cola y, si no, al diálogo; INVOICE-F18 `hecho` sin el «Pendiente», con la acción nueva y lo que necesita de Impresión y VeriFactu (por nombre).

### Vuelta 0
- **PRINTING-F01 (hub#1527, printing#37):** cada tarjeta de función dice en qué impresora imprime («Imprime en: Caja 1.»), la elegida si está activa o la primera activa de su función; la nota de Impresoras no habla de navegadores a quien la lee dentro de la app de ERPlora.
- **PRINTING-F02:** «Buscar impresoras» en Impresoras: dentro de la app pide la lista al dispositivo (`erplora_discover_printers`, que ya existe en la app nativa) y abre «Nueva impresora» rellena con la que se elija; marca «Ya añadida» lo que el negocio ya tiene; no ofrece la A4 de oficina; dice por qué no encontró nada (navegador, permiso de red local denegado —hub#1773—, app no vinculada a este negocio, fallo) y «Añadir por su dirección» sigue siempre ahí. Tests nuevos donde faltaba el guardarraíl: todo control de texto con caja `fill="outline"` + `mode="md"` (printing#50), la función es una de cuatro y nunca una palabra libre (hub#457), la hoja de prueba A4 firmada por el negocio en el idioma de quien prueba (hub#1735, hub#1803; el mutante «ERPlora Bridge» sobrevivía), y la carrera de dos cajas sobre la misma comanda forzada en vez de dejada al reloj de los hilos (hub#2029; el mutante sin `select_for_update` sobrevivía).

body:
Cactus is switching Minigraph-Cactus genome names to PanSN: `SAMPLE#HAPLOTYPE`, or just `SAMPLE` for haplotype 0 (ComparativeGenomicsToolkit/cactus#2051, for cactus#2048). Those names now go into the HAL as-is, so `resolve_haplotype_naming` has to split them on the `#`.

| HAL genome | path before | path now |
|---|---|---|
| `HG002#1` | `HG002#1#0#chr1` | `HG002#1#chr1` |
| `KOLF2.1J` | `KOLF2#1#chr1` (`stol("1J")` is 1) | `KOLF2.1J#0#chr1` |
| `GCA_054883195.1#0` | `GCA_054883195#1#chr1` | `GCA_054883195.1#0#chr1` |
| `HG002.1` (HAL from an older cactus) | `HG002#1#chr1` | `HG002#1#chr1` |
| `X#y` | `X#y#0#chr1` | error |

The old `SAMPLE.HAPLOTYPE` spelling is still read, but only when the haplotype is all digits. That reading is unambiguous: the new cactus rewrites any name ending in `.N` to `SAMPLE#N`.

author: nambok
body:
## Summary
Agents could read a team's databases, GraphQL APIs, logs and search cluster, but not a REST API of a system the team uses (a booking or payments system, a vendor's API). When data is synced from such a system, the source's own record is the only way to tell whether the source or the sync is wrong. This adds a read-only REST connection.

## Changes
- `common/src/live/rest.rs` (new): `Rest::get(path, query)`.
  - Only GET is sent, to the team's `https://` base address, with its key in the header it names (`check_header` refuses `Host`, `Cookie` and transport headers).
  - The path must sit under one of the team's allowed prefixes at a segment boundary, and can't climb out (`..`, `//`, `\`, a query or fragment in the path are refused). Query parameters are plain name/value pairs.
  - JSON results go through the shared redaction (default hidden fields plus the team's); text answers through the text redaction. Capped at 30,000 characters.
- `connectors.rs`: `ConnKind::Rest` with `header_name` and `paths`.
- Gateway: save (address, header, key, up to 20 paths, hidden fields) and test (a GET of the first path); an integrations card.
- Worker `ops_tools.rs`: the `rest_get` tool for work on repos the connection covers, logged like every lookup. Skills know the tool.

## Verification
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p common -p gateway -p worker --all-targets -D warnings` clean.
- `cargo test`: common 362, gateway 131, worker 428 passed, 0 failed. New tests in `rest.rs`: `addresses_headers_and_paths_are_checked`, `only_paths_under_an_allowed_prefix`, `queries_are_plain_pairs`, `a_get_sends_the_key_in_its_header_and_hides_sensitive_fields`, `a_path_outside_the_allowed_ones_is_never_requested`.
- Dashboard form: CoderHelm/coderhelm (separate PR).

author: paulovitorjp
body:
Fixes #130.

**Why:** Omarchy's universal clipboard bindings send Shift+Insert only to windows tagged `terminal`. SparkDown isn't tagged, so Super+V reaches it as **Ctrl+V** and Super+C as **Ctrl+C**. Until now the terminal passed Ctrl+V to the shell as `^V`, so nothing was pasted.

**Terminal pane:**
- **Linux:**
  - **Ctrl+V** pastes when the clipboard has text. When the clipboard is empty or unreadable it sends `^V` (0x16), so the shell's quoted-insert still works.
  - **Ctrl+C** copies when there's a selection, then clears the selection. With no selection it is still **SIGINT**, so Super+C with nothing selected interrupts, the same as a real Ctrl+C.
- **All platforms:** **Shift+Insert** pastes.
- Unchanged: Ctrl+Shift+C/V, ⌘C/⌘V on macOS, every other Ctrl key, and Windows' plain Ctrl+C/V. Editor panes aren't touched.

**Tests:**
- `clipboardAction`, one case per key combination on each platform:
  - Linux Ctrl+V gives `paste-or-ctrl-v`.
  - Linux Ctrl+C copies with a selection and returns null (SIGINT) without one.
  - Shift+Insert pastes.
  - Ctrl+D/Z/R/L/A stay with the shell.
  - Windows and macOS are unchanged.
- `pasteOrCtrlV`: pastes the text, and sends `^V` when the clipboard is empty or the read fails.
- **E2E (Ubuntu): new `terminal-clipboard` check.** It uses real X key events through xdotool, with `xclip` (added to the Ubuntu job) setting the clipboard:
  - Ctrl+V pastes and runs a command that writes a file.
  - Shift+Insert does the same.
  - Ctrl+C with no selection stops a running `sleep`.

author: fw-bot
body:
The "Calendar: Event Reminder" cron times out whenever it processes a
recurrent event that has an email, SMS or WhatsApp reminder, and that
reminder is never sent.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Create a daily recurrent event
2. Add an email reminder
3. When the reminder is due, the job times out three times in a row, then
   the cron marks it as failed without running it: the reminder is never
   sent and the recurrence is left with an empty trigger_id.

Since 19.0, ir.cron._clear_schedule deletes the cron's fired triggers in
the runner transaction, before the job runs, and keeps that transaction
open until the job is done. calendar_recurrence references ir.cron.trigger
through a foreign key with ON DELETE SET NULL, so deleting the fired
trigger locks the referencing calendar_recurrence row. The reminder job
runs in a separate transaction and, for recurrent events only, schedules
the next occurrence by writing trigger_id on that same calendar_recurrence
row: it waits on the lock held by the runner transaction, which in turn
only commits once the job has finished. The job deadlocks on itself and
times out.

Each timeout rolls back the trigger deletion and lastcall, so the next
attempt blocks the same way. After three timeouts, the cron skips the job,
deletes the trigger and moves lastcall to now, so every reminder due in
that window is lost.

Stop writing trigger_id on the recurrence, so the job never touches the
row locked by the runner. trigger_id was also used to avoid creating the
same trigger twice when the next occurrence is set up several times in a
transaction, e.g. on creation. Collect the alarm trigger dates in a
pre-commit hook instead, so each date is only created once.

author: catastrophe-brandon
body:
### Description

Add optional framework support for the HCC UI-testing agent's Stage login helper.

- Allow the narrowly scoped `mcp__stage-login__sign_in` MCP tool.
- Load MCP server configuration after instance config sync so the instance's `stage-login` server is available before manifest validation and the first cycle.
- Wait for the helper health endpoint at startup when configured.
- Reset the helper's one-password-attempt guard before each work cycle through an authenticated loopback request. The runner captures the reset token before environment sanitization; it is not passed to model tools or Chromium.
- Support `UI_BROWSER_PROXY` for Chromium while preserving existing proxy settings for Jira, memory, and model traffic.

These hooks are optional and are inactive for instances that do not configure the helper URLs, MCP server, or browser proxy override.

### Why

The UI-testing agent needs to sign in through the existing browser session without putting username/password values in model context, reports, or the general runner environment. Its dedicated helper resolves a requested persona alias and performs the sign-in. The per-cycle reset permits a later Jira ticket to start with a fresh one-attempt guard after an earlier failed login.

### Integration

The consumer is implemented in [hcc-framework-agent-dev PR #105](https://github.com/RedHatInsights/hcc-framework-agent-dev/pull/105). That PR adds the `stage-login` MCP manifest and deploys the helper as a loopback sidecar in the same pod as the runner and Chromium. The runner exposes the sign-in capability to the workflow, waits for helper readiness, and resets the guard at the start of each work cycle.

### Blast radius

- Existing instances keep their current behavior unless they set the new helper health/reset URLs or browser proxy override.
- The additional MCP tool is usable only when an instance provides the corresponding MCP server.
- The browser proxy override affects Chromium only; Jira, memory, and model routing retain their configured proxies.

### Validation

The consuming branch includes focused login-helper tests and a local cycle harness. The integrated sidecar has not yet been validated in the deployed App Interface environment; Stage reachability and the end-to-end sign-in smoke check remain deployment checks.

### Rollback plan

Revert this PR. The consumer can also disable the integration by removing the `stage-login` MCP server and helper-specific environment settings from its instance deployment.

### Checklist
- [ ] Tested against a deployed consuming service; Stage sidecar smoke check is pending.
- [ ] No breaking changes to existing consumers; changes are intended to be opt-in.
- [x] No hardcoded secrets, tokens, or passwords.
- [ ] Container image pinning is not changed by this PR.

author: klausricharz
body:
## Beschreibung

Die Skill-Vorschläge finden Skills auch über ihre Aliasse und schlagen immer den kanonischen Namen vor (`K8S` → Kubernetes, `Postgers` → PostgreSQL).

- **pwr-skill-service**
  - Aliasse werden mit denselben Analyzern wie der Name indexiert (exakt, Wortanfang, unscharf), aber in eigenen Feldern ohne Längennormierung. In den Namensfeldern hätte jeder Alias das Feld verlängert und Namenstreffer abgewertet: Mit fünf Aliassen stand Java bei `Jav` hinter JavaScript.
  - Jede Teilabfrage (exakt, Wortanfang, ähnlich) wertet den besseren Treffer aus Name und Alias (`DisjunctionMaxQuery`). Ein Alias-Treffer zählt damit wie ein Namens-Treffer, ein Skill mit passendem Namen und Alias zählt nicht doppelt. Vorgeschlagen wird der gespeicherte Name, jeder Skill einmal.
  - Der Index folgt Änderungen der Aliasse sofort (anlegen, entfernen, zusammenführen); beim Start wird er ohnehin neu aufgebaut.
  - Wortanfänge: Ein Wort passt, wenn es als Ganzes ein Wortanfang ist (`c++`, `k8s`) oder jeder seiner Teile mit mindestens zwei Zeichen (`.NET` → `net` für ASP.NET Core). Bisher reichte ein einzelner Teil, sodass `C++` alle Skills mit c brachte und `K8S` auch Scrum. Die unscharfe Suche gilt ebenso nur noch für Teile ab vier Zeichen (vorher fand `java8` über die 8 auch Kubernetes mit dem Alias K8S).
- **pwr-webclient**
  - `SkillSearcher` filtert die Vorschläge nicht mehr zusätzlich im Browser (`disableFiltering`). Der Filter verwarf alle Alias-Treffer (Kubernetes enthält nicht „K8S“) und hob die Reihenfolge aus #32 teilweise wieder auf; die Streutreffer, die er bisher verdeckte, liefert der Server nach der obigen Änderung nicht mehr.
  - Die Kategorie-Hierarchie wird unter dem eingegebenen Namen abgelegt. Bei Eingabe eines Alias stand bisher „Keine Kategorie gefunden“, jetzt „Kubernetes => Containers & Orchestration => …“.

Nicht umgesetzt: das optionale Kriterium, im Vorschlag den getroffenen Alias anzuzeigen („Kubernetes (K8S)“). Dafür müsste `/skill/search` statt Namen Objekte liefern, und der Webclient müsste angezeigten Text und übernommenen Namen trennen; das wäre ein eigenes Issue.

Closes #34

## Akzeptanzkriterien / Testplan

- [x] Alias exakt, als Wortanfang oder mit Tippfehler schlägt den kanonischen Skill vor (`K8S`, `k8`, `Postgers`, `psql`, `MS Az`), Tests in `SkillSearcherService_ExpectedResultITest`
- [x] Jeder Skill höchstens einmal, auch wenn Name und mehrere Aliasse passen
- [x] Exakter Alias-Treffer an erster Stelle (`JS` → JavaScript, `java 11` → Java)
- [x] Nach Anlegen, Entfernen und Zusammenführen ist die Suche ohne Index-Neuaufbau aktuell (`SkillAliasITest`)
- [ ] Optional: getroffenen Alias im Vorschlag anzeigen (siehe oben)
- [x] `./mvnw verify` grün (59 Tests, die Reihenfolge-Tests aus #32 unverändert grün), `npm run build` ohne neue Warnungen
- [x] Lokal im Webclient geprüft: Skill-Eingabe im Profil mit `K8S`, `postgers`, `Jav`, `C++`; Auswahl übernimmt den kanonischen Namen und zeigt dessen Kategorie

---

body:
Closes #217

Epic #181 · F2

Planning (`plan-validate`, `plan-post`, `plan-create`) now finds a PRD that was merged on GitHub (`merge-prd`, `commit-prd`, `escalate-to-full`) but isn't in this checkout yet. Nobody has to fast-forward by hand.

The change only adds a place to look:
- `prd_path(n)` is unchanged, and the working tree's `docs/prd/N-*.md` is still read first.
- Only when the working tree has no such file does `planning_ref` fetch `origin/<default_branch>`. It does this once per command, at the entry point, with a timeout (`PRD_FETCH_SECONDS`, 60s, checked to be positive).
- `prd_at` then reads the file at that ref with `git ls-tree` + `git show`. It is pure: no fetch.
- When the approved comment is known (`plan-post` and `plan-create`), `prd_at` prefers the file whose header links it. Otherwise it takes the first by name.
- A failed or timed-out fetch is reported on stderr, and the last fetched `origin/main` is read instead.
- `--from-file` never fetches and reads only the working tree, as before.
- Offline call sites still call `check_plan(plan)` exactly as before.
- `plan-create`'s PRD link comes from the path it found.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A new escalation test with no manual fast-forward (`test_commit_prd_then_planning_starts_with_no_fast_forward`) fails before the fix and passes after it. The existing tests/test_sdlc*.py pass unchanged. The new test isn't a line-for-line copy: the PRD lookup at origin happens at the entry points, so it asserts `plan_criteria(plan, "origin/main")` and also runs `plan-post --dry-run`.
- [x] After a full-lane merge, `plan-validate` in a checkout behind `origin/main` finds the PRD's criteria (`test_plan_validate_finds_a_full_lane_prd_merged_after_the_last_pull`). Before it runs, the test asserts that `origin/main` in the checkout doesn't have the PRD yet.
- [x] A checkout that has the PRD in its working tree reads it as today, with no fetch (`test_a_prd_in_the_working_tree_is_read_as_before_with_no_fetch`, and the `local` case of `test_plan_create_links_the_prd_it_found`).
- [x] A failed fetch is reported on stderr and the last fetched `origin/main` is used (`test_a_failed_fetch_is_said_...`, `test_a_fetch_that_hangs_is_bounded_...`). `--from-file` never fetches (`test_from_file_never_fetches_and_reads_only_the_working_tree`).
- [x] The plan-issue skill (step 2) tells the planner where to read a PRD the checkout hasn't pulled.
- [x] No test fetches from the network, and `uv run pytest` passes in full.

## Validation

- I put back base `tools/sdlc.py` from `origin/epic/181` and ran the two new tests: both failed. With the fix restored, both passed.
- `uv run pytest tests/test_sdlc_quick.py tests/test_sdlc_plan.py -q`, then the full `uv run pytest -q` (6570 passed).
- I ran the full suite once with a temporary guard in `planning_ref` that raised if `ROOT` was the real repo. Nothing tripped it: no test fetches from the real GitHub origin. The guard was removed before committing.
- Every new test runs in a scratch repo with a bare local `origin`, and `ROOT` points at it.

## Left alone

- #206 (checkbox criteria in a committed quick brief) is unchanged. It is about `parse_criteria` and its message, and this slice doesn't touch either.
- #143 (whether the path `codex-review --plan` names is readable from its checkout) is unchanged. That path isn't touched here.
- Adjacent: CLAUDE.md's layout table lists `plan-validate` as "only read". It can now run a `git fetch` of the default branch, which still writes nothing to GitHub. To be filed as debt.

author: victorbonnet
body:
Part of #38 (finding #19).

## What was wrong
- When the proxy could not read the sandbox's active policy, it refused the connection but recorded `not-allowed`.
- So `enclos net denied`, and the proxy's 403, told the user to `enclos policy allow` a destination that may already be allowed.
- `enclos status` counted these refusals under "review refused destinations".
- The design and ADR 0007 promised that every connection appears in the network log. But a connection whose record cannot be written still goes ahead, and nothing limits the log's size.

## The fix
- **New reason:** `policy-unreadable`. The connection is still refused, failing closed as before.
- **Messages:** the proxy's 403 and `enclos net denied` say there is nothing to allow, and point to `enclos logs <sandbox>`.
- **Status:** `enclos status` no longer counts these refusals among destinations to review. It suggests `enclos logs <sandbox>` instead, with the time of the last one in the last 7 days.
- **`Reason::nothing_to_allow`:** one exhaustive match decides which reasons leave nothing to allow; `net denied` and status use it.
- **Proxy log:** a proxy a session starts (no services installed) now writes to `logs/proxy.log`, like the proxy service, so `enclos logs` shows it. Before, it wrote to `<sandbox>/proxy.log`, which no command showed.
- **Docs:** `docs/design.md` (§1 principle 7, §5, §6, §13 step 5, §15), ADR 0007, ADR 0025, README, `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/getting-started.md` now say what happens today. A failed record write is reported in the proxy's log, and the connection goes ahead. Connections over the proxy's limit, and requests that name no destination, are refused without a record. Records are kept until the sandbox is removed.
- **Decision for you:** new ADR 0026, with `status: proposed`. It weighs failing closed against failing open when the log cannot be written. It lists retention, coalescing, and what a `503` would do to `enclos policy test`, as consequences still to decide.

## Tests
- **Proxy:** with a policy source that fails, the connection is refused with 403, recorded as `Denied` with `policy-unreadable`, and gets no allow hint.
- **Proxy, fail open:** with a log store that cannot write, an allowed tunnel is still served. This is the test to turn around if ADR 0026 is accepted.
- **Engine:** `net_denied` lists the refusal with its reason. Status does not count it and suggests `enclos logs home` instead of `enclos net denied`. A real refusal next to it is still counted, and after 7 days neither is suggested.
- **Engine, logs:** a proxy started by a session writes where `enclos logs` reads.
- **Model:** an exhaustive match ties each `Reason` to its place in `Reason::ALL`.
- **CLI:** the `net denied` text has no allow hint when only `policy-unreadable` rows exist, both hints when the rows are mixed, and only the allow hint for a plain refusal.
- `just ci` passes.

## Decisions
- **Logging completeness is yours to decide:** there's no fail-closed logging, retention or coalescing yet, as the review's validation asked. ADR 0026 recommends failing closed, but stays proposed.
- **Still a 403:** `policy-unreadable` keeps the 403 status, so `enclos policy test`, which counts only a 403 as closed, is unchanged.
- **Where the hint points:** to `enclos logs`, where the proxy writes its error, not to `enclos audit verify`.
- **Merge note:** #42 also adds a `Reason` variant (`idle`). Whichever PR merges second keeps both variants, sets `ALL` to 8, and gives `idle` an arm in `nothing_to_allow` and in the `ALL` test. The compiler asks for both arms.
- **Probes:** a proxy probe refused with `policy-unreadable` still counts as closed. The design now says it proves only that the proxy failed closed. Telling the two apart in `enclos policy test` is left for later.
- **Not changed:** `site/` and the architecture diagram (`docs/diagrams/`) still say "every connection is logged".

body:
This PR adds the logarithmic-series law `logarithmicSeriesMeasure q` on `ℕ`, advancing the `StandardDistributions/README.md` Layer 9.7 target "Yule–Simon and logarithmic series": for `0 < q < 1`, mass `-q^k / (k log (1 - q))` on positive integers, otherwise the zero law, with pgf `log (1 - q z) / log (1 - q)` exactly on `|q z| < 1`, the stated mean and variance, `D = (-∞, -log q)`, the mgf obtained from the pgf, and the characteristic function with the principal logarithm.

`LogarithmicSeries/Basic.lean` defines the measure and its real and `ℝ≥0∞` masses, and proves normalization, singleton masses, support on the positive integers (`logarithmicSeriesMeasure_singleton_ne_zero_iff`, `ae_pos_logarithmicSeriesMeasure`), parameter measurability, exact pgf integrability (`integrable_pow_logarithmicSeriesMeasure_iff`) and the pgf value. `LogarithmicSeries/Transforms.lean` proves the exact exponential-integrability domain `Iio (-log q)`, the mgf, cgf and characteristic function, the mean `-q / ((1 - q) log (1 - q))` and the variance `-q (q + log (1 - q)) / ((1 - q)² log (1 - q)²)`, with `HasLaw` corollaries. The characteristic function comes from Mathlib's `Complex.hasSum_taylorSeries_neg_log`, so the principal branch needs no separate argument.

The PR also adds two general lemmas to `TauCeti/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/NegLogOneSub.lean`: `Real.hasSum_pow_div_natCast` (the real counterpart of `Complex.hasSum_taylorSeries_neg_log`, a reindexing of Mathlib's `Real.hasSum_pow_div_log_of_abs_lt_one`) and `Real.summable_pow_div_natCast_iff` (summable exactly when `|x| < 1`). These give the normalization and the exactness of the pgf domain. The family convention follows Johnson, Kemp and Kotz, *Univariate Discrete Distributions*, 3rd ed., Chapter 7. No Mathlib infrastructure is vendored.

After this PR, Layer 9.7's logarithmic-series entry still needs the cumulative sums, least-crossing quantiles and support-endpoint limits that Layer 9 requires of every discrete family, and the compound-Poisson identity giving negative binomial `(r, 1 - q)`; the Yule–Simon half of 9.7 is untouched.

Closes #359

## What changed and why

The product page's lede and its meta description said Sleevesight "reads what your music player is playing". *Reads* invites the question of where and how; a product page should not raise it, and the mechanics go on a separate engineering page. Both now say "knows".

*How it works* gave the same mechanics in its first step ("Read: The player tells Sleevesight what it is playing"). Its steps are now **Track, Trace, Tell**, in three columns, as *You choose*'s tiles: the verb, in its colour, styled as *Privacy*'s column leads (19px semibold, above the 17px text); what the step does; then a short statement, in bold, at the foot of the column so the three line up. The step numbers go. The verbs are coloured: Track the wordmark's red (`--sight`), Trace an earth ochre (its own shade, browner than web search's amber), Tell the accent blue; each passes 4.5:1 in both colour schemes.
- **Track**: Sleevesight is notified when your music player starts a track, and knows its title, artists, album and cover. *Audio never touched.*
- **Trace**: Sleevesight finds the track's traces across the sources you choose. *Nothing made up.*
- **Tell**: Sleevesight shares what makes the artist, song and album worth knowing, in a few lines written by the AI service you choose. *Every fact cited.*

"Is notified" rules out listening without explaining how. Track and Trace are verbs in the heading and nouns in the text. A fourth step, Talk (the follow-up chat), is left to *Coming soon* until it ships.

*Coming soon* swaps its columns: what each example shows on the left, the box on the right, still a third of the width. Its markup order changes too, so on a phone each text comes before its box; each row starts with its heading, visually hidden, so a screen reader moving by heading reaches the text first, and the box's label is a `p`, hidden from screen readers, since the hidden heading carries the word. Each text opens with its subject in bold; the four with citations name them, and their sources, in a paragraph of their own ("Here, W1 and W2 are…").

The page's body text is 1 to 1.5px larger (body 18px, 17px on a phone); other headings, the header and the phone mock keep their sizes. Below 880px both sections stack, as *Coming soon* did before.

*Privacy*'s "What leaves the phone, and to whom" turns its two-item list into paragraphs, and the two columns' muted lines now start level (the columns share two rows through `subgrid`).

*Install* drops its line on the open-source implementation, which the footer already gives, and says Android and Google Play in one sentence, iOS in another.

Not changed: the README (its tagline and its own *How it works*, Read, Look up, Write, Check, which explains the notification listener) and the app's `first_run_intro` string, which says what the app reads and what leaves the phone; and the dated snapshot in `design/`, kept as a record. The `og:description` never had the phrase.

User-visible on the product page only; the README describes the app, not this page, so it needs no change.

## Verification

- Checked in Chrome at 1280px (three columns; *Coming soon* text left, boxes right) and in a 390px frame (columns and rows stacked; no horizontal scroll: `scrollWidth` 375 at a 390px viewport with its scrollbar; 48.5px from the first *Privacy* column's muted line to the second's lead, as before this PR). At 1280px the two *Privacy* muted lines start level.
- `grep -n "reads what\|tells Sleevesight" index.html` returns nothing; the page has no `twitter:description` and no structured data. Nothing else on the page or in its scripts refers to the step headings.

author: lsm
body:
Busy status toggles on `/neo` moved visible messages by 45 px and triggered resize-driven auto-scroll. Keep a fixed 24 px status slot (including its existing spacing) while showing/hiding its contents; truncate status text so word changes cannot wrap. The existing dots animate opacity only. Voice sampling now uses elapsed rAF timestamps at a 60 Hz ceiling, with elapsed-time smoothing, instead of advancing history every third frame.

Closes #7883

Causes on regression commit `a91a33806`:
- `packages/web/src/neo/NeoConversation.tsx:170-172` conditionally mounted the busy row, changing conversation height. `NeoLive.tsx:249-260` observes rail children and writes scrollTop on resize. Desktop has a fixed outer rail, but its conversation child still changes height.
- `packages/web/src/components/voice/VoiceWaveform.tsx:113-117` samples every third rAF (20 Hz on a 60 Hz display). `packages/web/src/lib/voice/voice-recorder-store.ts:204` reads local Web Audio, independent of transcription/network round trips. Paint already writes transform/opacity directly; no per-frame React/Preact state or whole-composer rerender. The elapsed timer updates once/second. This isolates a code cause; actual cellular/network performance was not tested.

Validation on the actual built `/neo`, headless Chromium, fresh isolated daemon/DB/HOME, synthetic publications and fake microphone with synthetic local analyser levels:

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Message bounding-box movement, desktop/mobile | 45 / 45 px | 0 / 0 px |
| Outer rail height movement, desktop/mobile | 0 / 45 px | 0 / 0 px |
| Rail/child resize callbacks per four busy toggles | 4 / 4 | 0 / 0 |
| Audio sampling median gap | 50 ms | 16.7 ms |
| Audio samples in ~1.8 seconds | 37 | 109 |
| Browser p95 frame interval | ~16.7 ms | ~16.7 ms |

Separate before evidence: `/private/tmp/hn-animation-baseline-VpsWTk/evidence/neo-animation-verify.json` (fails the layout assertion); after: `/private/tmp/hn-animation-after-4OpMDY/evidence/neo-animation-verify.json` (passes). Both directories retain desktop/mobile screenshots. Measurements use bounding boxes rather than CLS because scroll-driven movement is central to this bug.

The first commit contains failing cadence tests and the headless reproduction; the second fixes it and updates the verify skill. `bun run check` passes. Full web suite: 378 files, 8,550 passed, 2 existing skips. Synthetic 30/60/120 Hz cadence tests fail before and pass after. Headless recipe: Launch per verify skill, then `NODE_PATH=<playwright directory> VERIFY_BROWSER=<installed Chromium> node .claude/skills/verify/neo-animation-check.mjs <port> <run> verify`. No desktop GUI or port 8399, real data, model turns or credentials used.

For the iOS worker: reserve a fixed status-line container even while idle; clip/truncate changing copy and animate opacity/transform inside it. Busy visibility/word changes must not change the scroll content size or trigger scroll-to-bottom. For voice, drive rendering from a display link, use monotonic elapsed timestamps for a bounded audio sample cadence and delta-based smoothing, and read local audio levels independently of transcription networking. Keep frame-level values outside composer state. Verify stable message bounds and frame/sample cadence separately. iOS itself is not verified here.

Merge contract: four production files, 36 added / 18 removed lines; tests and verify helper/skill only otherwise. Manual squash only after `hyperneo-ai-test` approves the exact latest head and CI is green; auto-merge stays off.
