author: glennhickey
body:
Cactus is switching Minigraph-Cactus genome names to PanSN: `SAMPLE#HAPLOTYPE`, or just `SAMPLE` for haplotype 0 (ComparativeGenomicsToolkit/cactus#2051, for cactus#2048). The genome in a cactus `id=GENOME|CONTIG` name can therefore now contain a `#`.

`canon_name` only took a haplotype from after the last `.`:

| name | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| `id=HG002#1\|chr1` | `HG002#1#0#chr1` | `HG002#1#chr1` |
| `id=KOLF2.1J\|chr1` | `KOLF2#1J#chr1` | `KOLF2.1J#0#chr1` |
| `id=HG002.1\|chr1` (older cactus) | `HG002#1#chr1` | `HG002#1#chr1` |
| `id=CHM13\|chr1` | `CHM13#0#chr1` | `CHM13#0#chr1` |

With the old code, a GAF step naming such a sequence in cactus form could not be resolved against the PanSN graph rgfa-zip is given (`resolve_sn` skips its last-field fallback for names containing `#` or `|`). Its records were dropped silently.

Testing: `rgfa-zip.t` gets a new Z19 check. It takes the walks GAF, renames its queries and stable step names to cactus form (`id=SAMPLE#HAP|CONTIG`, and the old `id=SAMPLE.HAP|CONTIG`), and checks that both zip to the same graph as the PanSN-named GAF. The check fails on the old `canon_name` and passes with this change. `rgfa-zip.t`, `gaffilter.t`, `gaf2paf.t` and `test.t` all pass.

author: michitrader
body:
Last item of phase A in docs/DESIGN-OPEN-TUI.md.

- `/ui export [file]` writes layout, colours, words and behaviour as one JSON file `{format:"arxi-interface", version:1, ...}`. It never overwrites and refuses when nothing of yours is saved.
- `/ui import <file>` replaces the interface with the file's. Typed by the user only; the model has no tool for either, and its guide says so.
- Import validates before touching anything: format, version, unknown fields, trailing data, each part through the same loaders a model change uses, and a layout with no root (which `loadInterface` alone lets through and would draw nothing). A failure changes nothing and writes no undo file.
- It goes through the new `makeSaved` (shared with history restore): `/ui undo` returns, and it is a version in `/ui history`. It names the commands and keys the file adds. Refused with `-scene`. Max 1 MB.
- Not in the file: packages (a file from someone else must not install programs), `ui_tests.json`, history.

Honest limits: no trust prompt or signature for a file of unknown origin beyond the listing of what it binds; no partial merge; no import from a URL.

Tests: 19 new, two through the real loop. 18 mutants, all caught. Two were first reported uncaught for real reasons: a rootless layout passed `loadInterface` (fixed, with a test) and one mutant was filtered out of my own test selection (re-run, caught). Full `go test ./... -count=1`, vet and gofmt pass, including the Termux guard.

author: guyadam
body:
Preparation previews previously needed an externally provisioned execution boundary. This adds a runnable attended host that keeps provider checks in the trusted controller and runs the authenticated updater dry run inside a network-free, nonroot Docker container. The host uses existing signed policy and the preparation queue; it cannot apply changes or publish a PR.

The container uses a pinned local image and Docker endpoint, isolated client configuration, verified private launcher, read-only source/checkout/root, bounded writable backup/tmpfs, resource limits, and owned-container cleanup. A standalone diagnostic CLI verifies the exact repository and base before and after preview. Documentation covers provisioning, missing local context, and the remaining hosted acceptance boundary.

Validation: 118 runner tests; 39 coordinator tests (one platform skip); independent isolation/authority review; public release boundary check. A real disposable repository dry run against an authenticated published release returned current with zero changes. Negative container probes confirmed blocked egress, read-only mounts/root, absent host socket/sentinel, dropped capabilities and no privilege escalation. All nine exact-head CI checks passed, including complete safety and native Windows update suites. A real signed-in owner request also completed through the private hosted queue as current with zero changes; an identical result retry succeeded without requeueing. The attended host and temporary hosted configuration were removed afterward. This proves the disposable preview path, not real-repository apply/publication or every live failure mode.

author: nicdumz
body:
## Summary
- With `mutableUsers = false`, NixOS uses `userborn` to manage `/etc/passwd`/`/etc/group`, and userborn has **no cross-boot persistence** for dynamically allocated (unpinned) ids: every id without an explicit `uid`/`gid` is reallocated from scratch on every single boot, purely as a function of the current declared user/group set. Adding or removing any unrelated user/group elsewhere in the config can silently shift every subsequent unpinned id.
- This is what caused `/var/lib/mealie`'s files to end up owned by `node-exporter` on jonsnow after a reboot: mealie's uid drifted across boots and happened to land on whatever `node-exporter` got assigned that time. The same drift was found affecting `bazarr`, `grocy`, `jellyseerr`, `pangolin`, `pocket-id`, `prowlarr`, `traefik`, `victorialogs`, and the shared `media` group — every service with persisted state and no pinned id. All are now pinned to their current (correct, live) values. Services already covered by nixpkgs' static id list (`ids.nix`) — `hass`, `paperless`, `plex`, `prometheus`, `radarr`, `sonarr` — were left alone.
- Found and fixed in passing: `prowlarr`'s systemd unit disabled `DynamicUser` without setting an explicit `User`, so it has been silently running **as root** this whole time.
- Added an assertion in the persistence module so this class of bug can't recur silently: any `${namespace}.persistence.directories` entry (and its `configureParent` target, if set) must reference a user/group with an explicitly pinned `uid`/`gid`, or eval fails with a message explaining why.

## Test plan
- [x] `nix build .#nixosConfigurations.jonsnow.config.system.build.toplevel` succeeds, zero failing assertions
- [x] Verified pinned uids/gids match jonsnow's live `/etc/passwd`/`/etc/group` exactly
- [x] Deployed to jonsnow; `systemctl --failed` is empty after chowning drifted directories (victorialogs, radarr, prowlarr, mealie, jellyseerr, pocket-id) and fixing prowlarr's root-running bug
- [ ] Confirm uids/gids stay stable across jonsnow's next reboot

author: esopian
body:
## 🎯 TL;DR

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Chat now renders `MEDIA:` shares the way the Hermes desktop app does: quoted, backticked and spaced paths are read, audio and video play, text files show inline, and images zoom. Each known upstream MEDIA or directive bug in NousResearch/hermes-agent is held as a requirement with its own test. This replaces [#98](https://github.com/esopian/hermetic/pull/98), which closed automatically when its base branch was deleted after [#96](https://github.com/esopian/hermetic/pull/96) merged. It is now rebased onto `master`.

## 🧭 How it works

- **The desktop's `MEDIA:` reader** — `packages/core/src/shared/media-tags.ts` ports the desktop's `parts.ts`. `parseOutboxMediaLine` now reads every desktop form of a line. A chip is still drawn only for a path in the box's outbox, fetched by share id, which is [#96](https://github.com/esopian/hermetic/pull/96)'s MEDIA-only behaviour, kept as is.
- **Playback and text previews** — `files.content` takes a purpose (`image`, `playback`, `text`), and each purpose has its own type check and byte cap. `sniffMime` names audio and video from their magic numbers. `ShareCard` plays only `blob:` URLs the page created (`safeMediaSrc`).
- **Directives never stream half written** — the live hold (`createMediaHold`) also holds back an unfinished `[[audio_as_voice]]` or `[[as_document]]` until it completes (`partialDirectiveTail`).
- **One file, one share** — the box plugin keys its per-turn shares by the normalized absolute path, so `~/a b.pdf`, `/…//a b.pdf` and `/…/./a b.pdf` become one share and one chip.
- **Malformed silence markers** — `[SILENT` and `SILENT]` (a single missing bracket, nothing else in the reply) now read as silence. This is hermetic's own rule; upstream delivers them as text. The §9.2 silence paragraph and the §11 files-testing paragraph in `docs/design.md` are updated to match.
- **`ARTIFACTS_VERSION` 2 → 3** — the artifacts fingerprint lock arrived on `master` in [#102](https://github.com/esopian/hermetic/pull/102) after this branch was cut. The parser and share helpers live in `core/shared`, which hermeticd bundles, so the bundle version moves and fleets are offered the update.

### Upstream requirements

| # | Requirement | Test | Result | Note |
| - | ----------- | ---- | :----: | ---- |
| 1 | Streaming: no partial `MEDIA:` path or `[[…]]` directive ([#141584](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/141584), PR [#138551](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/138551)) | `media-tags.test.ts` › "a stream split inside a MEDIA path never shows the partial path"; "a directive split across deltas is never shown half written" | ✅ pass | A drive-path `MEDIA:` line is not held. The box never shares one, so it streams as prose and the final text matches what streamed. |
| 2 | Dedup a spaced path and its variants ([#120021](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/120021), [#78383](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/78383)) | `media-tags.test.ts` › "MEDIA:/tmp/AI Brain/report.pdf gives one candidate"; `test_plugin.py` › `test_a_spaced_path_and_its_normalized_variants_are_one_share` | ✅ pass | Fixed in the plugin: shares are keyed by the normalized path. |
| 3 | Every `MEDIA:` line renders ([#123567](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/123567)) | `media-tags.test.ts` › "two MEDIA: lines give two attachments" | ✅ pass | |
| 4 | Windows drive paths parse ([#34632](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/34632)) | `media-tags.test.ts` › "a drive path parses" | ✅ pass | A drive path parses but stays text, because it is not the box's file. |
| 5 | No trust from a URL's path shape ([#71559](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/71559)) | `chat-attachments.dom.test.tsx` › "a /relay/media/ URL from another origin does not render as authenticated media"; `media-tags.test.ts` › "a /relay/media/ URL is not trusted from its path shape" | ✅ pass | |
| 6 | Send and render agree ([#128855](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/128855)) | `media-tags.test.ts` › "a refused path does not render as a working attachment" | ✅ pass | |
| 7 | No replay ([#37358](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/37358), [#39607](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/39607)) | `hermes-chat-media.test.ts` › "re-rendering the transcript does not duplicate or re-attach old files" | ✅ pass | Covers history and the live hold. |
| 8 | Malformed or bracket-less `SILENT` does not leak ([#51438](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/51438), [#5023](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/5023)) | `silence.test.ts` › "a malformed or bracket-less SILENT marker does not leak as text"; `chat-silence.dom.test.tsx` › same name | ✅ pass | Hermetic renders silence markers itself (`silence.ts`), so this rule is implemented in code, not only recorded. |

### Follow-up decisions (not in this PR)

- **`[[audio_as_voice]]`** — hermetic has no voice-note rendering. A complete directive still shows as text; only a partial one is held while streaming. Decide whether to render it or strip it.
- **`[[as_document]]`** — the same choice. Upstream support is not stable yet (PRs [#137795](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/137795), [#125431](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/125431), [#72112](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/72112)).

## 🔍 Review guide

1. **The silence rule diverges from upstream** — `packages/core/src/shared/silence.ts` `rebracketed`
   - **Look for:** it applies only when the whole reply is the marker. Prose such as `Reply [SILENT if …` stays prose.
   - **Risk:** a reply of only `[SILENT` is now hidden here, while a messaging gateway delivers it as text.
2. **Plugin path normalization** — `packages/agentd/plugins/hermetic-files/__init__.py` `transform_llm_output`
   - **Look for:** `_in_outbox` and `_share` both get the normalized path. `_share` already ran `abspath`, so what the box receives is unchanged.
   - **Risk:** two lines that differ only in spelling now resolve to one share. That is the intent.
3. **Directive hold** — `packages/core/src/chat/hermes/hermes-chat-media.ts` `push`
   - **Look for:** only `[[` or a longer prefix of a directive is held, and `settle`, `end` and `cut` release it.
   - **Risk:** a stream that ends in a bare `[[` waits for the final text before showing it.
4. **Bytes by purpose** — `packages/core/src/files/files.ts`, `packages/app/src/handlers/files.ts`, `packages/ui/src/chat/components/blocks/ShareCard.tsx`.
5. **Rebase resolution** — `AGENTS.md` fixture paragraph: the only conflict. It keeps master's `/compact E2E_COMPACT_SLOW` and adds `E2E_MEDIA_KINDS`. Every other file merged cleanly, and `git range-diff` shows the three later commits unchanged.

## ✅ Acceptance tests

| Status | Check | Evidence |
| :----: | ----- | -------- |
|   ✅   | Targeted: `media-tags`, `silence`, `hermes-chat-media`, `fixture-chat-file-share`, `flows/share.flow` | 135 pass, 0 fail on the rebased branch. [#96](https://github.com/esopian/hermetic/pull/96)'s `fixture-chat-file-share` and `share.flow` tests are kept and pass. |
|   ✅   | `artifacts-version.test.ts` after the bump | Passes with fingerprint 3 recorded. |
|   ✅   | `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `bun run lint:biome`, `bun run lint:cfn`, `bun run lint:sh` | Clean on HEAD |
|   ❌   | `bun run check` (test step) | 10442 pass, 30 skip, 33 fail, 1 error. Every failure is a 5 s timeout in `packages/cli/test/cli.test.ts`, `packages/cli/test/fleets.test.ts` or `flows/subagent.flow` (the error is from `subagent.flow` too), on a host at load average ~10. Those three files rerun with `--timeout 60000`: 167 pass, 0 fail. This PR touches no CLI or subagent code. |
|   ⏭️   | WKWebView check of the share card | Not run: headless Linux host, no macOS. |
|   ⏭️   | `bun run ci` (`build`, `audit:dependencies`) | Not run. No dependency changes. |

## ⚠️ Risks & rollout

author: greatzachariah16-wq
body:
## Root cause found
- The main app now authenticates with Xora's secure `xora_session` cookie (`/api/auth`), but chat was still trying to read `firebase.auth.currentUser` and send a Firebase ID token to the Supabase Edge Function. That identity source no longer matches the active login system, so chat room/message requests fail even when the user is signed in.
- The chat page also rendered the sign-in prompt before `useAuth()` had finished restoring the saved session.
- Supabase currently has two discoverable circles, but their memberships were created with a legacy Firebase UID. `xora_auth_accounts.legacy_firebase_uid` currently has no mappings, so old memberships cannot safely be attributed to a current account automatically.

## Changes
- Add a same-origin `/api/chat` server route that validates the existing HttpOnly Xora session cookie and handles chat requests server-side.
- Update chat client requests to use that cookie-authenticated route instead of Firebase bearer tokens.
- Show a session-restoring state instead of a false sign-in prompt while auth is loading.
- The server route checks `legacy_firebase_uid` if a mapping exists, to support preserved memberships without guessing account ownership.

## Data preservation
- No chat tables or existing circle/message rows were deleted or rewritten. The two discoverable circles remain available in Explore; if legacy identity mapping is still absent, a user can rejoin a circle so it appears in their own list. Automatic restoration of prior memberships requires a verified legacy UID-to-account mapping.
- No subscription, video, feed, auth implementation, or Live TV playback logic changed.

author: marcoautomation2
body:
﻿`Picture` is a widget showing an `Image`; `Pane.picture{...}` adds one.
It is the piece the Fearless manager shape needs for its icons: the project tiles (icon over caption), the panel header and the claim rows.

- `.image(Image)`: like a new text, a new image grows the widget to fit it; `.pack` fits the widget to the image.
- The image always covers the whole widget, insets excluded.
- `.keepAspect(False)`: the image stretches to the widget.
- `.keepAspect(True)` (default): the last of `.width` and `.height` decides the other one, so the widget has the proportions of the image. A widget drawn larger by `.fill` shows the image scaled to cover it, centered, clipped on one axis.
- A size derived by keepAspect over the limit is an error: `keepAspect width 39988 is too large; it must be <= 32767`.

`AWidget.reStyle` calls a new `fit()` after every change of style or size, so insets, width, height, pack and image all keep the ratio; `fit()` does nothing for the other widgets.

Tests: seven size checks in `test_gui_image.fear`. TestAllFrontendCoordinatorIntegration passes (with FearlessLang/Commons#84, which makes building base fast again).

author: juicie-brucie
body:
## Summary

Static analysis of the depth hang from the 2026-10-20 #127 retry. The depth interface (port 10010) hung for 65 seconds with zero output while IR (port 10013) succeeded moments earlier with 30/33 data frames.

## Stall Candidates

Ranked by likelihood with evidence from `tools/raptor_client/main.cpp`:

1. **Client-side read blocking in start_stream reply** — MOST LIKELY
   - `ReadMessage()` at main.cpp:408-422 has no timeout (unbounded `recv()`)
   - No `fflush()` after the `[live] connected` line (main.cpp:1121)
   - Process at 0:00 CPU (blocked in kernel `recv()`)
   - 0-byte raw log (hang is before any `get_frame` calls)

2. **Daemon-side depth path** — PLAUSIBLE ROOT CAUSE
   - Daemon accepts TCP connection but doesn't reply to `start_stream` on depth interface
   - IR worked moments earlier, so daemon is running
   - Depth interface handler may be deadlocked or misconfigured

3. **Buffering/flush issue** — CONTRIBUTING FACTOR
   - No `fflush(stdout)` after line 1121, so the `[live] connected` line stays buffered
   - Makes the hang invisible to the operator

4. **Client-side connect blocking** — UNLIKELY
   - Test record says "connected per OS level"
   - If connect failed, we'd see an error message at lines 1117-1118

## Most Likely Scenario

The daemon accepts the TCP connection on port 10010, but when the client sends `ob_rpc_start_stream0-2-10`, the daemon's depth interface handler doesn't reply (or replies very slowly). The client's `ReadMessage()` blocks forever in `recv()`. The `[live] connected` line is buffered in stdout (no `fflush()` after line 1121) and never appears.

## Bounded-Wait Retry Plan

### Command

```bash
timeout 30 ./build/tools/raptor_client/raptor_client --live 127.0.0.1 10010 5 --dump-replies
```

Exit code 124 = timeout (hang confirmed); otherwise the process's actual exit code.

### Instrumentation (for the builder)

1. Add `fflush(stdout)` after line 1121 (the `[live] connected` line)
2. Add `fflush(stdout)` after line 1129 (the `[live] start_stream ->` line)
3. Add timestamps to measure delays between steps
4. Add a trace before `StartStream()`: `[live] calling start_stream...`

### Fix Options (for the builder)

**Option A:** Use `readReplyWithDeadline()` for the live path (the replay path already uses it at main.cpp:362-366, but the live path uses the unbounded `ReadMessage()`)

**Option B:** Add socket-level timeout with `setsockopt(SO_RCVTIMEO)` in `RpcClient::connect()`

**Option C:** Both for defense in depth

### What the record must capture

- Exit code (0 = success, 124 = timeout, other = process exit code)
- All stdout/stderr output (including the `[live] connected` line if it appears)
- Timestamps for each step (connect, start_stream, get_frame, stop_stream)
- Raw log file (bytes of any frames received)

## Open Questions

1. Why doesn't the daemon reply to `start_stream` on the depth interface?
   - Needs: daemon-side trace or log
2. Is the hang reproducible, or was the original a transient issue?
   - Needs: the bounded-wait retry to reproduce (or confirm it's gone)
3. Are there other unbounded reads in the live path?
   - Needs: review of all `ReadMessage()` calls

## Related Rows

- **#127** — the original hardware retry (IR pass, depth hang). This finding diagnoses the depth hang.
- **#132** — the depth capture. This finding unblocks #132 by providing a bounded-wait retry plan.
- **#105** — the original "zero frames" question for IR. Unrelated (IR, not depth).

## Provenance

Static analysis only, no device run. All claims `[inferred]` from `tests/results/2026-10-20-plan127-live-reply-dump-retry.md` and `tools/raptor_client/main.cpp`. The bounded-wait retry is a test-queue card, not this task.

Wall: `docs/recon/**` only. No code, no vendor binary, no device run.

## Recommended Row Move

`RECON` → `BUILD` (the fix is identified: add timeout to live path's RPC calls, add fflush for instrumentation)

Follow-up to #1732 (8.2, the macOS detached scope backend), which merged as `3ce7f6d4`.

- A new row tracks [#1741](https://github.com/s3ntin3l8/mullion-session-manager/issues/1741) — the 8.2 hardware validation: the Homebrew build of dtach behaving like the one measured here, and BSD `ps` rendering the fields the master lookup parses. It is one script.

Why it is tracked rather than folded into the merge: the backend is behind `process.platform === "darwin"`, so no Linux CI run can execute it, and the failure mode it guards against is quiet and macOS-only — if dtach hid its process title, the master lookup would find nothing and teardown would silently no-op, leaving agent processes running (the CPU this phase exists to reclaim).

Docs only — no code.

author: opaland
body:
Story 34.5 de `docs/SPRINT-STATUS.md` (veille du 18/10/2026).

## Changements
- La fiche d'une côte affiche l'**indice FIETS**, calculé par `EFProfile.fietsIndex`. La formule est H² / (D × 10) + (T − 1000) / 1000, H et D étant en mètres et T l'altitude du sommet.
  - Cette forme est celle de [Runalyze](https://runalyze.com/help/article/climb-score), vérifiée à la source.
  - Choix du dépôt : le bonus d'altitude est ramené à 0 sous 1000 m, sans malus pour une côte basse.
  - D'autres variantes du bonus (T / 1000, partie entière) sont citées par la veille, mais je ne les ai pas revérifiées à la source.
  - La formule est donnée en infobulle et n'est pas présentée comme officielle.
- H est calculé sur le profil lissé, en prenant le premier `ele0` et le dernier `ele1` des blocs de 1 km. Le sommet stocké est en effet le maximum brut de la montée, si bien qu'une pointe de bruit de 25 m faisait monter l'indice de 20 %. Sans blocs, on revient à sommet − pied.
- Quand une donnée manque ou que la côte ne monte pas, aucun indice n'est affiché : jamais 0 m supposé (règle 10).
- Au passage, la virgule décimale (oubli de la 35.19) s'applique maintenant à :
  - le score de la côte, dans la fiche et dans le catalogue des cols ;
  - l'indice d'irrégularité ;
  - les points et le facteur de fatigue de l'indice de douleur.

## Vérification
- `npm test` et `npm run lint` verts. `test/fietsIndex.test.js` couvre :
  - le terme de pente seul ;
  - le bonus d'altitude, et un bonus nul à 1000 m pile ;
  - les données manquantes ;
  - le calcul de H sur le profil lissé plutôt que sur le maximum brut.
- Playwright sur une étape hors-ligne : les indices s'affichent à côté de la catégorie, avec la virgule.
- Relecture adverse : le tri par score du catalogue reste numérique, l'infobulle est statique et aucun texte rendu ne garde de point décimal. Trois points ont été corrigés dans le second commit :
  - le facteur de fatigue affichait encore « ×1.3 » ;
  - le sommet brut gonflait H ;
  - les sources étaient affirmées sans vérification.
- Limite : hors-ligne, les profils sont simulés. Le Galibier y donne 23,4 parce que son profil généré monte à 14 % de moyenne, ce qui n'est pas une valeur réelle.

author: josephleekl
body:
**Context:**
The verbs backends hand-roll the 16 B `Payload` frame and the 256 × 64 B ring in several places. That fixes them to 8 B messages, and leaves the frame layout undocumented for out-of-tree backends.

**Description of the Change:**
- **Frame codec** (`common/interface/Frame.hpp`):
  - `stage`/`seal`/`poll`/`data` build and read a frame;
  - `RingGeometry` describes the ring.
  - Only the existing 16 B layout (BL16) is implemented. The other modes are named but refused, so a variable-length layout can be added in one place.
- **cpu_verbs**, and the host side of **gpu_verbs** through the shared verbs base, build and read frames through the codec instead of the `Payload` struct and ring constants. **The bytes on the wire are unchanged.**
- **Docs:** `doc/dev/backline.rst` describes the BL16 frame and the ring, the contract an out-of-tree backend has to meet, since `Frame.hpp` is not installed.

No change to behaviour, the transport ABI or library names.

**Benefits:**
- One place defines the frame layout, ready for larger messages.

**Possible Drawbacks:**
- The receive spin now calls through the codec, adding one predictable branch per iteration.

**Testing:**
- **New tests:**
  - the codec's output is byte-identical to `Payload`;
  - the BL16 ring matches today's constants;
  - an unimplemented mode is refused.
- **On a soft-RoCE host:** the transport Catch2 suites, lit, Backline pytest and demos 1/1a pass.
- **gpu_verbs** builds against ROCm 7.2 with no warnings. It is not yet run on a GPU.

author: jzhu13
body:
## Problem

- After cutover, an edit to a moved insight alert changes only the insight row. Its platform copy keeps the old name, threshold and on/off state until the next check, and some changes never reach it.
- A new insight alert in a team that has cut over starts on the insight stack and needs another cutover run.
- Deleting a moved alert leaves its copy, which the platform keeps evaluating until the next check switches it off.
- Logs closed the same gaps in #118309, on top of the platform write API (#118280 to #118317, merged).

## Changes

- **Insight API and Max tool:** saving a moved alert also writes its name, on/off, threshold, comparison and schedule restriction onto the platform copy, in the same transaction. A snooze becomes the copy's mute.
- **Platform API:** insight now registers a source config schema, so `PATCH /platform_alerts/<id>/` can edit an insight copy. The edit reaches the insight row through a mirror hook that locks the insight row first, the order every writer uses.
- **Refused edits:** a moved alert cannot move onto a detector, a real-time check or the investigation agent, because the platform cannot run those yet. Through the platform API, an insight copy cannot switch insights, be grouped, or take N-of-M or cooldown values the insight row cannot store.
- **Creates:** a new alert in a team where the platform owns at least one insight alert is handed to the platform at creation, using the cutover's handover. It then skips the copy-on-create follow from #120623, which would reset the owned copy.
- **Deletes:** deleting a moved alert ends its firings first, while their destinations exist. It then deletes the copy and the alert in one transaction. A copy whose alert goes another way, such as with its insight, switches itself off at its next check.
- **Cutover:** it skips an alert in a child environment, as logs does, because platform rows live on the project's root team. `hand_over`, `can_move` and `has_begun_cutover` are shared by the cutover and the create path.
- A cadence edit still reaches the copy at the next check (#120623), because the platform's edit contract leaves the schedule out.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** `test_alert_platform_owned.py` (writes) and `test_platform_cutover.py`

- An edit through each API reaches both rows.
- An edit onto a detector is refused, and neither row changes.
- A new alert is handed over only in a team that has begun the cutover.
- Deleting a moved alert deletes its copy.
- The cutover skips an alert in a child environment.
- Not run locally: the Django suites, because their setup drops the shared ClickHouse test database. CI runs them.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`)

- Part of the insight alerts cutover, stacked on #120703. It mirrors #118309 for logs. Before this layer, stack #119974 took a master merge so the platform write API was available.
- Skills: `/writing-tests`, `/improving-drf-endpoints`, `/simplify`, `/code-review`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `/stacking-prs`. CodeRabbit caught that the delete was not atomic, now fixed. The firing close stays outside the transaction, because its resolve reads committed history.
- Left as is: a platform-API enable does not reset the insight row's shadow due time, and the copy mapping is built twice per write.
- No duplicate: no open PR writes moved insight alerts. Public artifact: nothing here comes from a customer conversation, ticket or log.

author: slayerjain
body:
## What has changed?

The record step of the `http-postgres` and `postgres-wire-features` READMEs ran:

```bash
keploy record -c "docker compose up" --container-name api --delay 10
```

`keploy record` has no `--delay` flag. keploy/keploy#1684 (v2.1.0) kept it on `keploy test` only, the command that waits for the app before it sends requests. Record sends none of its own. So the walkthrough's first keploy command failed before anything was recorded:

```
Error: unknown flag: --delay
```

with exit code 8 and about 80 lines of usage text.

This PR drops `--delay 10` from the two record commands. The `keploy test ... --delay 20` steps are correct and unchanged.

No other README, script or doc in this repository passes `--delay` to `keploy record`. I checked with a grep that joins continued (`\`) lines.

Companion changes: keploy/docs#936 fixes the same flag on the installation pages, and keploy/keploy fixes the CLI's own `Example: keploy record ... --delay 6` hint (branch `train/fix/record-delay-hint`, 937548fa4).

## How has this been tested?

- With the current keploy, the old command exits 8 with `unknown flag: --delay`.
- Without `--delay`, `keploy record -c "docker compose up" --container-name api` records the `http-postgres` sample's traffic from `test.sh` and `test_projects.sh`: 35 tests, in a first-run walkthrough on Linux.

author: jconsidi
body:
## Summary

Makes clobber config driven and gives it bounds, so `build_bound_backward` can solve it.
Along the way, fixes two unchecked casts that segfaulted and a duplicate check that never fired.
Each commit stands alone:

- `bfc0c97` **build_bound_backward**: the `dynamic_cast<ConfigGameBase *>` was dereferenced unchecked, so a non config game segfaulted. It now names the game and exits 1.
- `ad3d333` **get_game**: `dynamic_cast<Game *>` was returned unchecked and no caller tests for null, so a puzzle name such as `slidingtile_3x3` segfaulted in any binary. It now throws `logic_error` naming the game, like `get_puzzle`.
- `eb370ac` **clobber move graph to config**: `generate-config-clobber.py` writes `move_graph_{0,1}.json`, a transcription of the former `ClobberGame::build_move_graph` with the same node names, order, changes and edge names. It also covers 2x2 so its hand written tests keep a `game.json`. `ClobberGame` now derives from `ConfigNormalPlayGame` like `CramGame`.
- `d968f47` **ConfigBase intersection component**: mirrors `union`. An empty input list throws rather than accepting every position.
- `4b41a7d` **clobber bounds**: every move removes exactly one hostile stone and keeps the friendly count, so after `p` ply character 1 has its initial count less floor(p/2) and character 2 less ceil(p/2). Each `bound,ply=NNN` is the intersection of those two exact counts, up to the last ply where neither is negative.
- `2f8d7d8` **gameconfig duplicate check**: `add_component` checked the outer dict instead of `components_data["components"]`, so a duplicate silently overwrote the first definition. It now raises `RuntimeError` like the node and edge checks.

## Testing

Move graph port, checked against the C++ graph it replaces:
- `render_move_graph` output for all eleven clobber sizes is byte identical before and after, covering node names, changes, edge names and sources, forward and backward.
- `solve_backward clobber_4x4` from an empty scratch gives the same result (P1 wins in 11 ply), and all 64 backward DFAs have the same sha256 as before.

Bounds, on clobber_4x4:
- Every `forward,ply=0..16` set from `build_forward` lies inside `bound,ply=0..16`. A deliberately shifted bound is caught at once, so the check is not vacuous.
- `build_bound_backward clobber_4x4 16 0` leaves nothing unknown and finds the initial position winning, matching `solve_backward`, in 1m40s against 5m38s.
- Every winning and losing set of that solve passes both the C++ and Rust `verify_*` programs, ply 16 as terminal and each earlier ply against the next.

Generally:
- `make test` passes, after a clean rebuild of all objects.
- All five `generate-config-*.py` scripts give identical output under the old and new `gameconfig.py` duplicate check.
- Before and after runs confirm both cast fixes: the old binaries segfaulted (exit 139), the new ones stop with a message.

## Known issues, not from this PR

- `cargo test` fails in `positions_manual` on `main` too, at `config/cram_2x2/positions-manual.json`, because the Rust side has no cram rules; `slidingtile_*` would fail the same way. With those manual files left out, the test passes on this branch's config (21 positions across 25 games, clobber_2x2 included).
- `makedepend` was missing in the Linux container used for this work, and there is no `.depend`, so header changes did not trigger rebuilds. The testing above used a clean rebuild for that reason.
- Clobber sizes without a config directory now fail at startup with a clear error instead of building from the dimensions.
- No test exercises the new `intersection` type's empty-input error.

author: spicysharkco
body:
Closes #1382

Cause: `manager` and `kubeconfig-generator` build the zap logger and call `ctrl.SetLogger` when the command is constructed, before cobra parses the command line. Their `--zap-*` flags are bound to options that were already copied, so they never reach the logger. `migrate` has no zap flags and uses whichever logger the other two set.

Fix: bind the zap flags once on the root command's persistent flags and call `ctrl.SetLogger` in the root `PersistentPreRun`, which runs after parsing. The two per-command blocks are removed. The default is still development mode with the console encoder, and `migrate` now takes the same flags. No subcommand defines its own `PersistentPreRun`, so the root one runs for all three.

The chart passes `--zap-devel` to the manager only when `loggingDevel.enable` is true, and to the kubeconfig generator only when `kubeconfigGenerator.loggingDevel.enable` is true. Both default to false, so nothing is passed; when it is passed, it equals the built-in default. Either way these deployments log as before. A deployment that passes `--zap-*` flags itself, for example through `extraArgs`, will now see them take effect: `--zap-devel=false` gives JSON output and `--zap-log-level=error` hides the info lines.

Test: there are no unit tests for these packages, so I ran the built binary with no kubeconfig. Each command logs its start-up lines and exits on the missing configuration (`manager` with `--pod-namespace=ns --serviceaccount-name=sa --webhook-ca-path=<file>`, `migrate` with `--tenant-control-plane=a/b --target-datastore=c`).

| command | flag | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `manager` | none | 6 INFO lines | 6 INFO lines |
| `manager` | `--zap-log-level=error` | 6 INFO lines | 0 INFO lines |
| `manager` | `--zap-encoder=json` | console lines | JSON lines |
| `migrate` | none | 1 INFO line | 1 INFO line |
| `migrate` | `--zap-log-level=error` | `Error: unknown flag: --zap-log-level` | 0 INFO lines |
| `migrate` | `--zap-encoder=json` | `Error: unknown flag: --zap-encoder` | JSON lines |
| `kubeconfig-generator` | none | 5 INFO lines | 5 INFO lines |
| `kubeconfig-generator` | `--zap-log-level=error` | 5 INFO lines | 0 INFO lines |
| `kubeconfig-generator` | `--zap-encoder=json` | console lines | JSON lines |

With no flag, the output of all three commands is the same before and after, except for the line numbers in the stack trace of the error. `--help` on the root command and on each subcommand lists the zap flags once. `go build ./...`, `go vet ./cmd/...` and golangci-lint with the repo config pass.

author: fredde87
body:
## What this is

CONTRIBUTING requires that *"the selected complete status root must cover every declared read
domain, proven by an exact-profile integration test"*. This is that proof, applied to the whole
registry at once rather than per model — so a new profile is covered by writing its declaration,
not by remembering to add a test.

Ten guards, parametrised over the registry: **78 cases across 12 models.**

- every claimed read domain has a typed body in the status root its grammar selects, is actually
  askable through a builder, and is consumed by `coordinator_status`
- declared segment paging matches the page geometry of the grammar it reads through, and those
  pages reach observed state
- scalar white-balance readback has a typed payload where claimed
- every declared video mode builds
- every advertised music mode can produce packets
- the parameter-write table agrees with the variants it gates, so the two places that each say
  *"this mode needs an `a3` upload"* cannot drift apart
- no conflict markers are committed

## No findings

**All pass on this tree — nothing here reports a current defect.** They are the checks whose
absence lets this class of breakage sit: a profile can declare a capability its grammar cannot
express, and nothing fails until a real device answers, at which point the reader's exception
lands inside the BLE notification callback and is swallowed.

## Two notes on how they're written

The status-root path is **derived** from the grammar name
(`speculative/<grammar>_status_reply.ksy`, with the two pre-convention names as commented
exceptions) rather than listed — a hand-kept list stops covering models added after it is written
instead of failing on them.

Skips are **explicit and reasoned** (runtime-resolved segment capability, or a domain the profile
does not claim) rather than silent `continue`s, so an exhaustive check cannot quietly become a
partial one.

No runtime code is touched. Happy to split or drop any individual guard you don't want.

## Validation

author: lukeberrycode
body:
## Summary

Adds a read-only GraphQL API at `/api/graphql`, using GraphQL Yoga in a Next.js route handler. The aim is to demonstrate GraphQL and experiment with it (README aims 2 and 3). Decision record: [ADR 0015](docs/adr/0015-graphql-api.md).

- **Libraries (pinned exactly):** `graphql-yoga` 5.24.1, `graphql` 16.14.2; dev: `vitest` 4.1.11. All released at least four weeks ago.
- **Schema** (`src/lib/graphql/schema.ts`): `image(id)`, `images(first, after)` (cursor pagination, newest first, 1 to 50 a page) and `collections`. Types: `Image`, `Region`, `Annotation`, `Author`, `Collection`, `ImagePage`, `PageInfo`. `Author` is only a name. No emails, approval state, user ids, fingerprints, storage keys or Auth.js rows. No mutations: writes stay in the server actions.
- **N+1:** nested fields use Prisma's fluent API, which batches `findUnique` calls into one query per level.
- **Limits** (`src/lib/graphql/limits.ts`): a validation rule allowing at most 8 levels and 200 fields (aliases included). Production turns off introspection (graphql-js's `NoSchemaIntrospectionCustomRule`) and GraphiQL. Yoga's own defaults also apply: no batching, no mutations over GET, masked errors in production.
- **Untrusted Markdown:** `bodyMarkdown` is returned as stored. Its schema description points to ADR 0008's rendering rules.
- **Docs:** ADR 0015 plus its index entry. README (stack, `npm test`, a "GraphQL API" section with an example `curl` query) and `docs/architecture.md` (overview, routes, directory layout, a GraphQL section).

## Testing

- `npm run lint`: clean.
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean (after `npx next typegen`, which generates the `PageProps`/`LayoutProps` types in a fresh clone).
- `npm test`: 17 Vitest tests pass. They cover nested results, no private fields (the fake DB returns whole user rows, including emails, and the response doesn't contain them), pagination and its bounds, collections, depth and field limits (fragments, aliases, a fragment cycle), and introspection and GraphiQL in development vs production.
- `next build`: succeeds; `/api/graphql` is dynamic.
- Manual checks against `next start` (no database): `{ __typename }`, the `first` bound error, introspection refused, GraphiQL not served (406), and GET queries work. This confirms that Next's bundle has no dual-package problem with graphql.
- Manual checks against a throwaway local Postgres (`prisma dev`, separate instance, since removed), with migrations applied and a few rows seeded: a nested query returned the expected data. Prisma's query log showed batched `IN (...)` queries. A page of 1 image and a page of 3 each took 11 SQL queries.

## Not verified

- No Playwright system test was added, and the existing system tests weren't run: they need `.env` with R2 credentials.
- Not tried on the Vercel preview yet. Worth running the example query in the README against the preview URL (GraphiQL is off there, because previews run with `NODE_ENV=production`).
- No rate limiting. The limits bound one request's cost, not the number of requests (see ADR 0015).

author: mmuhofy
body:
## What this changes

The app's chrome samples the terminal's **pixels** with `view.draw(canvas)`. That
works on the Termux view, which is a software-rendered View, and draws nothing
of the terminal on the engine's `GLSurfaceView` — the blur behind the top bar's
pills and the colour behind the selection menu would both go.

So the app no longer asks a view for pixels. It asks a **source** for the
terminal's appearance, and the source says which terminal answered.

## Two kinds, never interchangeable

`TerminalAppearanceKind` is `TERMUX` or `ENGINE`, and the kind is part of the
answer. A Termux-backed terminal never gets engine colours and the other way
round — a colour field from one terminal is not a colour field from the other.

- **The backdrop** gets a *colour field* from the engine: the background
  colours, one rectangle per cell, for the rows the strip covers. It is **not a
  picture** — no glyphs, because the engine reports colours, not what is drawn
  in the cells. Blurring it gives the pill the terminal's colours rather than
  its text.
- **The selection menu** gets the region's **average colour**, as a flat
  picture, and skips its blur: a flat picture blurred is the same flat picture.

The Termux path keeps both exactly as they were — the capture code was moved
**verbatim** into `TermuxAppearanceSource`, the same bitmap sizes, the same
no-translation strip, the same clip and translate, the same recycle on failure.

## Bounded

The engine is asked only for the rows and cells the region covers — never the
whole grid, whose answer is about 40 KB of text across JNI. The timers are
unchanged: 500 ms for the backdrop, 90 ms for the menu, on the main thread.

## Checklist

- [x] CI: `Build Debug` and `Unit Tests`
- [x] New user-facing strings: none
- [x] No build output in the diff
- [x] The Termux path is unchanged, statement for statement

## Notes for the reviewer

- **The app hosts no engine-backed terminal yet**, so `EngineAppearanceSource`
  has no caller. It is the half of the seam the P3 engine host will publish.
  Nothing about the engine path can be exercised on a device today.
- The app names `EngineSession` — it may ask a session for cell colours — and
  uses only its public API: `cellColors(...)` and the grid geometry. It never
  touches the engine's view or its renderer.
- Colours are resolved through `CellColor.backgroundRgb`, which applies the
  OSC 4/10/11/12 overrides. The renderer installs that table when it draws,
  so before the first frame the source sees the default palette.
- The engine's strip assumes the grid starts at the surface's top-left, which
  is true for the current renderer, and that the pill offsets are in the same
  pixels — they come from the pane's root bounds, so the engine view has to
  fill its `AndroidView` the way the Termux one does.
- **Pre-existing inaccuracy in the Termux path, reported and not fixed:** the
  selection menu samples the region at the *selection's* top-left with the
  menu's size, but the menu is drawn below the selection — so the blurred
  picture comes from a different part of the screen than the region behind the
  menu. The engine path inherits the same rectangle, so the two agree.
- **No tests**: the app module's test source set was outside the scope this
  change was given. The app module already has JUnit and Robolectric wired, so
  a test for the colour maths is possible later.

body:
The full home screen improvement plan: the numbers made sense only to someone who knew the scheduler, the cards hid most of the map, the map showed a slanted box at the edge of its data, and four game modes had no explanation.

## Numbers (phase 1)
- **Learning and known in one line:** `12 בלמידה · 0 ידועים · מתוך 202`, with known first once there is at least one. "Known" takes 21 days of stable memory, so new players saw "0 known" for weeks.
- **"מה זה ידוע?"** expands a one-sentence explanation in place (polite live region).
- **Rank progress bar** plus the existing `rank_next` line, until now only on Progress.
- **One done-for-today line:** `✓ סיימתם להיום. יש עוד 7 מקומות לתרגול, אם בא לכם.` The due count is now places, not cards, and the due line drops a zero part.

## Room for the map (phase 2)
- **Compact top card:** the rank leads (as the heading; "המפה שלך" stays as the pane title for screen readers), with the progress bar, next rank and counts under it. Rows wrap whole at large text sizes (`FlowRow`).
- **Streak** moved next to today's status in the bottom card.
- **Other modes fold** under "עוד דרכים לתרגל", so the daily session is the one obvious action. The camera keeps its framing while the list is open.
- **Map credits** moved off the card to a "© נתוני מפה" chip on the map (opens a dialog) and to Settings under the map section.

## The map (phase 3)
- **No more slanted box.** The map data stops at a lon/lat window, slanted on the Israeli grid, and the sea color showed past it. `tools/build_content.py` now emits `beyond_land` and `beyond_sea` layers (land all round, and the open Mediterranean to the northwest following the coast north of the window). `MapView` draws them first, and clips the neighbors' outline to the window so only real borders are stroked. Assets regenerated with the pipeline (rebuild is byte-identical, so the `content` check holds); `map.json` grows 120 → 126 KB.
- **Seas and countries are no longer painted** with the mastery wash on home. Once practiced, they tinted the whole background blue-grey and outlined the data's edge.
- **Legend** ("בלמידה" / "ידוע") over the map, in the same words as the counts.

## Modes explained (phase 4)
Each mode is a card with a one-line description, or when locked, what opens it ("ייפתח אחרי 4 מקומות שלמדתם (עכשיו 2)"). Locked cards are faded as a whole.

## Tests
- `./gradlew test` passes locally (all 33), plus `:app:assembleDebug`.
- New `MotivationTest.homeExplainsKnownPlacesAndCreditsTheMap` (counts, legend, explanation, credits dialog) and `homeWorksWithTheLargestText` (200% font: screenshot, then opens Blitz through the folded list).
- Tests that open modes from home now unfold the list first.
- Screenshots checked: light, dark, relief, modes open, 200% font.

author: tjfernandes
body:
Não havia forma de desligar o que o `deploy/amalia_online.sh` liga. Só o vLLM tinha `--stop`, no `amalia_llm.sh`.

## O que faz
`deploy/amalia_offline.sh` pára, por esta ordem:
1. **o vigilante** (`amalia_online.sh` em qualquer modo), senão voltava a repor tudo no minuto seguinte;
2. **o túnel** autossh para o VPS e o ssh filho dele;
3. **o uvicorn da 8001**, e com ele o SAM 3, os embedders e o ditado, com até 30 s para descarregar a GPU;
4. **o vLLM da 8004**, pelo `amalia_llm.sh --stop`.

Cada passo manda SIGTERM, espera e só manda SIGKILL se o processo não sair.

| Uso | Efeito |
|---|---|
| `deploy/amalia_offline.sh` | desliga tudo |
| `deploy/amalia_offline.sh --manter-llm` | desliga tudo menos o vLLM |
| `deploy/amalia_offline.sh --simular` | só mostra o que pararia |

Não mexe no nginx do VPS, num VLM na 8005 nem em instâncias de teste noutros portos. No fim lista o que ficou a correr e a memória da GPU. Recusa correr com sudo.

O `amalia_online.sh` ganha uma linha no cabeçalho a apontar para este script.

## Testes
- `--simular` sobre a produção real encontrou o túnel, o ssh, o uvicorn e o vLLM, e não parou nada.
- Uma cópia com os padrões trocados por processos falsos parou os quatro elos. O backend falso ignorava o SIGTERM e saiu com SIGKILL.
- O caminho real pelo `amalia_llm.sh --stop` não foi corrido, para não desligar a produção.
